bill_summary: This bill requires that ballot questions and petition signature pages be written in plain language that avoids legal jargon, passive voice, and double negatives to ensure voter understanding. It moves the certification deadline for ballot questions to July 1 preceding a general election, establishes a 15-day public comment period for the language of ballot questions, and mandates that the State Board of Elections and local boards post the full text of ballot questions and associated legislation links online at least 90 days before an election.
stakeholders: Maryland voters, petition sponsors, the Secretary of State, local boards of elections, and county and municipal attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Elections can handle the bill's requirements with existing resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation, including preparing guidelines for plain language, designing petition forms, managing the public comment period, and hosting the official ballot question information on its website.
The Secretary of State is required by the bill to prepare and certify information for statewide ballot questions and referendums to the State Board of Elections by specified deadlines.

The Attorney General is responsible for approving the summarizing statements for constitutional amendments and referendums to ensure they meet clarity standards and are devoid of technical terms as required by the bill.

The bill designates the Clerks of the Circuit Court as a secondary authority for certifying ballot questions and grants the Supreme Court of Maryland the power to adjust ballot certification deadlines under extraordinary circumstances.

The Department of Information Technology houses the Maryland Digital Service, which leads the Maryland Plain Language Initiative. This initiative sets the communication standards that the State Board of Elections must incorporate into its guidelines under the bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting employers and their agents, representatives, and designees from taking certain actions against an employee or applicant for employment because the employee or applicant takes certain actions regarding employer-sponsored meetings during which the employer communicates the opinion of the employer regarding religious matters or political matters; authorizing an employee to file a certain complaint with the Commissioner of Labor and Industry; etc.
Title: Labor and Employment - Mandatory Meetings on Religious or Political Matters - Employee Attendance and Participation (Maryland Worker Freedom Act)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Worker Freedom Act prohibits employers from discharging, disciplining, or penalizing employees or job applicants for refusing to attend or participate in employer-sponsored meetings where the employer communicates opinions on religious or political matters. It requires employers to notify employees of these rights through posters and model notices and authorizes the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to investigate complaints, mediate disputes, and assess civil penalties for violations.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Labor and Industry (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Maryland employees, job applicants, and employers (excluding religious organizations, certain political organizations, and educational institutions for specific academic purposes).
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $131,600 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire one investigator and a half-time assistant attorney general to manage complaints and enforcement. Costs are projected to increase to $173,100 by FY 2031. General fund revenues from civil penalties ($10,000 for initial violations and $25,000 for subsequent violations) are not expected to be material. Local government and small business impacts are estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commissioner of Labor and Industry, located within the Department of Labor, is the primary official responsible for enforcing the act. This includes investigating complaints, conducting mediation, assessing civil penalties, and developing the mandatory posters and notices for employers.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and represents the Commissioner in circuit court enforcement actions. The fiscal note specifically identifies the need for an Assistant Attorney General to support the bill's implementation.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies and benefits. Since the bill applies to the state as an employer, DBM would oversee compliance and the distribution of required notices across executive branch agencies.
The bill authorizes the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to petition the circuit courts for the enforcement of orders, which impacts the judicial system's workload and administrative procedures.

The bill applies to public higher education institutions as employers, but includes specific exemptions and permissions regarding communications that are part of coursework, academic programs, or symposiums.
As an independent public university and state agency, Morgan State is subject to the bill's requirements as an employer, including the specific provisions related to academic coursework and programs.
As an independent public honors college, Saint Mary's is subject to the bill's requirements as an employer, including the specific provisions related to academic coursework and programs.
The Commission coordinates policies for Maryland's higher education institutions, which are specifically mentioned in the bill regarding coursework and academic communications exemptions.
The bill includes specific provisions and exemptions for educational institutions and nonprofit training programs, which fall under the oversight and leadership of MSDE.

Synopsis: Establishing the Gambling Prevention Technology Pilot Program in the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission; requiring Bowie State University and Morgan State University to participate in the Pilot Program; requiring the Commission, in collaboration with certain entities, to designate certain no gambling zones on each campus, develop certain informational signage, and identify and implement certain technologies; and requiring the Commission to submit a report on the Pilot Program on or before January 1, 2031.
Title: Sports Wagering - Gambling Prevention Technology Pilot Program - Establishment
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Ways and Means; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Lottery and Gaming Control Agency, State
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Gambling Prevention Technology Pilot Program within the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission, requiring Bowie State University and Morgan State University to participate. The program involves designating 'no gambling zones' on campuses and requiring online sports wagering operators to use geofencing technology to block access to wagering platforms within these boundaries. The program aims to mitigate problem gambling among students and evaluate the effectiveness of such technology.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission (SLGCC)
stakeholders: Students at Bowie State University and Morgan State University, online sports wagering operators, and the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling.
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures for the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency increase by $90,600 in FY 2027 to hire a contractual program manager. Annual expenditures fluctuate between $59,700 and $114,500 through FY 2031 until the program's termination. Sports wagering revenues are not expected to be materially affected. Bowie State and Morgan State Universities are expected to collaborate using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the primary entity responsible for establishing and administering the Gambling Prevention Technology Pilot Program, overseeing sports wagering operators, and reporting findings to the Governor.

The university is explicitly named in the bill as a mandatory participant in the pilot program, required to collaborate on designating no-gambling zones and implementing prevention technologies on its campus.
Bowie State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland, is a mandatory participant in the pilot program, requiring system-level coordination and resource allocation.
The department administers the Problem Gambling Fund and oversees the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling, which is a required collaborator in the pilot program's implementation.
The fiscal note identifies a need for additional contractual personnel to manage the pilot program, requiring DBM's oversight of state personnel and budget execution.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the SLGCC, regarding the implementation of new sports wagering regulations and the enforcement of the pilot program's requirements.
As the state's lead IT agency, DoIT may be consulted on the technical viability, data security, and implementation of geofencing and real-time monitoring technologies required by the bill.

The commission establishes statewide policies for colleges and universities and may be involved in evaluating the pilot's findings to inform future gambling prevention policies across all Maryland institutions.
OLA is responsible for auditing state programs and will likely conduct fiscal compliance and performance audits of the newly established pilot program and its expenditures.
The agency is the recipient of the final report on the pilot program's findings and oversees the executive branch agencies (SLGCC and MDH) implementing the initiative.

Synopsis: Establishing the Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names to develop and implement a framework to identify real property owned by the State or a political subdivision that bears a Confederate name; and requiring the Commission to make recommendations regarding the real property that should be renamed and report its findings to the Governor, the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City, the governing body of each county, and the General Assembly by October 1, 2033.
Title: Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names - Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse

bill_summary: This bill creates a commission to identify and recommend renaming state and local government property (such as streets, buildings, and parks) named after Confederate figures or entities. The commission will consist of 24 members appointed by the Governor, hire an archivist from the Maryland State Archives, and must report its findings and recommendations by October 1, 2033.
responsible_party: Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names
stakeholders: Maryland state and local government entities (including counties and municipalities), the Maryland State Archives, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by $89,100 in fiscal 2028 for the Maryland State Archives to hire one archivist to staff the commission. Ongoing costs are estimated at $85,900 in fiscal 2029, $89,900 in fiscal 2030, and $93,800 in fiscal 2031. No impact on revenues is projected, and the bill is not expected to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Commission hire an archivist who must be an employee of the Maryland State Archives. The fiscal note attributes the personnel costs and position creation for this role to the Archives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes the Commission on State and Local Government Real Property Bearing Confederate Names, which is a temporary body tasked with conducting a specific study and providing recommendations, fitting the description of this collective entity.

The Commission is established as an independent unit within the Executive Branch. The Governor is responsible for appointing all 24 members and receiving the Commission's final report on findings and recommendations.

The bill requires the Governor to appoint 24 representatives (one from each county) with the advice and consent of the Senate. The Office of Appointments is responsible for vetting and recommending these candidates.

DBM will oversee the fiscal and personnel aspects of the bill, including the mandated appropriation for the archivist position and ensuring the Commission follows state travel regulations for expense reimbursement.
The bill specifically states that any money maintained by the Commission is subject to audit by the State, including the Legislative Auditor.

The Commission is tasked with identifying and recommending the renaming of state-owned real property, including buildings. DGS is the primary agency responsible for the planning and management of state facilities.

The bill's scope includes streets and roads. MDOT manages the state's transportation network and would be a key stakeholder in identifying and potentially renaming transportation-related real property.
The bill's scope includes parks. DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and state parks that would be subject to the Commission's review for Confederate names.

The Commission must develop a framework to identify properties and research their history. MDP oversees historical and cultural programs and provides technical assistance on land use, which is highly relevant to the Commission's mission.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies and commissions, the OAG would provide legal counsel to the newly formed Commission regarding its statutory duties and legal frameworks for property renaming.
The bill includes 'school districts' in its definition of political subdivisions whose property (such as schools) is subject to review and recommendation by the Commission.

Synopsis: Repealing a provision that authorizes a local department of social services to ask the juvenile court to find that reasonable efforts to reunify a child with the child's parent or guardian are not required if the local department concludes that a parent or guardian has involuntarily lost parental rights to a sibling of the child; and repealing the authorization for a juvenile court to waive a local department's obligation to provide certain services if a parent has involuntarily lost certain parental rights.
Title: Family Law - Children in Need of Assistance and Termination of Parental Rights (Right to Fight Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/29 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: Known as the Right to Fight Act, this bill repeals provisions that currently allow a local department of social services to request that a juvenile court waive the requirement for reasonable efforts to reunify a child with a parent if that parent has involuntarily lost parental rights to a sibling. It also repeals the court's authority to waive a local department's obligation to provide services in cases where parental rights to a sibling were involuntarily terminated.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services (DHS) and local departments of social services
stakeholders: Children in need of assistance (CINA), parents or guardians who have previously lost parental rights to a sibling involuntarily, and the Maryland Department of Human Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase by an estimated 300,000 annually for the Department of Human Services (DHS) due to a decrease in waivers for reunification services. This increase results from longer case resolution times, increased case management costs, monthly care stipends, and the provision of direct services such as parenting classes and therapy. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations of local departments of social services, which are overseen by DHS. It repeals provisions that allowed these departments to skip reunification efforts for parents who previously lost rights to a sibling, thereby increasing DHS's responsibility to provide services and manage cases. The fiscal note explicitly identifies an estimated $300,000 annual increase in DHS expenditures.

The bill amends statutes governing juvenile court proceedings for Children in Need of Assistance (CINA) and the termination of parental rights. AOC supports the judicial branch in implementing these procedural changes and was consulted for the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD's Parental Defense Division represents indigent parents in CINA and termination of parental rights proceedings. This bill directly affects the legal standards and protections available to their clients, requiring the state to provide services that were previously waivable.

The bill is expected to increase general fund expenditures by approximately $300,000 annually due to longer case resolution times and increased service provision. DBM is responsible for managing the state budget and overseeing these fiscal impacts.

OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Human Services and represents the state in civil and criminal appeals. Changes to family law and the standards for terminating parental rights will require legal guidance and defense from this office.

This office coordinates statewide efforts related to the well-being of children and families. Policies regarding child welfare, reunification, and the legal status of children in the foster care system fall within their policy coordination scope.

Synopsis: Requiring that an abortion be performed by a physician, rather than a qualified provider; repealing certain provisions of law related to State interference with an abortion, regulations related to abortion, and liability or criminal punishment for qualified providers who perform an abortion; prohibiting a physician from knowingly performing, inducing, or attempting to perform or induce an abortion under certain circumstances and subject to certain exceptions; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits physicians from performing abortions if a fetal heartbeat is detected, with limited exceptions for medical emergencies. It requires that abortions be performed only by licensed physicians, mandates specific informed consent procedures including sonograms, and establishes a private civil action mechanism for enforcement. Under this mechanism, private individuals can sue anyone who performs or aids in a prohibited abortion for statutory damages of at least $10,000 per violation. The bill also repeals existing state laws that prevent the state from interfering with abortion decisions before fetal viability.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland physicians
stakeholders: Pregnant women, licensed physicians, healthcare providers, the Maryland Department of Health, and the state court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is expected to decrease Medicaid general fund expenditures by approximately $11,300,000 annually (and $8,500,000 in FY 2027) due to a reduction in covered abortion procedures. The Maryland Department of Health will incur an annual cost of $8,787 for administrative materials and website updates. These savings may be offset by indeterminate increases in costs for labor, delivery, and newborn medical care for Medicaid-eligible individuals. Local circuit courts may experience increased expenditures to handle private civil actions authorized by the bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is mandated to create and provide informational materials and maintain a website. It also faces significant fiscal impact through the Medicaid program and oversight of the Board of Physicians.
Enforcement of the bill is handled exclusively through private civil actions, placing the entire burden of adjudication and implementation on the state court system.
As the manager of the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, the department will see direct fiscal impacts from changes in insurance coverage for abortions.
The office will likely be responsible for defending the state's immunity and the constitutionality of the bill's provisions in court.
The agency regulates health insurance carriers and enforces compliance with state insurance laws, which are directly affected by the bill's restrictions on abortion reimbursement.
The commission plans for state health system needs and oversees health care quality and accountability, which are significantly altered by the bill's new medical requirements.
The exchange manages the insurance marketplace, where the availability and nature of health plans will be affected by the bill's restrictive requirements.
The office oversees the executive branch departments implementing the bill and coordinates the state policy initiatives and immunity protections defined in the legislation.
The bill requires physicians to inform pregnant women about a father's liability for child support, which is a program administered by this department.

Synopsis: Proposing a Constitutional Amendment requiring that a special election be held at the same time as the regular statewide primary and general elections that are held in the second year of a term to fill a vacancy in the office of Delegate or Senator in the General Assembly if the vacancy occurs on or before the date that is 55 days before the deadline for filing certificates of candidacy for the regular statewide election that is held in the second year of the term.
Title: General Assembly - Special Election to Fill a Vacancy in Office
Status: In the Senate - Rereferred to Education, Energy, and the Environment

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This constitutional amendment alters the process for filling vacancies in the Maryland General Assembly. It requires a special election to be held concurrently with the regular statewide elections in the second year of a legislative term if a vacancy occurs at least 55 days before the candidacy filing deadline. The Governor would continue to make interim appointments to fill vacancies until a successor is elected or to fill the remainder of a term if the vacancy occurs late in the term.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland, Maryland State Board of Elections, and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Qualified voters in Maryland, candidates for the General Assembly, and political party central committees
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures may increase minimally to cover costs for printing and programming additional ballot styles for special elections; however, the Fiscal Note indicates these costs can be absorbed within existing resources. There is no impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is currently responsible for appointing individuals to fill General Assembly vacancies. This constitutional amendment would limit the duration of those appointments and require the Governor to issue proclamations for special elections if a vacancy occurs within a specified timeframe.

The State Board of Elections is responsible for the administration and supervision of all elections in Maryland. This bill creates a new requirement for special primary and general elections to fill legislative vacancies to be held concurrently with regular statewide elections.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and the General Assembly. They would be responsible for reviewing the legal sufficiency of the proposed constitutional amendment and advising on the implementation of new special election procedures.

The Secretary of State is the custodian of official state records, including commissions and laws. This bill changes the process and duration for which legislative commissions are issued, directly affecting the agency's record-keeping and administrative functions.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund to serve as a reserve asset for the State through the investment of cryptocurrency; and authorizing the State Treasurer to invest the funds obtained by the State through the enforcement of certain gambling violations into cryptocurrency.
Title: Strategic Digital Asset Reserve Act of Maryland
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:30 p.m.
bill_summary: The Strategic Digital Asset Reserve Act of Maryland establishes the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund administered by the State Treasurer. The fund's purpose is to invest in cryptocurrencies with a market capitalization of at least $500,000,000,000 using money seized and forfeited from state gambling violations, as well as other state appropriations, to serve as a reserve asset for Maryland.
stakeholders: Maryland State Treasurer's Office, Maryland Department of State Police, and individuals subject to asset forfeiture due to illegal gambling violations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances as illegal gambling seizures are typically handled by federal authorities rather than the State. If the fund is utilized, the State Treasurer may incur a one-time cost of approximately $10,000 to contract with a digital asset custodian and annual management fees of 3% to 5% of assets. No funding for this initiative is provided in the fiscal 2027 budget, and the bill has no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the State Treasurer as the administrator of the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund, granting them authority to invest State funds in cryptocurrency, manage custodial arrangements, and adopt necessary regulations.

The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund. As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller also monitors the fiscal impact of new special funds.
As a primary State authority for law enforcement, money seized by the Maryland State Police in connection with gambling violations would be directed to the newly established fund under the bill.
The bill allows the fund to consist of money appropriated in the State budget, requiring coordination with DBM for fiscal planning and budget execution related to the reserve fund.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which may include appropriations to the Maryland Digital Asset Reserve Fund.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the State Treasurer regarding the creation of the fund, the legality of cryptocurrency custodial agreements, and the drafting of new regulations for the State investment policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency regulates the gaming industry; the bill concerns the investment of proceeds derived from violations of gambling laws regulated and monitored within this sector.

The Board, which includes the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees significant state fiscal policies and contracts; establishing a cryptocurrency reserve represents a significant change in the State's fiscal management strategy.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to provide a toll-free voter hotline for incarcerated individuals to receive information about voting, request election-related materials, and report voting rights violations; and altering the circumstances under which an individual is not qualified to be a registered voter for the purpose of allowing individuals convicted of a felony and serving a court-ordered sentence of imprisonment for the conviction to register to vote.
Title: Election Law - Incarcerated Individuals - Voter Hotline and Voting Eligibility (Voting Rights for All Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: The Voting Rights for All Act restores voting eligibility to individuals serving a court-ordered sentence of imprisonment for a felony conviction. It requires the State Board of Elections to provide a toll-free voter hotline for incarcerated individuals to obtain voting information and report violations, and it removes reporting requirements regarding felony convictions and sentences from court clerks.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals serving sentences for felony convictions, the Maryland State Board of Elections, and the Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are expected to increase for the establishment and operation of a toll-free voter hotline by the State Board of Elections. Additional administrative costs will likely be incurred by the State Board and correctional facilities to facilitate voter registration and ballot access for incarcerated individuals. Specific fiscal estimates are unavailable because no formal Fiscal Note was provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primary tasks the State Board of Elections with providing a toll-free voter hotline for incarcerated individuals and managing the registration and eligibility changes for individuals convicted of felonies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is explicitly required to collaborate with the State Board of Elections to administer the voter hotline and manages the correctional facilities and incarcerated individuals affected by the eligibility changes.

The bill repeals requirements for clerks of the circuit and district courts to report felony conviction and imprisonment information to the State Administrator, representing a direct operational change for the judiciary's administrative arm.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and would be responsible for interpreting and defending these significant changes to election law.
The establishment of a new toll-free hotline and the administrative changes for the SBE and DPSCS will have a fiscal impact requiring budget oversight and personnel management.
The Governor oversees the executive agencies (SBE and DPSCS) implementing these policies and the bill represents a major shift in executive policy regarding voting rights.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for criminal justice strategies, this office is relevant to policy changes impacting the legal status and rights of justice-involved individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency represents indigent defendants and incarcerated individuals who are the primary population affected by the enfranchisement and the repeal of felony voting penalties.

Synopsis: Altering an exception to the prohibition against the possession of certain nondomesticated animals in the State by reducing from 10 days to 48 hours the amount of time a nonresident may travel through the State with an otherwise prohibited animal; repealing the exception to the prohibition against the possession by a person with certain disabilities of certain nondomesticated animals for a certain purpose; etc.
Title: Criminal Law – Nondomesticated Animal Prohibitions – Alterations
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: This bill expands the list of prohibited nondomesticated animals in Maryland to include zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies. It reduces the time nonresidents may possess such animals while traveling through the state from 10 days to 48 hours and repeals an exception that allowed these animals to serve as assistance animals for individuals with severe mobility disabilities.
responsible_party: Local animal control authorities and the Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Owners of zebras, kangaroos, wallaroos, and wallabies; nonresidents transporting nondomesticated animals through the state; and individuals with severe mobility-limiting disabilities who use assistance animals.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances. Potential misdemeanor fines for violations include up to $1,000 for individuals and up to $10,000 for other entities, but the overall financial impact and the effect on small businesses are estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mentions the Department of Natural Resources as the licensing authority for permits that allow individuals or entities to import, sell, or possess the nondomesticated animals listed in the bill. As the primary agency responsible for managing the state's natural resources and wildlife, they oversee the regulatory exceptions and permitting process for exotic or nondomestic species.

The bill repeals an existing exception that allowed individuals with mobility-limiting disabilities to possess these nondomesticated animals if they were trained as assistance animals. This directly impacts the rights and services coordination for the population the Department of Disabilities is charged with protecting and supporting.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing criminal laws. Since this bill amends the Criminal Law Article and creates new prohibitions (misdemeanors) regarding the possession and trade of certain animals, the agency would be responsible for enforcement actions.

The bill modifies criminal prohibitions and penalties related to nondomesticated animals. The Administrative Office of the Courts manages the judicial branch, which will process and adjudicate any misdemeanor charges or litigation arising from the updated law.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies like the Department of Natural Resources regarding the implementation and enforcement of new statutory prohibitions. They also represent the state in any legal challenges regarding the updated criminal law.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry to study and make recommendations on restructuring the State's electric utility industry; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly on or before November 1, 2027.
Title: Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland’s Electric Utility Industry to evaluate and make recommendations on alternative utility and governance models, such as publicly owned utilities and cooperatives. The task force is required to study electricity rates, infrastructure investment, legal implications of asset transfers, and the potential costs and benefits of transitioning to different market participation models.
stakeholders: Maryland electric ratepayers, investor-owned and municipal electric utilities, electric cooperatives, and PJM Interconnection, LLC.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by approximately $667,000 in FY 2027 and $333,000 in FY 2028 to hire a consultant to support the task force's duties. These costs are offset by a corresponding increase in special fund revenues from assessments imposed by the PSC on regulated public service companies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Public Service Commission (PSC) provide staff for the Task Force. Furthermore, the PSC Chair designates the Task Force Chair, and a member of the Commission is a required member of the Task Force. The fiscal note indicates a significant impact of approximately $1 million on the PSC for consultant services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary body, the Task Force to Study Restructuring Maryland's Electric Utility Industry, which falls directly under this collective designation for state-authorized task forces conducting special studies.

The Director of the Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) is a mandated member of the Task Force and is responsible for designating a representative from an independent electricity generation company to serve as a member.

The People's Counsel is a mandated member of the Task Force. The Task Force's focus on restructuring the utility industry and evaluating electricity rates aligns directly with the agency's mission to represent the interests of residential utility consumers.

The Secretary of the Environment is a mandated member of the Task Force. Restructuring the electric utility industry has significant implications for environmental quality and the state's climate commitments.

The Secretary of Transportation is a mandated member of the Task Force, as utility restructuring and grid management significantly impact the state's transportation infrastructure and electrification efforts.

The Task Force is required to analyze the legal implications of transferring privately owned electric company assets to public ownership, specifically through eminent domain. As the chief legal officer for the state and counsel to its agencies, the OAG will likely provide necessary legal guidance on these constitutional and statutory matters.

The Governor is responsible for appointing a public representative with expertise in the electric utility industry to the Task Force. Additionally, the Governor oversees the executive agencies participating in the study.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and personnel. The bill carries a fiscal impact involving special fund expenditures and assessment revenues that DBM must monitor, as well as provisions for travel reimbursements provided in the state budget.
The Office of Appointments within the Executive Department would likely assist the Governor in recruiting and vetting the required appointee with utility industry expertise.

Synopsis: Applying statewide certain provisions of law authorizing the use of speed monitoring systems in certain residential districts.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Speed Monitoring Systems - Residential Districts
Status: In the Senate - Second Reading Passed

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: This bill expands the authorization to install and use speed monitoring systems (speed cameras) on highways in residential districts with a maximum posted speed limit of 35 miles per hour to all local jurisdictions in Maryland, removing the previous restriction that limited such use to Anne Arundel, Montgomery, and Prince George’s counties.
responsible_party: Local jurisdictions and their governing bodies, and the District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, local governments, and residents in residential areas
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues from contested cases in the District Court may increase minimally starting in fiscal 2027. Local jurisdictions (other than those already authorized) will experience increased expenditures and revenues, potentially significantly, depending on the extent to which they choose to install and operate speed camera systems under the bill's expanded authority. Specific dollar estimates for the total impact are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates that general fund revenues from contested cases in the District Court may increase, and the Judiciary (AOC) provided information regarding the impact on court caseloads.

MDOT is the parent agency for the State Highway Administration and the Maryland Transportation Authority, which are both directly mentioned as entities authorized to use speed monitoring systems and provided information for the fiscal note.

The bill explicitly references the State Highway Administration's authority to use speed monitoring systems on specific interstates and establishes the engineering standards for speed limits in residential districts.
The bill explicitly identifies the Maryland Transportation Authority as an authorized user of speed monitoring systems on Maryland Route 200 (Intercounty Connector).
As a modal administration within MDOT, the MVA oversees highway safety initiatives and maintains driving records that are directly impacted by the automated enforcement of speed limits.

The Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing motor vehicle and criminal laws across the state and providing specialized support to local allied law enforcement agencies who will implement these speed monitoring systems.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (MDOT, MSP) responsible for transportation and safety, and the Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law.
The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for state agencies such as MDOT and provides counsel regarding the implementation and legality of state transportation laws.
The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and collector of revenues; the fiscal note mentions an increase in general fund revenues derived from contested speed camera citations.

Synopsis: Requiring that each legislative district established for the purpose of electing members of the House of Delegates consist of three single-member delegate districts; requiring the General Assembly to enact a law establishing and governing a Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention to establish legislative and congressional districts and establishing certain requirements regarding the Redistricting Convention; establishing the Redistricting Convention; etc.
Title: Districting - Single-Member Districts and Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/16 at 12:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to require that each legislative district for the House of Delegates be divided into three single-member delegate districts. It also establishes an elected 188-member Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention to draw legislative and congressional boundary lines every ten years following the decennial census, a duty previously handled by the Governor and General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections, Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention, Supreme Court of Maryland, Office of the Attorney General, and Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for the General Assembly and Congress, and residents of Maryland legislative and congressional districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will increase state expenditures every ten years beginning in fiscal 2031 to conduct elections for the 188 members of the Redistricting Convention. The state will also incur costs for convention operations, including travel reimbursements for members and administrative support from the Office of the Attorney General and Department of Legislative Services. There may be additional costs related to the Supreme Court of Maryland's expanded original jurisdiction over redistricting challenges. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly impacts the Governor's Office by proposing a constitutional amendment that removes the Governor's current authority to prepare and present legislative redistricting plans to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Office of the Attorney General, alongside the Department of Legislative Services, shall jointly staff the newly created Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Convention.
DBM is relevant as it oversees the state budget, and the bill requires that members of the 188-person Redistricting Convention be reimbursed for expenses as provided in the state budget.
The bill requires that all meetings of the Redistricting Convention be livestreamed for public observation, which falls under the telecommunications and digital services strategy managed by DoIT.

The Department of Planning typically manages the state's census data and GIS mapping infrastructure, which are essential technical resources for the Redistricting Convention's task of drawing boundary lines.

The bill grants the Supreme Court of Maryland exclusive original jurisdiction to hear challenges to redistricting plans or to establish plans if the Convention fails to do so; the AOC provides the operational and legal support for the judiciary to execute these duties.
SBE is a primary implementing agency responsible for determining the election date for the 188 convention members and apportioning seats among the counties based on decennial census data.

As the custodian of state laws and official records, the Secretary of State is relevant because redistricting plans certified by the Convention become law and are treated like bills for the purposes of publication and codification.

The bill establishes strict eligibility requirements for convention members, including prohibitions on current or former registered lobbyists; the State Ethics Commission regulates lobbying and would be involved in verifying such qualifications.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Civic Excellence Program for public high school students that exhibit civic readiness and engagement;  requiring a certain capstone project be included in the Program; authorizing a local school system to participate in the Program to recognize students for their civic readiness and civic engagement; and requiring the State Board of Education, no later than the 2027-2028 school year, to adopt certain regulations to establish criteria for awarding a seal of civic excellence.
Title: Public Schools - Maryland Civic Excellence Program - Established
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Awards, Medals, and Prizes -see also- Gaming&Gambl; Lottery

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Maryland Civic Excellence Program to recognize public high school students for their civic readiness and engagement. Participating local school systems award a 'Seal of Civic Excellence' and a cord, medal, or other insignia to students who meet criteria established by the State Board of Education. To qualify, students must complete a capstone project focused on civic service in state, county, or local government through an extracurricular activity.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Education and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Public high school students, local school systems, and public high schools in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Education can implement the program and adopt regulations using existing resources. For local school systems, participation is discretionary; systems that choose to participate may experience increased expenditures for staff and related program costs, though specific dollar estimates are unavailable. State and local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the State Department of Education and the State Board of Education to establish, administer, and regulate the Maryland Civic Excellence Program, including developing guidelines and criteria for the Seal of Civic Excellence.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program's focus on civic readiness, civic engagement, and service-based capstone projects aligns directly with this agency's mission to promote service and civic engagement and create workforce pathways through service.

The bill allows participating local school systems to collaborate with institutions of higher education to support the program's implementation. As the regulatory body for these institutions, the Commission may be involved in coordinating such partnerships.

As a collection of public institutions of higher education, the University System and its member institutions are potential collaborators for local school systems implementing the Maryland Civic Excellence Program.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is identified as a potential partner that local school systems may collaborate with to support the program's implementation.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College is a potential collaborator for local school systems seeking to support the civic excellence program.

Synopsis: Requiring a county that submits an application to the Secretary of Transportation for funding for certain transportation services for elderly and disabled persons to identify interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers in the application; requiring the Secretary to adopt procedures to ensure counties cooperate in establishing interjurisdictional paratransit service routes between facilities within certain networks of providers; etc.
Title: Transportation - Paratransit Services - Interjurisdictional Routes
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires counties that apply for State funding for elderly and handicapped transportation services to identify and establish interjurisdictional paratransit routes connecting to facilities within specific healthcare networks, including Adventist Healthcare, Johns Hopkins Medicine, LifeBridge Health, Luminis Health Maryland, MedStar Health, and the University of Maryland Medical System.
stakeholders: Elderly and handicapped residents, Maryland county governments, Baltimore City, and major healthcare provider networks.
fiscal_impact_summary: State requirements can be managed within existing budgeted resources. Total State funding for the Statewide Special Transportation Assistance Program (at least 4305908 adjusted for inflation) remains unchanged, but the bill may shift the distribution of these funds among local jurisdictions. Local governments are expected to see an indeterminate increase in expenditures to provide the mandated interjurisdictional paratransit routes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The Secretary of Transportation manages the Statewide Special Transportation Assistance Program (SSTAP), identifies funding for elderly and handicapped transportation in the budget, and is tasked with adopting procedures to ensure counties cooperate on interjurisdictional paratransit routes.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Transportation to consult with the Department of Aging in distributing funds and developing enforcement procedures. Furthermore, local area agencies on aging, which fall under this department's network, must certify approval of the projects for which counties seek funding.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Transportation consult with the Department of Disabilities regarding the distribution of funds and the creation of enforcement procedures for the paratransit program, which specifically serves handicapped individuals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and would be responsible for advising on the development of new procedures and enforcement mechanisms related to interjurisdictional paratransit requirements and county cooperation.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and long-term planning. The bill requires MDOT to identify specific amounts within its budget for these services, which DBM monitors to ensure efficiency and alignment with state resources.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and appoints the Secretary of Transportation. The bill modifies the administrative responsibilities and budget execution of a cabinet-level agency reporting to the Governor.

Synopsis: Requiring certain expedited proceedings in a wrongful detainer action if the property that is the subject of the action is, at the time of the complaint, advertised or listed for sale or lease by the complainant and requiring that notice of a hearing or appeal be served in person or, under certain circumstances, posted conspicuously on the property; requiring the District Court or the circuit court to issue a warrant within 24 hours if the court rules in favor of the complainant in an expedited wrongful detainer action; etc.
Title: Real Property - Expedited Wrongful Detainer Proceedings - Property for Sale or Lease
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m. (Economic Matters)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill establishes an expedited legal process for wrongful detainer actions when the real property in question is advertised or listed for sale or lease. It mandates specific shortened timelines for court summons, hearings, and judicial rulings, requiring the District Court to hold a hearing within five days of a complaint and issue a ruling within two business days. Additionally, it requires that warrants for possession be issued within 24 hours of a favorable ruling and executed immediately by the sheriff.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District Court and Circuit Courts) and local Sheriffs' Offices
stakeholders: Property owners listing real estate for sale or lease, individuals in actual possession of property without a legal right, the Maryland court system, and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While the Maryland Judiciary and local sheriffs' offices may experience operational impacts to meet the expedited schedules for hearings, appeals, and warrant executions, the fiscal note states that no significant expenditure or revenue changes are expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates specific, expedited timelines for processing wrongful detainer cases in both District and Circuit Courts, including requirements for immediate summons, hearings within five days, rulings within two business days, and warrant issuance within 24 hours. The Administrative Office of the Courts is the primary agency responsible for providing the operational, legal, and technological support needed to implement these procedural changes within the Maryland Judicial Branch.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the chief legal officer for the State, providing legal counsel to the Judiciary and all state agencies. The agency would be responsible for interpreting the new legal requirements for expedited proceedings and representing the state's interests or advising the courts on the implementation of these procedural changes to the Real Property Article.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development is tasked with ensuring safe and secure housing and overseeing community vitality. While the bill is procedural, it modifies the process for recovering possession of real property that is listed for sale or lease, which has implications for property owners and the broader real estate market within the department's policy scope.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an institution of higher education from denying access or services to a student based on the student's diagnosis of sickle cell disease; requiring an institution of higher education to provide reasonable accommodations for students with sickle cell disease; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop an education and awareness campaign, designed to enhance understanding of sickle cell disease and reduce stigmas, for institutions of higher education in the State regarding students with sickle cell disease; etc.
Title: Sickle Cell Disease - Institutions of Higher Education - Policies, Procedures, and Educational Campaigns (Kaitlyn's Law)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment and Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies

bill_summary: Known as Kaitlyn's Law, this bill prohibits Maryland institutions of higher education from denying access or services to students based on a sickle cell disease diagnosis and requires these institutions to provide reasonable accommodations. It mandates the Maryland Department of Health to collaborate with other state entities to develop an education and awareness campaign, clinical procedures, and a framework for assessing and supporting students with sickle cell disease.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Students with sickle cell disease and the faculty, health personnel, and administrative staff at Maryland institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $139,400 in FY 2027 and $157,900 in FY 2028. These funds will cover the costs of hiring contractual personnel at the Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Higher Education Commission to develop educational materials, clinical procedures, and monitoring frameworks. Public institutions of higher education and local community colleges are expected to implement the bill's requirements using existing resources, although some minor costs for student accommodations may be incurred.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency tasked with developing the education and awareness campaign, creating the framework and procedures for institutions of higher education, and providing technical assistance and monitoring. The fiscal note also identifies a significant expenditure increase for MDH to hire a nurse program administrator.

The Commission is explicitly required to consult with the Department of Health to develop the sickle cell framework and procedures, jointly provide technical assistance to institutions, and develop a process to monitor compliance. The fiscal note identifies a fiscal impact for MHEC to hire a contractual program manager.

As the governing body for 12 public institutions of higher education, USM is directly impacted by the bill's requirements to provide reasonable accommodations, establish reporting procedures, and ensure non-discrimination based on sickle cell disease diagnosis.

As a public institution of higher education and a state agency, Morgan State University must comply with the bill's mandates regarding student accommodations, access, and reporting procedures for sickle cell disease.
As a public honors college and independent state agency, the college is required to implement the bill's policies, procedures, and accommodation requirements for students with sickle cell disease.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Statewide Steering Committee on Sickle Cell Disease be consulted in the development of the framework, procedures, and educational materials, and that it helps provide technical assistance and monitoring.

DBM is responsible for the state's personnel and budget. The bill requires the creation of new contractual positions at MDH and MHEC, which has a fiscal impact that DBM must oversee in the state budget.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies and institutions. It would likely be involved in advising MDH, MHEC, and public universities on the legal requirements for 'reasonable accommodations' and the anti-discrimination protections mandated by the bill.

The department is responsible for ensuring programs and services are inclusive and integrated for residents with disabilities. Since sickle cell disease can be a disabling condition requiring reasonable accommodations in educational settings, this bill aligns with their core mission of advancing accessible housing and community living.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "student financing company" to exclude an institution of postsecondary education for purposes of certain registration and reporting requirements.
Title: Financial Institutions – Definition of Student Financing Companies – Alteration
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of a 'student financing company' to exclude institutions of postsecondary education. This change exempts these institutions from specific registration and annual reporting requirements mandated for entities providing student financing in Maryland.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Office of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Institutions of postsecondary education, student financing companies, and students who utilize student financing products
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. Specific revenue or expenditure estimates are unavailable because the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the definition of a 'student financing company' within the Financial Institutions Article, which falls under the regulatory oversight of the Department's Office of Financial Regulation. This office is responsible for the registration and reporting requirements that institutions of postsecondary education will be exempt from under this legislation.

MHEC is the state's central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education. Since the bill exempts institutions of postsecondary education from certain financial registration and reporting requirements, it directly affects the operational and regulatory environment of the institutions under MHEC's purview.

As the state's public higher education system comprising 12 institutions, USM is an 'institution of postsecondary education' that would be exempted by this bill from the registration and reporting requirements typically applied to student financing companies.

As a public, state-governed postsecondary institution, Morgan State University is directly impacted by the bill's alteration of the definition of student financing companies, which removes the university from certain regulatory requirements if it provides student financing products.

As an independent public honors college and an institution of postsecondary education, Saint Mary's is directly impacted by this legislation, which exempts it from registering as a student financing company with the Department of Labor.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor and the Maryland Higher Education Commission. It would likely be responsible for advising on the implementation of these definition changes and interpreting the extent of the exemption.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases and regulatory enforcement actions for various state agencies, including the Department of Labor. Changes to registration and reporting mandates for student financing entities could affect the scope or volume of administrative cases brought by or against the Office of Financial Regulation.

Synopsis: Requiring the District Court for Anne Arundel County to issue its summons for a trial to repossess for failure to pay rent to any constable or sheriff's designee; providing that a sheriff's designee in Anne Arundel County has the same authority and responsibility as a constable or sheriff in an action to repossess for a failure to pay rent; requiring a sheriff's designee to post a notice of a trial at a certain property or address; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Summons for Actions to Repossess for Failure to Pay Rent - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal procedures for summonses and trials in failure to pay rent cases specifically in Anne Arundel County. It requires the District Court to issue summonses to constables or sheriff's designees, changes the trial date from the 5th day to the 30th day after a complaint is filed, requires trial notices to be posted at the property at least 7 days before the trial, and limits the court to 100 such cases on any given day.
responsible_party: District Court for Anne Arundel County and the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's Office
stakeholders: Landlords and tenants in Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State finances, although the Judiciary anticipates operational impacts regarding case scheduling and high volumes in Anne Arundel County. Local expenditures may decrease if the bill leads to operational efficiencies and reduced overtime within the Anne Arundel County Sheriff's office. Revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations of the District Court in Anne Arundel County, which is supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts. It alters procedural requirements for issuing summonses, increases the timeline for trial from 5 to 30 days, and imposes a cap on the number of cases scheduled per day. The fiscal note explicitly identifies a moderate operational impact on the Judiciary.

Synopsis: Requiring certain interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports sponsored by certain schools and certain locker rooms to be expressly designated based on biological sex; prohibiting certain entities from taking certain adverse actions against a school for maintaining separate interscholastic and intramural junior varsity and varsity athletic teams or sports or locker rooms for students of the female sex; etc.
Title: Education - Interscholastic and Intramural Junior Varsity and Varsity Teams and Locker Rooms - Designation Based on Sex (Fairness in Girls' Sports Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: The Fairness in Girls' Sports Act requires that interscholastic and intramural athletic teams and locker rooms in Maryland public high schools and certain nonpublic high schools be expressly designated based on biological sex. The bill prohibits students of the male sex from participating on teams or using locker rooms designated for females, protects schools from adverse actions for maintaining these sex-based designations, and establishes a right for students or schools to bring civil actions for damages and legal fees in the event of violations or retaliation.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local school systems
stakeholders: Public and nonpublic high school students, local school systems, and athletic associations or organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal impact. Local school systems may incur additional costs related to potential civil litigation and locker room modifications; however, a reliable estimate of these costs is not feasible at this time according to the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office coordinates high-profile policy initiatives. This bill involves significant social and educational policy that aligns with executive oversight of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE).

While the fiscal note indicates no direct State fiscal impact, DBM is the principal fiscal agency and supervises budget execution and personnel policies that may be tangentially affected by changes in school system administrative requirements.

MSDE is the primary agency for the bill's implementation. It oversees public education policies and regulations, specifically those governing the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association (MPSSAA) which manages the athletic programs mentioned in the bill.

The OAG will be responsible for providing legal counsel to MSDE regarding the bill's compliance with federal laws like Title IX and constitutional Equal Protection clauses, and would represent the State in any resulting litigation.
The bill creates a new cause of action allowing students and schools to bring civil suits for damages, which will be adjudicated within the State's judicial system managed by the AOC.

The MCCR enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws. The bill's requirements for sex-based designation and its protections against 'adverse actions' may conflict with or impact the Commission's enforcement scope regarding sex and gender identity discrimination.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze the challenges related to the delay in student enrollment counts and its effect on school funding and the connection between growing student populations and the provision of school funding; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly on or before December 15, 2026.
Title: Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force on Education Funding and Student Population Growth to analyze challenges related to student enrollment counts and population growth as they relate to school funding. The Task Force is required to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, local boards of education, the Maryland State Department of Education, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) assumes that the task force can be staffed using existing resources, resulting in no net fiscal impact. However, the Office of the Governor estimates a fiscal 2027 requirement of $254,000 for contractual support and an executive assistant. No local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Office of the Governor to provide staffing for the Task Force and mandates that the Governor appoint nine members and the chair. The Governor's Office also noted a potential fiscal impact of $254,000 for contractual staff to fulfill this mandate.

As the agency overseeing public education funding and enrollment, MSDE is a primary stakeholder. A representative from the department is a named member of the Task Force, and the study directly concerns MSDE's core operations and funding formulas.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new temporary task force to address specific government issues (education funding and student population growth), falling under the regulatory and administrative scope of this entity.
The Office of the Comptroller is a named member of the Task Force, reflecting its role as the state's chief financial officer in analyzing fiscal data related to education funding.

The fiscal note identifies the Maryland Department of Planning as the agency responsible for school enrollment projections, which are a central component of the Task Force's required analysis of student population growth.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting the nine members and chair to be appointed to the newly created Task Force.

As the agency responsible for state budget development and long-term fiscal planning, DBM would be impacted by Task Force recommendations regarding changes to education funding formulas and state expenditures.

Synopsis: Clarifying that a communication between an attorney and a client that acts as a fiduciary is subject to the attorney-client privilege even if fiduciary funds are used to compensate the attorney for services rendered to the client.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Fiduciaries - Attorney-Client Privilege
Status: In the House - Returned Passed
bill_summary: This bill clarifies that communications between an attorney and a client acting as a fiduciary are protected by attorney-client privilege, even if fiduciary funds are used to pay for legal services. It further establishes that the fiduciary relationship itself does not result in a waiver of the attorney-client privilege.
stakeholders: Fiduciaries (including trustees, executors, and agents under power of attorney), legal professionals, and beneficiaries of estates and trusts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances. According to the fiscal note, the bill's impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes specific rules regarding the attorney-client privilege for fiduciaries, which directly impacts the rules of evidence and judicial proceedings overseen and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

This agency is responsible for the administrative probate of estates and serves the Orphans' Court; since the bill clarifies the legal protections for communications between attorneys and estate fiduciaries (executors and administrators), it is highly relevant to their core operations.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to agencies that may act in fiduciary capacities and represents the state in civil appeals where the application of fiduciary attorney-client privilege may be at issue.

DHS often manages cases involving foster care, adoption, and adult protective services where fiduciary relationships, including guardianship and powers of attorney, are common, making legal privilege clarifications relevant to their protective functions.

The agency serves as a fiduciary for the State Retirement and Pension System, managing multi-billion dollar assets for its members; the bill's clarification of attorney-client privilege for fiduciaries directly relates to their legal and administrative governance.

The department oversees advocacy and services for older adults who frequently utilize powers of attorney or have appointed fiduciaries, making the clarification of legal protections for those agents relevant to their mission.
The department coordinates services for individuals with disabilities, many of whom may have legal fiduciaries or guardians managing their care and community living arrangements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency functions as a fiduciary for voluntary supplemental retirement savings programs, and the bill's provisions regarding legal privilege for fiduciary communications are relevant to its operation.

As a state-sponsored retirement program for private-sector employees, the program acts in a fiduciary capacity, making the bill's clarification on attorney-client privilege relevant to its management.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies; to the extent those cases involve fiduciaries or the use of fiduciary funds for legal counsel, this bill clarifies the evidentiary standards for privileged communications.
