Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: The Bowen Levy Airway Clearing Device Act requires each county board of education to establish a policy for public schools to obtain at least one airway clearing device per school and authorizes school personnel to use the device during choking emergencies. It mandates training for staff, specific storage requirements in dining areas, and establishes a reporting system for incidents involving the device's use.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local county boards of education
stakeholders: Public school students, school nurses, school personnel, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Maryland State Department of Education are expected to be handled within existing budgeted resources. Local school system expenditures will increase by approximately 85200 dollars statewide to purchase at least one airway clearing device for each of the more than 1,400 public schools. Additional local costs include minimal training expenses and periodic replacement of device components every two to three years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including developing and disseminating the standard reporting form, collecting incident data from all public schools, and providing guidance to local boards of education on policy requirements.

MDH collaborates with MSDE to develop school health standards and guidelines; the agency also oversees local health departments that provide the school nurses mentioned in the bill's training and authorization requirements.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and MDH regarding the implementation of the bill and the interpretation of the liability immunity clause for school personnel responding to emergencies.

As an independent unit within MSDE focused on school safety training and resources, MCSS may be involved in developing or distributing the mandated training procedures for the use of airway clearing devices.

As a state agency that functions as a public school, MSD is directly affected by the mandate to obtain emergency devices, train its staff, and report any incidents requiring the use of the devices to MSDE.

Synopsis: Altering, for a certain licensing requirement, the definition of "money transmitter" under the Maryland Money Transmission Act to exclude a certain person designated as an agent of a payor for the purpose of the agent's provision of payroll processing services under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: This bill narrows the definition of a money transmitter under the Maryland Money Transmission Act to exclude payroll processing services that act as agents for a payor, provided specific contractual conditions are met, such as the payor remaining liable to employees if the agent fails to pay them.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Office of Financial Regulation)
stakeholders: Payroll processing companies, employers, and employees receiving payroll funds.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Labor are estimated to decrease by $6,000 annually starting in fiscal 2027 due to lost licensing fees from approximately three payroll processing companies that will no longer require licensing under the bill. There is no material impact on state expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor, specifically its Office of Financial Regulation, is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Money Transmission Act and licensing money transmitters. The fiscal note explicitly identifies a decrease in special fund revenue for this department due to fewer companies requiring licenses.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and would be responsible for interpreting the revised definition of 'money transmitter' and defending the state in any litigation related to the enforcement of the Act.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is concerned with regulatory changes that affect business operations in Maryland, such as reducing the licensing burden on payroll processing companies.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for overseeing budget execution and revenue estimation. It is relevant due to the bill's documented impact on state special fund revenues.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies; it would likely handle appeals if the Department of Labor disputes whether a payroll processor meets the bill's specific criteria for exclusion from licensing.

Synopsis: Requiring a public body that enters into an energy performance contract to comply with certain provisions of law regarding energy performance contracts; requiring the Maryland Clean Energy Center to hire or contract with navigators to assist a public body in creating an energy performance contract; altering the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program and the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund to allow for the issuance of certain grants and loans to certain public bodies; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Clean Energy Center to hire or contract with regional navigators to assist public bodies, such as local governments, schools, and hospitals, in developing energy performance contracts. It renames the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Loan Program to the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Grant and Loan Program, authorizing the Maryland Energy Administration to provide grants to public bodies in addition to loans. The bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation of $1,500,000 from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund to support the navigator program.
responsible_party: Maryland Clean Energy Center and Maryland Energy Administration
stakeholders: Public bodies including State agencies, counties, municipalities, public higher education institutions, local boards of education, State and local hospitals, and small businesses providing energy conservation services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund increase by $1,500,000 annually beginning in FY 2027. Nonbudgeted revenues and expenditures for the Maryland Clean Energy Center increase by the same amount. Additionally, the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund will experience indeterminate impacts as a portion of its funds transitions from loans (which are repaid) to grants (which are not), potentially reducing long-term revenue from loan repayments. Local governments and State agencies may experience net energy cost savings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the Maryland Clean Energy Center to hire or contract with navigators to assist public bodies in creating energy performance contracts and provides $1.5 million in annual mandated funding for this purpose.

The Maryland Energy Administration administers the Jane E. Lawton Grant and Loan Program and the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, both of which are significantly altered and utilized for funding under the bill.
The bill explicitly requires the Department of General Services to monitor the status of active energy performance contracts and review measurement and verification reports from units.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves energy performance contracts and receives annual reports on their status from the Department of General Services.
The Treasurer serves as the custodian of the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund and is responsible for financing state energy performance contracts through capital leases.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for the state budget process, which must now include the $1.5 million mandated appropriation for the navigator program.
The Governor is required to include a $1.5 million appropriation from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund in the annual budget bill to support the navigator program.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Jane E. Lawton Conservation Fund and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees these contracts.
Local boards of education are specifically included in the definition of public bodies eligible for grants and technical assistance for energy performance contracts.
State and local hospitals are defined as public bodies eligible for grant funding and navigator assistance to improve energy efficiency.
Public institutions of higher education are defined as public bodies that can enter into energy performance contracts and receive technical assistance and grants.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is a public body eligible for grant funding and navigator assistance under the bill.
As a public institution of higher education, St. Mary's College is a public body eligible for the grant and assistance programs established by the bill.
The Commission coordinates policies for public higher education institutions, which are public bodies eligible for the energy performance contract assistance and grants.
The definition of public bodies includes units of state government, including those within the judicial branch, making them eligible for programs under the bill.
The bill affects the Strategic Energy Investment Fund, which also provides funding for the Air and Radiation Administration within the Department of the Environment.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from constructing a data center in the State; prohibiting a unit of State or local government from approving a proposal for the construction of a data center in the State; providing for the termination of the Act if the General Assembly enacts legislation regarding the co-location of data centers with a new or existing natural gas power generation facility, nuclear power generation facility, or small module reactor; applying the Act prospectively; etc.
Title: Moratorium on Construction of New Data Centers - Co-Location and Generation Contingency
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/03 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.

bill_summary: This emergency bill establishes a moratorium on the construction of new data centers in Maryland and prohibits state and local government units from approving new data center proposals. The moratorium remains in effect until the General Assembly enacts legislation requiring all new data centers to be co-located with specific power generation facilities (such as natural gas, nuclear, or small module reactors) that can provide sufficient power to meet the data center's needs.
stakeholders: Data center developers, state and local government agencies, electric utilities, electricity ratepayers, and small businesses providing construction or operational services to data centers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances, but is expected to have significant indirect effects. These include potential reductions in tax and fee revenues from data center development and operation, as well as possible impacts on electricity rates. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as they are considered beyond the scope of the fiscal note, though the impact is anticipated to be significant.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MEA is responsible for advising the state on energy policy and maximizing energy efficiency. The bill's abrogation is contingent on legislation requiring data centers to be co-located with specific power generation facilities (natural gas, nuclear, or small module reactors), and MEA is required by prior law to assess the energy impacts of data center development.

The PSC regulates public utilities and sets electricity rates. The bill's abrogation clause directly concerns the construction of power generation facilities and managing the large electrical loads required by data centers, which impact utility rates for all Maryland residents.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is responsible for attracting and retaining businesses. A moratorium on constructing a specific industry's facilities (data centers) directly conflicts with its mission to stimulate economic growth and job creation.

MDE is responsible for environmental protection and permitting. It is also mandated by current law to assess the environmental impacts of data centers, making a construction moratorium and the potential for new co-located power plants highly relevant to its oversight.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and resource management through land use policy. The bill imposes a state-wide land use restriction on a specific facility type, which falls under the agency's planning and policy guidance role.

The OPC represents residential utility consumers in proceedings regarding rates and service quality. The fiscal note highlights the OPC's position that data center power needs significantly impact retail electricity rates, a core concern of this bill.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and coordinates state initiatives. This bill is an emergency measure with significant implications for the Governor's energy, environmental, and economic priorities.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector. The bill uses definitions from the Tax - General Article and will have significant indirect effects on state tax and fee revenues derived from data center construction and operation.

DBM is responsible for long-term fiscal planning and budget execution. The fiscal note indicates the bill will have significant indirect effects on state and local finances, which DBM monitors to ensure government efficiency.

MEDCO assists in the attraction and expansion of industry through real estate development and financing. The prohibition of data center construction affects its ability to support these large-scale industrial projects.

DNR manages public lands and natural resources. Large-scale data center construction and co-located power generation facilities have significant environmental and conservation impacts on state land and waterways.

The Department of Labor oversees workforce development and small business support. The fiscal note indicates the moratorium could meaningfully affect small businesses and laborers involved in the development and construction of data centers.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies. The office would be responsible for advising units of government on the legality and enforcement of the moratorium and its prospective application.

DoIT manages the state's IT strategy and infrastructure. While the bill focuses on private construction, the overall availability and development of data center infrastructure in Maryland is relevant to the state's digital ecosystem.

Synopsis: Providing that certain authorization for the holders of certain licenses to sell alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption in a certain manner applies only if the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore County has adopted certain regulations; authorizing the holders of certain licenses in Baltimore County that authorize the sale of alcoholic beverages at a restaurant or bar to sell certain alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Baltimore County - Alcoholic Beverages - Sale for Off-Premises Consumption
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Class B and Class D alcoholic beverages license holders (restaurants and bars) in Baltimore County to obtain a permit to sell mixed drinks or cocktails for off-premises consumption, provided the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners has adopted specific regulations. Sales must be accompanied by prepared food, provided in sealed containers, and completed before 11:00 p.m. to individuals at least 21 years of age.
responsible_party: Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class B and Class D alcoholic beverage license holders (restaurants and bars) in Baltimore County and their customers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not expected to materially affect Baltimore County finances or operations. The Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners is explicitly prohibited from charging license holders an additional fee for the permit authorized by the bill. Small business restaurants and bars in Baltimore County are likely to experience increased revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state official responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and enforcing state tax laws related to alcoholic beverages. This bill modifies the conditions under which certain license holders in Baltimore County may sell alcoholic beverages for off-premises consumption.

The bill specifically requires the local Board of License Commissioners to consider the 'public health impacts' of authorized sales for off-premises consumption. The Maryland Department of Health oversees public health policy and local health departments that may provide data or expertise on such impacts.

The OAG provides legal counsel and represents the state in matters involving the enforcement and interpretation of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article of the Maryland Code, which this bill amends.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly, including local laws that amend the statewide Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a unit of State government or other State entity that provides State aid from providing State aid to a nonprofit entity unless the nonprofit is current with certain obligations under federal, State, and local law.
Title: State Aid - Nonprofits - Status
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland State agencies and entities from providing State aid—including contributions, grants, or subsidies—to any nonprofit entity unless the nonprofit meets specific criteria: it must be in good standing with the IRS, current on federal, State, and local tax obligations, have a current charter on file with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and have filed its most recent tax forms such as IRS Form 990 or a personal property tax return.
responsible_party: Maryland State agencies and departments that provide State aid to nonprofit entities
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations seeking or receiving State aid and Maryland State agencies that administer grant programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill may have an operational impact on State agencies providing aid to nonprofits as they must verify compliance with the new requirements, but it is unlikely to materially affect State expenditures. State revenues and local government finances are not affected. Some agencies noted potential needs for additional staff or IT resources, but the Department of Legislative Services assumes grantors can largely fulfill requirements through existing resources or grantee affidavits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for supervising budget execution and state expenditures. It manages the reporting framework for State aid provided to grantees and determines the format for reports required from all grantors.

DoIT is mandated to develop and operate the searchable public website that tracks State aid and grantees. Any changes to the conditions for receiving aid may require adjustments to tracking and reporting systems managed by this department.

As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for verifying that entities are current on state tax obligations, which is a key requirement for nonprofits under the bill. The Comptroller also manages social organization reporting for State aid expenditures.

The department is a major grantor that provides significant State aid to nonprofits for behavioral health, developmental disabilities, and public health services. It would be responsible for verifying the compliance status of these numerous partners.

DHCD provides extensive State aid through grants and subsidies to nonprofits for affordable housing, community revitalization, and small business development, necessitating a robust verification process for all recipients.

DHS distributes State aid to nonprofit partners providing food assistance, energy assistance, and protective services. It will need to ensure all such entities meet the bill's tax and registration requirements.
Commerce provides grants and financial assistance to nonprofits in the arts, tourism, and economic development sectors. The bill adds a layer of compliance verification to their funding process.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This department relies heavily on nonprofit partnerships to create paid service opportunities and workforce pathways. It would be required to verify the standing of all nonprofit participants before providing aid.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office manages and allocates significant state and federal funding to nonprofit organizations for victim services, law enforcement support, and youth programs.
RMC administers the Rural Maryland Prosperity Investment Fund and other grants to nonprofit entities in rural counties, making them a primary grantor affected by the bill's restrictions.

As a state-chartered grant-making organization, the Trust awards numerous grants to nonprofits for environmental restoration and education, all of which must now meet the bill's specific compliance criteria.
MSDE provides State aid to various nonprofit educational partners, including those involved in early childhood development and special education services.
MDEM coordinates with nonprofits for disaster recovery and hazard mitigation, often involving the distribution of state funds that would fall under the definition of State aid.
MDE provides technical and financial assistance for environmental infrastructure and cleanup, which may involve grants to nonprofit environmental organizations.
DNR manages grant programs for conservation and restoration often executed by nonprofit stewardship organizations.
MDP, through entities like the Maryland Historical Trust, provides grants to nonprofits for cultural and historical preservation efforts.
The department provides State aid for workforce development and adult learning programs frequently operated by nonprofit entities.
MDoA oversees programs for older adults that are often delivered via nonprofit Area Agencies on Aging or community service providers.
MDA provides funding and support for agricultural promotion and soil conservation that may involve nonprofit grant recipients.
The department coordinates services for residents with disabilities, which includes funding nonprofit organizations that provide integrated community living and assistive technology services.
MDOT provides grants and technical assistance to various entities, including nonprofits involved in transit and transportation safety initiatives.
This department partners with and supports nonprofit organizations that provide advocacy and services to veterans and their families.
DJS provides funding for community-based treatment and rehabilitation programs often run by nonprofit service providers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS provides aid to nonprofits that facilitate rehabilitation and recidivism reduction programs for justice-involved individuals.
GOCI acts as a primary liaison between the state and the nonprofit community, advising the Governor on community service policies and facilitating partnerships that involve state funding.
This office coordinates support networks and initiatives like the ENOUGH Initiative, which often involve providing state funds to nonprofits addressing child poverty.
GGO provides technical assistance and resources to state agencies regarding grant management and compliance, making them a key advisory body for implementing the bill's new requirements.
The library agency administers state and federal grants to support public library systems and related nonprofit educational initiatives.
OAG would provide legal counsel to all state agencies on how to interpret and implement these new statutory compliance requirements for nonprofit grantees.
BPW oversees and approves significant state expenditures and procurement contracts, ensuring that all executive decisions involving state funds comply with the law.
DGS is the central procurement authority and may oversee certain types of state aid or contracts with nonprofits that would fall under the bill's scope.
As a state entity, USM institutions may provide grants or aid to affiliated nonprofits or community partners, requiring adherence to the bill's verification standards.
MSP was identified in the fiscal note as an agency that may provide forms of aid or support to nonprofits that would require status verification.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS coordinates the state's emergency medical services and may provide grants or equipment to nonprofit volunteer rescue squads.

Synopsis: Including institutions and programs of higher education in which a student is enrolled as part of a dual enrollment program in the definition of "school system"; adding certain offenses to the list of offenses a law enforcement agency must report to certain school personnel under certain circumstances; and authorizing State's Attorneys to make a certain notification if a student is arrested for certain offenses.
Title: School Systems - Reportable Offenses - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m. (Ways and Means)

bill_summary: This bill expands the list of 'reportable offenses' that law enforcement must report to school officials to include crimes such as stalking, distributing revenge porn, and threats of mass violence. It also includes institutions of higher education within the definition of a school system for students in dual enrollment programs and authorizes State's Attorneys to notify school officials of a student's arrest if law enforcement has not already done so.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), local school superintendents, school principals, and State's Attorneys
stakeholders: Maryland public and nonpublic school students (ages 5–22), students in dual enrollment programs, school administrators, law enforcement agencies, and State's Attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) can adjust its reporting requirements within existing resources, resulting in no state fiscal impact. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected by the changes to notification requirements and procedures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE is the primary agency responsible for overseen the Maryland public education system, adopting regulations for the handling of student information, and preparing the mandated annual report on reportable offenses.
MCSS, as an independent unit within MSDE, is directly responsible for coordinating school safety policies, managing safety grants, and training school safety personnel.

The bill expands the definition of 'school system' to include institutions of higher education for dual enrollment students, necessitating coordination of reporting policies and student data by the commission.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is mandated to notify school officials within 24 hours when a student is arrested for the expanded list of reportable offenses.
The bill authorizes State's Attorneys to notify school systems of arrests and requires judicial oversight for the release of confidential information about student reportable offenses.

DJS supervises youth in the justice system; changes to reporting requirements and the expanded list of offenses directly affect the coordination between justice and educational systems for their rehabilitation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy, advising on strategies related to the reporting of criminal acts and juvenile delinquency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires school officials to invite a student's attorney (often a Public Defender) to participate in conferences regarding the student's removal or exclusion from school programs.
As a state-governed higher education institution, MSU is impacted by the bill's expanded definition of school systems and the requirement to receive notifications for dually enrolled students.
As an independent public college, St. Mary's is subject to the bill's new notification requirements for students dually enrolled in its programs.
USM member institutions that enroll dual enrollment students are included in the expanded definition of school systems for arrest reporting and safety coordination.
The Governor's Office receives the annual report on reportable offenses and student outcomes, and the office oversees the executive branch departments implementing these changes.
As a state education agency serving students ages 5-21, the Maryland School for the Deaf must adhere to state-mandated safety and reportable offense notification procedures.
OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MSDE and MHEC regarding the legal implementation of reporting mandates and confidentiality protections.

Synopsis: Allowing, subject to certain limitations, a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for certain personal casualty losses of certain retirement assets from theft or a fraud scheme; and applying the Act to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification - Losses From Theft or Fraud

bill_summary: This bill establishes a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for personal casualty losses that occur as a result of theft or a fraud scheme involving assets in a qualified retirement plan. Taxpayers are required to submit a police report and documentation of the impacted assets to claim the subtraction.
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers who experience theft or fraud involving their qualified retirement plan assets
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may decrease by more than $1,000,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Additionally, local income tax revenues are estimated to decrease by more than $700,000 annually starting in fiscal 2027. The Comptroller’s Office is expected to handle the implementation with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing the new subtraction modification, updating tax forms, and processing claims for losses related to theft or fraud schemes.

The bill is projected to decrease general fund revenues by more than $1 million annually starting in fiscal 2027, which impacts the department's core duties of revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning.

The bill requires taxpayers to provide a police report to qualify for the subtraction modification. As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is involved in investigating such crimes and provided data for the fiscal analysis.

The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division provided information for the fiscal note and is responsible for investigating the types of fraud schemes and financial exploitation that the bill addresses.

The fiscal note specifically identifies elder financial exploitation as a significant source of the losses addressed by the bill, making it relevant to the department's mission to protect the rights and assets of older adults.
The Maryland Tax Court would be responsible for hearing appeals from final decisions made by the Comptroller regarding the eligibility of specific subtraction modification claims under this act.

Synopsis: Requiring that a motor vehicle be at least 25 years old in order to be eligible for registration as a historic motor vehicle.
Title: Vehicle Laws – Historic Motor Vehicles – Minimum Age
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/27 at 1:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill changes the eligibility requirements for registering a motor vehicle as a historic motor vehicle. It replaces the current requirement that a vehicle must be from model year 1999 or earlier with a requirement that the vehicle be at least 25 years old. Historic motor vehicles are subject to lower registration fees and are exempt from certain equipment and emissions inspection requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (Motor Vehicle Administration)
stakeholders: Owners of motor vehicles at least 25 years old, the Motor Vehicle Administration, and emergency medical services funds including the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund and the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately 1783188 in fiscal 2027 and by 7925280 in fiscal 2031. This revenue loss impacts the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) due to lower registration and VEIP fees, as well as the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF), the R Adams Cowley Shock Trauma Center, and the Maryland Trauma Physician Services Fund (MTPSF) due to the exemption of historic vehicles from the 40 dollar annual emergency medical services surcharge. Local government finances are expected to be minimally affected through the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief financial officer and principal revenue collector, the Comptroller monitors state revenue streams, which will be reduced by millions of dollars annually due to the expansion of historic vehicle registration eligibility.

The Department of Budget and Management is the state's principal fiscal agency; it is impacted by the significant multi-year reduction in special fund revenues (TTF, MEMSOF, etc.) estimated at up to $7.9 million annually by fiscal 2031.

MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which will experience a significant decrease in revenue from lower registration fees and the loss of emergency medical services surcharges for the affected vehicles.

bill_summary: This bill allows for the admissibility of intercepted wire, oral, or electronic communications and evidence derived from them in criminal trials or hearings under specific circumstances. stakeholders: Defendants, victims, and legal professionals within the Maryland criminal justice system
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. There are no explicit funding mandates or revenue changes described in the bill, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the administrative support for the Governor, who proposes the annual state budget and coordinates policy initiatives, this office is highly relevant as the bill proposes a massive overhaul of the state's tax structure resulting in an estimated $13.3 billion general fund revenue decrease, fundamentally altering the state's fiscal landscape.

The USM is impacted by the bill's reduction of the corporate income tax rate, which directly decreases revenue for the Higher Education Investment Fund used to support the system's institutions and research.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing bodies of Maryland political subdivisions, including Baltimore City, to designate noncontiguous blighted areas as development districts for Tax Increment Financing (TIF). It defines a blighted area as one where a majority of buildings have declined in productivity due to obsolescence or depreciation to the point that repairs are no longer justified, facilitating the issuance of bonds to finance redevelopment.

stakeholders: Local governments, small businesses within or adjacent to blighted areas, and construction and development companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected. Local revenues and expenditures are expected to increase beginning in FY 2027 as local governments issue TIF bonds and use proceeds for redevelopment purposes. Specific dollar amounts are unavailable as the impact depends on individual local government decisions and the scope of future projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is directly interested in tools like Tax Increment Financing (TIF) that stimulate the economy and attract business. The expansion of TIF authority to noncontiguous blighted areas provides more flexibility for the development projects the department promotes.

The fiscal note specifically mentions that local revenues may be pledged to debt issued by the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) in certain TIF circumstances. MEDCO provides specialized financing and real estate development services that are often used in conjunction with TIF districts.

DHCD is responsible for community revitalization and ensuring access to secure housing. This bill targets 'blighted areas' for development, which aligns with the agency's mission to invest in community improvements and address economic decline in specific neighborhoods.

The Maryland Department of Planning provides technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments regarding land use and sustainable growth. The designation of development districts is a core aspect of local planning and resource management overseen by the department.

Tax Increment Financing relies on property tax assessments, specifically the 'incremental valuation' above a 'frozen base.' Any expansion of development districts or changes to the definition of areas eligible for TIF (such as 'blighted areas') could lead to assessment disputes and appeals handled by this board.

As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller monitors state revenues and financial policy. While TIF is primarily a local tool, the resulting economic development impacts the state tax base and general fiscal health.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They may be called upon to interpret the new statutory definitions of 'blighted area' and the legal requirements for designating noncontiguous development districts.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes, including property tax assessments. If disagreements arise regarding the valuation of properties within these new noncontiguous TIF districts, the Tax Court would be responsible for adjudicating them.

stakeholders: Maryland veterans and retail vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is estimated to reduce state general fund revenues by $30,600 and Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund revenues by $4,200 in FY 2027, for a total state revenue decrease of $34,800. These revenue decreases are projected to grow slightly in subsequent years based on forecasted sales and use tax growth. The bill has no impact on state expenditures or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and is responsible for administering the sales and use tax. The bill explicitly grants the Comptroller the sole discretion to suspend the established tax-free day.

bill_summary: This bill standardizes the procedures for filling vacancies on local boards of education and the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners across Maryland, replacing various local methods with a uniform statewide process. bill_summary: This bill limits child support earnings or wage withholding to no more than 25% of an obligor's disposable earnings if the obligor's individual income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines. These limits apply unless the obligor was determined to be voluntarily impoverished in their most recent court order. The bill also requires withholding notices to employers to include these limits and allows employees to contest withholdings that exceed them.

stakeholders: Child support obligors with individual incomes at or below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines, employers processing wage withholdings, child support recipients, and the Maryland Department of Human Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general and federal fund expenditures increase by at least 3,810,749 dollars in FY 2027 for one-time programming costs to update the Child Support Management System and for at least 10 additional staff members to handle manual calculations and notices. Future year expenditures are estimated at approximately 800,000 dollars annually. Federal fund matching revenues will increase accordingly. There is a potential reduction in child support collections, which could affect federal performance incentive payments. Local circuit court operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. Small businesses may experience increased administrative workloads.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Child Support Administration regarding the interpretation and enforcement of new withholding limits and represents the state in related legal proceedings.

The agency administers pensions and disability benefits, which are included in the bill's definition of 'earnings' from which child support may be withheld subject to the 25% cap.
The Commission adjudicates worker's compensation payments, which are defined as 'earnings' subject to the bill's withholding limits and administrative contest procedures.

The bill directly impacts child support collections and the disposable income of low-income families, which are central factors in the office's mission to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility.
The team is tasked with identifying and testing strategies to reduce child poverty; the bill's changes to child support withholding for low-income obligors are directly relevant to this policy area.

The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Elections to refer reports of election misinformation or disinformation gathered through its portal to the State Prosecutor for investigation and potential prosecution, directly impacting the agency's criminal enforcement caseload regarding electoral integrity.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the Office of the Attorney General would provide legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and would likely be responsible for litigating the civil actions and seeking the injunctions authorized by this bill in state and federal courts.

The bill creates new civil causes of action for damages and injunctive relief, as well as a new criminal misdemeanor for the malicious use of deepfakes in elections, which will result in increased filings and proceedings within the state court system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense carrying a potential penalty of five years in prison for the use of deepfakes to produce materially false election information, necessitating legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent individuals charged under this provision.

As a state-operated broadcasting entity (Maryland Public Television), the commission is subject to the bill's regulations concerning deepfakes, including specific disclosure requirements and the duty to make a good faith effort to verify the authenticity of media to qualify for broadcaster exemptions.

stakeholders: Landlords of properties with septic systems, real estate buyers and sellers, on-site wastewater service professionals, and local health departments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, as it oversees the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals and is tasked with adopting the necessary regulations for the on-site wastewater industry.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment for regulation development and may be involved in consumer protection enforcement related to the bill's new septic system requirements for landlords and real estate contracts.

The bill establishes new mandatory provisions for real estate sales and rental agreements, which could lead to increased litigation and contract disputes that the judicial branch would be responsible for adjudicating.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits businesses and employers from using surveillance data and automated decision systems to set customized prices for goods and services or customized wages for employees. It classifies surveillance-based price setting as an unfair or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act and empowers the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to investigate complaints related to surveillance-based wage setting.
responsible_party: The Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry) and the Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, employees, job applicants, and businesses or employers utilizing automated pricing or wage systems
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund expenditures increase by $349,400 in fiscal 2027 for the Office of the Attorney General and the Maryland Department of Labor to hire 3.5 total staff members (technologists, investigators, and assistant Attorneys General) to handle enforcement and technical investigations. Annual costs are projected to rise to $468,800 by fiscal 2031. The bill is not expected to have a material impact on local government finances or state revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) is a primary implementing agency for this bill. The bill classifies surveillance-based price setting as an unfair trade practice subject to the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which the OAG's Consumer Protection Division enforces. Additionally, the Attorney General is authorized to bring civil actions for violations of the surveillance-based wage setting prohibitions.

The Maryland Department of Labor, specifically the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, is tasked with investigating complaints regarding surveillance-based wage setting and taking enforcement actions, including mediation or referring cases to the Attorney General.

The bill's definitions of 'Artificial Intelligence' and surveillance-based technologies are tied to the state's technical strategy and existing IT policies managed by DoIT. DoIT also supports the Governor's AI Subcabinet, which oversees state AI enablement and study roadmaps mentioned in the fiscal analysis.

The Governor's Office coordinates state policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch, including the Governor's AI Subcabinet which governs the use and assessment of AI systems in the state, directly overlapping with the bill's focus on automated decision systems.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies and resources. The bill's prohibition on surveillance-based wage setting applies to the State as an employer, necessitating DBM oversight of state agency pay practices.

As the state's primary economic development and business advocacy agency, the Department of Commerce is impacted by new regulations on how Maryland businesses set prices for consumer goods and services and how they manage wage setting.

The bill explicitly states that its protections do not diminish the rights of employees to collectively bargain over terms and conditions of employment. PERB, which centralizes labor relations for state and public sector employees, would oversee disputes or bargaining issues arising from these new wage-setting regulations.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. Enforcement actions taken by the Department of Labor or consumer protection disputes may be referred to OAH for impartial hearings and findings of fact.

The AOC provides operational and legal support to the judiciary. The bill creates new grounds for civil actions and refers to an AI Evidence Clinic Pilot Program in the courts to handle specialized technological evidence.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill and its fiscal note reference the Workgroup on AI Implementation and the Governor's AI Subcabinet, which are advisory bodies composed of public servants and experts tasked with recommending AI policies and monitoring state implementation.

stakeholders: Owners of residential rental high-rise buildings, fire alarm system technicians and companies, State and local fire marshals, and residents of high-rise buildings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically directs the State Fire Prevention Commission, an ongoing regulatory body, to adopt regulations for the licensing and regulation of fire alarm system technicians and companies.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the state's general fund expenditures, requiring new personnel and information technology upgrades. DBM is responsible for managing the state's budget, personnel resources, and the creation of new state employee positions.

The bill regulates fire safety equipment in residential rental high-rise properties. This aligns with the agency's mission to ensure Maryland residents have access to safe, secure, and affordable housing and its oversight of community revitalization and energy efficiency programs in rental properties.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Department of State Police and the State Fire Prevention Commission and would be involved in drafting the required regulations and providing guidance on enforcement and administrative procedures.

As a public university with urban residential facilities, Morgan State University may be subject to the bill's fire safety and sprinkler requirements for high-rise buildings during future substantial renovations.
As a state agency and public college with residential housing facilities, the college may be impacted by the fiscal and regulatory requirements regarding fire safety in high-rise buildings.

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to change the selection and tenure of circuit court judges. It replaces contested elections with a system where the Governor appoints judges with the advice and consent of the Senate, followed by periodic non-partisan retention elections where voters decide whether the judge should continue in office for a 10-year term.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland, the Maryland Senate, and the Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Current and future circuit court judges, Maryland voters, the Governor, and the Maryland Senate
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note is not present in the provided text. The bill mandates a statewide referendum in November 2026, which would incur State and local expenditures for ballot printing and administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the primary authority responsible for appointing circuit court judges under the proposed amendment and oversees the executive branch's role in the judicial selection and commission process.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for judicial vacancies, a process that would be fundamentally changed and expanded by this bill for all Circuit Court judges.
As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is directly impacted by changes to the selection, tenure, and mandatory retirement age of the judges it serves.

The SBE is responsible for administering the transition from contested elections to retention elections for circuit court judges and managing the statewide referendum required for this constitutional amendment.

The bill alters the tenure of judges (from 15 to 10 years for retained terms) and enforces a retirement age of 70, which directly affects the administration of pension and retirement benefits for the state's judicial system.

As the state's principal personnel and fiscal agency, DBM manages state employee benefits and policies, including those for the judiciary, and oversees the fiscal impact of constitutional changes on the state budget.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Governor and the Judiciary and would be responsible for representing the state in legal matters concerning the implementation of this constitutional amendment.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

The Secretary of State is the custodian of official records and commissions; the agency would be responsible for the administrative processing of commissions for judges appointed by the Governor.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to quarterly distribute a portion of the cannabis sales and use tax revenue to the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund.

The bill redistributes revenue from the General Fund to a nonbudgeted fund, impacting state revenue and the budget execution oversight provided by DBM. The Treasurer is responsible for the management and investment of state funds. As the bill increases revenues for the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund, the Treasurer's office would be involved in managing and protecting these funds.

The bill adjusts the distribution of sales and use tax revenue derived from cannabis sales, which is the industry regulated and overseen by the MCA. The MCA's own funding is also derived from the same tax distribution statute modified by the bill.

The Maryland Veterans Trust Fund is specifically established to provide monetary and other assistance to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families, making them direct beneficiaries of the bill's funding.

Synopsis: Requiring a landlord to provide air-conditioning to residential rental units in apartment buildings with four or more individual dwelling units in a certain manner beginning June 1, 2026, for newly constructed residential rental units and beginning October 1, 2026, for residential rental units that undergo renovation that includes the replacement or substantial upgrade of electrical systems or heating systems; and applying the Act prospectively.

bill_summary: This bill requires landlords of apartment buildings with four or more units to provide air conditioning from June 1 through September 30 each year. The requirement applies to newly constructed units starting June 1, 2026, and to existing units that undergo renovations involving the replacement or substantial upgrade of electrical or heating systems starting October 1, 2026. Landlords must maintain a temperature of no more than 80 degrees Fahrenheit in all habitable spaces of the rental units.

stakeholders: Landlords, tenants in apartment buildings with four or more units, and local housing authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not expected to be materially affected. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is highly relevant because the bill adds new habitability requirements for residential rentals to the Real Property Article. The DHCD is the state's primary agency for ensuring access to safe and affordable housing. This bill directly regulates the health and safety standards (air-conditioning) of residential rental units, which falls within the department's mission and programs.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and enforces state laws regarding consumer protection. Landlord-tenant laws and habitability standards are often interpreted or enforced through the OAG's consumer and civil rights frameworks.

The Department of Aging is dedicated to protecting the rights and quality of life for older adults. Regulation of indoor temperatures is a critical health and safety concern for the elderly population residing in multi-unit apartment buildings.

This department ensures that policies are inclusive and promote safe community living. Many individuals with disabilities are highly sensitive to heat, making state-mandated air-conditioning requirements a significant interest for this agency.

The Commission enforces anti-discrimination laws in housing. Changes to habitability standards under the Real Property Article can intersect with civil rights protections regarding safe and equitable housing conditions.

bill_summary: This bill allows voters who are currently unaffiliated with a political party to change their registration to a political party during early voting or on the day of a primary election. Once the change is requested at a polling place or early voting center, the voter is issued a provisional ballot for their newly selected party.
stakeholders: Unaffiliated registered voters in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are expected to increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in years with primary elections. According to an illustrative estimate in the Fiscal Note, total costs could reach approximately 180000, consisting of 66000 in State general fund expenditures and 114000 in local government expenditures. These costs cover additional paper ballots, provisional ballot election judges, voter education, and administrative revisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, including adopting regulations and procedures for party affiliation changes at early voting centers and polling places, and overseeing the issuance and counting of provisional ballots.

The bill references the Motor Vehicle Administration as a method for notifying changes in party affiliation. Additionally, the MVA's integrated voter registration systems may require updates to accommodate the change in processing party affiliations for unaffiliated voters.

The fiscal note indicates a notable increase in general fund expenditures for the state's share of additional ballots, election judges, and voter education, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and will be responsible for reviewing the new regulations and ensuring the implementation of the bill complies with existing state and federal election laws.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the State Board of Elections. The office is also responsible for proposing the state budget, which must account for the increased expenditures identified in the fiscal note.
As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT is indirectly impacted by any systems changes or registration coordination requirements mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Applying certain campaign finance requirements for a political committee to exploratory committees; establishing requirements and prohibitions for exploratory committees relating to the establishment of the committees, receipt of funds, and permissible disbursements; requiring an authorized candidate campaign committee that results from the exploratory committee to make any equipment purchases from the exploratory committee at the fair market value of the equipment; etc.
Title: Election Law - Campaign Finance - Exploratory Committees
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 2:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill establishes and regulates exploratory committees in Maryland for potential candidates to determine their viability for public office. It subjects these committees to the same campaign finance requirements as political committees, with the exception that donations to exploratory committees are not subject to contribution limits. The bill specifies permissible disbursements, such as polling, staff, and office space, and requires that remaining funds be returned to donors or distributed to specific entities like political parties or the Fair Campaign Financing Fund within 120 days of the candidate filing or declining to run.
stakeholders: Potential candidates for public office, political campaign contributors, and the State Board of Elections
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Elections can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources. State special fund revenues for the Fair Campaign Financing Fund may increase annually starting as early as fiscal year 2026 due to the collection of late filing fees or monetary penalties from exploratory committees. Local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for administering and supervising Maryland's election laws and campaign finance systems. This bill directly amends Title 13 of the Election Law Article, which the Board oversees, and requires them to manage the registration and regulation of exploratory committees.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for investigating and prosecuting criminal offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process and enforcement of state election laws. This bill expands the scope of campaign finance regulations to include exploratory committees, which fall under the Prosecutor's enforcement jurisdiction.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and handles legal interpretations of election law. The fiscal note explicitly mentions that the OAG has previously provided guidance on the legality of exploratory committees under current law.

The State Treasurer's Office is responsible for managing and protecting state funds, including the Fair Campaign Financing Fund. The fiscal note indicates that revenues for this specific fund may increase due to late fees and penalties collected from exploratory committees.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maternal Health Monitoring Pilot Program in the Maryland Department of Health to support pregnant and postpartum Maryland Medical Assistance Program recipients who have higher risks of pregnancy complications because of maternal hypertension or maternal diabetes; requiring the Department to select at least one managed care organization to administer the Program; requiring the managed care organizations to contract with a technology vendor to offer remote patient monitoring services to participants; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Maternal Health Monitoring Pilot Program
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maternal Health Monitoring Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Health to support pregnant and postpartum Medicaid recipients at high risk for complications due to maternal hypertension or diabetes. The pilot program utilizes remote patient monitoring technology to collect health data, which is reviewed by a clinical team including nurses and dietitians to provide health coaching and trigger medical escalations when necessary. The program operates through participating managed care organizations and contracted technology vendors from fiscal 2027 through 2028.
stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum individuals enrolled in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program with diagnosed maternal hypertension or diabetes; participating Medicaid managed care organizations (MCOs); and health care technology vendors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures are estimated to increase by $300,000 in fiscal 2027 and $300,000 in fiscal 2028 to support the pilot program, with an additional $86,000 in fiscal 2029 for program evaluation and reporting. The bill includes a mandated appropriation of $600,000 for fiscal 2028. Expenditures are expected to be funded 50% by State general funds and 50% by federal funds, with federal fund revenues increasing by $343,000 over the three-year period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maternal Health Monitoring Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). As the primary implementing agency, MDH is responsible for selecting managed care organizations, overseeing technology vendors, paying participant fees, ensuring geographic diversity, and submitting a final report on health outcomes and recommendations.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a $600,000 appropriation in the annual budget bill for fiscal year 2028. Additionally, the Department of Health is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

DBM is responsible for developing the state's budget and supervising budget execution. Since the bill includes a mandated appropriation for FY 2028 and involves significant fiscal impacts on the Medicaid program, DBM will be responsible for overseeing the allocation and use of these funds.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health. They would likely be involved in reviewing the contracts with Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) and advising on the implementation of the pilot program, including potential 1115(a) demonstration waiver applications.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and procurement contracts. The selection and payment of participating Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) to administer the pilot program may require BPW approval depending on the contract structures used.

The MHCC is responsible for planning for health system needs and improving access to care. The pilot program's focus on maternal and neonatal outcomes, and the requirement for data-driven reporting (including claims and electronic health records), aligns with the commission's role in health system monitoring.

The pilot program specifically aims to improve fetal and neonatal outcomes, such as reducing fetal mortality and preterm births. These goals align with the GOC's mission to promote the well-being of Maryland's children.

GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to oversee state agency activities. The bill requires a comprehensive evaluation and report on specific health metrics (morbidity, mortality, hospital stays) which falls under GOPI's mandate for enhancing government responsiveness and delivering measurable results.

The report required by the bill must include data on hospital readmissions, ICU admissions, and lengths of hospital stays. The HSCRC, which regulates hospital rates and monitors quality and population health outcomes, has a direct interest in these metrics.

Synopsis: Altering the prohibition against taking and breaking open a letter; providing that a person may not knowingly and intentionally open mail addressed to another without permission of the person or an authorized designee; providing certain penalties for violations of the Act; prohibiting the theft of mail under certain circumstances; prohibiting a person from possessing an arrow key under certain circumstances; and providing for concurrent jurisdiction in the District Court and circuit court to try a violation of the Act.
Title: Mail Theft
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill creates specific criminal offenses and graduated penalties for the theft of mail based on the number of items stolen. It also prohibits the unauthorized opening of mail, the theft of mail using an 'arrow key' (a specialized key used by postal and delivery services), and the possession of an arrow key with intent to commit a crime. Additionally, the bill establishes concurrent jurisdiction between the District Court and circuit courts for these offenses.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and the Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Maryland residents and mail recipients, the U.S. Postal Service, common carrier delivery services, law enforcement, and individuals prosecuted for mail-related offenses.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations. While the bill establishes new criminal penalties and fines, the fiscal impact on the Office of the Public Defender and the court system is anticipated to be minimal and absorbable within existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the criminal jurisdiction of the District Court and circuit courts under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to accommodate new felony mail theft and arrow key offenses, which requires operational coordination from the AOC.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note explicitly mentions an increase in workload for the Office of the Public Defender, as the agency will be responsible for representing indigent defendants charged with the newly created misdemeanor and felony offenses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The creation of new felony offenses with sentences of up to five years of imprisonment directly impacts the state's correctional facilities and the Division of Parole and Probation, which are managed by DPSCS.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing new criminal statutes and investigating violations related to theft and the possession of burglary-related tools like arrow keys.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates state public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice policy, making the establishment of new criminal classifications for mail theft highly relevant to their mission.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state on the enforcement of criminal laws and represents the state in civil or criminal appeals resulting from the application of this new legislation.
DJS may be responsible for youth who are charged under these new criminal provisions, necessitating adjustments to juvenile assessment and rehabilitative programming.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for enforcing this law and coordinates the policy initiatives that led to its introduction.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a State entity or a political subdivision of the State from assigning a Confederate name to real property owned by the State or political subdivision; and defining "Confederate name" as any name that commemorates or references any aspect of the states in rebellion, operating as the Confederate States of America, from 1861 to 1865 or any person or entity that serviced voluntarily with or on behalf of the Confederate States of America in any military or civilian capacity.
Title: State and Local Government - Real Property - Confederate Naming Prohibited
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/02 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
