The State's Attorney is authorized to notify the local school superintendent of the investigation and is required to notify them if the student is later cleared as a suspect. The bill also expands the annual reporting requirements for the Maryland State Department of Education to include demographic and academic data for students identified as suspects in these investigations.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education, State's Attorneys, local school superintendents, and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Students aged 5 to 21, local school systems, State's Attorneys, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the provided text does not include the formal Fiscal Note. The bill's financial implications are likely limited to administrative costs for law enforcement and State's Attorneys to manage the new notification timelines and for the Maryland State Department of Education to expand its data collection and reporting on reportable offenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the State Board (of Education) to adopt regulations regarding the use and destruction of information related to student suspects and requires the Department (MSDE) to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly on these incidents.

As a primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly responsible for notifying State's Attorneys when a student is identified as a suspect in a felony or crime of violence, or when a student is no longer a suspect.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The bill requires annual reporting of the race, ethnicity, gender, and disability status of students identified as suspects, which the Commission may monitor to ensure there is no discriminatory impact in the application of these notification laws.

bill_summary: This bill updates the Maryland Uniform Simultaneous Death Act to align with the national Uniform Simultaneous Death Act. It introduces a 120-hour survival requirement for individuals to be considered to have survived a decedent for inheritance, property distribution, and insurance purposes. Additionally, it establishes evidentiary procedures for determining death and provides liability protections for third-party payors who act in good faith when distributing assets.
stakeholders: Property co-owners, beneficiaries, estate executors, insurance companies, and trustees.
fiscal_impact_summary: No formal Fiscal Note is present in the provided text. The bill does not contain specific funding allocations or revenue mandates. It primarily affects the private distribution of assets. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills is the primary agency responsible for the administrative probate of estates and the collection of inheritance taxes. This bill directly alters the legal standards for inheritance and property devolution in cases of simultaneous death, which is central to the agency's core function.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish new evidentiary procedures and rules for determining survival in legal disputes. The Judicial Branch will be responsible for adjudicating these matters and managing property deposited with the court during disputes.

The bill defines 'governing instrument' to include insurance and annuity policies and 'payor' to include insurers. It establishes new rules for how insurance proceeds must be distributed when beneficiaries and the insured die nearly simultaneously.

The bill's definition of 'governing instrument' includes pensions and retirement benefit plans. As the administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System, this agency is a 'payor' that must comply with the 120-hour survival requirement for beneficiary payouts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Teachers & State Employees Supplemental Retirement Plans

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies on changes to the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article and may be involved in litigation or interpretation regarding the Uniform Simultaneous Death Act.

As the central personnel agency managing state employee benefits, DBM is impacted by definitions involving the state as a 'payor' for various employee benefit plans and the legalities of asset distribution to survivors of state employees.

The Comptroller oversees the collection of state revenues, including inheritance taxes. Changes to the rules of inheritance and property devolution could affect tax calculations and revenue collection procedures.

The bill explicitly references the Health - General Article for the definition of death and the procedures for death certificates. MDH's Vital Statistics Administration is responsible for the death certificates that will serve as prima facie evidence under this Act.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives; as this bill updates a uniform act and impacts multiple executive agencies (MDH, DBM, etc.), it requires administrative oversight.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to develop and maintain a flood risk disclosure statement for residential real estate transactions. Starting July 1, 2027, sellers of residential properties with four or fewer units must provide this form to potential buyers before entering into a contract of sale. The disclosure must detail whether the property is in a flood hazard area, its flood insurance history, any past claims for flood damage, and whether federal disaster assistance has been received for the property.
stakeholders: Sellers and buyers of residential real property with four or fewer single-family units
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. No impact on state revenues is expected, and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the primary implementing body tasked with developing, publishing, and maintaining the mandatory real property flood risk disclosure statement form.

The Department of Labor regulates and licenses real estate professionals, who are responsible for ensuring that these mandatory disclosures are properly integrated into property transactions.
The bill creates new statutory requirements for real estate sales contracts, which may increase the number of contract-related disputes and administrative workload for the state's judicial system.
The agency coordinates with FEMA regarding flood hazard mapping and disaster assistance, both of which are central data points required in the new disclosure form.

The bill's focus on residential real property disclosures is relevant to the department's mission of supporting safe and secure homeownership for Maryland residents.

The bill stipulates that civil penalties assessed by the Commissioner are subject to the notice and hearing requirements of the Administrative Procedures Act, which are adjudicated by this agency.

bill_summary: This bill establishes regulations to prevent waterborne diseases, specifically Legionnaires’ disease, by requiring public water suppliers to maintain minimum disinfectant residual levels and perform regular testing. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulatory body for public water systems in Maryland, MDE is tasked with adopting regulations, establishing a public database for water distribution system disruptions, conducting investigations of residual disinfectant violations, and performing water system testing upon notice of Legionnaires' disease diagnoses.

MDH is a primary implementing agency responsible for conducting comprehensive investigations of Legionnaires' disease cases, testing fixtures at water exposure points, developing a public awareness campaign, and maintaining a registry of de-identified case data.

MES operates numerous water and wastewater systems for state and local government clients. The bill's requirements for minimum disinfectant residual levels and increased testing will have a significant operational and fiscal impact on the systems they manage.

As the agency responsible for the maintenance and operation of state-owned facilities, DGS must ensure that covered state buildings implement the water management programs required to control Legionella.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates large correctional facilities which likely meet the criteria for 'covered buildings' under the ASHRAE standards, requiring the implementation of new water management programs and potential infrastructure upgrades.

The PSC regulates for-profit water utilities. These utilities will incur costs to comply with the new disinfectant and testing standards, which may result in rate cases and oversight by the Commission to adjust consumer costs.

The University System manages numerous buildings and campuses that serve as both water suppliers and owners of 'covered buildings' (dorms, labs, etc.). The fiscal note identifies significant costs for USM to comply with the bill.
The Judiciary manages courthouses and facilities that must comply with the building water management program requirements. They are specifically identified in the fiscal note as an impacted entity.

DBM is the principal fiscal and personnel agency. It will be responsible for overseeing the significant general fund expenditure increases for MDE and MDH staff and the fiscal impact on other state agency facility budgets.
Local school systems, overseen by MSDE, are building owners and sometimes water suppliers. The bill requires schools to implement water management programs and may necessitate facility upgrades.
MDOT and its sub-administrations (MVA, SHA, MTA, etc.) operate facilities and terminals that will be subject to the bill's water management program requirements for covered buildings.
The IAC oversees funding for public school capital improvements. Compliance with new water safety standards may lead to requests for capital funding for school water system upgrades.
As an independent state university, Morgan State manages its own facilities and will be responsible for implementing water management programs for its covered buildings.
OAH may be required to adjudicate contested cases related to MDE's enforcement actions and civil penalties imposed on water suppliers for non-compliance with the new standards.

OPC represents the interests of residential utility consumers. The significant costs for water utilities to comply with the bill will likely result in rate increases for consumers, necessitating advocacy from this office.
The college operates its own facilities and will be responsible for implementing water management programs for its covered buildings, as noted in the fiscal analysis.
The Governor receives the annual report required by the bill and oversees the executive agencies (MDE and MDH) responsible for the primary implementation of the new regulations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDE and MDH and would be involved in defending the new regulations and handling legal enforcement of penalties.
The Secretary of State may be involved if there are international implications or inter-state coordination regarding water quality standards, though their role is secondary.

Synopsis: Providing that an incarcerated individual who is serving a certain sentence for a certain sexual crime may be considered for parole only one time after becoming eligible; providing that if a victim, victim's family, victims' advocacy organization, or victim's representative objects to the granting of parole to a certain individual, parole shall be denied permanently; etc.
Title: Violent Criminals - Parole Limitation and Legislative Testimony Removal (Sexual Offender Accountability and Victim Protection Act)
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Judiciary; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Hate Crimes

bill_summary: This bill, the Sexual Offender Accountability and Victim Protection Act, limits individuals convicted of specific sexual crimes and sentenced to life plus additional years to a single parole consideration. It mandates that if a victim, their family, or an advocacy group objects to parole, it must be permanently denied. Furthermore, the bill requires the Maryland General Assembly to remove online records of legislative testimony provided by individuals convicted of violent crimes upon a victim's request and establishes a formal process for others to request access to those records.
responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission and the Maryland General Assembly
stakeholders: Victims of sexual and violent crimes, their families and representatives, victims' advocacy organizations, incarcerated individuals convicted of specified sexual or violent crimes, and Maryland General Assembly committee staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill creates administrative requirements for the Maryland Parole Commission regarding victim notification and permanent parole denial. It also imposes administrative duties on General Assembly committee managers to process and review requests for removed legislative testimony. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Parole Commission, an agency within this department, by restricting the number of times an individual can be considered for parole and mandating a permanent denial of parole if a victim or the Commission objects.

The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the General Assembly and executive agencies regarding the constitutionality and implementation of the parole restrictions and the removal of public records. They would also defend the state in potential legal challenges to the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates statewide public safety and victim services policies. The bill's focus on sexual offender accountability and enhanced victim rights in the parole process aligns directly with its mission.

Limiting parole opportunities for individuals serving life sentences will lead to an increase in the average length of incarceration, resulting in significant long-term fiscal impacts on the state budget and prison population management.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Maryland Parole Commission. This bill significantly alters executive branch policy regarding parole eligibility and the granting of parole.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents indigent defendants, many of whom are serving sentences affected by this bill. The bill curtails the future parole rights and due process of their clients by allowing for a permanent veto of parole.

As the central depository for government and legislative records of permanent value, the mandate to remove legislative testimony records from public access affects the agency's mission to preserve and provide access to the state's historical records.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Senate and the House of Delegates beginning with the 2033 legislative session; altering the method and timing of the election of State Senators; and requiring a Delegate who seeks election for a certain Senate term to vacate the seat of Delegate on the first day of the next immediately following legislative session.
Title: General Assembly - Membership, Election Timing for State Senators, and Eligibility
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/09 at 2:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to increase the membership of the Maryland General Assembly to 48 Senators and 144 Delegates beginning with the 2033 legislative session. It alters the election schedule for State Senators to establish staggered four-year terms starting with the 2032 election and requires any serving Delegate who seeks election to the Senate for a term beginning before their House term expires to vacate their seat.
responsible_party: Maryland General Assembly and the State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, current and future members of the Maryland General Assembly, and candidates for legislative office.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures will increase starting in 2033 to account for the salaries, benefits, and office expenses of four additional legislators (one Senator and three Delegates). The State Board of Elections will also incur costs to include the proposed constitutional amendment on the 2026 general election ballot. Since a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the timing and method of State Senator elections, including a complex ranking system based on vote totals to determine term lengths. The agency must also manage the statewide referendum required for this constitutional amendment.

The Governor is constitutionally required to receive election returns and proclaim the adoption or rejection of constitutional amendments. Additionally, the Governor oversees the filling of vacancies in the General Assembly, which is impacted by the new vacancy requirements for Delegates seeking Senate seats.

The agency provides the data analysis and technical assistance used in legislative redistricting. Increasing the number of Senate and House seats (from 47/141 to 48/144) necessitates significant changes to the state's legislative district mapping and demographic calculations.

The agency administers the pension system for legislators. Increasing the number of legislators and introducing staggered 2-year and 4-year terms requires adjustments to their tracking of service credits and retirement eligibility for members of the General Assembly.
The OAG provides legal counsel on constitutional amendments and election laws. They would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new term-length determination method based on vote rankings.
As the principal custodian of the state's official records and laws, the Secretary of State must record and maintain the updated Maryland Constitution following the referendum.

The addition of one Senator and three Delegates involves long-term fiscal impacts on the state budget regarding legislative salaries, benefits, and office staff expenditures managed within the state's personnel framework.

The Commission manages financial disclosures and ethics training for all state legislators. An increase in the number of members of the General Assembly directly increases the volume of the agency's compliance and oversight activities.
The Comptroller is responsible for paying state employees, including legislators. Adding new members to the General Assembly would require administrative updates to the state's payroll processing.
The agency is the central depository for government records of permanent value, including the results of constitutional referendums and updated versions of the Maryland Constitution.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to include the option on the certificate of candidacy form for candidates for congressional offices to indicate that, if elected, the candidate and the candidate's spouse will not engage in certain stock trading activities during the candidate's term of office; and requiring the State Board to publish on its website information concerning candidates for congressional offices who make that indication.
Title: Election Law - Certificate of Candidacy for Congressional Offices - Stock Trading Activities (Congressional Stock Trading Transparency Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/21 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: The Congressional Stock Trading Transparency Act requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to add an option to the certificate of candidacy form for candidates for the U.S. Senate or U.S. House of Representatives to indicate whether they and their spouses will refrain from buying, selling, or exchanging individual stocks during their term of office. The State Board must also publish a list of candidates who make this indication on its website.
stakeholders: Candidates for the office of United States Senator or Representative in Congress and their spouses
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact, and the State Board of Elections can implement the requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the State Board of Elections to modify the certificate of candidacy forms for congressional candidates to include a stock trading pledge and requires the Board to publish this information on its official website.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies like the State Board of Elections and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new form requirements and providing guidance on their implementation.

The bill references the existing requirement for candidates to file financial disclosure statements with the State Ethics Commission (or other required reports) as a condition of a valid certificate of candidacy, which is the primary subject of this legislation.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain documentation relating to real property may be used to establish a rebuttable presumption of ownership of the property in certain court proceedings.
Title: Courts - Evidence - Proof of Ownership of Real Property
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill allows a new owner of real property to use specific documentation, such as a deed submitted for recordation, a HUD-1 settlement statement, or a closing disclosure, to establish a rebuttable presumption of ownership in court proceedings. The purpose is to allow property owners to engage in legal actions to protect their property during the administrative period required to officially record a deed.
stakeholders: New real property owners and parties involved in legal proceedings regarding real property ownership
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances, and no specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new evidentiary standards for court proceedings and grants the Supreme Court of Maryland, which the Administrative Office of the Courts supports, the authority to adopt implementing rules and forms.

As the agency responsible for supporting homeownership and community development, this department is a primary stakeholder in property ownership verification and was consulted during the fiscal analysis of the bill.
The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates property assessment and tax disputes where the rebuttable presumption of ownership created by this bill would be directly applicable.
The Register of Wills manages probate and estate administration, where establishing real property ownership during the processing time for a deed transfer is frequently necessary.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state and its agencies on the interpretation and application of new evidentiary statutes in civil and criminal litigation.
Administrative Law Judges at the OAH may be required to apply this rebuttable presumption of ownership in contested administrative cases involving state agencies and property interests.
As the primary manager of state-owned real estate and acquisitions, the agency is impacted by rules governing the legal protection of property during the transition period before a deed is recorded.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a health care provider from using the health care provider's human reproductive material when providing assisted reproductive treatment without the consent of the recipient of the treatment; prohibiting a health care provider from using a donor's human reproductive material to provide assisted reproductive treatment without the donor's informed consent or in a manner that is inconsistent with the donor's consent; etc.
Title: Health Care Providers - Assisted Reproductive Treatment - Informed Consent and Fraud
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg

bill_summary: This bill establishes strict informed consent requirements for health care providers performing assisted reproductive treatments (ART), such as in vitro fertilization and insemination. It prohibits providers from using their own human reproductive material without the recipient's consent and requires separate written consent from both donors and recipients. The bill also forbids providers or their employees from misrepresenting donor identity, genetic history, or the quality of reproductive material. Unauthorized use of a provider's own material is classified as a felony, and the bill creates civil liability for damages, including liquidated damages of up to $50,000 and attorney's fees.
responsible_party: Maryland health care provider licensing boards and the state court system
stakeholders: Health care providers performing assisted reproductive treatments, fertility clinic employees, sperm and egg donors, patients receiving fertility treatments, and children born as a result of assisted reproductive treatment.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the bill text. However, the bill establishes a new felony offense for unauthorized use of a provider's reproductive material, punishable by a fine of up to $5,000. Additionally, health care providers may be subject to civil lawsuits for violations, with potential liquidated damages of up to $50,000 per violation, as well as compensatory damages and legal fees. Specific state-wide expenditure and revenue estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Health - General Article and requires health care providers to report misuses or errors in human reproductive material to their respective licensing boards, which are housed under the Maryland Department of Health.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new civil causes of action for medical liability and damages against health care providers for unauthorized use of human reproductive material. As the office responsible for mandatory arbitration of medical malpractice claims, HCADRO would likely manage the initial filing of these claims.

The bill establishes new civil causes of action with specific statutes of limitations and creates a new felony offense for unauthorized use of a provider's own reproductive material, which will impact court caseloads and judicial procedures.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the health occupations licensing boards and the Department of Health, and would likely be involved in advising on the implementation and enforcement of the new reporting and fraud requirements.

The bill requires reporting violations to licensing boards. Contested disciplinary actions taken by these boards against health care providers for violations of this section would be adjudicated through the Office of Administrative Hearings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new felony offense punishable by up to 10 years in prison, which could impact the state's correctional system population and parole/probation caseloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense. The Office of the Public Defender would be responsible for representing indigent health care providers charged with this crime.
As the primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be involved in investigating allegations of health care provider fraud and criminal violations of this section.

Synopsis: Requiring each county and municipal automated traffic enforcement program to submit to the Vision Zero coordinator an annual report containing certain information regarding each citation issued under the program during the quarter to a motor vehicle registered in another state.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Out-of-State Drivers - Automated Enforcement (Out-of-State Driver Accountability Act)
Status: In the Senate - Second Reading Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration

bill_summary: The Out-of-State Driver Accountability Act requires county and municipal automated traffic enforcement programs to submit annual reports to the State's Vision Zero coordinator regarding citations issued to vehicles registered in other states. These reports must include specific registration details, payment status, and cumulative summaries of out-of-state citations and collections.
responsible_party: The Vision Zero coordinator within the Maryland Department of Transportation and local governments operating automated traffic enforcement programs.
stakeholders: Out-of-state drivers, local county and municipal governments, and the Maryland Department of Transportation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Local governments may incur minimal administrative costs to prepare and submit the required reports, but local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department's Vision Zero coordinator receive and manage annual reports from local jurisdictions regarding out-of-state citations. It also requires the coordinator to collaborate with local programs for implementation.

As a division of MDOT, the MVA is responsible for driver and vehicle services, including registration data and reciprocity agreements that identify out-of-state vehicle owners, which is central to the bill's focus on out-of-state driver accountability.

The Maryland State Police enforce motor vehicle laws and manage work zone speed control systems, which are among the automated enforcement programs listed in the bill. They are also listed as a primary information source in the fiscal note.

SHA is responsible for the state's roadway safety and the infrastructure that supports various automated enforcement systems mentioned in the bill. They also support the overall Vision Zero policy goals.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to MDOT and the Vision Zero coordinator regarding the reporting requirements, data sharing, and potential legal challenges related to enforcing citations against out-of-state residents.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including MDOT and the Vision Zero program, and handles the high-level policy coordination related to traffic safety initiatives.

The Lieutenant Governor often chairs task forces and advisory councils related to public safety, including work zone safety, which is specifically cited as a type of automated enforcement covered by the bill.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state and would oversee any budgetary adjustments or personnel impacts (though minimal per the fiscal note) within MDOT resulting from this new reporting requirement.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Baltimore County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on certain real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026.
Title: Baltimore County – Property Tax Credit – Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing body of Baltimore County to grant a property tax credit equal to 100% of the county property tax imposed on real property owned by the Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34, located at 730 Wampler Road, Middle River, Maryland.
stakeholders: Fraternal Order of Police Lodge 34 and Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Baltimore County property tax revenues may decrease by approximately $9,600 annually beginning in fiscal 2027, to the extent the property tax credit is granted by the county. County expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief executive, the Governor's Office is responsible for signing this bill into law or exercising veto power after it passes the General Assembly.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and the Governor's Office, reviewing legislation for constitutionality and legal sufficiency.
The PTAAB is an independent agency that hears appeals regarding disputes over real property tax assessments and property tax credits, such as the one authorized by this bill for Baltimore County.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, including appeals from the decisions of the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board regarding property tax credits.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Motor Vehicle Administration to take possession of certain motor vehicle registration cards and registration plates that were issued by another jurisdiction but is being used or displayed on a motor vehicle by a person who has been a resident of the State for more than 60 days; prohibiting a title service agent from selling or offering for sale a motor vehicle registration issued by another jurisdiction to a resident of this State; altering a certain policy of the State; etc.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Out-of-State Vehicles - Improper Registration
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill establishes a formal enforcement process to bring motor vehicles owned by Maryland residents that are improperly registered in other states into compliance with Maryland law. It authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to issue warnings, impose civil fines of $7 per day for continued noncompliance, and suspend driver's licenses for violators. The bill also prohibits title service agents from selling out-of-state registrations to Maryland residents and allows the State to enter into reciprocal agreements for the enforcement of automated traffic violations with other jurisdictions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation, Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA)
stakeholders: Maryland residents operating vehicles with out-of-state registrations, title service agents, and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues, primarily for the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), are projected to increase by $15,375,437 in FY 2027 as residents bring vehicles into compliance; additional excise tax revenues could range from $26,200,000 to $65,500,000. TTF expenditures are estimated to increase by $379,365 in FY 2027 to cover the cost of five new customer service agents and administrative operations. Local governments are expected to see an increase in highway user revenues and the recovery of past-due automated enforcement citations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and manages the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF). The bill has a significant fiscal impact on the TTF and requires MDOT to oversee the primary implementing agency.

The MVA is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including issuing warnings, assessing civil fines, suspending driver's licenses, and entering into reciprocal enforcement agreements with other jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a notable increase in revenues for the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund (MEMSOF) and trauma funds overseen by MIEMSS, resulting from registration surcharges on newly compliant vehicles.

The Department of the Environment co-manages the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP). The bill will increase VEIP activity and revenue as out-of-state vehicles are brought into Maryland compliance.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are involved in traffic enforcement and are authorized to take possession of illegal or improperly used registration plates as described in the bill.
DBM is the principal personnel and fiscal agency; the bill requires the creation of five new state positions and involves significant administrative expenditures and revenue tracking.
The bill establishes a new civil action in rem for persistent registration violations and involves the suspension of driving privileges, which impacts court proceedings and judicial record-keeping.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies; they would be responsible for advising MVA on the legality and structure of reciprocal enforcement agreements and the new civil action processes.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures; any major procurement of technology or services to implement the new reciprocal enforcement or fine tracking systems would require their approval.
As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors state revenues. The bill is projected to generate millions of dollars in new special fund revenue across multiple accounts.

Synopsis: Providing that it is lawful for a person to intercept an oral communication if the person is working as a fair housing tester for a fair housing testing program operated by the federal government, the State, a local government, or a nonprofit civil rights organization under certain circumstances; and providing that the contents of an intercepted oral communication may be used only for the purpose of enforcing federal, State, or local fair housing laws.
Title: Evidence – Interception of Oral Communications – Fair Housing Testing
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill allows fair housing testers working for government programs or specific nonprofit civil rights organizations to intercept oral communications without the consent of all parties, provided the tester is a party to the communication and the recording is intended to gather evidence of fair housing violations. The intercepted evidence is only admissible for enforcing federal, state, or local fair housing laws.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and state and local fair housing enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Fair housing testers, nonprofit civil rights organizations, property owners and managers, and government agencies involved in fair housing enforcement
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances or operations. No specific revenue or expenditure figures are provided as the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to establish new rules for the admissibility of evidence obtained through the interception of oral communications. It specifically affects how courts must handle evidence in trials or hearings involving fair housing violations.

The Commission is the primary state agency responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination laws in housing. The bill specifically empowers fair housing testing programs—which the Commission may operate or oversee—by allowing testers to record communications as evidence of violations.

The department is responsible for ensuring residents have access to safe and secure housing. Fair housing testing is a critical tool for identifying discrimination that prevents residents from securing housing, directly aligning with the department's mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under current law, intercepting oral communications without consent is a felony. By creating a lawful exception for fair housing testers, the bill directly impacts the criminal statutes that the Office of the Public Defender would navigate when representing indigent individuals who might otherwise face surveillance-related charges.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are responsible for enforcing criminal laws, including those related to illegal electronic surveillance. This bill creates a statutory exception to the wiretap felony for housing testers, which impacts police investigative and arrest protocols.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including those involving regulatory enforcement and potential housing discrimination claims where this type of recorded evidence might now be introduced.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the Commission on Civil Rights and other state agencies. They would be responsible for interpreting these new evidentiary rules and using this evidence in civil rights litigation.

Synopsis: Requiring institutions of higher education to develop and implement an academic forgiveness policy on or before August 1, 2026, that applies to applicants who earned unsatisfactory or failing grades at a prior institution of higher education under certain circumstances.
Title: Higher Education - Academic Forgiveness Policy - Established
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland institutions of higher education that receive State funding to establish an academic forgiveness policy by August 1, 2026. The policy allows applicants to elect to have unsatisfactory or failing grades earned seven or more years prior to their application disregarded during the admissions process.
responsible_party: Maryland institutions of higher education that receive State funding
stakeholders: Prospective higher education students with academic records older than seven years and Maryland institutions of higher education receiving State funds.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the mandate for institutions to develop and implement a new academic forgiveness policy by August 2026 suggests that these institutions would likely incur administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission is responsible for establishing and overseeing statewide policies for public and private institutions, including the implementation of the mandated academic forgiveness policy.

As the primary public higher education system in the state, the University System of Maryland must develop and implement the required academic forgiveness policies across its 12 member institutions that receive state funds.

As a state-funded public university independent of the University System, Morgan State University is directly required by the bill to implement an academic forgiveness policy for its admissions process.
As Maryland's public honors college and an independent state agency receiving state funds, the college is mandated to develop and implement the academic forgiveness policy described in the bill.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Higher Education Commission and the public institutions of higher education, and would likely assist in drafting and reviewing the required academic forgiveness policies for legal compliance.

This agency collects and analyzes student performance data from the Higher Education Commission and partner institutions. Changes in how prior grades are treated in the admissions process may impact data collection, reporting, and longitudinal studies of student outcomes.

The department advocates for veterans' educational benefits. Veterans are often non-traditional students who may have prior academic records from 7+ years ago and could significantly benefit from the academic forgiveness policies established by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Aging to conduct an annual financial stress test for each continuing care in a retirement community provider; requiring a continuing care in a retirement community provider to meet with a resident association at least quarterly and in a certain manner; requiring a provider to make agendas and minutes of certain meetings accessible to the provider's subscribers; etc.
Title: Continuing Care Providers - Financial Stress Tests, Transparency, and Governing Bodies
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:45 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Continuing Care -see also- Long-Term Care; Nursing Homes

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Aging to conduct annual financial stress tests for continuing care retirement community providers and publish financial stability grades on its website. It also mandates that providers meet with resident associations at least quarterly, provide meeting agendas and minutes to subscribers, and requires that subscriber members of a provider's governing body be elected by the resident association rather than selected by the provider.
stakeholders: Subscribers (residents) of continuing care retirement communities, continuing care retirement community providers, and the Maryland Department of Aging.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by at least $270,500 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Aging to hire two analysts and secure contractual services for a financial grading system. Ongoing annual expenditures are estimated to range from $200,900 to $228,300 through FY 2031. Special fund revenues to the Continuing Care Fund may increase by an indeterminate amount if provider fees are raised to offset these administrative costs. There is no impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Department of Aging to conduct annual financial stress tests for continuing care providers, hire analysts to perform these tests, and manage the results through its Financial Review Committee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill assigns a specific new duty to the Department of Aging's Financial Review Committee, which is a permanent advisory body composed of experts appointed to evaluate the financial condition of providers.

The bill requires the hiring of two new analysts and involves a significant increase in special fund expenditures, which falls under the oversight of the Department of Budget and Management for personnel and fiscal planning.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to the Department of Aging regarding the implementation of the new stress tests and the public grading system for private providers.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Aging, and is responsible for the overall state budget process which includes the new special fund expenditures and personnel required by this bill.

bill_summary: This bill creates the crime of benefits exploitation, prohibiting individuals from using deception, coercion, or isolation to recruit, harbor, transport, or obtain a person for the purpose of misappropriating their government benefits. It defines government benefits to include programs like Social Security, Medicare, SNAP, and veterans benefits, and establishes a graduated system of misdemeanor and felony penalties based on the monetary value of the benefits involved.
stakeholders: Recipients of government benefits (including elderly and disabled individuals, veterans, and low-income families), law enforcement agencies, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender.

No material impact is expected on local finances. While the Office of the Public Defender indicated a need for additional staff, the Department of Legislative Services determined that the bill's workload can likely be handled with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new criminal offense for the exploitation of government benefits specifically administered by DHS, including TANF, SNAP, TDAP, and Public Assistance to Adults (PAA).

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and already possesses authority to bring civil actions against exploitation of vulnerable adults. This bill expands the criminal law framework in a related area.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

The bill specifically addresses the exploitation of 'elderly' adults within its definition of coercion, aligning with the department's mission to protect the rights and quality of life for older adults.

The bill's definition of coercion includes 'exerting financial control over a disabled' adult, making it relevant to the department's role in advocating for and protecting the rights of residents with disabilities.
The bill explicitly lists 'veterans benefits' as a protected government benefit, which is the core area of support provided by this agency to Maryland's veterans.
As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, MSP would be responsible for investigating reports of benefits exploitation and enforcing these new criminal statutes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for election administration, the State Board is directly responsible for the bill's expanded public notice requirements, maintaining the central web repository for election policy changes, and overseeing the administrative policies affected by the act.

The bill specifies the Circuit Court for Anne Arundel County as the exclusive venue for certain actions and establishes mandatory judicial standards, expedited pretrial and trial proceedings, and specific remedy requirements that the court must follow.

The bill's definition of 'Local Government' and 'Governing Body' explicitly includes county boards of education and their elected members, subjecting school board election policies and boundary changes to the act's anti-suppression and notice requirements.

The bill defines voting assistance for people with disabilities as an 'administrative policy affecting voting rights' and requires local governments to take appropriate steps to provide meaningful notice of proposed changes to residents with disabilities.

The department is relevant due to the fiscal impact of the bill, which includes potential state liability for attorney's fees and litigation costs in enforcement actions and the administrative costs associated with new notice and reporting requirements for state boards.

fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services indicates that the bill's requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. State and local revenues and expenditures are not anticipated to be materially affected. Small business impacts are expected to be minimal.

DHCD must be consulted by MDE during the regulatory process and is also granted authority to approve the installation of submeters by local housing authorities.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division is explicitly named as a state-level body responsible for handling complaints from occupants regarding water submeter billing and violations if local agencies lack jurisdiction.
The Board of Public Works is given specific authority in the bill to approve the installation of individual submeters by local housing authorities.

fiscal_impact_summary: If approved by voters in the 2026 general election, the bill is expected to increase State and local expenditures beginning in FY 2028 for primary election implementation. While the total impact is indeterminate, an illustrative estimate from the Fiscal Note suggests a State general fund expenditure increase of $154,000 and a collective local government expenditure increase of at least $480,000 in FY 2028. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections (SBE) is the primary agency responsible for supervising and administering elections in Maryland. The bill requires that all returns from the constitutional amendment vote be made to the Governor and mandates that the Governor issue a formal proclamation declaring the amendment adopted if it is ratified by the voters.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records, including laws and constitutional amendments. If ratified and proclaimed by the Governor, the Secretary of State would be responsible for recording the amendment.

Synopsis: Expanding the authority of the Treasurer of the Maryland Environmental Service to delegate certain functions to the Deputy Treasurer of the Service; increasing the threshold amount from $25,000 to $50,000 or less for estimated contract costs under which the Service may use the small procurement process; and altering the process for providing notice of the establishment or adjustment of certain rates charged for Service projects, products, or services.
Title: Maryland Environmental Service - Authorizations and Requirements - Alterations
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 77

bill_summary: This bill expands the authority of the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) Treasurer to delegate financial duties to the Deputy Treasurer and increases the cost threshold for the Service's small procurement process from $25,000 to $50,000. It also updates the public notice requirements for establishing or adjusting service district rates, requiring at least 60 days' notice and allowing for modern notification methods such as website postings, emails, or text messages in addition to traditional newspaper advertisements.
stakeholders: Residents and ratepayers within Maryland Environmental Service districts, Maryland Environmental Service leadership and staff, and vendors or contractors bidding on Maryland Environmental Service projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material effect on State or local finances. According to the fiscal note, the Maryland Environmental Service may experience administrative efficiencies by raising the small procurement threshold to $50,000, which aligns it more closely with standard State procurement thresholds and allows for faster procurement of certain goods and services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary subject of the bill, the Maryland Environmental Service (MES) is directly affected by changes to its internal financial governance, deputy treasurer authorities, procurement thresholds, and public notice requirements for its service districts.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland State Treasurer to determine the type and amount of surety bonds or insurance coverage for the MES Treasurer and Deputy Treasurer. Additionally, the MES Treasurer must deposit funds in financial institutions authorized by the State Treasurer.

The Board of Public Works oversees state procurement policies and significant expenditures; altering the small procurement threshold for a state instrumentality like MES falls under its general purview of fiscal integrity and procurement oversight.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller has a direct interest in the financial accounting systems, debt payment arrangements, and procurement thresholds of state instrumentalities like MES.

The bill amends the Natural Resources Article of the Maryland Code. As the agency responsible for environmental conservation and managing the article under which MES is established, DNR has a related administrative and policy interest.

MES provides technical environmental services, such as water and wastewater management, which are core to MDE's mission. Changes to how MES sets rates and notifies residents in service districts impact MDE's broader environmental infrastructure goals.
This is a departmental bill submitted on behalf of a state executive instrumentality. The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives for agencies like MES.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the slaughter of racehorses for commercial purposes, such as human or animal consumption. It also bans the purchase, sale, transfer, or transportation of racehorses if the person knows or should know the horse will be slaughtered for commercial purposes. Violations are classified as misdemeanors subject to fines and potential imprisonment, and the State Racing Commission or the State Department of Agriculture may suspend or revoke licenses of violators.
responsible_party: State Racing Commission and the Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Racehorse owners, breeders, trainers, transporters, and commercial entities involved in the horse racing industry.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 from fines collected for violations ($1,000 to $2,000 for individuals and $2,500 to $5,000 for entities). These fines are distributed to the horse racing special fund. State expenditures are not directly affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Racing Commission, which is an entity within the Department of Labor, is the primary regulatory body responsible for overseeing the horse racing industry. This bill specifically tasks the Commission with adopting regulations, collecting fines for the racing Special Fund, and revoking or suspending licenses for violations.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Department of Agriculture to revoke or suspend licenses it issues to persons found in violation of the racehorse slaughter prohibition. Additionally, the Maryland Racing Commission must consult with this department when adopting regulations to carry out the bill's provisions.

The bill creates new misdemeanor offenses regarding the slaughter, purchase, sale, or transport of racehorses for commercial purposes. These criminal charges would be adjudicated through the Maryland judicial system.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Racing Commission and the Department of Agriculture. They would likely assist in the drafting of new regulations and represent the agencies in legal challenges related to license revocations or enforcement actions.

The Treasurer's Office is responsible for the management and distribution of state funds. The bill directs fine revenue to the racing Special Fund, an account for which the Treasurer serves as a principal custodian.

The Comptroller, as the state's chief financial officer, oversees the collection and distribution of state revenues. The bill modifies the composition of the racing Special Fund by adding fine revenue collected under the new prohibition.

The Maryland State Police enforce criminal and motor vehicle laws. They may be involved in enforcing the bill's prohibition on the transportation of racehorses within the state if intended for commercial slaughter.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes misdemeanor penalties that include potential imprisonment for up to one year. This could impact the department's responsibilities regarding pretrial detention or the supervision of individuals sentenced to probation.

The Governor oversees the executive branch departments involved in implementing this bill (Labor and Agriculture) and is responsible for proposing the state budget, which includes the special funds affected by these fines.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM supervises budget execution and revenue estimation. It would oversee the fiscal impact of the new fine revenue distributed to the racing Special Fund.

bill_summary: This bill increases the statutory limit on the aggregate outstanding and unpaid principal balance of revenue bonds issued by the Maryland Transportation Authority from $4.0 billion to $5.0 billion.
stakeholders: Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA), Maryland Department of Transportation, toll facility users, and federal emergency response agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the Maryland Transportation Authority's (MDTA) debt capacity by $1,000,000,000. Nonbudgeted revenues will increase as MDTA issues additional bonds, with planned issuances expected to exceed the current $4,000,000,000 limit starting in fiscal 2029. Corresponding nonbudgeted expenditures will increase for related debt service. This increase is intended to provide liquidity for the reconstruction of the Francis Scott Key Bridge and other capital preservation projects while awaiting federal reimbursement.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency governed by this legislation, the MDTA's statutory revenue bond debt limit is increased by $1 billion to facilitate the financing of the Francis Scott Key Bridge reconstruction and other capital projects.
MDTA is a modal administration within MDOT; the department requested this bill to ensure adequate funding for its comprehensive transportation capital program and emergency infrastructure needs.
The Treasurer oversees the issuance of state bonds, manages state funds and bond sale revenue, and serves on the Board of Public Works which reviews major financial authorizations.

The Board of Public Works, which includes the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees significant state expenditures and the fiscal integrity of the state's capital projects and bond activities.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for long-term fiscal planning and monitoring the debt capacity and financial health of state entities.
The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and is a member of the Board of Public Works, which provides oversight for state expenditures and bond issuances.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and MDOT/MDTA operations and serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which approves major transportation expenditures.

bill_summary: The Transportation Investment Priorities Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to develop and implement a project-based scoring system to evaluate and prioritize major surface transportation projects for inclusion in the Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP). The bill defines major surface transportation projects as those exceeding $5 million in total cost. Additionally, it restructures the Maryland Transportation Commission by altering its membership to 13 members, changing the chair to the Secretary of Transportation, and expanding its duties to include reviewing budget updates and prioritization guidelines.
stakeholders: Local governments, metropolitan planning organizations, transit agencies, and Maryland residents who utilize state highways and transit systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a new prioritization and scoring process for transportation projects with total costs exceeding $5,000,000. While the bill text does not provide specific appropriation amounts or revenue changes, it requires MDOT to identify available funds for these projects biennially after accounting for department operating costs, maintenance, and other mandatory grants. A formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not provided in the text, so specific state and local fiscal impacts are indeterminate beyond the procedural requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary department responsible for the Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP), the Department of Transportation (MDOT) is the lead agency implementing the bill's requirements for a new project-based scoring system and restructuring the Maryland Transportation Commission.

Projects within the State Highway Administration (SHA) are specifically identified as 'major surface transportation projects' that must be evaluated and scored using the new prioritization system before being included in the CTP.
Projects within the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) are classified as 'major surface transportation projects' and are subject to the new project-based scoring system for capital prioritization.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly alters the membership, chair, meeting frequency, and responsibilities of the Maryland Transportation Commission, which is a body encompassed by this collective designation.

The bill includes Maryland Transportation Authority projects in the definition of capital projects and requires their capital and operating programs to be summarized in the CTP. Their funding needs are also considered before determining available funds for the surface project scoring cycle.

While its projects are excluded from the new surface scoring system, the administration's capital funding needs must be identified and accounted for before the Department determines available funds for the project-based scoring cycle.
The administration's projects are excluded from the scoring process, but its capital funding needs are explicitly factored into the prioritization cycle's budget determination.
The MVA is an administration under MDOT whose capital funding needs must be identified and prioritized prior to the allocation of funds for the major surface transportation project scoring process.

The Governor is responsible for appointing eight members to the Maryland Transportation Commission under the new structure and oversees the executive branch departments implementing the CTP scoring system.
This office will be responsible for vetting and recommending the eight members appointed by the Governor to the restructured Maryland Transportation Commission.
The bill includes 'sustainable land use' as a policy goal for project evaluation, and MDOT is required to coordinate with local planning efforts during its annual county visits regarding the CTP.
The project evaluation process must consider climate change, environmental goals, and the Greenhouse Gas Emissions Reduction Act, which are primary focus areas for the MDE.
The bill maintains the requirement for MDOT to consult with the Department of Natural Resources regarding water access for recreational activities when developing projects for the CTP.
The Consolidated Transportation Program must specifically include a summary of plans to increase commuter access between University of Maryland campuses, which is a core component of the USM.

As the agency responsible for developing the state's budget and long-term fiscal planning, DBM is impacted by the restructuring of transportation investment priorities and the financial forecasts associated with the CTP.

bill_summary: This bill delays the decentralization of the Guaranteed Access Grant Program until the 2029-2030 financial aid award year. This postponement shifts the timeline for when Maryland's higher education institutions must assume responsibility for notifying students of their awards and issuing those awards, a task currently performed by the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
stakeholders: Undergraduate students eligible for the Guaranteed Access Grant, Maryland higher education institutions, and the Maryland Higher Education Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures for the administration of Guaranteed Access Grants at institutions of higher education are delayed until FY 2029. General fund expenditures intended to cover these administrative costs and the corresponding higher education revenues are also delayed. Additionally, Maryland Higher Education Commission programming costs for system updates are postponed. Specific dollar estimates are not provided in the fiscal note as exact costs depend on individual institutional implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill delays planned general fund expenditures and potential revenue allocations intended to support the administrative costs of decentralizing the grant program to institutions of higher education, impacting the state's fiscal planning overseen by DBM.
As a departmental bill requested by the Higher Education Commission, this represents a policy initiative of the executive branch which is overseen and coordinated by the Governor's Office.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission is the primary agency responsible for the bill request. The bill delays the transfer of grant administration responsibilities from MHEC's Office of Student Financial Assistance to individual institutions.
MHEC is the primary departmental requester and is responsible for centrally administering the Guaranteed Access Grant Program; the bill extends this central authority until the 2029-2030 award year.

The agency links student financial aid data from MHEC to workforce outcomes; delaying the decentralization of grant awards maintains the current data reporting structure between MHEC and the MLDS for several additional years.

As a state institution of higher education, Morgan State University is directly impacted by the delay of the decentralization process, which defers its responsibility to notify students and issue awards for the Guaranteed Access Grant Program.
As the state's public honors college and an independent state agency, its financial aid office's transition to a decentralized model of grant administration is delayed by four years under this bill.

The bill delays the transfer of administrative burdens and associated costs to USM's constituent institutions, which were previously scheduled to take over award notifications and issuance for the GA Grant in 2025.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland National Guard's tuition assistance program to include 'training assistance' for expenses such as industry-required tools, uniforms, and licensing costs. It also broadens the list of eligible institutions to include career and trade schools recognized by the Maryland Higher Education Commission or the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council, and removes the 50% tuition waiver requirement for private vocational schools.
stakeholders: Active members of the Maryland National Guard and Maryland postsecondary vocational, trade, and career schools.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially impact State or local finances. While it expands the types of expenses and institutions eligible for assistance, the program's spending is limited to the amount provided in the State budget. For fiscal years 2025 through 2027, the budget allocation for this program is $600,000 annually. No local government impact is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is responsible for certifying the eligibility of National Guard members for tuition and training assistance. The bill was also introduced at the request of the Military Department.

The bill directly impacts the members of the Maryland National Guard by expanding the types of educational institutions they can attend and the specific expenses (training assistance) covered by state funds.

The bill defines eligible institutions as career schools recognized by the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC). MHEC is also responsible for maintaining the list of institutions offering tuition waivers to Guard members.

The bill expands eligible institutions to include those recognized by the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Council (MATC), which is a body overseen by the Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.
The University System of Maryland is explicitly listed as a qualifying institution where National Guard members may utilize the tuition and training assistance provided under the bill.
Morgan State University is specifically named in the bill as an eligible institution for National Guard service members to receive tuition and training assistance.
St. Mary's College is specifically named in the bill as an eligible institution for National Guard service members to receive tuition and training assistance.
The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state budget, which provides the funding (currently $600,000 annually) for the Military Department's tuition assistance program.

bill_summary: This departmental bill updates the administrative and regulatory framework for public school construction in Maryland. It clarifies the State Superintendent's role in approving school facility projects involving student-occupied spaces, increases the cost threshold for change order approvals from $50,000 to $200,000, and repeals the requirement for the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) to approve 75% of preliminary funding by December 31. Additionally, the bill refines criteria for state debt service reimbursement on unused school buildings and aligns statutory reporting for facility assessments and alternative energy systems.
responsible_party: Interagency Commission on School Construction and the State Superintendent of Schools
stakeholders: Local education agencies, county governments, and Maryland public school students.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is largely procedural and does not have a direct fiscal impact on State or local finances. While the bill adjusts reporting deadlines and alters the timeline for funding allocations, these administrative changes are expected to be managed with existing resources and may allow for more efficient use of agency funds.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Interagency Commission on School Construction is the primary agency implementing the bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations for state funding eligibility, conducting maintenance and facility assessments, managing project allocations, and establishing an appeals process for local jurisdictions regarding project funding.

The bill mandates that the State Superintendent of Schools (the head of MSDE) or their designee must approve school site proposals, construction plans for new buildings, and significant renovations or additions to existing school facilities that affect student-occupied spaces.

The bill clarifies the Department of General Services' role in reviewing design and construction documents for major school construction and systemic renovation projects, as well as its collaboration with the IAC to develop submission and approval timelines.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures, including the capital funding for school construction, and plays a role in the reimbursement of state debt service for school buildings that are no longer used for eligible educational purposes.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the state's capital budget, which includes the school construction allocations and debt service management affected by the bill's procedural and reporting changes.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is involved in school construction financing and implementation (such as through the Built to Learn Act), and its projects are subject to the IAC approval processes and terminology updates outlined in this bill.

The Governor's Office receives mandated reports from the IAC regarding maintenance effectiveness and facility assessments. Additionally, the Governor chairs the Board of Public Works, which manages school construction funding and debt reimbursement.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees school construction spending and debt service reimbursement. The agency also monitors the fiscal integrity of state revenues used for these projects.

The State Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works and manages state bonds and insurance. The bill's provisions concerning the reimbursement of outstanding state debt service for transferred school property directly intersect with the Treasurer's financial management duties.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the IAC, MSDE, and other state agencies regarding the implementation of new regulations, contract requirements, and legal procedures for debt service reimbursement.
The bill requires school facility assessments to include data on lead paint and asbestos, hazards for which the Department of the Environment maintains regulatory oversight and safety standards.

Synopsis: Repealing a requirement that a certain police employee or deputy State fire marshal is entitled to a certain pay rate on promotion to a higher rank if a certain other police employee or deputy State fire marshal in the same rank is at a lower pay rate.
