bill_summary: This bill mandates the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) to designate priority watersheds for flood-related studies every five years and requires local subdivisions within these watersheds to conduct detailed studies and GIS mapping for review. It updates the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program by authorizing up to $20,000,000 in annual funding, requiring that 40% of funds benefit underserved communities, and adjusting grant allocation caps for watershed studies and the acquisition of flood-damaged properties.
stakeholders: Maryland counties and municipalities, residents of flood-prone areas, and underserved or overburdened communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: Starting in FY 2026, the bill authorizes the Governor to include up to $20,000,000 annually in the State budget for the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program. It requires that at least 40% of this funding be used for projects benefiting underserved or overburdened communities. The bill also modifies grant limits, capping study-related grants at 5% of the total appropriation starting in FY 2029 and property acquisition grants at 25% of annual funds. Local subdivisions will face costs to conduct mandated watershed studies, which may be partially or fully offset by state grants provided under the program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. It is tasked with designating priority watersheds, reviewing and approving subdivision watershed studies and GIS maps, and administering the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program.

The Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) is specifically named as a consulting agency for watershed designations and guidelines. It also reviews local response plans for automated flood warning projects and is the lead agency for a required study on local hazard-planning requirements under Section 2 of the bill.

The Department of Planning is a required consultant for watershed designations and guidelines. Additionally, its State Clearinghouse is responsible for reviewing all project applications for grants under the Comprehensive Flood Management Grant Program.

The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is specifically named in the bill as an agency that must be consulted by MDE when designating priority watersheds and developing guidelines for watershed studies.
The Department of Agriculture (MDA) is specifically named in the bill as an agency that must be consulted by MDE when designating priority watersheds and developing guidelines for watershed studies.
The Board of Public Works (BPW) must approve the use of state debt proceeds and the awarding of grants for watershed studies and flood management capital projects as outlined in the bill.

The Governor's Office provides executive oversight for the implementing agencies and is specifically authorized by the bill to include appropriations of up to $20,000,000 in the annual State budget for the grant program.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is responsible for state budget development and personnel. It would manage the fiscal execution of the $20 million appropriation for the flood management program mentioned in the bill.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is required to approve the grants and expenditures for the flood management programs and studies established or modified by this bill.
The State Treasurer's Office is a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve grant expenditures and the use of State debt for the programs mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Altering and updating the standards and procedures governing the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program related to the approval of regulations, local program comprehensive reviews, locational standards for growth allocation, correcting mapping mistakes, and tree replanting.
Title: Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program - Standards and Procedures
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Chesapeake Bay -see also- Chesapeake Bay Restoration
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This departmental bill updates standards and procedures for the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Protection Program. Key changes include extending the mandatory local program comprehensive review period from 6 to 10 years, refining the standards for growth allocation and mapping corrections, and requiring that court-assessed damages for illegal tree cutting be paid to the local jurisdiction rather than the Department of Natural Resources.
responsible_party: Critical Area Commission (Department of Natural Resources)
stakeholders: Local jurisdictions, property owners, developers, and licensed environmental professionals including foresters and landscape architects within the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to have a significant fiscal impact on State or local finances. According to the fiscal note, the proposed changes reflect current practices, including the distribution of damages for illegal tree clearing to local governments rather than the State.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays Critical Area Commission is housed within the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). The bill specifically alters the distribution of court-assessed damages for illegal tree cutting, redirecting them from the Department to local jurisdictions, and involves the State Forester in replanting plans.

The bill deals with land use classifications, mapping criteria, and growth allocation standards within the Critical Area, which are central to the Department of Planning's role in promoting sustainable growth and land use technical assistance.

This multi-agency initiative is specifically tasked with coordinating state efforts (including DNR, MDE, and MDP) to protect the Chesapeake Bay and ensure sustainable development, which are the primary objectives of the Critical Area Protection Program.

The bill provides that the Critical Area Commission chair may refer matters to the Attorney General to bring legal actions against individuals who violate tree cutting or clearing regulations within the Critical Area.

The bill specifies the role of circuit courts in assessing damages for illegal tree cutting, and the Administrative Office of the Courts was identified as an information source for the fiscal note regarding judicial impact.

As the agency responsible for water quality and environmental protection, the Department of the Environment has overlapping interests in the standards governing development and habitat protection in the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council is responsible for advising the Governor on the management and restoration of the Chesapeake Bay. This bill directly updates a core program used to manage land use and water quality in the Bay's watershed.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Critical Area Commission is an executive-level regulatory body that functions as a permanent commission with administrative and regulatory duties as defined by this general agency category.

Synopsis: Repealing certain fees charged to certain banking institutions by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation; altering certain provisions relating to the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, including the purpose and administration of the Fund; altering the date by which the Commissioner may match certain investments in the Fund from June 30, 2028, to June 30, 2030; altering and providing for certain assessment offset credits for certain banking institutions and credit unions; etc.
Title: Financial Institutions - Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund and Regulation of Entities - Revisions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 131

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.

bill_summary: This bill revises the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund by expanding its purpose to include providing grants and financial assistance to consumers and businesses in low- to moderate-income tracts. It extends the authority of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to match private investments in the fund until 2030, creates a new assessment offset credit for financial institutions that offer Maryland Opportunity Accounts, and updates the definition of an emergency to include cybersecurity incidents requiring bank closures.
responsible_party: Commissioner of Financial Regulation (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: State-chartered banking institutions, credit unions, and residents and businesses located in low- to moderate-income census tracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, special fund revenues will decrease by an estimated 25000 in FY 2027, 35000 in FY 2028, and 52000 annually from FY 2029 to FY 2031 due to new assessment offset credits for financial institutions. Special fund expenditures will increase by approximately 14000 in both FY 2029 and FY 2030 to account for extended matching contributions to the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund. Additionally, the Commissioner is authorized to provide an equity capital investment of up to 2500000 from the Banking Institution and Credit Union Regulation Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Department of Labor. Its Office of Financial Regulation (OFR) is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including managing the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund, overseeing assessment offset credits, and regulating banking institutions and credit unions.

The bill explicitly designates the State Treasurer as the custodian of the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund. The Treasurer is responsible for investing the fund's money in the same manner as other State money and managing its interest earnings.

The bill specifies that the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the net interest on all State money allocated to the Maryland Community Investment Venture Fund. As the chief financial officer, the Comptroller's office manages the state's accounting systems and revenue tracking impacted by the bill's fiscal changes.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. The bill establishes a new special, nonlapsing fund and alters state revenues through assessment changes, requiring DBM oversight for the state budget process.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like the Department of Labor and enforces consumer protection laws. The bill's changes to legal definitions (e.g., 'emergency' for bank closures) and prohibitions on misrepresentation of financial entities involve the OAG's regulatory and enforcement interests.

Synopsis: Altering the day that a certain campaign finance report is due to be filed with the State Board of Elections; requiring that a certain campaign finance report cover a certain time period; and altering, from January 1 of the year of the election to July 1 of the year before the election, the earliest date on which the State Board of Elections may begin making distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund.
Title: Campaign Financing - Campaign Finance Reporting Deadline and Fair Campaign Financing Fund Distributions
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled
bill_summary: This bill modifies the reporting deadlines and coverage periods for campaign finance entities and alters the timeline for public funding distributions. It moves the annual January campaign finance report deadline from the third to the fourth Wednesday of the month and specifies the reporting period for that report. Furthermore, it allows candidates for Governor and Lieutenant Governor participating in the public financing program to begin receiving distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund on July 1 of the year preceding the election, rather than January 1 of the election year.
stakeholders: Gubernatorial and Lieutenant Governor candidates, campaign finance entities, and the Maryland State Board of Elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill does not directly affect State or local finances. While the bill shifts the earliest possible date for distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund to six months earlier, it does not change the total amount of public funding available to candidates or the overall balance of the fund (which was $10,400,000 as of October 2025).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the State Board of Elections. The agency is primarily responsible for supervising campaign finance reporting deadlines and authorizing distributions from the Fair Campaign Financing Fund.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and, according to the fiscal note, administers the Fair Campaign Financing Fund and is responsible for making the actual distributions once authorized by the State Board of Elections.
The bill directly impacts the timing of public campaign funding available to candidates for Governor, moving the earliest distribution date six months earlier.

The Fair Campaign Financing Fund provides public contributions specifically for gubernatorial tickets, which include the Lieutenant Governor. Changes to the distribution timeline directly affect these candidates.

The Office of the State Prosecutor is responsible for enforcing state election and campaign finance laws. Changes to reporting deadlines and distribution rules fall under their oversight for potential investigations or prosecutions of violations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and the General Assembly on the constitutionality and implementation of changes to election and campaign finance law.

Synopsis: Establishing competitive proof of concept procurements as an authorized procurement method; providing that a competitive proof of concept procurement may have multiple phases of evaluation; requiring a unit of State government to obtain the approval of the Chief Procurement Officer or a designee before conducting a certain competitive proof of concept procurement; altering the required contents of a competitive proof of concept procurement solicitation; etc.
Title: State Procurement - Competitive Proof of Concept Procurement
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer

bill_summary: This bill establishes competitive proof of concept procurements as an authorized source selection method for State agencies. It allows units to solicit proposals for testing, evaluating, or piloting goods, services, or technology in real-world environments and enables them to proceed to full implementation or deployment based on the results of the evaluation phases.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of General Services and the Maryland Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: State agencies and units of government, the Chief Procurement Officer, technology and service vendors, and small, minority, and veteran-owned business enterprises.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no material effect on State or local finances. While it may create operational efficiencies for agencies by streamlining the procurement pathway from testing to deployment, it does not include new spending mandates or revenue changes. The bill also includes provisions for establishing participation goals for Minority Business Enterprises and Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprises at specific phases of the procurement process.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency that requested the bill, DGS is the primary entity responsible for its implementation. The Chief Procurement Officer, located within DGS, is granted new approval authority over these procurements, and the department is tasked with adopting the necessary regulations. DGS also manages eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA), where solicitations and awards must be posted.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Information Technology approve all competitive proof of concept procurements related to IT. DoIT is also required to consult on regulations and enter into memoranda of understanding with units conducting these procurements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office is responsible for establishing guidelines for minority business enterprise (MBE) participation goals in these procurements and has the authority to grant exemptions from Small Business Reserve (SBR) designations if deemed impracticable.

The OAG is required to consult on the establishment of MBE guidelines for this procurement method. Additionally, the fiscal note indicates the OAG has already provided critical legal guidance regarding the limitations of current proof of concept laws.

As the highest administrative body for state expenditures and procurement contracts, the Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant contracts that would result from the full implementation phases authorized by this bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch units implementing this bill and houses the Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs. The Governor also serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which reviews related contracts.

As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is responsible for the oversight and approval of significant state procurement contracts, including those resulting from the expanded proof of concept method.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which must approve major state contracts and expenditures arising from the procurement processes established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This board would be responsible for adjudicating any bid protests or contract disputes that arise from the use of this new competitive proof of concept procurement method.
OLA would be responsible for auditing state agencies' compliance with the new procurement regulations and procedures established by this bill.

Synopsis: Renaming the Council on Open Data to be the Council for Open Data; altering the membership and member terms of the Council; and altering the Council's responsibilities to include advising on data initiatives and priorities and identifying and exploring ways in which partnerships may be developed and strengthened to connect Maryland data with communities and social service organizations.
Title: State Government – Council for Open Data – Membership and Responsibilities
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 104

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill renames the Council on Open Data to the Council for Open Data and reduces its membership from 37 to 11 members, designating the State Chief Data Officer as the chair. It expands the definition of data to include statistical or factual information regardless of whether it is a final version and tasks the council with advising on data initiatives and developing partnerships with community and social service organizations.
stakeholders: State and local government agencies, academic institutions, private and nonprofit sector representatives, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources, and state revenues are not affected. There is no material impact on local government operations or finances, and the bill is expected to have minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing several members of the Council (including local, private, academic, and nonprofit sector representatives) and may designate additional staff for the council's operations.

This is a departmental bill for DoIT. The State Chief Data Officer (a position within DoIT) becomes the Chair of the Council, and the department retains primary staffing and coordination responsibilities for the state's open data policy.
The Secretary of Agriculture is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The Secretary of Budget and Management is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The Secretary of Commerce is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The State Superintendent of Schools is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.

The Secretary of Planning is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The Secretary of Transportation is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The Secretary of the Environment is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The Adjutant General is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.
The Secretary of State Police is removed as a statutory member of the Council as part of the bill's streamlining of membership from 37 to 11 members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Council for Open Data is an advisory body whose structure, membership, and mandates are specifically modified by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy is removed as a statutory member of the Council.
The Governor's Homeland Security Advisor is removed as a statutory member of the Council.

The Director of the Governor's Office of Performance Improvement is removed from the Council (where they previously served as Vice Chair), and the office's shared staffing responsibilities are eliminated.
The Council is mandated to invite and encourage the judicial branch to utilize state open data portals and adopt consistent data policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of MIEMSS is removed as a statutory member of the Council.
The State Archivist is removed as a statutory member of the Council; however, the Council remains responsible for advocating for sound records management and data preservation practices.
The university is a potential source for the required council member representing the university sector.

Synopsis: Requiring buses operating on fixed local routes funded by a county or municipal corporation and operated by a county or municipal corporation or a contractor for a county or municipal corporation to allow passengers to embark and disembark at the entrance of early voting centers located within one-half mile of the route.
Title: Election Law - Early Voting Centers - Bus Stops
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 106

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: The bill requires buses on fixed local routes funded and operated by a county or municipality to allow passengers to embark and disembark at the entrance of early voting centers if the center is within one-half mile of the route. This requirement applies during early voting days and must be implemented to the maximum extent practicable and consistent with accessibility requirements. Express, commuter, Maryland Transit Administration, and Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority routes are specifically exempt.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and local government transit agencies
stakeholders: Maryland voters, local governments, municipal corporations, and contracted bus operators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct impact on State finances. Local government expenditures are expected to increase beginning in fiscal 2028 due to route deviations, communication costs, and temporary signage. While total impact is indeterminate, Prince George's County estimates an expenditure increase of at least $37,300 in fiscal 2028. Potential increases in fare revenue may partially offset costs in some jurisdictions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for supervising and administering elections in Maryland, the State Board of Elections requested this departmental bill and is responsible for implementing early voting procedures and informing the public about center locations.

Although the bill specifically excludes the Maryland Transit Administration, MDOT remains the state's lead agency for transportation policy and coordination. The bill directly impacts local transit systems which MDOT interacts with and supports.

The bill mandates that bus stops at early voting centers must be consistent with accessibility requirements, which falls under the department's mission to coordinate inclusive services and accessible transportation for residents with disabilities.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The State Board of Elections is an executive entity that submitted this departmental request under the Governor's administration.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and would be responsible for advising on the interpretation of the bill's requirements and compliance with accessibility laws.
DGS manages and maintains state-owned facilities, some of which are used as early voting centers and would be the destination for the required bus stop deviations.
DBM oversees the fiscal and personnel management of the state agencies involved in implementing or advising on this law.

Public schools are frequently used as early voting centers; therefore, changes to bus access at these facilities during election periods are relevant to the department's oversight of local school systems.
Certain judicial facilities serve as early voting centers. The requirement for buses to stop at the entrance of these centers impacts facility access managed by the Judiciary.
The Secretary of State is the custodian of official state records and is responsible for processing acts and laws passed by the General Assembly.

The Department of Planning coordinates sustainable growth and infrastructure through initiatives like 'Smart, Green & Growing,' which includes enhancing public transportation access and land use planning.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Various advisory bodies related to civil rights, disabilities, or elections may be involved in studying or providing recommendations regarding the implementation and impact of this legislation.

Synopsis: Limiting the personal information that may be collected, maintained, processed, and retained by units of State government under certain circumstances; requiring certain personal information to be deleted or de-identified under certain circumstances; requiring each unit to post a certain privacy notice on its Internet website and establishing certain requirements for privacy notices and privacy policies; requiring each unit of State government to designate a Privacy Officer; etc.
Title: Maryland Data Privacy and Protection Act of 2026
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Biometrics -see also- Artificial Intelli; Identif; Fingerprt
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The Maryland Data Privacy and Protection Act of 2026 regulates how units of the Maryland State government collect, process, and retain personal information. It mandates data minimization, requires each unit to designate a Privacy Officer and post privacy notices, and directs the Department of Information Technology to establish privacy and security standards for third-party IT contracts involving personal data.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Information Technology (DoIT) and individual units of State government
stakeholders: Maryland residents, State government agencies, and third-party information technology contractors
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to be implemented within the existing resources of most State agencies, though some departments, such as the Comptroller's Office and the Maryland Department of Transportation, may experience an increase in expenditures related to additional staffing needs. The bill is not expected to affect State revenues or materially impact local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, DoIT is tasked with establishing privacy guidelines and standards, adopting regulations and model templates for all units of State government, and overseeing basic security and privacy requirements in state contracts.
The bill requires individual agency Privacy Officers to coordinate with the Office of the Attorney General to ensure compliance with the new privacy and data protection mandates.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is responsible for adopting regulations that exempt specific personal records from certain requirements under the bill, based on the recommendation of the Secretary of Information Technology.

The fiscal note specifically identifies the Comptroller's Office as an agency that may experience a significant fiscal impact and increased workload, as it was not previously subject to similar executive privacy orders.

State units that maintain personal records are required by this legislation (through existing referenced statutes) to submit annual reports regarding those record sets to the Secretary of General Services.
The fiscal note identifies the Department of Transportation as an agency that anticipates an increased staff workload to comply with the bill's data minimization and reporting requirements.
The fiscal note specifically lists the Department of Disabilities as an agency that anticipates an increased workload and potential fiscal impact due to the new data privacy mandates.

The bill codifies and expands upon privacy mandates previously established by Executive Order within the Governor's Office, and the Governor's Office oversees the executive branch units required to appoint Privacy Officers.

While the Judicial Branch is exempt from certain annual reporting requirements, the fiscal note indicates the Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted and the bill interacts with the Public Information Act which affects judicial records.

The bill specifically identifies records deposited in the Maryland Hall of Records (managed by the Archives) as being exempt from certain personal record requirements under the Public Information Act.

SponsorPrimary: Chair, Government, Labor, and Elections Committee

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person for the Address Confidentiality Program; and providing the contact person acts as the contact for inquiries about the Program from local boards of elections and Program participants on matters related to the implementation of the Address Confidentiality Program.
Title: State Board of Elections - Address Confidentiality Program - Designation of Contact Person
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 108

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person to handle inquiries from Address Confidentiality Program participants and local boards of elections. It also clarifies that local boards of elections must use a program participant's actual address for all election-related purposes, including absentee ballots.
stakeholders: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, harassment, or human trafficking who participate in the Address Confidentiality Program; local boards of elections; and the State Board of Elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Elections can designate a contact person and establish regulations using existing resources, and there is no effect on State revenues. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically requires the State Board of Elections to designate a contact person to handle inquiries from program participants and local boards of elections. It also authorizes the agency to adopt regulations to implement address confidentiality procedures within the state's election systems.

The Secretary of State administers the Address Confidentiality Program. This departmental bill was introduced at the request of the Secretary of State to improve interagency coordination and ensure participants receive timely responses to election-related inquiries.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for the State Board of Elections and the Secretary of State. The agency would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the implementation of the bill and the review of the new regulations authorized under the act.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Information Technology Investment Fund, at the discretion of the Secretary of Information Technology, to be used to support State-owned communication sites, communication facilities, and telecommunications equipment used in connection with certain technology agreements; and requiring, by January 15 each year, the Secretary to submit a report to the General Assembly specifying the amount of money paid into the Fund that was allocated to certain programs.
Title: Department of Information Technology – Information Technology Investment Fund – Uses
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.

bill_summary: The bill authorizes revenues from Resource Sharing Agreements (RSAs) within the Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF) to be used, at the discretion of the Secretary of Information Technology, to support State-owned communication sites, facilities, and telecommunications equipment. It also requires the Secretary to submit an annual report to the General Assembly specifying how these funds were allocated.
stakeholders: Department of Information Technology, State agencies utilizing communication infrastructure, and private companies involved in telecommunications resource sharing agreements.
fiscal_impact_summary: Expanding the authorized use of Resource Sharing Agreement (RSA) revenues does not affect overall State revenues or expenditures, although the distribution of funds within the Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF) may change between fiscal 2027 and 2031. For context, RSA revenues to the ITIF totaled $790,534 in fiscal 2025. The Department of Information Technology can fulfill the bill's reporting requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) is the primary agency affected by this bill, as it was introduced at their request. The bill grants the Secretary of Information Technology discretionary authority over the use of the Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF) and imposes new annual reporting requirements on the agency.

The Board of Public Works is responsible for approving Resource Sharing Agreements (RSAs). Since the bill expands the authorized uses of revenues specifically generated from these RSAs within the Information Technology Investment Fund, the Board's oversight of the underlying agreements is directly linked to the bill's implementation.

The bill explicitly mentions the Statewide Public Safety Interoperability Radio System (Maryland First). The Maryland State Police is a primary user and stakeholder of this communication infrastructure, which is supported by the Information Technology Investment Fund.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the development and execution of the state budget, including the management and allocation of state funds like the Information Technology Investment Fund.

MDOT manages significant state rights-of-way and infrastructure often used in Resource Sharing Agreements. The bill's provisions regarding state-owned communication sites and facilities used in RSAs impact MDOT's assets and coordination with DoIT.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Information Technology. The Secretary of IT, who is granted discretionary authority by this bill, serves at the pleasure of the Governor.

The Comptroller, as a member of the Board of Public Works and the state's chief financial officer, has a role in approving the Resource Sharing Agreements that generate the fund's revenue and oversees state revenue collection.
The Treasurer manages state funds and serves on the Board of Public Works, which approves the Resource Sharing Agreements mentioned in the bill and fiscal note.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including DoIT, and would be responsible for reviewing the legality and form of the expanded uses of the Information Technology Investment Fund and the associated Resource Sharing Agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is identified as a stakeholder in the fiscal note and relies on the statewide public safety radio systems supported by the fund for emergency medical communications.

DHCD is identified as an information source in the fiscal note, likely due to its role in community infrastructure and potential overlaps with state-owned communication facilities in community development projects.

OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance audits of executive branch agencies. The expansion of authorized uses for a state fund and the new reporting requirements for the Secretary of IT would fall under their auditing purview.

DGS manages state-owned facilities and real estate. The bill's focus on state-owned communication sites and facilities may involve DGS in terms of facilities management, leasing, or maintenance coordination.

Synopsis: Altering the manner in which the chair of a campaign finance entity is appointed; providing that the treasurer is the financial steward of a campaign finance entity; altering requirements for assets received by or on behalf of a campaign finance entity and disbursements made by or on behalf of a campaign finance entity; repealing the authority of the chair of a campaign finance entity to approve a disbursement on behalf of the campaign finance entity under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Election Law - Campaign Finance Entities - Oversight and Control of Campaign Funds
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill designates the treasurer as the financial steward of a campaign finance entity and authorizes them to appoint agents to handle disbursements. It prohibits candidates from accessing or making disbursements from campaign accounts, updates procedures for appointing campaign managers, and establishes civil penalties for unauthorized financial activities and failures to report compensation agreements.
stakeholders: Political candidates, campaign treasurers, campaign managers, campaign finance entities, and authorized agents of campaign committees.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund revenues for the Fair Campaign Financing Fund may increase starting in fiscal 2027 due to new civil penalties. Certain violations, such as making disbursements without proper written designation of an authorized agent, are subject to a penalty of $1,000 plus the amount of the disbursement. The total revenue increase cannot be reliably estimated. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of campaign finance in Maryland, SBE is responsible for implementing the bill's requirements, including the oversight of campaign managers, the registration of authorized agents, and the collection of increased civil penalties. The bill was requested as departmental legislation by SBE.

The OSP is tasked with investigating and prosecuting offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process and election laws. The bill's changes to the fiduciary duties of campaign agents and restrictions on candidate access to funds provide new legal parameters for enforcement and investigation into financial misconduct.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and represents the state in civil and criminal matters. They would be involved in interpreting the new fiduciary duty requirements and defending the imposition of the new civil penalty structure.

OLA conducts fiscal and performance audits of state agencies, including the State Board of Elections. New financial stewardship roles and penalty mechanisms introduced by this bill would be subject to OLA's review during periodic audits of SBE's operations.

OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases. They would likely handle appeals regarding civil penalties imposed by the State Board of Elections for violations of the bill's campaign finance management requirements.

The State Treasurer's Office acts as the custodian of state funds. They are responsible for managing the Fair Campaign Financing Fund, which receives revenues from the civil penalties modified by this bill.
As the state's principal revenue collector, the Comptroller is involved in the overall accounting and receipt of state funds, including penalties collected for violations of campaign finance law.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the State Board of Elections. Additionally, the bill impacts the regulation of gubernatorial campaign finance entities used by the Governor and Lieutenant Governor.

The office is tasked with creating a statewide data strategy, establishing data governance and literacy programs, and maintaining a state data inventory. Additionally, the bill mandates that each principal State department appoint an Agency Data Officer to manage departmental data quality, privacy, and sharing in collaboration with the State Chief Data Officer.

GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies to oversee state government operations. The establishment of statewide data standards and interoperability will directly support and impact their performance metrics and accountability goals.

As the state's central repository for linked education and workforce data, MLDS will be heavily impacted by the data governance, de-identification standards, and interoperability guidelines established by the new State Chief Data Officer.
The OAG will likely provide legal guidance on the development of data privacy, sharing agreements, and de-identification standards required by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Administrative Office of the Courts or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland to administer and implement certain provisions of law relating to financial disclosure statements for State officials of the Judicial Branch and candidates to be a State official of the Judicial Branch and maintain and make available to the public the records and statements of State officials of the Judicial Branch and candidates to be a State official of the Judicial Branch; etc.

bill_summary: This bill transfers the responsibility for administering and maintaining financial disclosure statements for State officials and candidates of the Judicial Branch from the State Ethics Commission to the Administrative Office of the Courts or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland. It also repeals the requirement that the Supreme Court transmit copies of these statements to the State Ethics Commission.
responsible_party: Administrative Office of the Courts or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland
stakeholders: State officials of the Judicial Branch (including judges, magistrates, and commissioners), candidates for judicial office, and the public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the fiscal note, the Judiciary and the State Ethics Commission can implement the requirements using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) or another body designated by the Supreme Court of Maryland must administer and implement financial disclosure requirements for judicial officials and candidates, which includes maintaining records and making them available for public inspection.

This departmental bill was requested by the State Ethics Commission to remove its requirement to receive and maintain copies of financial disclosure statements from the Judicial Branch, thereby reducing its administrative burden and clarifying that ethics administration for the Judiciary resides within that branch.

Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Veterans and Military Families, Department of

bill_summary: The Military Family Inclusion Act updates the membership of several Maryland state boards and commissions—specifically the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust, the Maryland Veterans Commission, and the Maryland Youth Advisory Council—to include representatives for military families and caregivers of service-disabled veterans. The bill also establishes specific criteria and procedures for the removal of organizations or representative seats from the Maryland Veterans Commission.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Military families, service-disabled veterans, family caregivers of veterans, and youth from military families.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, altering the composition of the specified entities does not materially affect State government operations or finances. There is no local fiscal impact and minimal to no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by DVMF. The agency is responsible for staffing the Maryland Veterans Commission and the Maryland Veterans Trust, both of which have their membership and governance structures altered by the bill. The Secretary of DVMF also serves as the chair of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary purpose is to alter the membership and operational rules of several state bodies, including the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, the Maryland Veterans Commission, and the Maryland Youth Advisory Council.

DHS staffs the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which is expanded by this bill to include a family caregiver of a service-disabled veteran. Additionally, the Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex officio member of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees.

The Governor's Office for Children appoints members to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council. The bill adds a new requirement for the office to appoint a youth who has an immediate family member who is a service member.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, the Maryland Veterans Commission, the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees, and the Maryland Youth Advisory Council.
The Office of Appointments will be responsible for recruiting and vetting the new members added to various commissions and boards by this legislation on behalf of the Governor.
The Adjutant General is an ex officio member of the Board of Trustees for the Maryland Veterans Trust, which has its quorum and governance rules updated by this bill.

The Secretary of Aging is an ex officio member of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees and the department is represented on the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, both of which are affected by this bill.

The Secretary of Health is an ex officio member of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees and the department is represented on the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, both of which are affected by this bill.
The Secretary of Labor is an ex officio member of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees, which is affected by the bill's changes to board governance.

The Secretary of Disabilities is an ex officio member of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees and the department is represented on the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, both of which are affected by this bill.
The Student Advisory Council to the Maryland Higher Education Commission nominates members to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council, which is expanded by this bill.
The USM Student Council nominates members to the Maryland Youth Advisory Council, which is expanded by this bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing the approval of certain contract modifications to State contracts if the modification does not materially change the scope of the work and does not increase the contract by more than a certain amount; altering the definition of "contract modification" for certain State procurements; and requiring a procurement officer to document certain contract modifications.
Title: State Procurement - Streamlining Contract Modifications
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Government, Labor, and Elections; Withdrawn
bill_summary: The bill streamlines State procurement by authorizing procurement officers and department heads to approve contract modifications that do not materially alter the scope of work, provided the cost increase remains within specific thresholds related to small procurement limits. It also updates the legal definition of 'contract modification' and requires documentation of such changes in the official procurement file.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of General Services, the Chief Procurement Officer, and heads of primary procurement units
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies, procurement officers, and private contractors holding State contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill modifies administrative approval thresholds for State contract modifications. A formal Fiscal Note with specific revenue or expenditure estimates is not included in the provided text. The financial impact is limited to the procedural streamlining of modifications within thresholds linked to small procurement limits, though specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a primary procurement unit and the agency that requested the bill, DGS is the principal implementer. The Secretary of DGS typically serves as the Chief Procurement Officer, who is granted specific authority under this bill to approve contract modifications up to five times the small procurement threshold.

The Board of Public Works oversees all significant state procurements and expenditures. This bill streamlines the approval process for contract modifications, impacting the volume and type of contract changes that require higher-level executive oversight or adherence to Board-established regulations.

MDOT is a primary procurement unit with significant independent contracting authority. The bill's provisions regarding the head of a primary procurement unit's ability to approve larger contract modifications directly impact MDOT's operational efficiency and internal procurement procedures.

DBM is a primary procurement unit responsible for state personnel and service contracts. The bill grants DBM's head authority to approve contract modifications without higher-level intervention if they meet specific fiscal and scope criteria.

DoIT is a primary procurement unit for the state's IT goods and services. The bill's streamlining of contract modifications directly applies to DoIT's procurement officers and leadership in managing technology contracts.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies on procurement law and contract interpretation. They would be responsible for advising agencies on the redefined 'contract modification' and ensuring that approvals comply with the new statutory limits.

The bill mandates that procurement officers document contract modifications in the procurement file. OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of these files to ensure state agencies are adhering to procurement laws and proper documentation standards.

The State Treasurer's Office is designated as a primary procurement unit under the State Finance and Procurement Article and is a member of the Board of Public Works, giving it both direct operational and oversight interest in procurement streamlining.

USM is a primary procurement unit with delegated authority. The changes to contract modification procedures and approval thresholds apply to the system's various institutions and procurement officers.
As a primary procurement unit, Morgan State University's procurement officers and leadership gain the modified approval authorities granted by the bill for their institutional contracts.
As a designated primary procurement unit, the college is directly impacted by changes to the approval process and documentation requirements for state contract modifications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MSBCA adjudicates contract disputes. Changes to the definition of 'contract modification' and the authorized approval process may affect the resolution of legal disputes regarding contract performance and changes.

The Comptroller serves on the Board of Public Works and oversees state payments. While not a primary procurement unit, the agency monitors contract expenditures and the fiscal integrity of the state's procurement system.

Synopsis: Altering the type of toilet that certain food establishments may use to comply with the requirement to provide a convenient lavatory; requiring that the fee for an on-farm food service facility license be determined by the Maryland Department of Health based on certain factors and prohibiting the fee from exceeding $100; establishing a 1-year term for an on-farm service facility license; and requiring the Department, in consultation with other departments and stakeholders, to adopt regulations governing on-farm service facility licenses.
Title: Food Establishments - Lavatory Requirement and On-Farm Food Service Facility License
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: The bill updates the regulatory and licensing framework for food establishments located on farms. It permits agritourism businesses, wineries, and farm breweries to use various types of portable toilets, including water-based flush models, to meet lavatory requirements. Furthermore, it establishes a one-year license for on-farm food service facilities, replacing the previous 30-day limit, and caps the license fee at $100 while requiring the Maryland Department of Health to adopt specific health and safety regulations for these operations.
stakeholders: On-farm business owners, agritourism operators, Class 4 limited wineries, Class 8 farm breweries, and local health department inspectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are expected to increase minimally, estimated at approximately $5,000 annually starting in FY 2027, based on an estimate of 50 facilities paying a maximum $100 license fee. Local health departments are expected to handle additional inspection and enforcement responsibilities using existing resources, although local officials note that the $100 fee cap may not fully cover all administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for determining the on-farm food service facility license fee, adopting regulations regarding food preparation and sanitation, and overseeing the licensing and regulation of these facilities.

The bill explicitly requires MDH to consult with the Department of Agriculture when adopting regulations for on-farm food service facility licenses, as the bill directly impacts farm operations and agritourism.

The bill explicitly requires MDH to consult with the Department of the Environment when adopting regulations, particularly concerning wastewater management, water access, and the placement of toilets near wells.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MDH in the drafting and implementation of the new regulations required by the bill and ensures compliance with existing state health and administrative laws.

Synopsis: Altering the effective dates of enrollment in a Small Business Health Options (SHOP) Exchange plan for individuals who enroll during certain special enrollment periods.
Title: Health Insurance – Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) Enrollment – Effective Dates
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 137

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: This bill aligns Maryland law with federal regulations by updating the effective dates for health insurance coverage enrollment through the Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) during special enrollment periods. It ensures that for individuals enrolling during these periods, coverage typically begins on the first day of the month following their plan selection, removing previous delays for selections made late in a month.
stakeholders: Small employers with 1 to 50 employees and their eligible employees and dependents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, the bill codifies existing practices that already align with federal regulations. The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange currently operates the SHOP platform in accordance with these standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the requesting agency and the primary regulator of the state's insurance market, the Maryland Insurance Administration is directly responsible for enforcing the provisions of the bill and ensuring that health insurance laws regarding SHOP enrollment effective dates align with federal regulations.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange administers the Maryland Health Connection, which includes the Small Business Health Options Program (SHOP) platform directly affected by this legislation's changes to enrollment effective dates.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, assisting in the interpretation and implementation of these statutory changes to ensure compliance with federal law.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, and coordinates the policy initiatives and departmental legislation that includes this bill.

Synopsis: Continuing the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists, in accordance with the provisions of the Maryland Program Evaluation Act (sunset law), by extending to July 1, 2032, the termination provisions relating to the statutory and regulatory authority of the Board.
Title: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists - Sunset Extension
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 135

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the statutory and regulatory authority of the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists by five years, moving the board's termination date from July 1, 2027, to July 1, 2032.
responsible_party: State Board of Environmental Health Specialists
stakeholders: Licensed environmental health specialists and the Maryland Department of Health
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill maintains State special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists through fiscal 2032. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Environmental Health Specialists is a regulatory unit housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill is a departmental request from MDH to extend the board's statutory and regulatory authority.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel. The bill maintains special fund revenues and expenditures for the board through FY 2032, requiring DBM to continue oversight of the board's fiscal execution and state employee positions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Maryland Department of Health and its boards. The Governor is responsible for signing the legislation and for the final appointment of members to the State Board of Environmental Health Specialists.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards. Continuing the Board of Environmental Health Specialists ensures the office will remain responsible for recommending individuals to fill its nine board member seats.
The OAG provides primary legal counsel to all state boards and commissions, including representing the Board of Environmental Health Specialists in legal matters and disciplinary proceedings.

The OAH provides an impartial hearing process for contested cases involving state agencies. If the Board of Environmental Health Specialists takes disciplinary action against a licensee, the contested case would likely be adjudicated by the OAH.

While the board is located in the Department of Health, the professionals it licenses (environmental health specialists) are critical to the environmental monitoring and enforcement missions described in the summary for the Maryland Department of the Environment.

Synopsis: Requiring a carrier that issues Medicare supplement policies to issue a Medicare supplement policy to an individual who meets certain criteria during certain special enrollment periods.
Title: Medicare Supplement Policies - Issuance - Requirements
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 139

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: This bill requires insurance carriers that offer Medicare supplement policies in Maryland to issue those policies to eligible individuals during two new 63-day special enrollment periods. The first period applies to individuals who lose coverage under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) after having been enrolled in Medicare Part B for at least six months. The second applies to individuals who became eligible for Medicare before 2020 and qualify for a federal guaranteed issue right. During these periods, carriers are prohibited from denying coverage or discriminating in pricing based on an applicant's health status or medical history.
stakeholders: Medicare-eligible individuals, particularly those losing Medicaid coverage or those eligible for Medicare prior to 2020, and insurance carriers that issue Medicare supplement policies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's impact on the state is minimal, as any additional workload for the Maryland Insurance Administration can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on state revenues or local government finances. The bill is also determined to have minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary agency responsible for regulating insurance carriers and enforcing the provisions of the Insurance Article. This is a departmental bill requested by the MIA, and the Insurance Commissioner is specifically tasked with adopting regulations to implement the bill.

The bill creates a special enrollment period for individuals transitioning out of the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health. The department will be responsible for providing the necessary documentation of termination or disenrollment required by applicants.

The Department of Aging supports older adults who are the primary users of Medicare and Medicare supplement policies. The bill directly affects the ability of this demographic to access supplemental insurance during specific life transitions.

The bill and existing law sections being amended address Medicare eligibility due to disability for individuals under age 65. The Department of Disabilities coordinates services for these residents and is impacted by changes to their health insurance access.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the legal representative for the state and provides counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration regarding the interpretation, implementation, and enforcement of new insurance laws.

Synopsis: Altering the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program, including by establishing requirements regarding an automated external defibrillator (AED) coordinator, repealing certain provisions of law regarding regional council AED committees, and exempting certain law enforcement agencies from being required to obtain a certificate for an AED deployed in a patrol vehicle of the law enforcement agency; establishing certain certification qualifications for grocery stores and restaurants under the Program; etc.
Title: State Emergency Medical Services Board - Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program - Revisions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 91

Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator (AED) Program by establishing the role and requirements for an AED coordinator, clarifying certification rules for entities including grocery stores and restaurants, and exempting law enforcement patrol vehicles from certification requirements. It also repeals obsolete provisions related to regional council AED committees and streamlines program reporting and administration.
responsible_party: Maryland State Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Board and the Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems (MIEMSS)
stakeholders: Businesses, associations, and government agencies participating in the AED program; grocery stores and restaurants; law enforcement agencies; and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact as the changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances. The Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems also determined that the bill has minimal or no impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS is the primary state agency responsible for administering the Public Access Automated External Defibrillator Program. This departmental bill was introduced at their request and grants the EMS Board (administered by MIEMSS) new oversight authorities, including the ability to adopt regulations and delegate power to the Institute.

The bill amends Section 21-330.3 of the Health-General Article to update AED requirements for grocery stores and restaurants. As the department responsible for public health services and the regulation of health care facilities and food service providers, MDH is impacted by the shift in certification and maintenance standards for these businesses.

The bill specifically exempts law enforcement agencies from being required to obtain a certificate for AEDs deployed in patrol vehicles. As the state's primary law enforcement agency, this reduces administrative requirements for the Maryland State Police.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for state agencies and boards. The bill alters statutory civil immunity provisions for entities and individuals providing AED services, which requires legal guidance and potential representation from the OAG regarding liability issues.

DGS manages state-owned facilities and oversees the Maryland Capitol Police. The bill impacts DGS via the law enforcement vehicle certification exemption for its police force and references requirements for public buildings to maintain AEDs and naloxone.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education focused on school safety, MCSS provides coordination and training for safety programs. Changes to AED program requirements, including coordinator duties and training standards, affect safety protocols in schools which MCSS oversees.

Public library systems are required by law to maintain AEDs and comply with the Public Access AED Program. Updates to the program's requirements for registration, maintenance, and coordination directly impact the operations and compliance of the state library network.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals specific statutory provisions related to Regional Council AED committees, which functioned as advisory bodies for the program.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Maryland Insurance Commissioner's enforcement authority over third-party administrators (TPAs). It authorizes the Commissioner to deny, revoke, or suspend a TPA's registration and impose civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation for breaches of any Maryland insurance law or regulation, rather than limiting enforcement to the specific subtitle governing TPAs.
stakeholders: Third-party administrators (TPAs), insurance companies, plan sponsors, and plan beneficiaries.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State revenues or expenditures. The Maryland Insurance Administration can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is the primary agency responsible for the bill's implementation. The bill was introduced as a departmental request from the MIA and directly expands the enforcement and regulatory authority of the Maryland Insurance Commissioner, who heads the agency.

Enforcement actions taken by the Insurance Commissioner, such as the denial, suspension, or revocation of a registration, are subject to the hearing provisions of the Insurance Article. The Office of Administrative Hearings is the central panel responsible for adjudicating such contested cases and regulatory disputes.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative and counsel for all state agencies, including the Maryland Insurance Administration. It would provide legal support for the expanded enforcement actions authorized by the bill and represent the state in any subsequent appeals in court.

The Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (IWIF) specifically serves as the third-party administrator (TPA) for workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees. Because the bill alters the registration standards and enforcement penalties for all TPAs, IWIF is directly impacted as a regulated entity under this framework.

Synopsis: Requiring the Secretary of Aging to lead implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan which is a multisector plan on aging that transforms programs, services, policies, institutions, and systems to address the growing population of older adults in the State; requiring the Department to maintain a publicly accessible resource on the Department's website for monitoring implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan; and requiring the Department of Aging to staff the Commission on Aging.

bill_summary: The bill codifies the Longevity Ready Maryland (LRM) Plan and requires the Secretary of Aging to lead its implementation with goals focusing on economic opportunity, health, wellness, mobility, and building a longevity ecosystem. It updates the duties of the Secretary to include evaluating the needs of older adults, advocating for policy changes, and maintaining a public resource for monitoring the plan's progress. Additionally, the bill reforms the membership and duties of the Commission on Aging, requiring it to advise on the LRM Plan and ensuring its membership reflects the state's diversity.
stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, family caregivers, Area Agencies on Aging, and State and local government units involved in aging services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact as it generally codifies existing policies and procedures established by Executive Order 01.01.2024.01. The Maryland Department of Aging provides staff for the Commission on Aging within existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Aging is responsible for leading the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan, staffing the Commission on Aging, and conducting extensive reporting and policy advocacy for older adults.

The bill codifies an initiative established by Executive Order and requires the Secretary of Aging, a member of the Governor's Executive Council, to report annually to the Governor on implementation progress and policy recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly alters the membership, duties, and operational requirements of the Commission on Aging, a permanent advisory body within the executive branch.
One of the core pillars of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan is 'optimizing health, wellness, and mobility.' Additionally, the Commission on Aging must include an expert in health care.
The plan's goal to 'promote economic opportunity' specifically targets older adults in the workforce, and the bill requires cross-sector collaboration on employment policies for the aging population.
The bill's goals include promoting economic opportunity and addressing the 'longevity ecosystem,' which MDoA notes will have a meaningful impact on small businesses and the state's GDP.
The Longevity Ready Maryland Plan includes 'optimizing mobility' as a primary goal, which directly intersects with MDOT's mission to manage the state's transit and infrastructure systems.

The bill amends the Human Services Article of the Maryland Code and requires coordination of programs related to the well-being and independence of older adults, which often overlaps with DHS social service programs.
The bill specifically mandates that the Governor appoint 'one veteran with a demonstrated interest in the implementation of the Longevity Ready Maryland Plan' to the Commission on Aging.

The LRM Plan is required to address the growing population of older adults, including those with different abilities, and the Commission's membership is intended to reflect the diversity of the disability community.
