Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from knowingly making or using, or causing to be made or used, a false record or statement resulting in underpayments of unemployment insurance contributions or payment of unemployment insurance benefits of more than $15,000 in a calendar year; altering the enforcement mechanisms related to workplace fraud laws, living wage laws, and prevailing wage laws, including authorizing the Attorney General to investigate and bring suit in a certain manner; etc.
Title: Fraud Prevention, Prevailing Wage, and Living Wage - Prohibitions, Penalties, and Enforcement
Status: In the Senate - Second Reading Passed with Amendments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill enhances the enforcement of Maryland's workplace fraud, prevailing wage, and living wage laws by authorizing the Attorney General to investigate and bring civil suits and establishing joint and several liability for general contractors for violations committed by their subcontractors. It requires the Maryland Department of Labor to notify licensing authorities to suspend or revoke professional licenses for certain labor law violations and mandates that one-third of specific civil penalties be paid directly to affected employees. Additionally, the bill requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to develop training programs and form language for contractors regarding these labor requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Commissioner of Labor and Industry) and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Maryland employees, general contractors, subcontractors, and professional licensees under the Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund expenditures increase by $110,800 in fiscal 2027 for the Office of the Attorney General to hire one additional assistant Attorney General to handle increased investigations and litigation. These costs are projected to grow to $150,500 by fiscal 2031. State general fund and Unemployment Insurance Trust Fund revenues, as well as local income tax revenues, may increase minimally due to higher compliance and penalty collections, although a reliable estimate for these increases is not available.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Commissioner of Labor and Industry as the primary implementing authority, responsible for investigating violations, issuing citations, developing training programs, and coordinating with other state agencies on workplace fraud and wage law enforcement. Additionally, the department's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing is required to suspend or revoke licenses based on violations.

The bill significantly expands the Attorney General's authority to investigate and prosecute workplace fraud, prevailing wage, and living wage violations. It requires monthly coordination meetings with the Labor Commissioner and includes a fiscal impact for additional legal staff to handle the increased caseload.

The bill mandates that the Commissioner of Labor and Industry delegate hearing authority to the Office of Administrative Hearings for citations and proposed penalties related to workplace fraud, ensuring a formalized adjudicatory process for contested violations.

The bill expands the right of individuals and the state to bring civil actions for economic damages, restitution, and penalties in circuit courts, and allows for judicial review of final administrative orders regarding workplace fraud.

The Comptroller is explicitly named as a coordinating agency required to share information regarding suspected worker misclassification and is identified as an entity that may issue final orders for restitution in related tax and labor compliance cases.

As a major 'public body' that contracts for construction services, MDOT is directly impacted by provisions regarding joint and several liability for general contractors and is required to withhold payments from employers cited for knowing violations of the Workplace Fraud Act.

As the state's central procurement authority and a public body contracting for construction, DGS must implement the bill's requirements for withholding contract payments from violators and managing potential debarment impacts related to wage and fraud violations.
DBM is named as a state agency required to cooperate and share information concerning suspected failures to properly classify individuals as employees, assisting in statewide enforcement efforts.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state contracts and procurement policies that are impacted by the bill's changes to prevailing wage, living wage, and workplace fraud enforcement mechanisms.
The agency is required to share information and coordinate with the Department of Labor regarding suspected misclassification and may issue related orders for compliance with insurance requirements.
The Commission is identified as a coordinating body for information sharing and is authorized to issue orders for restitution and compliance in cases involving employee misclassification.
The Secretary of State is included in the list of agencies required to cooperate and share information regarding the suspected failure to properly classify individuals as employees.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments implementing the bill and coordinates policy initiatives such as the Joint Enforcement Task Force on Workplace Fraud, which is reinforced by the bill's interagency cooperation requirements.

Synopsis: Exempting certain contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade from certain prohibitions on the provisions that may be included in State contracts.
Title: State Contracts - Prohibited Provisions - Exemptions
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill exempts certain contracts entered into by the Office of International Trade within the Maryland Department of Commerce from specific legal prohibitions on state contract provisions, such as requirements for indemnity, binding arbitration, and out-of-state legal venues, to facilitate international business development activities.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of International Trade
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Commerce, Office of International Trade, and international business entities engaging in trade opportunities with the State.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact as it codifies existing practices within the Office of International Trade.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for the bill (requested by the department), the Department of Commerce's Office of International Trade is the direct beneficiary of the exemption to include specific provisions in its international business development contracts.

The bill impacts legal standards for state contracts, specifically terms regarding indemnification, arbitration, and legal counsel. The OAG serves as the state's chief legal officer and is responsible for reviewing contracts for legal sufficiency and representing the state in disputes.

DGS is the central procurement authority for Maryland. Changes to the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding contract provisions and exemptions directly affect the department's role in setting and overseeing state procurement policy.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state contracts and expenditures. This bill alters the legal requirements for contracts involving international trade that may come before the Board for approval.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency adjudicates disputes between the state and contractors. The bill's exemption of certain international contracts from prohibitions on binding arbitration and venue selection directly impacts how legal disagreements involving these contracts are resolved.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and procurement policies that ensure fiscal efficiency, and it is frequently consulted on legislation affecting state finance and procurement law.

Housed within the Secretary of State's office, this division coordinates the state's international engagement. The bill facilitates international business activities, which aligns with and affects the broader international engagement strategy managed by this division.

The Secretary of State coordinates international affairs and diplomatic liaisons for Maryland. While the bill specifically targets the Department of Commerce, the subject matter overlaps with the Secretary's role in managing international relationships and state records.

The Treasurer manages the state's insurance protection and financial liabilities. Exempting contracts from prohibitions on indemnification and liability limits potentially affects the state's financial risk profile managed by this office.

As a member of the Board of Public Works and the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees state expenditures and contract compliance, including those impacted by changes to procurement standards.

Synopsis: Providing for command and control of State active duty personnel during mobilizations of the Maryland National Guard.
Title: Maryland Military Department – Supervision of State Active Duty Personnel
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 96

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that during State active duty, all members of the Maryland Military Department, including the National Guard and the Maryland Defense Force, are under the operational command and control of the Adjutant General or a designated National Guard officer, regardless of whether the Adjutant General or designee is in State active duty or in a federal status where the Governor remains the Commander in Chief.
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard, the Maryland Defense Force, and State operations personnel within the Maryland Military Department.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, the legislation codifies existing practice regarding the chain of command during state active duty mobilizations to ensure operational effectiveness.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General is the primary official whose command and control authority is established and clarified by this bill during State active duty mobilizations.

The bill directly impacts the command structure of the Maryland National Guard and the Maryland Defense Force during State active duty operations, ensuring they remain under the operational control of the Adjutant General.

The Governor is the Commander-in-Chief of Maryland's military forces. The bill clarifies command authority during situations where the Governor is the commander-in-chief and the Adjutant General is in a federal status.
The bill reenacts provisions that allow the ranking military officer on State active duty to direct and control the Department of State Police during specific exigencies and public crises.
MDEM is the principal agency for coordinating disaster response, which is the primary scenario where the militia is ordered into State active duty under the command structures defined in this bill.
This office advises the Governor on public safety and disaster readiness; the clarification of military command and control during state emergencies is relevant to their strategic oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Transportation Authority to design and locate the entrances, exits, and associated roads of the new bridge over the Patapsco River that will replace the collapsed Francis Scott Key Bridge to ensure that a vehicle that will not cross the bridge is not required to pay a toll.
Title: Maryland Transportation Authority - Patapsco River Toll Bridge - Design
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Transportation Authority to design the entrances, exits, and associated roads of the new bridge replacing the Francis Scott Key Bridge to ensure that vehicles not crossing the bridge are not charged a toll.
stakeholders: Motorists using roads near the new Patapsco River bridge and the Maryland Transportation Authority
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided with the bill text. The bill may result in indeterminate design and construction costs for the Maryland Transportation Authority to ensure that tolling is only applied to vehicles crossing the replacement bridge. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Transportation Authority to design and locate the entrances, exits, and associated roads of the new bridge over the Patapsco River to ensure vehicles not crossing the bridge are not tolled.
As the umbrella agency for Maryland's multi-modal transportation network, MDOT oversees the coordination of state highways and transit that will connect to the new bridge.

The Board of Public Works must approve significant state expenditures and procurement contracts, including those for the design and construction of major infrastructure like the Patapsco River bridge replacement.
The State Highway Administration maintains the state-numbered roads that lead into the bridge's entrances and exits, making their coordination essential for the bill's design requirements.
DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and oversight of state agency resources, including the potential fiscal impact on toll revenues and project costs related to the bridge's design.
As a member of the Board of Public Works and the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller oversees the fiscal integrity of the contracts and revenue models associated with the new bridge.
The Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works and manages state funds and debt, including bond issuances that may be related to the financing of the bridge project.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, chairs the Board of Public Works, and sets the policy priorities for major infrastructure reconstruction projects.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland Transportation Authority, regarding compliance with the statutory requirements for the bridge design and tolling.

Synopsis: Requiring, by October 1, 2026, and each October 1 thereafter, the Office of the Attorney General to publish a handbook summarizing State law, federal law, and case law related to wearing, carrying, and transporting a handgun in public in Maryland; and requiring the handbook to be drafted in plain language so it can be easily understood without special knowledge of relevant law and in a format that can be easily used to teach certain required firearms courses.
Title: Handguns - Wear, Carry, and Transport Laws - Handbook Publication
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: This bill requires the Office of the Attorney General to publish and annually update a plain-language handbook summarizing State and federal laws and court cases regarding the wearing, carrying, and transporting of handguns in public. The handbook must be formatted for use in required firearm safety courses.
stakeholders: Handgun permit applicants, firearm safety instructors, and individuals who wear, carry, or transport handguns in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Office of the Attorney General can draft and publish the required handbook using existing budgeted resources. There is no anticipated material effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Office of the Attorney General to draft, publish, and annually update a handbook summarizing all state, federal, and case law applicable to the wearing, carrying, and transporting of handguns in public.

The handbook must be drafted in a format compatible with firearm safety courses, which are approved and overseen by the State Police. Additionally, the State Police are currently responsible for distributing summaries of new firearms laws and managing handgun permit training requirements.

Synopsis: Establishing that a new public record is not created if, in responding to a certain request under the Public Information Act, a custodian conducts certain data manipulation.
Title: Public Information Act - Data Manipulation
Status: In the House - Hearing 1/27 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill specifies that under the Maryland Public Information Act, a custodian does not create a new public record when they perform data compilation, extraction, querying, statistical aggregation, or other data manipulation that their existing records database program is already capable of performing.
responsible_party: Custodians of public records in Maryland State and local government agencies
stakeholders: Applicants requesting public records and government custodians of public records
fiscal_impact_summary: The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Although some agencies, such as the Comptroller and the Maryland State Department of Education, claimed the bill would require additional staff and technology funding (ranging from approximately $97,200 to $199,700), DLS disagreed with these assessments. DLS noted that the bill does not mandate additional data manipulation but simply clarifies that existing capabilities do not constitute the creation of a new record.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OAG is the chief legal representative for the state and is responsible for publishing the Public Information Act Manual. They provide legal counsel to all state agencies regarding PIA compliance and would be responsible for interpreting the bill's provisions on data manipulation.

As the agency responsible for the state's IT strategy and infrastructure, DoIT manages the database capabilities mentioned in the bill. Their systems and programming standards will determine whether a specific query or extraction is technically 'capable of being performed,' which is the threshold for the bill's new definitions.

The Comptroller's Office handles a high volume of complex financial data requests. In the fiscal note, they indicated that the bill would expand the scope of required data queries and might necessitate additional staffing to manage custom data extraction requests.

MSDE manages extensive student and educational performance data. The agency noted in the fiscal analysis that the bill could lead to significantly increased workloads for data analysts and requirements for software upgrades to handle more complex data manipulation requests.

The University System manages massive amounts of institutional and research data. They indicated a potential need for increased software and personnel expenses to comply with expanded data manipulation requirements established by the bill.

As the central support agency for the Judiciary, the AOC is responsible for managing judicial records and was consulted as an information source for the impact of changes to the Public Information Act.

The Department of Health manages a vast array of public health, provider, and Medicaid data. They were specifically listed as an information source and frequently handle complex data queries that would fall under the bill's new criteria.

MDOT and its sub-agencies, particularly the Motor Vehicle Administration, process significant volumes of records. Changes to what constitutes a 'new record' for electronic databases would directly impact their operational workflow for PIA requests.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS handles highly sensitive records regarding justice-involved individuals and facility operations. The bill’s provisions on data extraction and metadata removal are particularly relevant to their records management duties.

The Maryland State Police handle a high frequency of public information requests related to law enforcement incidents and traffic safety. The clarification on data querying and aggregation directly impacts how they fulfill these electronic record requests.

As a primary regulator of a new industry, the MCA was consulted for this bill and handles sensitive licensing and compliance data that is frequently the subject of complex public information requests.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and appointments to the Public Information Act Compliance Board. The bill's change to the PIA affects records management standards for all executive agencies under the Governor's purview.

DBM is responsible for state personnel and fiscal planning. They would be involved if agencies require the additional staff positions claimed in the fiscal note to handle the anticipated workload increase.
MDE was listed as an information source and manages environmental data systems that are subject to technical data extraction and query requests under the bill.
DNR manages significant amounts of conservation and public land data. They were identified as an agency that would be impacted by standardized rules regarding data manipulation for public records.
As a regulatory agency consulted for the fiscal note, the MIA maintains consumer and provider data that could be subject to aggregation or statistical queries defined by the bill.
DHCD was identified as an information source and maintains databases related to community revitalization and finance that are subject to the Public Information Act.
Department of Commerce was consulted during the bill's analysis and maintains business and economic data systems affected by the clarified requirements for data compilation.
The PSC regulates public utilities and manages substantial regulatory data. They were listed as an information source regarding the operational impact of the bill's definitions of data manipulation.

Synopsis: Altering the definitions of "community association" and "local code violation" to authorize community associations to seek judicial relief for nuisance abatement in Baltimore County; requiring certain notices relating to nuisance actions to be provided to the county code enforcement agency and certain tenants and property owners; repealing a provision of law requiring a certain court to determine the amount and conditions of a bond filed by a community association in a certain nuisance action; etc.
Title: Baltimore County - Nuisance Actions - Community Association
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/31 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: This bill updates the definitions of 'community association' and 'local code violation' to authorize community associations in Baltimore County to seek injunctive relief in the Circuit Court for nuisance abatement. It establishes specific notice requirements for code enforcement agencies, tenants, and property owners before an action can be brought, and repeals the requirement that the court determine the amount and conditions of a bond to be filed by a community association seeking relief.
responsible_party: Circuit Court for Baltimore County and the Baltimore County Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Community associations, residents, property owners, and tenants in Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State or Baltimore County finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial procedures by altering definitions of standing, notice requirements, and service of process for nuisance actions in the Circuit Court for Baltimore County. It also repeals the court's requirement to determine bond amounts, directly affecting court operations and legal administration.

As the chief legal officer for Maryland, the OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies. The bill amends the Real Property Article of the Maryland Code, requiring the OAG to ensure that expanded standing for community associations and new notice requirements comply with state property laws and constitutional due process.

The bill's focus on nuisance abatement to improve resident well-being and neighborhod quality aligns with the department's mission to ensure safe housing and support community revitalization. It also specifically coordinates with local housing code enforcement agencies which overlap with state-level housing standards.

The bill impacts the legal tools available to community associations, which are key stakeholders served by this office. The agency facilitates partnerships and provides advice on policies related to community services and local needs, making the standing of neighborhood organizations highly relevant to its work.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. As the bill requires the Governor's signature and involves the coordination of various state articles (Environment, Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis), it falls under the Governor's role in enforcing state laws and overseeing executive agencies.

The bill includes a specific rule of construction to ensure it does not grant standing for actions involving violations of alcoholic beverages or cannabis laws, thereby protecting the administration's specific regulatory jurisdiction over its subject matter.

The bill contains an explicit exclusion for any matter requiring a permit or license under the Environment Article, ensuring that the new community association nuisance standing does not infringe upon the department's regulatory and enforcement authority.

Synopsis: Providing that a manufacturer, distributor, or factory branch may not take an adverse action against a dealer for disclosing on its website that the advertised price of a vehicle is the manufacturer's minimum allowable advertised price and that the dealer may offer a lower price for the vehicle.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Manufacturers and Dealers - Prices Listed on Dealer Websites (Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act)
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: The Jack Fitzgerald Price Transparency Act prohibits vehicle manufacturers, distributors, or factory branches from taking adverse actions against dealers for disclosing on their websites that an advertised price is the manufacturer’s minimum allowable price and that the dealer may offer a lower price. This protection applies as long as the dealer does not engage in false or deceptive advertising or violate other laws intended to protect the public.
stakeholders: Motor vehicle dealers, manufacturers, distributors, factory branches, and vehicle consumers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. Small business impact is estimated to be minimal. The Motor Vehicle Administration, which licenses manufacturers and dealers, is the primary oversight body, but no significant expenditure or revenue changes are anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary agency responsible for licensing and regulating motor vehicle manufacturers, distributors, and dealers in Maryland. This bill directly governs the regulatory standards for manufacturer-dealer relationships and advertising, which are under MVA's jurisdiction.

MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the implementation of the Transportation Article of the Maryland Code. This bill amends that article to regulate manufacturer actions against vehicle dealers.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDOT and MVA and has a mandate to enforce consumer protection laws, which are relevant to the bill's requirements for price transparency and its references to deceptive advertising prohibitions.

OAH provides impartial hearings for contested administrative cases. Any regulatory disputes or licensing challenges arising between the MVA and industry participants under this new law would be heard by OAH.

The bill references existing laws against deceptive advertising that carry criminal penalties. The state court system, supported by the AOC, would adjudicate any criminal prosecutions resulting from violations of these advertising standards.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for this bill's implementation and is required to sign the legislation into law.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose of the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund; requiring the Comptroller to administer the Fund at the direction of the Office of Social Equity; altering requirements for a certain county plan for the distribution of funds from the Fund; requiring a county to consult with the Office to make any adjustments to the county plan; altering the requirements for a certain report on the Fund; requiring the Comptroller, in consultation with the Office, to ensure compliance with provisions of law governing the Fund; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the administration and oversight of the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund. It mandates that the Comptroller administer the fund under the direction of the Office of Social Equity and requires counties to develop detailed plans for fund distribution in consultation with stakeholders. The bill also specifies authorized uses for the money, focusing on community-based initiatives in areas disproportionately impacted by cannabis law enforcement, and increases reporting requirements for local jurisdictions.
responsible_party: Comptroller and the Office of Social Equity
stakeholders: Residents of communities disproportionately impacted by cannabis enforcement, community-based organizations, and local government jurisdictions.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State special fund expenditures increase by $90,008 in FY 2027 to cover administrative costs for the Office of Social Equity, including hiring a program analyst. This funding is derived from adult-use cannabis sales and use tax revenues, which reduces the amount available for distribution to the General Fund, the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund, and local governments. Consequently, local government revenues and expenditures are expected to decrease beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Comptroller to administer the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (at the direction of the Office of Social Equity), account for the fund, and pay out money from it. The Comptroller is also responsible for ensuring compliance with the law governing the fund.

The bill requires the Office of Social Equity to consult with the Office of the Attorney General to determine which communities have been most impacted by the disproportionate enforcement of cannabis prohibition for the purpose of fund distribution.
The bill specifies that the State Treasurer shall hold the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund separately and invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other State money.
The bill explicitly states that the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

The bill has a fiscal impact requiring new staff and special fund expenditures for the Office of Social Equity, which DBM oversees as the principal fiscal and personnel agency. The bill also affects the distribution of cannabis tax revenues to the General Fund.

The fiscal note indicates a decrease in revenue for the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund, which is administered by the Department of Commerce. The bill also mentions the Office of Social Equity's role in assisting Commerce with that fund.

The fund established by the bill is authorized to be used for education and after-school programs, as well as truancy and absenteeism intervention programs, which align with MSDE's oversight of public education.

The fund may be used for behavioral health crisis response services. Additionally, the fiscal note shows a revenue decrease for the Cannabis Public Health Fund, which is administered by the Department of Health.
The bill identifies housing and homelessness prevention initiatives as authorized uses for the money distributed from the fund to local jurisdictions.

The bill targets low-income communities and families impacted by incarceration for community-based initiatives, aligning with the Department of Human Services' mission to assist vulnerable populations and those in economic need.
The bill authorizes the use of funds for job training and workforce development programs, which are primary responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Labor.
The bill permits fund expenditures for transportation improvements in high-density areas that have public transportation, impacting infrastructure projects overseen by MDOT.

The Governor appoints the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, which is the primary entity directing the fund's administration. The bill also impacts the General Fund and reflects the administration's policy priorities regarding economic mobility.

The bill relates to the broader regulatory framework of the cannabis industry and specifies that the Office of Social Equity (the fund's director) provides recommendations to the MCA on diversity and social equity regulations.

Synopsis: Authorizing an address in this State supplied by a commercial mail receiving agency to be designated as the principal office of a Maryland corporation, limited liability company, limited liability partnership, or limited partnership; and defining "commercial mail receiving agency" as a person that is authorized by the U.S. Postal Service to accept delivery of mail on behalf of another person as a business service.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Principal Offices - Private Mailboxes
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill allows Maryland corporations, limited liability companies, limited liability partnerships, and limited partnerships to designate an address provided by a commercial mail receiving agency (CMRA) as their principal office, provided they have a valid agreement in accordance with U.S. Postal Service regulations.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
stakeholders: Maryland corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs), limited liability partnerships (LLPs), limited partnerships, and commercial mail receiving agencies (CMRAs).
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues are expected to increase starting in fiscal 2027 as business entities pay a $25 filing fee to change their principal office to a CMRA address. The State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) is anticipated to handle the bill's administrative requirements within existing resources. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the administrative departments responsible for corporate filings and must sign the bill into law. The office coordinates policy initiatives related to the state's business climate.

The bill and fiscal note explicitly state that commercial mail receiving agencies must provide contact information to law enforcement agencies upon request, making this relevant to the State Police's investigative capabilities regarding business entities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), on the interpretation and enforcement of the Corporations and Associations Article.
As the primary economic development agency, Commerce is impacted by changes to business registration requirements that affect the ease of operating a corporation or LLC in Maryland.

The Comptroller relies on accurate business address information for tax collection, auditing, and enforcement. Changes to the definition of a principal office affect how businesses are tracked for revenue purposes.
DBM is responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal planning; the bill is projected to increase special fund revenues through filing fees collected for address changes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies a potential meaningful impact on small businesses, as the bill allows smaller entities to use mail service providers as a principal office instead of maintaining a physical commercial lease.

The Secretary of State is a custodian of official records and manages registrations for various entities; the legal definition of a 'principal office' is foundational to their record-keeping and regulatory duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on public safety strategies; the bill's requirement for CMRAs to share data with law enforcement involves the office's mission to coordinate criminal justice policy.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from being stopped, detained, or arrested for certain civil offenses while the individual is in a judicial facility or is traveling within 1 mile of a judicial facility for the purpose of attending a meeting, a hearing, or another official proceeding in the Judicial facility except under certain circumstances; establishing that evidence obtained in violation of the Act is inadmissible in a proceeding over which a State court or State or local agency has jurisdiction; etc.
Title: Judicial Facilities - Stops, Detentions, and Arrests - Limitations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/04 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Public Buildings and Facilities -see also- Stadiums; St Hse
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill prohibits law enforcement or other government agents from stopping, detaining, or arresting an individual for civil-only offenses while the individual is inside a judicial facility or traveling within one mile of a judicial facility for a meeting, hearing, or other official proceeding. These actions are only permitted if the agent provides prior notice to the presiding judge or court administrator and ensures the action does not disrupt proceedings or deter access to justice. Evidence obtained in violation of these rules is inadmissible in State proceedings, and individuals may bring civil actions for damages and legal fees. The Attorney General is also authorized to seek injunctions against violators.
responsible_party: Maryland Attorney General, law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals attending judicial or quasi-judicial proceedings, law enforcement agencies and officers, court administrators, and judges.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While the bill allows for civil actions, damages, and attorney's fees, and authorizes the Attorney General to seek injunctions, no specific dollar estimates for these impacts are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates operations within judicial facilities, specifically impacting courthouses and requiring notice to be provided to court administrators prior to certain stops or arrests.

The bill's definition of 'judicial facility' explicitly includes administrative hearing facilities. As the central panel for state administrative hearings, the OAH's facilities are directly governed by the stop and arrest limitations.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions to enjoin violations of the Act. Additionally, the OAG provides legal guidance on related immigration enforcement and facility access policies.
The Commission is a quasi-judicial agency that operates hearing facilities where official proceedings take place, placing its locations within the definition of judicial facilities.
As an independent administrative agency that performs quasi-judicial functions and holds hearings, its facilities are subject to the bill's restrictions on stops and arrests.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, its officers are included in the definition of a 'person' restricted from making civil-related stops and arrests near judicial facilities without meeting specific notice requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD represents clients in judicial facilities and has a significant interest in 'access to justice' and the bill's provision making evidence obtained in violation of these rules inadmissible.
The MVA conducts a high volume of administrative hearings (quasi-judicial proceedings) at its facilities, which would likely fall under the definition of judicial facilities.
The PSC is an administrative agency that conducts quasi-judicial proceedings and sets rates, making its hearing locations judicial facilities under the bill.
This agency provides administrative review through local boards that conduct hearings, making their meeting locations judicial facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As an agency responsible for adjudicating contract disputes through an administrative hearing process, its facilities are covered by the bill.
The PERB adjudicates unfair labor practice charges and conducts hearings, placing its proceedings and locations under the bill's purview.
DGS manages, owns, or leases many state facilities, including those used for judicial or quasi-judicial proceedings, and oversees the Maryland Capitol Police.
MDOT oversees various administrations (like MVA) that conduct hearings and manages its own police forces that are subject to the bill's arrest limitations.
The MDTA maintains its own police force, which is subject to the bill's restrictions on stops and arrests for civil offenses near judicial facilities.
The MTA operates its own police force and conducts administrative functions that may involve quasi-judicial processes or proximity to judicial facilities.
The Register of Wills operates offices within courthouses in every county, placing their staff and operations within the immediate vicinity of regulated judicial facilities.
The Department conducts administrative hearings for various regulatory and unemployment insurance matters, making its hearing sites judicial facilities.
The MIA conducts administrative hearings regarding insurance rates and compliance, making its hearing rooms subject to the bill's definitions.

Synopsis: Requiring an incarcerated individual to undergo an assessment for indicators of a developmental or intellectual disability at intake at a State correctional facility by a certain clinical professional; authorizing a certain clinical professional to make a recommendation about a certain incarcerated individual; and prohibiting a State correctional facility from putting a certain incarcerated individual in restrictive housing for more than 15 consecutive days in a 30-day time period unless the individual commits a certain prohibited act.
Title: Correctional Services - Restrictive Housing - Individuals With Developmental or Intellectual Disabilities
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Violence -see also- Domestic Violence; Hate Crimes

bill_summary: This bill requires State correctional facilities to screen incoming incarcerated individuals for developmental or intellectual disabilities. If a clinical professional identifies such a disability, the facility is generally prohibited from placing the individual in restrictive housing for more than 15 consecutive days within a 30-day period, except when the individual commits specific prohibited acts such as violence, extortion, or escape attempts.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals with developmental or intellectual disabilities and staff at Maryland State correctional facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to affect State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing State correctional facilities, DPSCS is directly responsible for implementing the new intake assessment requirements and adhering to the restrictive housing limits for individuals with developmental or intellectual disabilities.

The bill utilizes clinical definitions for disabilities from the Health-General Article and involves clinical professionals trained in mental health, which falls under the department's public health and behavioral health oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is mandated by existing law to collect, analyze, and report annual data from correctional units regarding the use of restrictive housing, a process directly impacted by the bill's new restrictions and assessment criteria.

This department is the principal state agency for coordinating policies and services for individuals with disabilities; the bill establishes specific protections for these populations within the state's correctional system.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including DPSCS and MDH, regarding the implementation of new laws and compliance with constitutional or statutory requirements related to incarcerated individuals.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Commissioner of Correction, who is specifically tasked in the bill with making reasonable determinations regarding threats posed by incarcerated individuals.

Synopsis: Requiring each local school system to identify, in its regular safety evaluation, issues of accessibility for individuals with disabilities; and requiring local school systems to include in a certain annual report instances in which a public school facility became inaccessible for a student with a disability in a manner that could impede evacuations or emergency response.
Title: Public Schools - Individuals With Disabilities - Accessibility and Emergency Planning
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland local school systems to identify accessibility issues for individuals with disabilities as part of their regular school safety evaluations and to report specific instances where facilities became inaccessible for students with disabilities in ways that could impede emergency responses or evacuations.
responsible_party: Maryland Center for School Safety and local school systems
stakeholders: Students with disabilities, school staff and visitors with disabilities, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) can implement the bill's requirements with existing resources. Local school systems are not expected to see a material financial impact because the bill does not change existing federal or state accessibility laws, only evaluation and reporting protocols.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local school systems to submit safety evaluations and annual reports concerning accessibility and emergency planning to the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS). MCSS is also tasked with consulting on updates to school emergency plans to correct identified weaknesses.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the public school system and the local school systems mentioned in the bill. Additionally, the Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within MSDE, and MSDE previously established the emergency planning guidelines referenced in the bill's implementation history.

The bill mandates that local school system safety coordinators coordinate with the Interagency Commission on School Construction's (IAC) facility assessment process when identifying issues with public school facilities that could impact safety and accessibility.

The bill is specifically focused on accessibility and emergency planning for individuals with disabilities. The Department of Disabilities is the principal agency for ensuring inclusive policies and accessibility across all state programs and services.

As the agency responsible for coordinating the state's preparedness and response for emergencies, the department has an interest in the updates to school emergency plans and evacuation protocols for vulnerable populations.

The bill includes provisions regarding the confidentiality of reports and exemptions from the Maryland Public Information Act, which may require legal interpretation and guidance from the Office of the Attorney General.
The Governor oversees the executive branch departments involved (MSDE, Disabilities, Emergency Management) and coordinates broad policy initiatives related to safety and accessibility.

The department oversees the state budget; while the fiscal note indicates the bill can be implemented with existing resources, any future capital or operational adjustments identified through the safety evaluations would involve DBM oversight.

Synopsis: Authorizing a member of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System to receive certain service credit on the redeposit of contributions from the Employees' Pension System or the Teachers' Pension System.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Redeposit of Accumulated Contributions - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/18 at 12:45 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill allows members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) to receive service credit for prior membership in the Employees' Pension System (EPS) or the Teachers' Pension System (TPS) by redepositing their withdrawn accumulated contributions plus interest in a single payment.
stakeholders: Active members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System who previously forfeited service credit by withdrawing contributions from the Employees' Pension System or the Teachers' Pension System.
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities and contributions are expected to increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount. The State Retirement Agency identified 253 active CORS members eligible to buy back service credit, though the net impact depends on the number of members who participate and their specific salary and service history. Any state costs are assumed to be allocated 60% to general funds, 20% to special funds, and 20% to federal funds. Local government liabilities for the CORS municipal pool may also increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), the agency is responsible for managing the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS), the Employees' Pension System (EPS), and the Teachers' Pension System (TPS). This bill directly alters the administration of service credits and the redeposit of contributions within these systems.

DBM is the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the state. This bill impacts state employee benefits and increases unfunded pension liabilities and employer contributions, which directly affects the state budget and personnel policies managed by DBM.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary employer of the correctional officers who belong to CORS. Changes to retirement benefits and service credit portability directly impact the compensation and benefits structure for the department's workforce.

The State Treasurer acts as the chief financial agency and plays a key role in the management of state funds and the retirement system's board. The bill's impact on state pension liabilities and the movement of state funds for service credits falls under the Treasurer's financial oversight responsibilities.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works. The agency is involved in paying state employees and overseeing state expenditures, including the increased pension contributions required by this bill.

The Governor's Office is responsible for proposing the annual state budget and overseeing executive branch operations. The fiscal note indicates a potentially significant increase in state pension liabilities and general fund expenditures, which must be accounted for in the Governor's budget proposals.

Synopsis: Requiring a landlord to provide certain written disclosures before accepting an application or screening fee; providing that a prospective tenant shall be allowed to dispute and provide evidence regarding certain information contained in a tenant screening report; establishing that a landlord is not liable for certain information included in a tenant screening report under certain circumstances; requiring a landlord to report certain information to a person that produces tenant screening reports; etc.
Title: Landlord and Tenant - Residential Housing - Rental Applications and Tenant Screening
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/02 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill establishes regulations for residential rental applications and tenant screening processes in Maryland. It requires landlords to provide prospective tenants with a disclosure form regarding screening criteria and fees before accepting any application fees. The bill also restricts landlords from considering shielded court records or certain old eviction-related records, mandates written notice for 'adverse actions' (like application denials), allows tenants to dispute inaccurate screening reports, and establishes civil penalties for violations.
responsible_party: The Department of Housing and Community Development and the Attorney General
stakeholders: Residential landlords, prospective tenants, and companies that produce tenant screening reports.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's penalty provisions are not expected to have a material impact on State or local finances. The Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division, can manage the requirements with existing resources. Small business landlords may experience a meaningful impact due to new compliance requirements and potential liability for civil penalties or private legal actions. Specific dollar estimates for total revenue from civil penalties are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) create a disclosure form that landlords must provide to prospective tenants, outlining screening criteria, fees, and contact information.

The bill authorizes the Attorney General to adopt regulations for its implementation. Additionally, violations of certain provisions are deemed unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill regulates the use of court records and shielded records in tenant screening, defines 'proceedings' based on court filings, and establishes new civil causes of action that will be adjudicated within the state court system.

The Commission on Civil Rights enforces anti-discrimination laws in housing. Since tenant screening reports and the use of court records (specifically failure-to-pay-rent proceedings) often have a direct impact on fair housing and equal access to accommodations, this bill is relevant to their regulatory scope.

As the office responsible for coordinating policy initiatives and overseeing the executive branch, the Governor's Office would be involved in the broader implementation of new housing policies and the coordination between DHCD and the Attorney General.

Synopsis: Requiring employers with 100 or more employees that reduced their workforce in the State by a least 10 employees while using automation technology to submit certain information to the Secretary of Labor concerning the number of employees employed, automation technology deployed or used, and certain employees separated from employment during the immediately preceding calendar year; requiring a certain covered employer to pay a certain assessment for each displaced employee reported by the covered employer; etc.
Title: Automation Technology Deployment Assessment and Displaced Employee Retraining Fund - Established
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Technology -see also- AeroT; BioT; EnergyT; InfoT; MedT; etc
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Displaced Employee Retraining Fund to support training, job placement, and service programs for workers separated from employment due to automation technology. It requires employers with 100 or more employees to report workforce reductions of 10 or more individuals caused by automation and pay a $900 assessment per displaced employee into the fund. Employers can reduce the assessment by 50% by providing severance pay, certified retraining, or successfully placing the employee with a small Maryland-based employer.
stakeholders: Employers with 100 or more employees in Maryland, employees displaced by automation technology, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $657,100 in FY 2028 to cover Maryland Department of Labor staffing and a $300,000 one-time IT system upgrade. Special fund revenues to the Displaced Employee Retraining Fund increase beginning in FY 2028 from employer assessments; while the total is indeterminate, illustrative estimates range from $1,512,000 to $3,024,000 annually. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including collecting annual reports from covered employers, administering the Displaced Employee Retraining Fund, adopting regulations, and enforcing civil penalties.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the Displaced Employee Retraining Fund separately and to invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other state money.
The bill explicitly requires the Comptroller to account for the Displaced Employee Retraining Fund, a new special, nonlapsing fund created by the legislation.

The OAG will provide legal counsel to the Department of Labor regarding the implementation of the new assessment and the adoption of regulations, and will likely represent the state in appeals related to the significant civil penalties established by the bill.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact requiring significant general fund expenditures for new personnel and IT system upgrades at the Department of Labor, which falls under DBM's budgetary and personnel oversight.

As the state's chief policy-making body for the workforce system, the board's strategy is directly impacted by the creation of the Displaced Employee Retraining Fund and the focus on individuals displaced by automation.

The bill creates new civil penalties for employers who fail to report or pay assessments; appeals of these administrative decisions would likely be adjudicated by ALJs within the Office of Administrative Hearings.
The Secretary of Labor is required to report annually to the Governor regarding the number of covered employers, displaced employees, and policy recommendations to support those employees.

The bill centers on the deployment of automation technology, including AI and machine learning, which are subjects under DoIT's strategic and policy governance as the state's lead AI oversight agency.

The reporting of employees displaced by automation provides a new and specific dataset regarding workforce outcomes that is highly relevant to the Center's mission of analyzing student and workforce performance trends.

Synopsis: Providing that a certain landlord may not refuse to rent to a prospective tenant who pays rent with the assistance of an income-based housing subsidy under certain circumstances, subject to a certain exception; establishing that a violation of the Act is a discriminatory housing practice and is subject to enforcement by the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights; and requiring that a certain landlord offer a certain tenant the option of having positive rental payment history reported to a certain consumer reporting agency.
Title: Landlord and Tenant - Discrimination in Housing for Income-Based Housing Subsidies and Positive Rental History Reporting
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill prohibits landlords from discriminating against prospective tenants who use income-based housing subsidies (such as Section 8 vouchers) by barring them from rejecting applicants based on income levels, credit scores, or specific adverse credit history. It also requires landlords who own six or more residential units to offer tenants the option to have their positive rental payment history reported to a consumer reporting agency, for which the landlord may charge a fee of up to $10 per month.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and the Secretary of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Prospective and current tenants, particularly those receiving income-based housing subsidies, and landlords who own six or more residential rental units in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no anticipated material effect on State or local government operations or finances. The bill allows landlords to charge a fee to tenants for rental history reporting, but this does not result in State or local revenue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines a landlord's refusal to rent to tenants based on income-based housing subsidies as a discriminatory housing practice, which falls directly under the enforcement jurisdiction of the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to adopt regulations regarding the form and process for landlords to offer tenants the option of reporting positive rental payment history.
The bill provides for civil actions in circuit court for discriminatory housing practices, which impacts the Judiciary's workload and case management.
Discriminatory housing practice complaints filed through the Commission on Civil Rights are subject to administrative hearings conducted by independent Administrative Law Judges at the OAH.

As the chief legal officer for the State, the OAG provides legal counsel to both the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights and the Department of Housing and Community Development regarding enforcement and regulatory implementation.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "medical record" for purposes of law governing the confidentiality of medical records to require that certain information be recorded by a health care provider through certain means, instead of entered into the record of a patient or recipient, and to include certain electronic messages.
Title: Confidentiality of Medical Records - Definition of Medical Record
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill expands and clarifies the definition of a "medical record" for confidentiality purposes to include any information recorded by a health care provider through written, electronic, audio, or video means, and specifically includes electronic messages that identify or can be associated with a patient.
stakeholders: Health care providers, patients, recipients of health care, and pharmacies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no impact on State or local government finances as the change to the definition of a medical record is technical in nature. The impact on small businesses is estimated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is an independent regulatory agency within the Maryland Department of Health responsible for planning the state's health system needs and increasing accountability. Altering the definition of what constitutes a 'medical record' directly impacts their data collection, privacy policies, and regulatory oversight of health care providers.

As the primary state agency for health policy and regulation, MDH oversees the Health-General article of the Maryland Code where this definition is housed. The department must ensure that its own public health services, Medicaid operations, and the providers it regulates comply with the updated confidentiality standards.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and other state entities regarding the Confidentiality of Medical Records Act. They will be responsible for interpreting the expanded definition and advising agencies on compliance and liability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees the statewide emergency medical services (EMS) network. Since EMS providers generate and transmit medical records—often via electronic, audio, or video means—the bill's definition change directly impacts their operational and documentation standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS provides direct health care to individuals in the state's correctional facilities. Expanding the definition of a 'medical record' to include electronic messages and various recording formats requires the department to update its record-keeping and privacy protocols.

DJS is responsible for the medical care of youth in the juvenile justice system. They must ensure that all electronic messages or recordings regarding the health of youth in their care are treated as confidential medical records per the new definition.

DVMF operates the Charlotte Hall Veterans Home. As a health care facility, it must comply with the state's medical record confidentiality laws, and the staff must adapt to the broader inclusion of electronic messages in the medical record.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HCADRO administers arbitration for medical malpractice claims. The legal definition of a 'medical record' is central to the evidence used in these proceedings and determines what information must be produced or protected under confidentiality laws.

The MCA maintains registries for medical cannabis patients and caregivers. The clarified definition of medical records may affect how the administration handles patient-related electronic communications and data.

The USM includes several institutions that provide direct clinical care and train health care professionals. These entities must update their administrative and educational protocols to reflect the inclusion of electronic messages and other media in the official medical record.

Public school systems overseen by MSDE maintain health-related records for students. The updated definition impacts the management of electronic communications between school health staff and families regarding student health.

DHS handles foster care and child protection services, which involve the management of health-related information. The expanded definition of a medical record applies to the documentation they collect and share regarding vulnerable children.

As a state-run school providing comprehensive support services, including health monitoring for students, MSD must ensure its health documentation practices align with the expanded legal definition of medical records.

The Judicial Branch handles medical records as evidence in various civil and criminal matters. A statutory change to the definition of a medical record affects the scope of discoverable information and the procedures for sealing or protecting patient data in court.

Synopsis: Requiring certain persons that receive certain State economic development assistance to make a certification each year that the person was not the subject of a certain final adverse determination  and is not currently failing to comply with certain outstanding requirements under a prior final judgment or order; requiring a certain unit of State government to initiate a pause on disbursements or approvals of certain economic development assistance or the award or renewal of certain State contracts; etc.
Title: Recipients of Economic Development Assistance or State Contracts - Certification of Compliance With State Labor Laws
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/17 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires companies that receive at least $100,000 in state economic development assistance or $250,000 in state contracts to certify annually that they have complied with Maryland labor laws, including wage and child labor regulations. If a company fails to certify or has significant unresolved labor violations, the state must temporarily pause new funding disbursements, assistance approvals, and contract renewals.
responsible_party: State administering agencies, the Board of Public Works, and the Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Businesses receiving significant state assistance or contracts, state procurement and economic development agencies, and employees protected by state labor laws
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates administrative requirements for state agencies to track certifications and manage funding pauses for non-compliant recipients. While the bill specifies that no new audit program is created and allows for integration into existing vendor portals, the administrative burden may have fiscal implications. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note were not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Board of Public Works with designating state portals for certification filing, adopting a single-question model certification form, and overseeing procurement contracts that would be subject to the 'pause' mechanism.

As the state's primary economic development agency, Commerce is explicitly named as a potential host for the certification portal and is a primary 'administering agency' for the grants, loans, and tax credits affected by the bill.

As the central procurement authority, DGS is a primary 'administering agency' for State procurement contracts and would be responsible for initiating 'pauses' on contracts and renewals for non-compliant recipients.

The bill's certification requirement is based on compliance with specific labor laws (Title 3 of the Labor and Employment Article) enforced by this department. Their final adverse determinations are the triggers for the 'pause' in funding or contracts.
MDOT manages a massive volume of procurement contracts and would act as an 'administering agency' required to implement certification requirements and pauses for its vendors and contractors.

The bill authorizes referring willfully false certifications to the Office of the Attorney General under the Maryland False Claims Act and relates to suspension and debarment proceedings where the OAG provides legal counsel.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM oversees budget execution and procurement policy, and would be an 'administering agency' for various state contracts affected by these certification requirements.

The Comptroller sits on the Board of Public Works and is responsible for administering tax credits, which are specifically defined as 'economic development assistance' subject to the bill's certification requirements.
This department provides significant economic development assistance through grants and loans to small businesses and municipal infrastructure, making it an 'administering agency' under the bill.
TEDCO provides grants and investments that constitute 'economic development assistance.' It would likely be an 'administering agency' required to collect certifications before disbursing funds.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides loans and grants for the agricultural sector, which fall under the bill's definition of 'economic development assistance' requiring labor law compliance certification.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which oversees significant state contracts and is tasked with designating the portal and form used for the labor law certifications.
The USM and its constituent institutions engage in significant procurement activity and would be 'administering agencies' for contracts meeting the $250,000 threshold.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office monitors state procurement programs; the bill adds a new labor compliance layer to the procurement process that overlaps with the office's oversight of state contracts.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission to accept as a registered vendor any person that is registered through a vendor registration process as a vendor with Montgomery County or Prince George's County; and authorizing the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission to enter into certain memoranda of understanding with Montgomery County and Prince George's County.
Title: Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission – Vendor Registration PG/MC 107–26

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
