Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC) and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) to accept any person or entity registered as a vendor through the vendor registration processes of Montgomery County or Prince George’s County as a registered vendor for the commissions. It also authorizes the commissions to enter into memoranda of understanding with these counties to facilitate the implementation of the vendor registration process.
responsible_party: Maryland–National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC) and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC)
stakeholders: Vendors and businesses registered with Montgomery County or Prince George's County, the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission, and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, so specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are unavailable. The bill creates an administrative mandate for M-NCPPC and WSSC to recognize existing county-level vendor registrations, which may result in minor administrative costs or operational efficiencies for the commissions and participating counties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central procurement authority, DGS manages statewide vendor registration systems. Changes to the registration requirements for large regional commissions like M-NCPPC and WSSC may impact procurement standards and inter-jurisdictional vendor reciprocity.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office oversees the state's socioeconomic procurement programs. Standardizing vendor registration between the commissions and the counties can facilitate easier access for small, minority, and women-owned businesses to participate in regional contracts.
The bill amends the Land Use Article concerning the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission. MDP coordinates closely with M-NCPPC on land use policy and regional planning initiatives.

The bill authorizes the commissions to enter into Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs) with Montgomery and Prince George's counties. The OAG typically provides legal review and counsel for such agreements and statutory compliance.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination date of certain provisions of law that authorize a county board of education to provide transportation to and from school for certain students using a vehicle other than a certain type of school vehicle; and requiring the State Department of Education, in consultation with county boards of education and the Motor Vehicle Administration, to study the current regulations for vehicles other than a certain type of school vehicle and report the results to certain committees by January 1, 2027.
Title: County Boards of Education - Student Transportation - Sunset Repeal and Study
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

bill_summary: This bill repeals the June 30, 2026, termination date for laws that allow Maryland county boards of education to use alternative vehicles, rather than standard Type I or Type II school buses, to transport specific student groups like homeless youth and students with disabilities. It also requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to review current regulations for these alternative vehicles and report its findings to the General Assembly by January 1, 2027.
stakeholders: Maryland county boards of education, students requiring specialized transportation (including students with disabilities, homeless youth, and foster children), and private transportation contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative costs for MSDE to conduct the required study and report can be handled with existing budgeted resources. Local school system expenditures for student transportation may decrease beyond fiscal 2026 as the bill allows for the continued use of alternative vehicles, avoiding the higher costs associated with standard school buses for specific routes. No specific dollar estimates for these potential savings are provided in the fiscal note.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the State Department of Education to lead a comprehensive review of regulations governing the transportation of public school students in alternative vehicles and to report its findings to the General Assembly.

The bill explicitly requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to consult with the State Department of Education on the review of safety regulations and standards for vehicles and drivers involved in alternative student transportation.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT is directly involved in the consultative process and the broader implications for transportation safety standards and vehicle regulation defined in the bill.

The bill requires the State Department of Education to examine the Public Service Commission's regulations for transportation network operators to determine if school transportation rules can be aligned with those standards.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of Anne Arundel County to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the county property tax imposed on real property that is located in a Rural Legacy Area, subject to certain land preservation programs, and for which the property owner has sold certain development rights under the Rural Legacy Program; applying the Act to taxable years beginning after June 30, 2026; etc.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Property Tax Credit - Rural Legacy Program
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the governing body of Anne Arundel County to establish a property tax credit for real property located within a Rural Legacy Area, provided the owner has sold the property's development rights under the Rural Legacy Program.
responsible_party: Governing body of Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Owners of real property in Anne Arundel County Rural Legacy Areas who have sold their development rights.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Locally, Anne Arundel County property tax revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $27,825 annually beginning in fiscal 2027, assuming the credit is granted. This estimate is based on the 21 properties currently identified as having Rural Legacy conservation easements in the county. County expenditures are not expected to be affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) oversees the Rural Legacy Program and manages the Rural Legacy Areas defined in the Natural Resources Article, which are the specific areas and programs targeted by this property tax credit bill.

The Board of Public Works approves the grants and the purchase of conservation easements under the Rural Legacy Program, which is the mechanism by which property owners sell development rights and become eligible for the proposed tax credit.
The Department of Planning is involved in sustainable growth and land use planning, including coordination with programs like Rural Legacy to preserve farmland and natural resources.

The Department of Agriculture manages the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), a similar land preservation program mentioned in the bill and fiscal note as a precursor to the proposed credit.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies implementing the Rural Legacy Program and the Governor serves as a member of the Board of Public Works, which approves the program's grants.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, such as DNR, regarding the implementation of the Rural Legacy Program and the interpretation of the Natural Resources Article.

Synopsis: Extending the deadline by which the Department of the Environment is required to submit a certain report on the synthetic turf industry and synthetic turf disposal from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027.
Title: Environment - Synthetic Turf Industry and Disposal Study - Deadline Extension
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: This bill extends the deadline for the Maryland Department of the Environment to submit a comprehensive study and report on the synthetic turf industry and disposal from July 1, 2026, to January 15, 2027. The report must address industry guidelines, disposal methods, recycling rates, and proposals for improving waste management.
stakeholders: Maryland Department of the Environment, Synthetic Turf Council, synthetic turf industry representatives, synthetic turf producers, retailers, and users, local governments, county school systems, higher education facilities, and professional sports organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: Extending the deadline for the required report does not materially affect State or local finances or operations. The Department of Legislative Services notes that the fiscal impact is minimal or none, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable because no significant financial changes are anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires consultation with county school systems, which are overseen by the Maryland State Department of Education, regarding the study on synthetic turf usage and disposal.

As the agency responsible for the maintenance and management of state-owned facilities, DGS is impacted by findings regarding the proper disposal and recycling of synthetic turf used on state properties.
The Department of the Environment is the primary agency responsible for conducting the study and submitting the report on the synthetic turf industry and disposal by the extended deadline.
The bill requires the Department of the Environment to consult with higher education facilities, which fall under the regulatory and coordinating oversight of the Commission.
The IAC oversees the planning and funding of school capital projects, including the installation and life-cycle management of synthetic turf fields at public schools.
MES provides technical and operational services for waste management and recycling, making it a relevant stakeholder in the study's focus on synthetic turf disposal and recycling methods.
The Maryland Stadium Authority manages major sports facilities that utilize synthetic turf and is a stakeholder representing the professional sports organizations mentioned in the bill.
As a higher education institution with its own facilities, Morgan State University is a stakeholder and user of synthetic turf identified for consultation in the study.
As a public honors college and state agency, Saint Mary's is a stakeholder and user of synthetic turf facilities that would be consulted during the study.
The University System of Maryland operates numerous higher education facilities that use synthetic turf and is explicitly identified as a stakeholder for consultation in the study.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Health Care Commission by reducing from nine to eight the number of members who are individuals who do not have any connection with the management or policy of a health care provider or payor and including an administrator of a hospital; and altering from five to four the number of Commission members who must be residents of different counties with a population of 300,000 or more.
Title: Maryland Health Care Commission - Membership
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 38

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the Maryland Health Care Commission by reducing the number of public members from nine to eight and adding a seat for a hospital administrator. It also adjusts residency requirements for the commission, decreasing the minimum number of members from counties with a population of 300,000 or more from five to four.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission and the Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Hospital administrators, health care providers, health care payors, and residents of Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill has no direct effect on State or local governmental finances, as altering the membership of the commission does not impact expenditures or revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the appointing authority for the Maryland Health Care Commission. This bill modifies the statutory criteria and categories of professionals the Governor must select and appoint to the commission.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is an independent regulatory body housed within the Department of Health. Changes to the commission's membership composition affect the leadership and perspective of a key entity within the department's administrative umbrella.

As the primary subject of the bill, the Maryland Health Care Commission's board composition is directly altered, including the addition of a hospital administrator and changes to the residency requirements for its members.

This office is responsible for recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions. The bill imposes new requirements for identifying a hospital administrator and tracking county population thresholds for residency compliance.

Synopsis: Allowing a credit against the State income tax for certain income taxes and penalties attributable to an early withdrawal of retirement funds due to financial exploitation; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Credit for Income Taxes and Penalties Due to Financial Exploitation
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Ways and Means; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: This bill establishes a nonrefundable credit against the Maryland State income tax for individuals who incur income taxes and federal penalties due to early withdrawals from retirement funds necessitated by financial exploitation. The credit is equal to the lesser of the State income tax attributable to the withdrawal or the federal tax penalties paid under Section 72(t) of the Internal Revenue Code. To claim the credit, taxpayers must provide an affidavit and documentation of the exploitation from sources such as law enforcement, adult protective services, or a court.
stakeholders: Victims of financial exploitation who are subject to federal early retirement withdrawal penalties, primarily individuals under the age of 59.5.
fiscal_impact_summary: Maryland general fund revenues will decrease by an indeterminate amount annually beginning in fiscal 2027. The Department of Legislative Services cannot provide a specific estimate due to a lack of data regarding the number of eligible taxpayers and the amount of their associated penalties. The Comptroller's Office can implement the changes with existing resources, and there is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's chief tax collector and is responsible for administering the income tax system, including the processing and verification of the new tax credit established by this bill.

The bill specifically requires documentation from Adult Protective Services (APS), which is a program under the Department of Human Services, to verify instances of financial exploitation for tax credit eligibility.
The bill identifies law enforcement agencies as a primary source of documentation required for taxpayers to prove financial exploitation when claiming the tax credit.
The bill allows for court-issued documentation, such as restitution orders, to serve as evidence for the tax credit, requiring coordination with judicial records.

The bill references documentation from financial institutions reporting under the Maryland SAFE Act; the Department of Labor regulates the financial institutions and industries involved in these reports.
The OAG enforces state laws related to consumer protection and financial crimes and was a consulted source for the fiscal analysis regarding the bill's legal definitions and impacts.
As the agency responsible for state revenue estimation and fiscal planning, DBM is impacted by the reduction in general fund revenues resulting from the nonrefundable income tax credit.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Child Support Administration to take action to secure an assignment to the State of any rights to support on behalf of a child receiving foster care maintenance payments; and requiring a court to terminate a child support order that was previously established or assigned for a child receiving a foster care maintenance payment under certain circumstances.
Title: Family Law - Child Support - Assignment of Rights
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Child Support Administration to secure an assignment of support rights to the State for children in foster care only in limited and appropriate circumstances. It allows for the discontinuation of these assignments and requires the court to terminate existing child support orders for children receiving foster care maintenance payments upon a filing by the Administration, without requiring a showing of material change of circumstance.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services (Child Support Administration and Social Services Administration)
stakeholders: Children in foster care, parents of children in foster care, and the Maryland Department of Human Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and federal fund expenditures increase by $98,500 in fiscal 2027 for one-time programming costs. Special fund revenues decrease by approximately $120,000 in fiscal 2027 and $160,000 annually thereafter due to the reduction in child support payments assigned to the State. Federal fund matching revenues increase by an estimated $49,300 in fiscal 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judiciary by mandating that courts terminate specific child support orders for children in foster care upon the filing of a request by child support authorities, notably removing the standard requirement for a showing of material change of circumstance.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact, including one-time programming expenditures and an ongoing annual decrease in special fund revenues from child support collections, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget and revenue estimation.

As the primary implementing agency, DHS oversees both the Social Services Administration and the Child Support Administration, which are responsible for determining when to secure or discontinue support assignments and for adopting the regulations required by the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy coordination; the Governor is responsible for signing the legislation into law and proposing the state budget, which is impacted by the bill's fiscal provisions.

The bill's focus on adjusting child support obligations for families with children in foster care aligns with the GOC's mission to coordinate policies that reduce child poverty and enhance family economic mobility.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and would be responsible for providing legal counsel to DHS during the development of new regulations and representing the state's interests in related child support legal matters.

Synopsis: Altering the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board by removing a member who is chosen from a list of nominees provided by the Association of Independent Schools and increasing the number of members chosen from lists provided by the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities.

Status: In the House - Returned Passed

bill_summary: This bill alters the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board by removing a member who is a certified nonpublic school classroom teacher chosen by the Association of Independent Schools and replacing them with a second representative from the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities. The two representatives from the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities must consist of one licensed special education teacher currently providing classroom instruction and one administrator or supervisory staff member.
responsible_party: Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board
stakeholders: Members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, the Association of Independent Schools, and the Maryland Association of Nonpublic Special Education Facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The changes to the composition of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board do not have an operational or financial effect on the State, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board (PSTEB) sets educational policies and certification standards for educators, which is a core function of the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). The bill explicitly states that the staff for the Board must be provided by the State Board of Education.

This office is responsible for the recruitment, vetting, and recommendation of candidates for state boards. The bill alters the specific statutory requirements for candidates and nominating organizations (shifting from nonpublic school teachers to representatives of special education facilities) that this office must manage for the Governor.

The Governor is the constitutional authority responsible for appointing the members of the Professional Standards and Teacher Education Board, and this bill modifies the legal composition of the board that the Governor must oversee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly modifies the permanent composition and membership requirements of an established executive board tasked with providing expertise on professional teacher standards.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system to receive information related to a school or student safety concern; requiring the Center to develop operational guidelines and procedures, and to provide training relative to the system; requiring each local school system to participate in the anonymous reporting system, subject to a certain exception; requiring a certain custodian of records to deny inspection of information and materials related the system; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to develop and administer an anonymous reporting system for school or student safety concerns. Local school systems are required to participate in this system by July 1, 2027, unless they operate a substantially similar system. The bill also ensures the anonymity of reporters by exempting information related to the system from public records inspection.
stakeholders: Maryland students, parents, school personnel, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact because the bill codifies existing practices. The Maryland Center for School Safety already operates the Safe Schools Maryland anonymous reporting system, and local school systems are already in compliance with the bill's requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Maryland Center for School Safety as the primary agency responsible for developing and administering the anonymous reporting system, creating operational guidelines, and providing training to school personnel.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is an independent unit within the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). The bill also tasks the Center with assisting the Department in evaluating safety data systems and preparing annual reports for public review.

As the chief legal representative for the state, the OAG provides counsel to MSDE and the Center. Additionally, the bill amends the Public Information Act within the General Provisions Article to protect reporting system records, which directly relates to the OAG's role in oversight and interpretation of the PIA.
The bill requires the Maryland Center for School Safety to submit summaries of reports on school resource officers and reports on life-threatening incidents to the Governor.

Synopsis: Altering the number of members on the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County; and altering the membership of the Board to reflect the change in Baltimore County councilmanic districts.
Title: Education - Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County - Membership
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill reduces the membership of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County from 15 to 11 members. It reconfigures the board's composition to include nine members, each representing one of the nine councilmanic districts, and two at-large members, aligning the board with the expanded Baltimore County Council district structure.
responsible_party: Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County
stakeholders: Members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County, the Governor of Maryland, the Maryland Senate, and the residents of Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no impact on State finances. Locally, the bill is expected to result in a minimal decrease in reimbursement expenditures for the Community College of Baltimore County beginning in fiscal 2027 due to the reduction in board size from 15 members to 11. Local revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the primary authority responsible for appointing the members of the Board of Community College Trustees for Baltimore County. This bill directly alters the composition and geographic requirements for those appointments.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for state boards and commissions. It will be responsible for managing the administrative transition, including handling term terminations and filling newly structured seats on the board.
As the central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, this agency oversees the community college system and its governance structures.
This agency is responsible for establishing statewide policies and overseeing the standards for public colleges and universities, including community colleges affected by governance changes.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and state boards. They may be involved in advising on the legal implementation of terminating board terms and redistricting trustee seats.
As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, the department monitors the administrative efficiency of state-appointed boards, although the bill has no direct impact on the state budget.

Synopsis: Requiring an applicant for appointment as a commissioner of a bicounty commission to submit a certain statement to the Prince George's County Office of Ethics and Accountability; requiring the chief administrative officer for Prince George's County to transmit the financial disclosure statements of commissioners or appointed applicants of bicounty commissions to the Office; and requiring the Office, rather than the chief administrative officer for Prince George's County, to take certain actions regarding the statements.
Title: Bicounty Commissions - Public Ethics - Financial Disclosure Statements PG/MC 105-26

bill_summary: This bill requires individuals applying for appointment as a commissioner of a bicounty commission in Prince George's County to submit financial disclosure statements to the Prince George's County Office of Ethics and Accountability. It transfers several administrative responsibilities, including the retention, return, and public inspection of these statements, from the county's chief administrative officer to the Office of Ethics and Accountability.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Office of Ethics and Accountability
stakeholders: Applicants for appointment as bicounty commissioners, current bicounty commissioners in Prince George's County, and members of the public interested in examining financial disclosure statements.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Locally, the bill does not materially affect government operations or finances, as it primarily shifts administrative duties regarding financial disclosure statements within Prince George's County. Specific dollar estimates for revenues or expenditures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the State Ethics Commission, as it requires the agency to receive electronic financial disclosure statements from bicounty commissioners and applicants, and mandates the deletion of these records for non-appointed applicants upon notification from local offices.

The Office of Appointments is responsible for recruiting and vetting candidates for state and bicounty boards and commissions. New financial disclosure filing requirements for applicants to these positions directly impact the vetting process and the information that must be collected from candidates.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for appointing members to various boards and commissions, including bicounty commissions; this bill alters the procedural requirements for those appointees and candidates.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a law enforcement officer from engaging in certain sexual acts, sexual contact, or vaginal intercourse with a student enrolled in a school where the law enforcement officer is assigned as a school resource officer; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction is subject to a term of imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine not exceed $3,000 or both.
Title: Criminal Law - School Resource Officers - Prohibition on Sexual Activity with Students
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill prohibits law enforcement officers assigned as school resource officers from engaging in sexual contact, vaginal intercourse, or sexual acts with students enrolled in the school where the officer is assigned. A violation is a misdemeanor punishable by up to three years in prison and/or a fine of up to $3,000.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and state and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: School resource officers, students enrolled in Maryland schools, local education agencies, and the Baltimore City School Police Force
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Individuals convicted of a violation are subject to a fine of up to $3,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 3 years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch, including the state agencies responsible for law enforcement and education. The Governor is also responsible for signing the bill into law.
The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies regarding the implementation and enforcement of new criminal laws.

MSDE oversees the state's public education system. As the bill concerns conduct by officers assigned to schools and references the Education Article, the department's policies regarding school safety and local school system coordination are directly impacted.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense punishable by up to three years of imprisonment. DPSCS would be responsible for the supervision or incarceration of individuals convicted under this statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises the Governor on public safety and criminal justice strategies, including policies related to law enforcement conduct and victim services.

MCSS is the primary state entity for school safety coordination and oversees the certification and training of school safety personnel, including school resource officers. They are directly involved in the oversight of the individuals targeted by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants. This bill creates a new criminal offense that their attorneys may be required to defend.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police troopers may serve as school resource officers and are subject to the conduct prohibitions established in the bill.
The AOC provides operational support to the state's courts, which will handle the prosecution and adjudication of cases arising from the new criminal prohibition.

Synopsis: Increasing the number of members on the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation from 9 to 12.

bill_summary: This bill increases the number of voting members on the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation from 9 to 12. It adjusts the board composition to require 7 lawyers and 5 nonlawyers and increases the number of votes needed to remove a board member from 7 to 9.
stakeholders: Maryland Legal Services Corporation, the Governor of Maryland, the Maryland State Senate, and lawyers admitted to the Bar in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State or local fiscal impact. According to the Fiscal Note, altering the composition of the board does not affect State operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is the statutory authority responsible for appointing the voting members of the Board of Directors of the Maryland Legal Services Corporation; this bill directly increases the number of appointments the Governor must make and maintain.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and recommending candidates for state boards and commissions; the expansion of the MLSC board from 9 to 12 voting members increases the administrative workload for this office in managing these specific appointments.

The Maryland Legal Services Corporation provides grants for civil legal assistance to low-income residents, which directly impacts the state's judicial system; additionally, the Administrative Office of the Courts was a primary source of information for the bill's fiscal note.

bill_summary: The Maryland Beverage Container Recycling Refund and Litter Reduction Program establishes a statewide deposit-return system for beverage containers made of glass, metal, or plastic. Starting in 2029, consumers will pay a 10-cent deposit on containers of 24 ounces or less and a 15-cent deposit on larger containers, which are refunded upon the return of the empty container to a retailer or redemption facility. The bill requires beverage producers to form a stewardship organization to manage the program, meet specific redemption and recycling performance targets, and finance the system through registration fees, unclaimed deposits, and scrap material sales.
stakeholders: Beverage producers, retailers, distributors, on-premises sellers (such as bars and restaurants), consumers, local governments, and material recovery facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by 360,800 in FY 2027 for Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) startup costs, which will be reimbursed by producer registration fees in FY 2028. Ongoing MDE administrative costs are estimated between 518,600 and 575,200 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2031, fully offset by special fund revenues from producer registration fees. Local governments may experience reduced revenue from scrap material sales, though the bill provides for compensation for documented net losses to local waste management systems through 2031. Ten percent of unclaimed deposits will be transferred to the Chesapeake Bay Trust to fund a new recycling grant program beginning in 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, MDE's Office of Recycling is responsible for administering the Maryland Beverage Container Recycling Refund and Litter Reduction Program, setting fees, approving stewardship plans, and enforcing compliance.
The bill explicitly designates the Chesapeake Bay Trust to administer the Beverage Container Recycling Refund Grant Program, which is funded by a portion of unclaimed deposits.
The fiscal note identifies that MES may be meaningfully affected by a reduction in revenues and demand for its recycling services in jurisdictions where it operates material recovery facilities.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to MDE for regulation development and handle civil and criminal enforcement actions; the fiscal note specifically allocates new legal positions for these tasks.
The State Highway Administration (SHA), a modal unit of MDOT, is expected to see fiscal impacts through potentially reduced costs for routine litter removal and remediation on state highways.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the State Recycling Trust Fund and establish a separate account for the fees and penalties collected under the new program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new permanent body, the Redeemable Beverage Container Recycling Refund Advisory Council, to advise MDE on program implementation and plan approval.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments involved and the Governor receives reports on the program's recommendations and impacts on county and municipal budgets.
The State Treasurer is responsible for holding the State Recycling Trust Fund and investing the money within it as part of their custodial duties for state funds.
DBM will oversee the personnel and budgetary aspects related to the five new state positions required at MDE to implement the program.
DGS, which manages state-owned facilities, may be impacted by the logistics of beverage container collection at state sites and as a consumer of beverages in its procurement role.
The judiciary will handle any civil actions, injunctive relief, or criminal prosecutions resulting from violations of the program's regulations.
Higher education institutions are identified in the fiscal note as potential grant recipients, redemption sites, or consumers affected by the refund deposit system.
As a state university, MSU may be impacted as a consumer of beverages, a potential grant recipient, or by hosting redemption infrastructure on its campus.
As an independent state unit, SMCM may be impacted as a consumer, potential grant recipient, or through requirements for on-site container management.

Synopsis: Establishing certain civil liability for an individual who, under color of law, deprives another of a right, a privilege, or an immunity secured by the U.S. Constitution.
Title: Civil Actions - Violation of Constitutional Rights (No Kings Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill creates a state-level civil cause of action allowing individuals to sue government officials or employees who, while acting under the color of law, deprive them of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured by the U.S. Constitution. Aggrieved parties may seek damages, declaratory relief, and injunctive relief, and the court is authorized to award reasonable attorney's fees and expert witness fees to prevailing plaintiffs.
responsible_party: Maryland State Treasurer’s Office and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Individuals whose constitutional rights are violated by government actors, state and local government employees, state agencies, local governments, and law firms specializing in civil rights litigation.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to cause a significant increase in state and local expenditures. For the state, personnel expenditures for the State Treasurer’s Office and the Office of the Attorney General are estimated to increase by $206,800 in FY 2027. Furthermore, special fund expenditures may rise significantly due to higher payments from the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) for claims and litigation, leading to higher general fund assessments for state agencies. Local governments face potentially significant increases in costs for litigation, judgment awards, and insurance premiums. Small business law firms may see a meaningful impact from increased litigation opportunities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which is responsible for paying claims and litigation expenses for state employees. The bill is expected to significantly increase claims and expenditures for the SITF, and the Treasurer's Office anticipates needing an additional claims investigator to handle the increased workload.

The OAG represents the state and its personnel in litigation. The bill's creation of a state-level civil rights cause of action will increase the OAG's litigation volume, and the fiscal note indicates the agency will require at least one additional Assistant Attorney General to handle cases and potential awards of attorney's fees.

The bill creates a new cause of action that will be litigated in state courts. Furthermore, the bill contains specific provisions regarding civil actions, injunctive relief, and the awarding of legal fees specifically against judicial officers.

As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, its officers frequently act 'under color of law' and are likely to be primary defendants in actions alleging the deprivation of constitutional rights under this new statute.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Personnel in correctional and pretrial facilities act under color of law; the bill's creation of a state-level civil rights remedy is highly relevant to litigation frequently brought regarding constitutional rights in detention and supervision settings.

The bill impacts MDOT through its law enforcement components, such as the MTA Police. The fiscal note explicitly highlights that MTA's tort liability is not subject to the same limits as the Maryland Tort Claims Act, increasing fiscal exposure for constitutional claims against its officers.

The Department oversees the Maryland Natural Resources Police (NRP). The fiscal note explicitly notes the bill's potential to increase litigation against individual NRP officers and impact the agency's operational and multi-jurisdictional efforts.

DBM oversees the budget and personnel assessments for all state agencies. Higher SITF losses from the bill will lead to increased insurance assessments against state agencies, directly impacting their general fund expenditures and budgetary planning.

DJS personnel who supervise youth in residential facilities act under color of law and are subject to constitutional liability, making the agency a likely subject of increased litigation under the bill's provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and coordinates public safety policies; changes in the legal liability and immunity standards for law enforcement officers directly impact state public safety policy and risk management.

The Commission is responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination and civil rights laws. This bill aligns with its mission by providing a statutory private right of action for individuals whose constitutional rights are violated by persons acting under color of law.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and its personnel. The Governor is also responsible for appointing judicial officers, who are specifically mentioned in the bill's provisions regarding liability and relief.

bill_summary: This bill establishes standardized procedures for political party central committees to follow when filling vacancies in the Maryland General Assembly. It requires a minimum seven-day application period, public advertisement of the vacancy (including translation into other languages if required by the federal Voting Rights Act), online posting of applications, public meetings for candidate interviews, and public votes conducted by roll call or signed ballot. It also mandates that any central committee member applying for the vacancy must recuse themselves from the selection process.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections and political party central committees
stakeholders: Political party central committees, individuals seeking appointment to the Maryland General Assembly, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Election Law Article and establishes requirements for political party central committees when filling vacancies in the General Assembly. As the agency responsible for supervising elections and ensuring compliance with election laws, the State Board of Elections is relevant to the administration and oversight of these new statutory procedures, particularly the translation requirements tied to local boards of elections.

Under the Maryland Constitution, the Governor is the final authority who appoints individuals to fill General Assembly vacancies based on recommendations from central committees. This bill regulates the transparency and procedural integrity of the process that generates those recommendations, directly impacting a constitutional duty overseen by the Governor's Office.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and state agencies regarding the implementation of state and constitutional laws. They would likely be involved in interpreting the interaction between these new statutory requirements and the Maryland Constitution, or defending the law if it is challenged by a political party.

bill_summary: This bill requires all bidders or offerors for State procurement contracts to certify that they and their affiliates are not engaging in any actions that violate the U.S. Constitution or the Maryland Constitution. Contractors must also agree to refrain from such violations for the duration of the contract, and a specific clause reflecting these requirements must be included in State procurement contracts.
responsible_party: State procurement officers and primary procurement units, including the Department of General Services and the Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: State procurement bidders, offerors, contractors, and their corporate affiliates and divisions
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note states there is no state fiscal impact, as the administrative requirements of the bill can be handled with existing budgeted resources. The bill does not materially affect local government finances, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central procurement authority, DGS is responsible for implementing the bill's requirements to obtain constitutional compliance certifications from bidders and include specific clauses in state contracts.

MDOT is a primary procurement unit that manages significant state contracts for transportation infrastructure and services, making it directly responsible for enforcing the bill's certification requirements.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts and ensures fiscal decisions follow state law; it would likely oversee the adoption of these new contract clauses in the COMAR regulations.
The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies on procurement matters and would be responsible for advising on the legal standard and language of the constitutional compliance certifications.
DBM is a principal agency for state fiscal and personnel matters and often plays a key role in statewide procurement policy and budget execution oversight.
USM has significant independent procurement authority and would need to implement these certification and contract clause requirements for its institutions.
DoIT manages major information technology procurements and would be required to integrate these constitutional certifications into its bidding and contracting processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Board of Contract Appeals
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MSBCA adjudicates bid protests and contract disputes; it may be called upon to resolve disagreements regarding the validity of a bidder's certification or contract terminations related to constitutional violations.
As a state university with its own Board of Regents and independent procurement activities, MSU would be responsible for complying with these new procurement regulations.
As an independent public honors college with separate procurement responsibilities, it would be required to include the mandated clauses in its contracts and verify bidder certifications.
OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits and would likely include the presence and documentation of these required certifications in their reviews of agency procurement processes.

Synopsis: Establishing that a private road open to public travel for 20 years or more shall be considered offered for dedication to public use; and establishing that the State, a county, or a municipality shall be considered to have accepted an offer for the dedication of a road to public use under the Act if the State, county, or municipality repairs and maintains the road in the same manner as a public road.
Title: Real Property - Dedication - Roads
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/05 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill establishes that a private road open to public travel for 20 years or more is considered offered for dedication to public use. It further provides that the State, a county, or a municipality is considered to have accepted the offer if they provide maintenance and repairs to the road in the same manner as a public road.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (State Highway Administration), counties, and municipalities
stakeholders: Private road owners, the general public, state and local government agencies, and small businesses in the road construction and maintenance sector.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund may increase significantly for the reconstruction and maintenance of roads. The State Highway Administration estimates that reconstruction can cost over 1,000,000 per lane mile and maintenance averages 11,700 per lane mile. A hypothetical scenario of 10 miles of road per year suggests annual costs of 10,600,000. Local governments face similar expenditure increases for road upkeep and potential liability exposure. Highway user revenue distributions among local jurisdictions may also be affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Highway Administration (SHA) by establishing criteria for the dedication and acceptance of private roads. The fiscal note specifically mentions that SHA would be responsible for reconstructing and maintaining these roads to meet state standards, resulting in significant potential expenditures for the Transportation Trust Fund.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration (SHA), MDOT is responsible for the Transportation Trust Fund, which the fiscal note identifies as being significantly impacted by the costs of maintaining and reconstructing newly dedicated roads.

The bill involves complex legal definitions of real property dedication and acceptance, as well as liability issues. The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies like MDOT and was consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note regarding current common law and statutory standards.

The bill has significant fiscal implications for the State's budget and long-term fiscal planning, particularly concerning the allocation of funds within the Transportation Trust Fund and potential shifts in state expenditures for road maintenance and liability.

The fiscal note indicates a potential reallocation of local highway user revenues among jurisdictions based on changes in road mileage. The Comptroller's office is responsible for the distribution of various state revenues and oversees fiscal integrity.

The bill modifies the legal framework for property dedication, which is a matter of common law often adjudicated in the courts. The Administrative Office of the Courts was a contributor to the fiscal note, reflecting the judiciary's role in interpreting property disputes and condemnations.

The Maryland Department of Planning is responsible for promoting sustainable growth and land use policy. Changes in the legal status of private roads to public use impact local and state planning, infrastructure development, and data analysis related to land use.

The Board of Public Works oversees the acquisition and transfer of state property. Establishing the acceptance of dedicated land into the state's inventory may involve oversight or procedural engagement by the Board.

Synopsis: Authorizing a District Court commissioner to issue a summons based on an application for a statement of charges filed by a certain individual under certain circumstances; prohibiting a District Court commissioner from issuing an arrest warrant based on an application for a statement of charges filed by a certain individual; requiring a District Court commissioner to refer a certain summons to the State's Attorney's office; requiring the District Court to provide victims of crime with access to certain information; etc.
Title: Criminal Procedure - District Court - Issuance of Summonses and Arrest Warrants
Status: In the Senate - Third Reading Passed with Amendments (35-11)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: The bill restricts District Court commissioners from issuing arrest warrants based on applications filed by civilians, authorizing them to issue summonses instead. It requires these applications to be referred to the State's Attorney for review to determine if an arrest warrant is necessary. Additionally, the bill increases the maximum jail sentence for making false reports of crimes, mandates restitution for such offenses, and requires the Maryland Judiciary to collect and report annual data on charging documents.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and State's Attorney's Offices
stakeholders: Judicial officials, State's Attorneys, law enforcement officers, crime victims, and individuals filing or subject to criminal statement of charges.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $276,010 in fiscal 2027 for one-time computer programming related to data reporting and cross-agency process tracking. Local State's Attorney's offices will experience operational impacts from the required review period for civilian-initiated summonses, though significant fiscal impacts are not anticipated for local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) is highly relevant as it provides operational and technological support to the Maryland Judicial Branch. The bill requires the Maryland Judiciary to conduct one-time computer programming ($276,000 cost) to track summonses and warrants, and mandates that the Judiciary submit an annual report to the General Assembly disaggregated by county, race, sex, and age.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this agency is relevant because the bill fundamentally alters the criminal procedure for issuing summonses and arrest warrants and increases penalties for false reports.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is relevant because the bill changes the procedure by which criminal cases are initiated and charges are issued, directly impacting the defendants they represent. The bill also increases the criminal penalty and requires mandatory restitution for false statements.

The bill explicitly defines 'police officers' as individuals who retain the authority to file for arrest warrants through District Court commissioners, unlike civilian applicants. Changes to these filing practices and the referral process for civilian complaints affect law enforcement operations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is relevant because it manages the state's correctional facilities, pretrial detention, and the Division of Parole and Probation. Changes in the issuance of arrest warrants versus summonses impact detention intake and the enforcement of court-ordered restitution.

The OAG is the chief legal representative for the state and provides counsel to state agencies on criminal laws and procedures. They also represent the state in criminal appeals, which may arise from the interpretation of these new summons and warrant procedures.
DBM is relevant because the bill requires a $276,000 increase in general fund expenditures for the Judiciary to implement computer programming and tracking systems.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Governor's final approval and involves the administration of justice, which is a key policy area for the executive branch.

bill_summary: This bill requires county boards of education to submit an annual Student Residency and School Zones Report to the Maryland Department of Planning and the Interagency Commission on School Construction. The report must include school zone boundaries, student residence locations, and school capacity details. The bill also limits the impact of local Adequate Public Facilities Ordinances (APFOs) by preventing them from delaying the processing and completion of subdivision or site development plans based on school capacity, though the issuance of final permits may still be delayed.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning, Interagency Commission on School Construction, and County Boards of Education
stakeholders: County boards of education, housing developers, local governments, and the Interagency Commission on School Construction
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill imposes administrative costs on county boards of education to generate annual reports and on the Interagency Commission on School Construction to adopt regulations and manage submissions. Local jurisdictions may see impacts on development timelines due to restrictions on Adequate Public Facilities Ordinances. Because the formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires county boards of education to submit annual Student Residency and School Zones Reports to the Commission and tasks the Commission with adopting regulations for the formatting and submission of these reports.

The bill mandates that county boards of education submit school residency and zone reports to the Department of Planning, which aligns with its mission to provide data analysis and policy guidance for sustainable growth and land use.

As the agency responsible for oversight and leadership of the 24 local school systems, the Department of Education is relevant because the bill imposes new reporting requirements on those local boards regarding student population and school capacity.

The bill impacts housing development by prohibiting local adequate public facilities ordinances (APFOs) from delaying the processing and completion of subdivision or site development plans based on school capacity.

The agency is responsible for linking and analyzing student data to inform policy decisions; the new reporting requirement for student residency and school capacity data provides relevant information for its longitudinal analysis.

The Authority is involved in the design and construction of public schools through specific state programs; changes to school capacity reporting and land use ordinances related to schools may impact their project planning.
The OAG would likely provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of the new reporting requirements and the interpretation of the restrictions on local adequate public facilities ordinances.

bill_summary: This bill alters and expands the jurisdiction of the Maryland Capitol Police (MCP) within the Department of General Services. It increases the law enforcement radius around State-owned or State-leased buildings from 1,000 feet to 2,000 feet and grants MCP officers statewide authority to investigate and enforce criminal, parking, and motor vehicle laws, provided they comply with notification requirements for other relevant law enforcement agencies.
stakeholders: Maryland Capitol Police, public officials, state employees, and local law enforcement agencies including the Baltimore Police Department and Maryland State Police.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the expansion of jurisdiction for the Maryland Capitol Police is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Capitol Police is a unit within the Department of General Services. This bill directly expands the jurisdiction, powers, and administrative responsibilities of this unit, making DGS the primary implementing agency.

The bill requires the Maryland Capitol Police to provide notification to the Secretary of State Police reasonably in advance of investigations or enforcement actions taken under their new statewide authority.
The bill maintains the Board of Public Works' authority to designate public improvements or grounds over which the Maryland Capitol Police have jurisdiction.

The bill specifically identifies the Chief of Police of the Maryland Department of Health Secured Transport and Investigation Unit as an official who must receive notification following certain enforcement actions by the Capitol Police.

The bill specifically identifies the Superintendent of the Maryland Department of Natural Resources Police as an official who must receive notification following certain enforcement actions by the Capitol Police.

The bill specifically identifies the Chief of Police of the Maryland Transit Administration Police Force (a unit of MDOT) as an official who must receive notification following certain enforcement actions by the Capitol Police.

The Maryland Capitol Police are responsible for the protection of public officials, including those within the Executive Department. The expansion of their statewide jurisdiction and authority over the protection of these individuals is relevant to the office's oversight and security.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the OAG will likely be involved in drafting the required memoranda of understanding (MOU) with Baltimore City and advising on the regulations and policies for the new statewide jurisdiction.

The bill repeals specific jurisdictional language regarding buildings previously administered by the Maryland Department of Labor, consolidating them under the general category of State-owned or State-leased buildings.

bill_summary: This bill enters Maryland into the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact, allowing school psychologists licensed in a member state to obtain equivalent licenses to practice in other member states. It establishes the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission to oversee the compact, handle dispute resolution, and facilitate information exchange between participating states.
stakeholders: Licensed school psychologists, Maryland public and state-approved nonpublic schools, and students receiving school psychological services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) general fund expenditures increase by $30,000 in FY 2027 for one-time state licensure system enhancements, plus $7,000 annually for compact participation fees. There is a potential minimal increase in state revenue from a $10 license fee. Local school systems may see improved recruitment of school psychologists, though there is no direct impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency. It is responsible for licensing school psychologists, representing Maryland on the Compact Commission, managing information sharing, and handling disciplinary investigations. The fiscal note specifies $37,000 in MSDE expenditures for system upgrades and participation fees.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MSDE and the General Assembly. This bill enters Maryland into a legally binding interstate compact involving regulatory cooperation, rulemaking, and potential legal proceedings in which the OAG would represent the state's interests.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires applicants for multistate licensure to undergo criminal background checks. The fiscal note explicitly mentions that the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), located within DPSCS, will collect fees and process these state and national checks.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for oversight of the state budget and expenditures. The bill requires a one-time general fund expenditure of $30,000 and recurring annual fees of $7,000, which must be managed through DBM's budget execution processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the School Psychologist Interstate Licensure Compact Commission, a new joint government agency composed of representatives from member states to oversee the compact's administration, rulemaking, and enforcement.

Section 5 of the Compact specifically addresses the licensure and relocation needs of active military members and their spouses, facilitating their ability to practice school psychology across state lines, which aligns with the DVMF mission to support military families.

The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies implementing the compact and receives notifications regarding default, suspension, or termination of the state's membership in the compact. The Governor is also responsible for appointing the state's commissioner to the Compact Commission.

The fiscal note identifies $30,000 in costs for one-time enhancements to the state's licensure system. DoIT oversees state IT strategy and infrastructure and would likely coordinate or approve these technological modifications to MSDE's systems.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) oversees behavioral health services and regulates health care professionals. While MSDE is the lead, MDH was consulted for the fiscal note and shares a policy interest in the availability of mental health professionals like school psychologists.

The GOC focuses on the well-being and health services of Maryland's children. Expanding the pool of available school psychologists through interstate licensure directly impacts access to mental and behavioral health services for children, a key priority for this office.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in selecting and vetting individuals for state boards and commissions. This office will be involved in the process of identifying a qualified individual to serve as Maryland's Commissioner on the Compact Commission.

bill_summary: This bill requires retail service station dealers to prominently display the 'standard price' for motor fuel—defined as the price available to all customers without conditions—on their signage. bill_summary: The Affordable Solar Act alters the State's renewable energy portfolio standard (RPS) to include specific targets for energy generated from qualifying distributed and utility-scale solar systems. It authorizes the purchase and installation of portable residential solar energy systems, creates a new category of solar renewable energy credits (SREC-IIs), and mandates the Public Service Commission (PSC) to procure 4,000 megawatts of additional solar capacity by 2036. The bill also establishes an escrow account to manage alternative compliance payments and redirects a portion of public service company franchise tax revenue to support solar initiatives.
stakeholders: Electric companies, electricity suppliers, solar energy developers, residential and industrial electricity customers, and clean energy craft workers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill redirects 75% of the public service company franchise tax revenue collected from customers using more than 100 megawatts of electricity from the General Fund to a new solar escrow account. It also redirects alternative compliance fees from the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund to the same escrow account. The PSC must manage the procurement of 4,000 megawatts of solar capacity, with a legislative cap on net residential ratepayer cost increases limited to 5% of the average annual electric bill. Specific total dollar estimates are unavailable in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Public Service Commission as the primary regulatory and administrative body for the Affordable Solar Act. The PSC is tasked with implementing the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard changes, issuing solicitations for 4,000 MW of solar capacity, establishing and administering the Distributed Solar Facilities Incentive Program and the Utility-Scale SREC-II Program, and determining SREC/SREC-II obligations for electric companies.

The bill significantly impacts the Maryland Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is managed by the MEA. It redirects alternative compliance fees (ACFs) that currently flow into the SEIF to a new escrow account for solar procurement. This represents a major fiscal shift for MEA's primary funding source.

The bill requires that utility-scale solar projects selected under the program include community benefit agreements and pay prevailing wages. It specifically requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to determine prevailing wage rates for these projects and mandates the use of registered apprenticeship programs overseen by the department.

The bill establishes a new nonbypassable surcharge on customer utility bills to recover costs associated with SREC and SREC-II purchases. As the advocate for residential utility consumers, the Office of the People's Counsel will be responsible for representing consumer interests regarding these new charges and the overall ratepayer impact of the solar incentive programs.

The bill alters the allocation of the Public Service Company Franchise Tax, requiring that 75% of revenues from customers using more than 100 MW of electricity be allocated to a specific escrow account rather than the General Fund. As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for managing these state revenues.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the state budget by redirecting revenue from both the Strategic Energy Investment Fund and the General Fund (via franchise tax) into a new escrow account. DBM is the principal agency for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the policy initiatives regarding renewable energy and the coordination of the state budget, both of which are significantly altered by the Affordable Solar Act. The office also coordinates the policy initiatives and intergovernmental relations related to the state's energy goals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and the Maryland Energy Administration. This bill will require significant legal support for drafting new regulations, reviewing solicitation documents, and interpreting the complex new statutory requirements for SREC-II procurement and labor compliance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires utility-scale solar project applications to include community benefit agreements that promote opportunities for local, small, minority, women-owned, and veteran-owned businesses. This office monitors and implements the state's socioeconomic procurement programs related to these business types.

The bill mandates the solicitation of 2,000 MW of utility-scale solar, which involves significant land use planning and coordination with local governments. The Department of Planning provides data analysis and policy guidance on sustainable growth and resource management related to such developments.

As the state's official green bank, the MCEC is tasked with advancing the adoption of clean energy and energy efficiency products. The creation of a massive new solar procurement and incentive framework directly impacts the market for clean energy financing in which MCEC operates.

The bill requires the PSC to recognize the environmental and public health benefits of solar projects located on brownfields or contaminated sites. MDE is the state's primary agency for environmental protection and restoration and oversees the remediation of such sites.

The Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works and acts as the state's chief financial agency. The bill involves significant shifts in state fund management, tax revenue allocation, and the creation of an escrow system, which falls under the Treasurer's broader responsibility for managing and protecting state funds.

The bill specifically references DGS's energy sales in Section 7-705. As the agency responsible for sustainability and energy conservation initiatives for state-owned facilities, the DGS is impacted by changes to the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard and SREC procurement rules.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that certain public safety employees, including paid firefighters and members of the State Fire Marshal's office, who suffer from hypertension are presumed to have a compensable occupational disease and are presumed to be disabled if they meet specific criteria. To qualify, an individual must be diagnosed by an authorized provider, have been prescribed medication for hypertension for at least 90 consecutive days, have completed two years of cumulative service in the state, and be employed in a relevant role at the time of the claim.
responsible_party: Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission, Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, and state and local government employers of public safety personnel
stakeholders: Paid firefighters, firefighting instructors, rescue squad members, advanced life support unit members, sworn members of the Office of the State Fire Marshal, and state and local government employers
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government expenditures, as well as Chesapeake Employers’ Insurance Company expenditures, may increase minimally starting in fiscal 2027 due to the expanded occupational disease presumption for hypertension. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the principal fiscal and personnel agency for the state, DBM is responsible for managing state employee benefits and supervising the budget execution for any increased expenditures resulting from workers' compensation claims.

MDOT is the parent agency for modal administrations such as the Maryland Aviation Administration, whose firefighters and rescue personnel are specifically impacted by the expanded occupational disease presumption.

The Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (now Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) acts as the third-party administrator for all workers' compensation claims filed by State of Maryland employees and will handle the additional claims resulting from this bill.
The bill explicitly covers paid firefighters and rescue personnel employed by an airport authority; the MAA operates BWI and Martin State Airport and employs these personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and regulates the statewide EMS network, including the rescue squads and advanced life support units whose members are granted the hypertension presumption.

The Maryland State Police houses the Office of the State Fire Marshal, and sworn members of that office are specifically granted the hypertension occupational disease presumption by this legislation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and represents the state in civil matters, including defending against or managing contested workers' compensation claims.
The bill references collective bargaining agreements as potential exceptions to certain benefit limitations, which falls under the regulatory purview of PERB for public sector labor relations.

The Commission is the primary agency responsible for administering the Workers' Compensation Law, adopting regulations to define 'authorized providers,' and adjudicating the claims established by this presumption.

The SIF investigates workers' compensation claims involving pre-existing conditions that increase disability; hypertension claims often involve such complexities and frequently require SIF involvement.
