Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill updates the terminology used for State parks that preserve and interpret the history of underrepresented populations, specifically removing the word "historical" from the titles of "State historical parks," "Freedman’s State Historical Park," and "Port of Deposit State Historical Park" while maintaining their original historical purposes and missions.
stakeholders: Underrepresented communities (including African American, Asian, Indigenous or Native American, and Hispanic or Latino populations), local governments in Montgomery County, Baltimore City, and Cecil County, and the Maryland Park Service.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances. According to the fiscal note, signs and publications have not yet been produced for the renamed parks, so there are no associated replacement costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary agency responsible for managing the State park system and implementing the terminology changes and park establishments mandated by the bill.

The Secretary of Planning and the Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is housed within this department, are designated members of the stakeholder advisory committee for Port Deposit State Park.
The Secretary of Commerce is designated as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee for the newly established Port Deposit State Park.

The Secretary of the Environment serves on the stakeholder advisory committee for Port Deposit State Park, and the Commission on Environmental Justice and Sustainable Communities provides input on the establishment of State parks.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration, a modal agency of MDOT, is designated as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee for Port Deposit State Park.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration is specifically named as a member of the stakeholder advisory committee for the Port Deposit State Park.

The agency oversees several ethnic and cultural commissions, such as the Commission on Indian Affairs and the Commission on Asian Pacific American Affairs, which are required to provide input on the establishment of specific State parks.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates input from several existing commissions and establishes new stakeholder advisory committees to oversee the management and scope of Freedman's State Park and Port Deposit State Park.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments and commissions involved in park establishment and is responsible for policy coordination related to the state's natural and historical resources.

Synopsis: Prohibiting provisions of the governing documents of a condominium or homeowners association from unreasonably restricting the governing body from installing or authorizing the installation of electric vehicle recharging equipment; establishing that the installation or authorization of electric vehicle recharging equipment by a governing body is subject to certain budget processes of the condominium or homeowners association for a common area renovation or alteration similar in cost or magnitude; applying the Act retroactively; etc.
Title: Condominiums and Homeowners Associations - Governing Documents - Electric Vehicle Recharging Equipment
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill prohibits condominium and homeowners association (HOA) governing documents from unreasonably restricting the association's governing body from installing or authorizing electric vehicle (EV) charging equipment in common or limited common use parking areas. It mandates that such installations follow the association's standard budget process for similar common area renovations and requires the governing body to consider the community's parking needs. Additionally, it allows governing bodies to grant three-year renewable licenses for the equipment and electricity supply, and the provisions apply retroactively to existing governing documents.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of condominiums and homeowners associations
stakeholders: Residents, unit owners, and lot owners in condominiums and homeowners associations; governing boards of common ownership communities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. The fiscal note indicates that small business impacts are minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division is responsible for enforcing laws related to consumer rights and often provides guidance on homeowners association (HOA) and condominium disputes. This bill directly alters the enforcement of covenants and restrictions within these communities.

The Maryland Energy Administration is tasked with promoting renewable energy and energy efficiency. This bill aligns with their mission by facilitating the expansion of electric vehicle (EV) recharging infrastructure within residential common ownership communities.

The Secretary of State's office is responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums. Since the bill mandates changes to how condominium governing documents address EV equipment, it falls within their regulatory and records oversight purview.
The bill establishes new legal standards for governing documents and applies them retroactively, which may lead to litigation or requests for judicial interpretation within the court system.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and signs legislation into law. This bill touches on environmental policy and housing regulation, which are key areas of executive policy coordination.

The Department of Planning promotes sustainable growth and provides land use guidance. The integration of EV charging in community parking structures is a component of modern sustainable residential planning.

Synopsis: Adding Class B (on-sale) beer and wine and Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses to the list of alcoholic beverages licenses for which the prohibition against issuing multiple licenses for the same person or premises in Prince George's County does not apply.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Multiple Licenses Prohibition - Exceptions PG 313-26
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill allows individuals or entities in Prince George's County to hold multiple Class B (on-sale) beer and wine licenses or Class B (on-sale) beer, wine, and liquor licenses by exempting these categories from the general prohibition against holding multiple alcoholic beverages licenses.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurant and hotel owners in Prince George’s County, alcoholic beverage license applicants, and the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Prince George's County revenues will increase based on the number of new licenses issued; Class B beer and wine licenses have an annual fee of $365, while Class B beer, wine, and liquor licenses have an annual fee of $2,305. The county can handle additional enforcement with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the principal state official responsible for regulating the alcohol, tobacco, and motor fuel industries and collecting related state revenues. This bill directly modifies alcoholic beverages licensing restrictions, which falls within the agency's broader regulatory and tax collection oversight for the industry.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides counsel on the implementation and interpretation of state laws, including the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article. The agency is responsible for ensuring that amendments to the state code are legally sound and providing guidance to executive bodies on these changes.

As the chief executive, the Governor signs legislation into law and oversees the administrative support for the executive branch. This bill specifically impacts local alcoholic beverages licensing rules within Prince George's County, requiring the Governor's final review and signature.

The Maryland Department of Commerce is tasked with retaining and expanding existing companies and stimulating the state's economy. By allowing business entities to hold multiple Class B alcoholic beverages licenses, the bill facilitates the growth and expansion of hospitality and restaurant businesses in Prince George's County.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County from approving the transfer or sale of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license; requiring a Class A license holder to return the license to the Board if the license expires or the license holder no longer wishes to hold the license; and prohibiting the Board from reissuing a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages Licenses - Prohibition on Transfer of Class A Beer, Wine, and Liquor License PG 314-26
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Government, Labor, and Elections; Withdrawn
bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners from approving the transfer or sale of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license. It requires license holders to return the license to the board if it expires or is no longer wanted and prohibits the board from reissuing such licenses.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class A beer, wine, and liquor license holders in Prince George's County and the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state impact and does not materially affect Prince George's County finances or operations. While Class A licenses carry a $910 annual fee, the prohibition on transfers and reissuance is not expected to significantly impact county revenue or operations, and the small business impact is considered minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary state-level agency responsible for regulating the alcoholic beverages industry. This bill significantly changes the regulatory framework for Class A licenses in Prince George's County by prohibiting their transfer, sale, or reissuance, which falls within the Comptroller's broader industry oversight.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies and boards. They would be responsible for interpreting these changes to the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article and defending the state against potential legal challenges regarding the prohibition of the sale of business assets (licenses).

The bill impacts small businesses and the local economy in Prince George's County by prohibiting the transfer or sale of Class A licenses, which are valuable business assets. This affects business succession planning and the economic viability of certain retail establishments.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs all legislation into law. This bill directly regulates a board that operates under state statutory authority granted by the General Assembly and the Executive.

Synopsis: Authorizing Prince George's County to retain, by local law, a portion of a certain fee, not to exceed 10 cents for each bag, that retail establishments in the county are required by local law to charge a customer for providing a single-use or reusable carryout bag.
Title: Prince George's County - Authority to Retain Fee for Single-Use and Reusable Bags PG 403-26
Status: In the House - First Reading Government, Labor, and Elections and Economic Matters

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Prince George’s County to enact local legislation allowing the county to retain a portion of the fee (up to 10 cents per bag) that retail establishments charge customers for single-use or reusable carryout bags. The funds collected by the county under this authority must be directed to the county’s General Fund.
stakeholders: Retail establishments and customers in Prince George’s County
fiscal_impact_summary: Prince George's County may experience an increase in General Fund revenue from retaining up to 10 cents per carryout bag fee. The total fiscal impact is indeterminate as it is contingent upon the county enacting a local law and the subsequent volume of bag sales; a formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor must review and sign this bill into law; the office also coordinates policy initiatives that may include local sustainability efforts.
As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller monitors point-of-sale transactions and fees that may intersect with sales tax administration or retail auditing.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state and reviews the legality of legislation, ensuring that the proposed expansion of local government fiscal authority is consistent with state law.
This bill impacts the economic operations of retail establishments in Prince George's County, which falls under Commerce's mission to support and advise the state's business community.
The bill relates to land and water quality by discouraging single-use bags through fiscal policy, aligning with the department's mission of environmental protection and waste reduction.
Planning provides data analysis and policy guidance to local governments regarding sustainable growth and effective resource management.
This multi-agency initiative coordinates efforts to reduce the state's carbon footprint and promote environmental preservation, which is supported by legislation targeting bag waste.

Synopsis: Altering the jurisdiction of the juvenile court by repealing provisions specifying that the juvenile court does not have jurisdiction over a child alleged to have committed any crime punishable by life imprisonment.
Title: Juvenile Court - Jurisdiction (Youth Charging Reform Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: The Youth Charging Reform Act expands the jurisdiction of the juvenile court by repealing provisions that automatically sent children charged with certain serious crimes—including kidnapping, robbery, and various firearm offenses—to adult criminal court. Under the bill, these cases will now originate in juvenile court, though children 16 and older charged with crimes punishable by life imprisonment will still be excluded from juvenile jurisdiction and tried in adult court.
stakeholders: Juveniles under the age of 18 charged with criminal offenses, the Department of Juvenile Services, the Office of the Public Defender, and local State's Attorneys' offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Public Defender are estimated to decrease by as much as $1,400,000 in FY 2027 and $1,850,000 annually thereafter due to a reduction in adult court transfer hearings. The Department of Juvenile Services may experience significant cost savings from operational efficiencies, though these could be partially offset by an increased demand for juvenile services. Local expenditures for State's Attorneys' offices are expected to increase significantly, with several jurisdictions reporting the need for dozens of additional personnel to manage the shifted caseload and expedited juvenile timelines.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly expands juvenile court jurisdiction, directly shifting more youth from the adult system into the care, supervision, and rehabilitative programs of the Department of Juvenile Services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a significant potential decrease in agency expenditures of up to $1.4 million due to a projected 75% reduction in mandatory juvenile transfer hearings.
The bill alters the original jurisdiction of the court system for specific crimes committed by youth, requiring significant operational and administrative updates across the judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The jurisdictional shift is expected to reduce the number of youth held in adult pretrial detention centers and sentenced to adult correctional facilities managed by the department.
The bill modifies the definition of 'reportable offenses' in the Education Article, which is a core component of the agency's mission to manage school safety reporting and data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary coordinating body for public safety, this agency advises on criminal justice strategies and manages funding for programs that support youth involved in the justice system.
The bill amends the Education Article regarding the definition and reporting of off-campus offenses, impacting state education policy and safety protocols for local school systems.
The agency is involved in the reporting of delinquency adjudications and the state-mandated fingerprinting of children for certain delinquent acts identified in the bill.
As the chief legal officer, the OAG provides counsel to executive agencies and the Governor on the implementation of these significant changes to criminal and juvenile procedure.
The department is responsible for overseeing the significant fiscal shifts and resource reallocations between the adult and juvenile justice systems identified in the fiscal note.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates high-level policy initiatives, including major reforms to the state's juvenile justice and criminal laws.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements and prohibitions regarding food labeling; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health, in conjunction with the University of Maryland Extension and food donation organizations, to create educational materials to inform consumers about the meaning of quality dates and safety dates for food labels by July 1, 2028, and to post the information on the Department's website.
Title: Public Health - Food Labeling - Requirements
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes standardized labeling requirements for food items to communicate quality and safety dates, specifically requiring terms like 'Best if Used By' for quality dates and 'Use By' for safety dates. It prohibits the use of 'Sell By' dates for retail consumers on food manufactured after July 1, 2028, and requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop educational materials to inform consumers about the meaning of these labels.
stakeholders: Food manufacturers, processors, retailers, consumers, food donation organizations, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $125,000 in FY 2027 and $125,000 in FY 2028 for contractual services to develop educational materials and update regulations. Local health departments may experience increased expenditures to enforce retailer compliance. Small businesses involved in food manufacturing and retail will be required to comply with new labeling standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency for this bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations, creating an educational program and materials in conjunction with partners, and maintaining information on its website. The fiscal note identifies a $250,000 general fund expenditure for MDH over two years for contractual services related to food science research and marketing.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Health create educational materials and programs in conjunction with the University of Maryland Extension, which is the outreach and education arm of the University of Maryland, College Park, a USM institution.

The bill establishes specific labeling requirements for 'Grade A milk products' and food manufactured or processed in Maryland. The Department of Agriculture supports the economic viability of the state's farming and agribusiness sectors, including dairy and food quality assurance, which are directly impacted by these new regulatory standards.

The fiscal note indicates a potentially 'meaningful' impact on small businesses, including food manufacturers, processors, and retailers, who must comply with the new labeling prohibitions (such as the 'Sell by' date ban) and standard terms. Commerce is the state's primary agency for business retention and economic development.

The Office of the Attorney General will be required to provide legal counsel to the Department of Health during the development of new regulations and the implementation of the enforcement framework for the labeling requirements and prohibitions.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for overseeing the $125,000 annual general fund expenditure in FY 2027 and FY 2028 required for the Maryland Department of Health to implement the bill's provisions.

As the manager of the state's major wholesale produce and seafood markets, the Authority is relevant because the businesses operating within its facilities must comply with the new labeling standards and the prohibition on 'Sell by' dates for food items sold or distributed to consumers.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of the standard deduction allowed for certain individuals from $3,350 to $4,100 under the Maryland income tax; and applying the Act to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Standard Deduction - Alteration
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill increases the Maryland individual income tax standard deduction from $3,350 to $4,100 for individual filers and from $6,700 to $8,200 for heads of household, surviving spouses, and joint filers. It also adjusts the cost-of-living indexing mechanism by setting 2025 as the new base year for annual standard deduction adjustments starting in tax year 2027.
stakeholders: Maryland individual income taxpayers, including single filers, heads of household, surviving spouses, and spouses filing joint returns.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a decrease in State and local income tax revenues due to the increased standard deduction amounts. fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a licensure exemption for certain property managers, which is expected to result in a decrease in licensing fee revenue for the State Collection Agency Licensing Board. However, specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the associated Fiscal and Policy Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly concerns the State Collection Agency Licensing Board, which is a regulatory unit within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department is responsible for the licensing and regulation of various professions and financial industries, including collection agencies.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor and its licensing boards. Furthermore, the OAG's Consumer Protection Division enforces laws regarding debt collection practices, which are directly impacted by new licensing exemptions for property managers.

As the agency responsible for supporting rental housing and ensuring residents have access to secure housing, DHCD is impacted by legislation that defines and regulates the activities of property managers in their interactions with residential tenants regarding rent and fee collection.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. If a property manager's status or eligibility for this licensing exemption is challenged by the Department of Labor, the OAH would likely handle the resulting administrative hearing.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a landlord from using certain algorithmic devices to determine the amount of rent to charge for, occupancy levels of, and lease terms and conditions for a residential dwelling unit; making a violation of the Act an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Residential Leases - Use of Algorithmic Device by Landlord to Determine Rent, Occupancy, and Lease Terms - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits residential landlords from using algorithmic software to set rent, occupancy levels, or lease terms if that software relies on nonpublic competitor data. Such use is classified as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, making it subject to the state's existing enforcement mechanisms and civil penalties.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Residential landlords, tenants, property management companies, and developers of rent-pricing software.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific fiscal estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill creates a new violation under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which may lead to an indeterminate increase in State general fund revenue from civil penalties and potential enforcement-related expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly makes the use of certain algorithmic devices by landlords an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act. The Office of the Attorney General is the primary agency responsible for enforcing this Act through its Consumer Protection Division.

As the state's lead agency for residential housing policy and ensuring access to affordable housing, the Department of Housing and Community Development is directly impacted by regulations concerning how rent, occupancy, and lease terms are determined in the Maryland rental market.

The bill creates new prohibitions within the Real Property and Commercial Law articles and allows for enforcement and penalties. This is likely to result in increased civil litigation and enforcement actions that must be processed through the state judicial system.

Synopsis: Decreasing from eight to four the number of screens in a motion picture house above which the motion picture house is required to provide open movie captioning.
Title: Places of Public Accommodation - Open Movie Captioning
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc

bill_summary: This bill expands the requirement for motion picture theaters to provide open movie captioning by lowering the threshold for applicability. Under the bill, motion picture houses with four or more screens (reduced from the previous requirement of eight or more screens) must provide at least two open-captioned screenings per week for each movie during the first three weeks of its premiere, provided the movie is available with open captioning.
stakeholders: Owners and operators of motion picture houses with four or more screens, movie theater patrons, and individuals with hearing impairments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. Small business movie theaters with four to seven screens may experience a meaningful fiscal impact; revenues could potentially decrease if open captioning deters some viewers or increase if it attracts more hearing-impaired customers or other patrons who prefer captioning.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary state agency responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination laws in places of public accommodation. This bill directly amends the standards for public accommodations (motion picture houses) that the MCCR is charged with enforcing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency's mission is to promote the welfare of Deaf and hard of hearing residents by advocating for equal access to public resources and community life. The bill's requirement for expanded open movie captioning directly aligns with their primary advocacy goals and constituency.

The Department of Disabilities is the principal agency for coordinating services and ensuring inclusive policies for residents with disabilities. Improving accessibility in public spaces like movie theaters falls under their broad mandate for community living and inclusive settings.

The Office of Administrative Hearings was identified in the fiscal note as a source of information. It would be responsible for providing an impartial hearing process for any contested enforcement cases brought by the Commission on Civil Rights regarding movie captioning compliance.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was listed in the fiscal note as an information source. Any civil litigation resulting from the enforcement of these public accommodation laws would impact the state's judicial system.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and executive agencies like the Commission on Civil Rights. They would likely represent the state in civil appeals or litigation related to the enforcement of this statute.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies responsible for implementation and coordinates broad policy initiatives related to civil rights and disability services.

Synopsis: Increasing the compensation of the president, the vice president, and other members of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to be $25,000, $24,000, and $23,000, respectively; and increasing the scholarship award to $23,000 for a student member of the board who completes a full term on the board for a term that begins on or after July 1, 2029.
Title: Anne Arundel County Board of Education - Member Compensation and Student Member Scholarship - Increase
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill increases the annual compensation for the president, vice president, and members of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education by $8,000 each. It also increases the scholarship award for the student member of the board from $15,000 to $23,000 for terms beginning on or after July 1, 2029.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education
stakeholders: Members of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education and the student member of the board
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Anne Arundel County expenditures will increase by approximately $32,700 in fiscal 2029 and by $64,000 annually starting in fiscal 2030 to cover the increased salary and scholarship costs. The increases take effect at the start of the next term of office for elected members and for student terms beginning on or after July 1, 2029.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the leadership and oversight of Maryland's 24 local school systems, the Department of Education is relevant to legislation that amends the Education Article regarding the governance and compensation of local boards of education.

The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the General Assembly and oversees the execution of state laws, including those governing local school board structures.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Transportation, as part of the planning and implementation of certain major highway expansion projects, to perform an impact assessment of the project and develop and implement a corresponding multimodal transportation program; requiring the Department, beginning with the Consolidated Transportation Program for fiscal year 2028 through 2033, to evaluate certain major capital projects for their impact on greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle miles traveled; etc.
Title: Transportation - Major Highway Capacity Expansion Projects and Impact Assessments (Transportation and Climate Alignment Act of 2026)
Status: In the Senate - Laid Over (Senator Hershey) Adopted

Chesapeake Bay -see also- Chesapeake Bay Restoration

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to conduct impact assessments on major highway expansion projects costing over $100 million to measure their effect on greenhouse gas emissions and vehicle miles traveled. For projects that increase emissions, MDOT must implement multimodal transportation programs (such as transit, bicycle, and pedestrian infrastructure) to offset the impact, ensuring the net emissions are zero or negative. It also requires MDOT to evaluate all major capital projects in the Consolidated Transportation Program for climate impacts and set statewide and regional emission reduction targets.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, commuters, transportation industry contractors, and residents of overburdened and underserved communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures increase by $1.5 million in fiscal 2027 for the development of an impact assessment tool. Starting in fiscal 2028, annual expenditures increase by approximately $100,000 ($50,000 from the TTF and $50,000 in nonbudgeted funds for the Maryland Transportation Authority) to conduct project assessments. Long-term fiscal impacts may be significant, potentially reaching hundreds of millions or billions of dollars, to fund required multimodal mitigation projects or due to the deferral of highway projects that do not meet emission targets. There is no direct impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill, including performing impact assessments, developing multimodal transportation programs, and evaluating major capital projects for greenhouse gas and vehicle miles traveled impacts.

SHA is specifically required by the bill to issue reports before proceeding to final project planning phases for major highway projects and is the primary entity for highway capacity expansion projects.
As noted in the fiscal note, MDTA is expected to conduct similar impact assessments and evaluations for its toll-facility projects, with significant nonbudgeted fiscal impacts.
The bill aligns with the State's Climate Pollution Reduction Plan managed by MDE and utilizes community definitions (overburdened and underserved) established in the Environment Article.
The bill's offsetting activities include land use changes and transit-oriented development, which fall under the purview of MDP's sustainable growth and comprehensive planning mandates.
The bill involves greenhouse gas reduction targets, electrification of state vehicles, and solar energy generation on state property, all of which are coordinated or managed by MEA.
The bill has a significant fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund and requires long-term fiscal planning for offsetting multimodal transportation programs.
This multi-agency initiative coordinates the types of sustainable development, environmental protection, and community revitalization strategies mandated as offsets in the bill.
The OAG will provide legal counsel to MDOT and SHA in developing the new regulatory processes for capacity expansion impact assessments.
The BPW oversees and approves significant state contracts for the major transportation and multimodal infrastructure projects impacted by this legislation.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller will oversee the approval of significant contracts for projects and offsets mandated by the bill.
As a member of the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer will oversee the fiscal integrity and contract approval for major transportation expansion and mitigation projects.
The Governor oversees the executive branch departments (MDOT, MDE, MDP) implementing the climate alignment strategies and coordinates the underlying policy initiatives.
DGS manages state sustainability initiatives and was identified in the fiscal note as a source of information regarding the bill's impact.

Synopsis: Establishing the Adult Prison School Board Model Development Committee to develop a comprehensive plan for a school board system to oversee correctional education for individuals subject to the criminal and juvenile justice systems; and requiring the Committee to issue an interim report by June 1, 2027, and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by June 1, 2028.
Title: Adult Prison School Board Model Development Committee
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m. (Ways and Means)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Adult Prison School Board Model Development Committee to create a comprehensive plan for a school board system to oversee correctional education for individuals in the criminal and juvenile justice systems and to conduct a fiscal mapping project to determine funding requirements.
stakeholders: Individuals subject to the criminal and juvenile justice systems, Maryland State agencies including the Department of Labor and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, and nonprofit correctional reform organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $111,518 in FY 2027 and $98,760 in FY 2028 to hire one contractual position to support the committee's research, planning, and reporting mandates. There is no impact on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Department of Education is mandated to provide staff for the Committee and the State Superintendent of Schools is a named member of the committee. Additionally, the Department is responsible for the fiscal mapping and research required by the bill, with the fiscal note identifying a direct expenditure impact for contractual staffing within the department.

The Secretary of Labor is an ex-officio member of the committee. The Department's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning currently oversees the Office of Correctional Education, which provides the services that would be governed by the proposed school board system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Public Safety and Correctional Services is a member of the committee, and the agency manages the adult correctional facilities where the proposed school board would operate. The bill also specifically includes representation for Maryland Correctional Enterprises, which is a unit within this department.

The Superintendent for the Juvenile Services Education Program (JSEP), which is overseen by DJS, is a named member of the committee. The committee is tasked with developing a plan that oversees correctional education for individuals within the juvenile justice system.

The bill explicitly requires the committee to develop an independent relationship with DBM to establish and manage capital and operating budgets for the new school board system. DBM is also central to the required fiscal mapping project.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the committee's chair and several key members, and the committee must submit its interim and final reports to the Governor.

The Secretary of Higher Education is a named member of the committee, and the commission is suggested as a permanent member of the future school board. The committee's plan will likely involve post-secondary education standards which MHEC regulates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes a new temporary development committee tasked with specific study, planning, and recommendation duties, which fits the category of an executive committee or task force.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is Maryland's coordinating body for criminal justice policy and currently staffs the existing Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission, whose recommendations are reflected in this legislation.

The bill recommends that the Department of Information Technology be represented on the resulting school board system, reflecting the technical infrastructure needed for modern correctional education.
The Office of Appointments will be responsible for recruiting and vetting the individuals the Governor appoints to the new committee.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and commissions and would likely be involved in the legal formation and advisory work of the new committee and its comprehensive plan.

Synopsis: Renaming the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to be the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; renaming the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing to be the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing; and altering the membership of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
Title: Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing and Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing - Renaming
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill renames the Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing to be the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing, and similarly renames the Maryland Advisory Council on Deaf and Hard of Hearing. It expands the membership of the council to 19 members by adding the Secretary of Disabilities or a designee. The bill also requires that existing printed materials, such as letterhead and business cards, be used up before new ones with the updated name are printed.
responsible_party: Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing
stakeholders: Deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing individuals in Maryland, and the Maryland Department of Disabilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's state fiscal impact is minimal. Costs related to renaming the office and advisory council can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, as the bill mandates the use of current printed supplies until they are exhausted. The Maryland Department of Disabilities can also fulfill its new seat on the advisory council with existing resources. There is no impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's primary purpose is to rename this office to the Office of the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing and restructure its associated Advisory Council.
The Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is a unit within the Governor's Office, and the Behavioral Health Advisory Council mentioned in the bill is also located within the Office of the Governor.
The bill expands the membership of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing to include the Secretary of Disabilities or their designee.
The Superintendent of the Maryland School for the Deaf serves as a mandatory member of the renamed and expanded Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

The bill amends the Education Article regarding the Deaf Culture Digital Library, which is overseen by the Maryland State Library Agency, requiring coordination for sensitivity training and advisory board participation.
The Secretary of Aging or their designee is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

The bill amends the State Personnel and Pensions Article to clarify immediate vesting rights for the Director of the newly renamed Office, which falls under DBM's purview as the central personnel agency.
The State Superintendent of Schools is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
The Secretary of Health is a mandated member of the Advisory Council and the department must cooperate with the Office on specific programs related to individuals who are deafblind.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
The Secretary of Human Services is a mandated member of the Advisory Council and the department must cooperate with the Office on specific programs for individuals who are deafblind.
The Secretary of Labor is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

The Secretary of Transportation is a mandated member of the Advisory Council, and the Office Director serves on the State Coordinating Committee for Health and Human Services Transportation within MDOT.
The bill specifies vesting rights for the Director of the renamed Office within the state retirement system managed by this agency.
This office is responsible for the recruitment and vetting of the members appointed by the Governor to the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.
A representative from the Commission on Civil Rights is a mandated member of the Maryland Advisory Council on the Deaf, Deafblind, and Hard of Hearing.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to establish an enhanced reimbursement structure for Maryland Medicaid Assistance Program providers that deliver medical services to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities; and providing the Act is contingent on the availability of federal funds through the federal Health Equity for Adults with Disabilities (HEADs UP) Act or any other federal law or funding stream supporting health care equity for individuals with intellectual or developmental disabilities.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Individuals With Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities - Provider Reimbursement
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish an enhanced reimbursement structure for Medicaid providers who deliver medical services to individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. The structure is designed to provide higher reimbursement rates that account for the specialized training, additional time, and communication supports often required to treat this population. The bill's implementation is contingent upon the availability of federal funding through the Health Equity for Adults with Disabilities (HEADs UP) Act or similar federal sources.
stakeholders: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and healthcare providers participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid).
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in an increase in State expenditures to provide enhanced reimbursement rates to Medicaid providers, as well as a corresponding increase in federal fund revenues. However, the bill is explicitly contingent on the availability of federal funding from the HEADs UP Act or other federal streams; if federal funds are not made available by December 31, 2036, the act will be null and void. Because a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the text provided, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill explicitly directs MDH to establish an enhanced reimbursement structure, set rates, and adopt regulations for providers serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

As the principal state agency for coordinating and improving services for residents with disabilities, this department is directly impacted by changes to healthcare reimbursement structures intended to improve service capacity and clinical quality for its primary constituency.

The bill specifically requires the Maryland Department of Health to consult with the Office of the Attorney General to determine if federal funds are available through the HEADs UP Act or other streams, which is the triggering condition for the Act to take effect.

As the agency responsible for developing the state budget and supervising budget execution, DBM is heavily involved in any legislation that mandates changes to Medicaid reimbursement rates, which represent a significant portion of state expenditures.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including MDH. The bill's implementation depends on federal funding and executive branch coordination, aligning with the Governor's role in overseeing policy initiatives and the annual budget.

Synopsis: Authorizing under certain circumstances and requiring under certain circumstances the Motor Vehicle Administration to suspend the registration of motor vehicles involved in violations recorded by a speed monitoring system placed on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) in Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Speed Monitoring Systems - Maryland Route 210 - Penalties PG 306-26
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/18 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill authorizes and, under specific conditions involving multiple or high-value overdue citations, requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to suspend the registration of motor vehicles involved in speed monitoring system violations on Maryland Route 210 (Indian Head Highway) in Prince George’s County. To reinstate a registration suspended under the bill, the vehicle owner must pay all overdue civil penalties, fees, and court costs, as well as a $30 administrative fee to Prince George’s County.
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners traveling on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County, the Prince George's County government, and the State Highway Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures from fiscal 2027 through 2029 by encouraging the payment of overdue speed camera fines on Maryland Route 210; as a baseline, $334,456 in net revenue was remitted to the State from these cameras in fiscal 2023. General fund revenues will increase to the extent more citations are contested in court. Prince George's County will collect a $30 administrative fee for each registration reinstatement. The authorization for the speed monitoring systems on this route is currently scheduled to terminate on September 30, 2028.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes and requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to suspend motor vehicle registrations for unpaid or uncontested speed monitoring violations on Maryland Route 210. It also mandates that the MVA issue written notices to owners and submit annual reports to the General Assembly regarding these suspensions.

As noted in the fiscal note, fine revenues from speed cameras on Maryland Route 210 are remitted to the State Highway Administration (SHA). Because this bill increases enforcement mechanisms (suspensions), it is expected to increase fine collections, thereby increasing the revenue available to SHA for safety improvements on that specific highway.

The bill's enhanced enforcement measures for speed monitoring citations are expected to increase the number of contested cases in the District Court, which falls under the oversight of the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The bill provides that vehicle owners whose registrations are suspended may request a hearing under Title 12, Subtitle 2 of the Transportation Article, which involves the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) and its administrative law judges.

As the parent department for both the Motor Vehicle Administration and the State Highway Administration, the Department of Transportation oversees the modal administrations responsible for implementing the bill's registration suspension mandates and managing the resulting safety improvement funds.

The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for receiving net fine revenues from the county and distributing them to the State Highway Administration, a process that will see increased volume due to the bill's enforcement provisions.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Motor Vehicle Administration and would represent the agency in the event of legal challenges to the registration suspension process or administrative appeals.

Synopsis: Requiring nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives to notify each resident and prospective resident in writing or by written electronic communication if the nursing home, assisted living program, nurse midwife, or licensed certified midwife either does not maintain professional liability insurance or professional liability insurance coverage has lapsed; and requiring conspicuous posting of the information that the professional liability coverage has not been maintained.
Title: Professional Liability Insurance Coverage - Nursing Homes, Assisted Living Facilities, Nurse Midwives, and Licensed Certified Midwives - Disclosure (Nyeli Rose Lewis Act of 2026)
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 33

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants
Nursing Homes -see also- AsstLiving; ContinCare; LTCare
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill, known as the Nyeli Rose Lewis Act of 2026, requires nursing homes, assisted living programs, nurse midwives, and licensed certified midwives to provide written or electronic notification to residents, prospective residents, or patients if the provider does not maintain professional liability insurance or if such coverage has lapsed and has not been renewed. It also requires these providers to post a notice regarding the lack of insurance in a conspicuous location within their facility or place of practice.
stakeholders: Residents and prospective residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities, patients of nurse midwives and licensed certified midwives, and the healthcare providers and facilities themselves.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of nursing homes, assisted living programs, and health occupations via the Board of Nursing, the Maryland Department of Health is responsible for the implementation and enforcement of the bill's professional liability insurance disclosure requirements.

The agency regulates the professional liability insurance market in Maryland and investigates consumer complaints; it is a critical stakeholder regarding the insurance lapses and renewals mentioned in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office administers the mandatory arbitration system for medical malpractice claims; the availability of professional liability insurance directly impacts the legal proceedings and potential recovery for patients under their jurisdiction.

The agency is dedicated to protecting the rights of older adults in long-term care settings; these disclosure requirements directly impact the transparency and consumer protections for the residents they serve.

The OAG provides primary legal counsel to the Department of Health and its various boards, assisting in the enforcement of the new disclosure mandates and representing the state in related litigation.
The commission's mission involves increasing healthcare accountability and informing consumer decision-making, which are the primary objectives of requiring insurance disclosures from providers.

OAH is responsible for adjudicating contested regulatory cases; it would hear any appeals from nursing homes, assisted living facilities, or midwives facing penalties for non-compliance with the bill.

Synopsis: Establishing a Class B-SEC (small event center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George's County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County to issue the license for use in certain small event centers in the county; defining "small event center" as a venue that operates on a per-event basis or on a limited schedule without standard daily hours of operation; limiting the number of Class B-SEC licenses that the Board may issue per license year and per State legislative district; etc.
Title: Prince George's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class B-SEC (Small Event Center) License PG 312-26
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: This bill creates a Class B-SEC (small event center) beer, wine, and liquor license in Prince George’s County for venues that operate on a per-event basis and can accommodate between 75 and 110 individuals. It establishes requirements for capital investment, dining facilities, and food availability while limiting the number of licenses to 24 per year and no more than three per State legislative district.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Small event center owners and operators in Prince George’s County, event attendees, and the Prince George’s County Board of License Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Prince George’s County license fee revenues are expected to increase by approximately $10,500 annually starting in fiscal 2027, based on an estimate of three businesses applying for the new $3,500 license. There is no impact on State finances or local expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill grants direct authority to the Prince George's County Board of License Commissioners to issue and manage the new Class B-SEC licenses. This board is a permanent body authorized by the General Assembly with specific regulatory and administrative duties in the county.

The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and regulates the alcohol industry. The agency oversees the broader regulatory and tax framework, including sales tax collection from the entities that would hold this new liquor license.

The Governor is responsible for appointing officials to various state-authorized boards and commissions, which includes the Board of License Commissioners for Prince George's County tasked with implementing this bill.

This office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the state-authorized boards and commissions, such as the local liquor board, ensuring the body responsible for issuing these licenses is properly staffed.

The creation of a Class B-SEC license for small event centers provides a new business and economic opportunity for small venues in the county, which aligns with the department's mission to stimulate economic growth and job creation.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides legal counsel to state-authorized boards and agencies regarding the interpretation and enforcement of new alcoholic beverages laws.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State, a unit of local government, a county sheriff, or any agency, officer, employee, or agent of the State or a unit of local government from entering into an immigration enforcement agreement; and requiring the termination of an existing immigration enforcement agreement immediately on the taking effect of the Act.
