bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland State and local government entities, including county sheriffs, from entering into immigration enforcement agreements with the federal government to enforce civil immigration law. It also mandates the immediate termination of any such existing agreements, such as 287(g) agreements, upon the bill's enactment as an emergency measure.
responsible_party: The State of Maryland, local government units, and county sheriffs
stakeholders: State and local law enforcement agencies, county sheriffs, and individuals subject to civil immigration enforcement within Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances. While specific jurisdictions including Allegany, Carroll, Cecil, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, St. Mary’s, and Washington counties are required to terminate existing 287(g) agreements, no specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditure changes are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are directly prohibited by the bill from entering into or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements with the federal government.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees state correctional facilities and parole/probation functions; the bill directly prohibits its agencies and employees from participating in civil immigration enforcement agreements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, directly advising the Governor on policy impacts like those mandated by this bill.

This office serves as the primary liaison to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which is the federal entity that enters into the immigration enforcement agreements (such as 287(g)) that this bill prohibits.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and has previously issued guidance to law enforcement regarding interactions with federal immigration authorities; it would likely oversee the legal termination of existing agreements.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for enforcing the state's mandate to terminate existing immigration enforcement agreements across all state agencies and units.
The MDTA maintains its own nationally accredited police force, which is subject to the bill's prohibition on state agencies entering or maintaining immigration enforcement agreements.
MDOT oversees several modal administrations with law enforcement functions (such as the Maryland Transit Administration police) that are subject to the bill's prohibitions.
The department oversees the Natural Resources Police, who are state officers prohibited by the bill from entering into immigration enforcement agreements.
As an agency that manages youth in detention and community supervision, DJS and its employees are prohibited from engaging in civil immigration enforcement under the bill.
As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM monitors the operational and budget execution impacts for agencies required to terminate existing federal agreements.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide certain coverage related to orthoses beginning January 1, 2027; clarifying that certain mandated benefits related to prostheses include all prostheses determined by a treating health care provider to be medically necessary for completing daily living activities, essential job-related activities or performing certain other physical activities; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Orthoses and Prostheses (So Every Body Can Move Act)
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: Known as the 'So Every Body Can Move Act', this bill requires the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and certain health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide coverage for orthoses and clarifies requirements for prosthetic coverage. The mandate includes devices determined by a treating health care provider to be medically necessary for activities of daily living, essential job-related activities, and physical activities—such as running, biking, and swimming—to maximize whole-body health and limb function. The bill also establishes standards for the repair and replacement of these devices and requires carriers to meet provider network adequacy requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Medicaid enrollees, individuals with private health insurance, health care providers specializing in orthotics and prosthetics, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill results in a minimal special fund revenue increase of $125 for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2027 from rate and form filing fees. No fiscal impact is expected for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program as the bill codifies existing coverage updates already implemented by the department. The estimated annual cost to expand orthoses coverage in the commercial health insurance market is approximately 1450000. Local government expenditures may increase to the extent that the mandate raises premiums for fully insured employee health plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article to require the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which the Department of Health (MDH) administers, to provide coverage for orthoses. MDH is also specifically tasked with receiving compliance reports from managed care organizations and submitting a joint report to the General Assembly.

The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding coverage for orthoses and prostheses by private carriers. The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is responsible for regulating these carriers, processing rate and form filings, receiving compliance reports, and collaborating with MDH on a joint report to the General Assembly.

The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is an independent regulatory agency within MDH that, according to the fiscal note, was responsible for reviewing utilization codes and evaluating the cost impact of requiring coverage for orthoses to inform this legislation.

The bill focuses on improving mobility through mandated coverage for orthoses and prostheses, which is central to the Department of Disabilities' mission to coordinate services and improve the quality of life for Marylanders with disabilities.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) oversees the state's health insurance marketplace. The fiscal note mentions the impact of the bill on qualified health plans and essential health benefits (EHBs) offered within the Exchange.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note discusses the bill's impact on the state's health plans and includes DBM's assessment that the impact would be negligible.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to MDH and MIA regarding the implementation of new insurance mandates and the drafting of required reports and regulations.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Council to include an examination of the capacity of health care providers to deliver care to certain individuals and to identify methods by which the State can assist health care providers in delivering care to certain individuals; establishing the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program in the Maryland Department of Health to lead the State's public health efforts relating to brain health and dementia; etc.
Title: Health - Dementia Services and Brain Health Program and Provider Resource Toolkit
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to lead the state's public health efforts regarding brain health and dementia. It mandates the creation of a clinical provider resource toolkit to support healthcare providers in delivering evidence-based, person-centered care, and modifies the responsibilities and staffing of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council.
stakeholders: Individuals with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias, their caregivers, and health care providers in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $77,700 in FY 2027, reflecting the cost of hiring one program administrator to manage stakeholder coordination and the resource toolkit. Expenditures are projected to increase annually, reaching $103,500 by FY 2031. The bill also contains specific mandated appropriations for the Director of Dementia Services and Brain Health and the Council, including at least $87,600 for FY 2026 and at least $89,900 for FY 2027 and each subsequent year. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Dementia Services and Brain Health Program within the Maryland Department of Health, creating a new Director position and tasking the agency with leading the State’s public health efforts regarding brain health and dementia, including the creation of a provider resource toolkit.

The agency is explicitly named in the bill as a required partner for the Maryland Department of Health in developing the provider resource toolkit and is tasked with providing ongoing assistance and staff support for the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory duties of the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council, a permanent advisory body, requiring it to examine healthcare provider readiness and identify methods for state assistance.

The bill mandates that the Governor include specific minimum annual appropriations in the budget bill for the Program and Council and requires the Council to advise the Governor on policy and funding issues related to dementia.

As the agency responsible for budget development and personnel management, DBM will oversee the execution of the mandated annual appropriations and the management of the new full-time program administrator position necessitated by the bill.

The bill requires the new program to coordinate with academic institutions and continuing education providers to promote dementia-specific education, training, and certification for healthcare professionals.

As the provider of much of the state’s medical and health-related education, USM institutions are primary partners for the coordination of dementia-specific education and training initiatives mandated by the bill.

The Commission is a key stakeholder in the State-led care transformation initiatives that the bill requires the new Program to collaborate with to incorporate dementia-capable care practices into healthcare models.

The OAG provides legal counsel and representation to the Maryland Department of Health and other state agencies, which will be required as the department implements new program mandates and coordinates resource toolkits.

DoIT oversees state digital services and strategy; they may be called upon to support the development, security, and maintenance of the centralized, up-to-date digital resource toolkit for healthcare providers.

Synopsis: Establishing that every person has the right to hunt, fish, or harvest wildlife, including the right to use traditional methods to hunt, fish, or harvest wildlife, subject to certain regulations and restrictions; establishing that the right to hunt and fish is forever preserved for the public good; and establishing that fishing and hunting are preferred means of managing and controlling wildlife in the State.
Title: Natural Resources - Right to Hunt, Fish, and Harvest Wildlife
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/16 at 12:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; FishNets&Dev
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Plants -see also- Invasive Species; Trees; Weeds

bill_summary: This bill proposes an amendment to the Maryland Constitution to establish a right for individuals to hunt, fish, and harvest wildlife using traditional methods, subject to regulations for wildlife conservation. It designates hunting and fishing as the preferred methods for managing and controlling wildlife in the state and requires that these rights be preserved for the public good.
stakeholders: Maryland residents, hunters, anglers, and state wildlife management officials
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill indicates that hunting and fishing activities contribute to tax revenues and employment and support conservation efforts through federal funding.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is the primary agency responsible for managing the state's wildlife and fisheries. This bill directly impacts their mandate by establishing hunting and fishing as the preferred means of wildlife management and creating a constitutional right that DNR must accommodate in its regulations and enforcement activities.

This bill proposes a constitutional amendment that must be submitted to the qualified voters of the state for adoption or rejection. The State Board of Elections is responsible for administering the referendum process at the 2026 general election.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. Specifically, the Governor is required by the bill to receive the election returns and issue a proclamation if the constitutional amendment is adopted by the voters.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state. They would be responsible for providing legal counsel regarding the implementation of this new constitutional right and defending the state in any litigation challenging the scope of 'traditional methods' or the balance between the right and existing regulations.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records and the Great Seal. They are responsible for the formal record-keeping and processing of laws and amendments passed by the General Assembly and ratified by voters.

The bill's changes to wildlife management and the establishment of hunting/fishing as preferred management tools impact agricultural lands and the economic viability of resource-based industries supported by the Department of Agriculture.

The bill explicitly finds that hunting and fishing are valued parts of the state's cultural heritage and economy. The Department of Commerce, which handles economic development and tourism, would be impacted by the formal recognition of these activities as protected rights.

OTD is responsible for promoting Maryland's recreational and cultural assets. The establishment of a constitutional right to hunt and fish enhances the state's profile for outdoor recreation and tourism, which are key components of OTD's marketing mission.

As the support agency for the Judicial Branch, the AOC is relevant because courts will likely need to adjudicate cases where individuals cite the new constitutional right as a defense against existing natural resources regulations or trespass charges.

The OAH hears contested cases involving state agencies, including DNR. A constitutional right to hunt and fish would likely be raised in administrative hearings regarding the suspension or revocation of hunting and fishing licenses.

The Council addresses challenges in rural counties where hunting and fishing are significant economic and cultural activities. This bill directly supports the interests of the rural communities the agency represents.

The State Archives is the depository for government records of permanent value. A constitutional amendment represents a permanent change to the state's foundational documents, which the Archives must preserve and make accessible.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to conduct at least two on-site unannounced inspections of each certified recovery residence annually; authorizing the Department to direct the recovery residence credentialing entity to revoke the certification of a certified recovery residence that fails to correct a deficiency within 1 month after notice of the deficiency is provided; etc.
Title: Health Facilities - Certified Recovery Residences - Unannounced Inspections
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct at least two unannounced on-site inspections of each certified recovery residence annually. It establishes a one-month remediation period for residences found to be noncompliant and authorizes the Department to direct the credentialing entity to revoke the certification of residences that fail to correct deficiencies.
stakeholders: Certified recovery residences and individuals with substance-related or addictive disorders
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least $373,600 in FY 2027, which accounts for the bill's October 1, 2026 effective date. This funding is required for the Maryland Department of Health to hire five staff members to conduct inspections and manage compliance notifications. Expenditures are projected to grow to approximately $496,500 by FY 2031. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 448 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to perform at least two unannounced on-site inspections per year for every certified recovery residence in the state. The department is also responsible for managing the deficiency notice process and directing the revocation of certifications for non-compliant residences.

According to the fiscal note, the bill requires at least $373,600 in general fund expenditures in FY 2027 and the hiring of five additional full-time staff members (special program coordinators) to handle the inspection workload. DBM oversees the state budget and personnel management associated with these impacts.

If a certified recovery residence contests a deficiency finding or the revocation of its certification as authorized by this bill, the Office of Administrative Hearings would likely be the venue for the resulting administrative legal proceedings.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health. They would be involved in advising on the implementation of the new inspection regulations and representing the state in any litigation or appeals arising from certification revocations.

Synopsis: Altering a certain provision of law authorizing a law enforcement officer to conduct an otherwise lawful custodial interrogation of a child if the child's parent, guardian, or custodian consents to the custodial interrogation of the child without the child's consultation with an attorney.
Title: Juvenile Justice Restoration Act
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Judiciary

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill allows a law enforcement officer to conduct a custodial interrogation of a child without a prior attorney consultation if the child's parent, guardian, or custodian consents to the interrogation. This creates an additional exception to the existing legal requirement that a child must consult with an attorney before an interrogation can take place.
responsible_party: Maryland law enforcement agencies and the Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Juveniles in Maryland, their parents or guardians, and Maryland law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill can be implemented with existing budgeted resources at the state level, and revenues are not affected. Local finances and operations are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the statutory mandate of the Office of the Public Defender to provide legal consultation to children in custody, as it introduces an exception allowing parents or guardians to waive this mandatory consultation.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police must implement these revised protocols for the custodial interrogation of juveniles.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary body for coordinating public safety and criminal justice policy; this bill represents a significant shift in juvenile justice and law enforcement interrogation standards.

DJS is responsible for youth involved in the juvenile justice system; changes to interrogation rules directly affect the front-end of the delinquency process and the evidence available in their cases.
The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article and sets new standards for the admissibility of statements in court, creating a rebuttable presumption that judges must adjudicate.
The bill specifically includes School Resource Officers (SROs) in its definition of law enforcement. MCSS is responsible for training, policy, and oversight related to SROs in Maryland schools.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and law enforcement on the implementation of these rules and represents the state in appeals regarding the admissibility of statements.
The DNR Natural Resources Police are law enforcement officers who must comply with the bill's requirements when interrogating children for conservation or criminal violations.
MDOT's law enforcement units, such as the Maryland Transportation Authority Police and Transit Police, must adhere to these interrogation protocols for juveniles.
The bill impacts school environments as it explicitly includes school resource officers in its interrogation rules, which falls under the broader educational leadership of MSDE.
The office coordinates policy related to the well-being of children and reducing child poverty, with a direct interest in policies affecting children's interactions with the justice system.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a court or a party in a criminal or juvenile delinquency case from disclosing or allowing inspection of a certain court filing or record to a nonparty unless the court or the party redacts certain identifying information relating to a certain victim of sexual assault or victim of stalking that appears in the filing or record, unless the Court finds clear and convincing evidence that there is good cause to order otherwise; etc.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Protection of Identity of Victim of Sexual Assault or Stalking
Status: In the Senate - Favorable Report by Judicial Proceedings

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires the redaction of identifying information for victims of sexual assault or stalking in criminal or juvenile delinquency court filings and records before they can be disclosed to a nonparty. It mandates that courts redact this information from existing records upon the victim's request and establishes a procedure for health occupations boards to petition for access to unredacted records for disciplinary purposes, provided the victim is notified and does not object.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Victims of sexual assault and stalking, defendants in criminal or juvenile delinquency cases, nonparties seeking access to court records, the Maryland Judiciary, State's Attorneys, and health occupations boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $13,500 in fiscal 2027 to cover one-time programming costs for the Judiciary. Beyond these costs, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts court operations by requiring the redaction of victim identifying information from electronic and paper filings. The fiscal note specifies a $13,500 expenditure for the Judiciary for one-time programming costs to implement these requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As a frequent party in criminal and juvenile delinquency cases, the Office of the Public Defender is prohibited from disclosing or allowing inspection of records containing victim identifying information unless redacted. They must comply with the bill's procedural mandates.

The bill explicitly provides a mechanism for Health Occupations Boards—which are regulated and housed within the Maryland Department of Health—to petition the court for unredacted records to investigate or discipline licensees for sexual misconduct.

The bill specifically applies to juvenile delinquency cases. As the agency responsible for managing and supervising youth in the juvenile justice system, DJS is a primary stakeholder in the proceedings where these redaction rules will apply.

As the primary law enforcement agency, the State Police generate charging documents and other case records that are specifically cited in the bill as requiring redaction of victim identifying information before disclosure to nonparties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and victim services policy. The bill establishes new criminal procedure protections for victims of sexual assault and stalking, aligning with GOCPP's mission to reduce crime and support victim services.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the health boards mentioned in the bill. They may also be involved in criminal appeals or representing the state's interest regarding the interpretation of these new privacy protections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees pretrial and correctional records and may be a party to or holder of records in criminal cases subject to the bill's redaction and disclosure requirements.

DHS assists victims of abuse and neglect and is frequently involved in juvenile delinquency and social service cases. The protections for victims of sexual assault and stalking intersect with their role in providing aid and preventative services to vulnerable individuals.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency. While the fiscal impact is relatively low ($13,500), the department oversees the budget execution and planning for the agencies impacted by the bill's requirements.

Synopsis: Altering the membership and duties of the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council; requiring the Council to submit annual reports of its work and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026, and each year thereafter; and repealing the termination date of the Council.
Title: Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council - Membership, Duties, and Sunset Repeal
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council (ZEEVIC) as a permanent entity by repealing its sunset provision. It alters the council's membership and redefines its duties to focus on identifying barriers and recommending policies for the integration of zero-emission vehicle charging infrastructure into the State's transportation network, including residential and commercial developments. It also mandates a permanent annual reporting requirement for the council.
stakeholders: Zero-emission vehicle owners and manufacturers, electric companies, fleet vehicle operators, local governments, and the environmental community.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill's requirements for staffing and reporting can be managed with existing resources by the Maryland Department of Transportation and associated agencies. There is no estimated impact on state or local revenues, and the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing several members of the Council, designating its chair or cochairs, and receiving the Council's annual reports on zero-emission vehicle infrastructure.
The bill adds the Secretary of Agriculture (or their designee) as a permanent member of the Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council.
The Secretary of Commerce is a statutory member of the Council, which is tasked with recommending policies that impact business investment in electric vehicle infrastructure.

The Secretary of the Environment is a member of the Council. The Council's work directly aligns with the department's mission to implement environmental laws and manage pollution control related to vehicle emissions.

The Secretary of General Services is a member of the Council. DGS is relevant due to its role in managing state-owned facilities and vehicle fleets, which are central to the Council's focus on charging infrastructure and fleet purchases.

The Secretary of Planning is a member of the Council. The department's focus on sustainable growth and infrastructure development is directly relevant to the Council's mandate to integrate charging infrastructure into the state's transportation network.
MDOT is the primary agency for the Council; the Secretary serves as a member, and the department is explicitly tasked with providing staff support to the Council.

The Director of MEA is a member of the Council, and the agency is mandated to provide assistance in staffing the Council. The Council's mission to advance clean energy and EV adoption is central to MEA's core responsibilities.

The Executive Director of the Commission's technical staff is a member of the Council, and the PSC is required to provide staff support assistance. The Council's work involves utility-related infrastructure and regulatory goals relevant to the PSC.
The People's Counsel is a statutory member of the Council, representing the interests of residential utility consumers in discussions regarding electric vehicle charging infrastructure and policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Zero Emission Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Council is a state council governed by this bill, which makes it permanent and alters its membership and duties.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the industry and public representative positions on the Council.
The bill removes a representative of an institution of higher education from the Council's membership, directly impacting the representation of state universities in this policy body.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from suspending or revoking a license to practice veterinary medicine in the State, reprimanding or censuring a licensee, or placing a licensee on probation solely on the basis of the licensee discussing or recommending the use of cannabis or a product that contains cannabidiol on an animal for potential therapeutic effect or health supplementation purposes.
Title: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners - Grounds for Disciplinary Action - Restrictions
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 47

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.
Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners from taking disciplinary actions, such as suspending or revoking a license, against a veterinarian solely for discussing or recommending the use of cannabis or cannabidiol (CBD) products on an animal for therapeutic or health supplementation purposes.
responsible_party: State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed veterinarians, veterinary practitioners, and animal owners in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. According to the Fiscal Note, the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners has not taken any formal actions to date that would be prohibited under the bill, and the impact on small veterinary businesses is expected to be minimal or nonexistent.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is a unit within the Department of Agriculture, and the bill directly amends the Agriculture Article to restrict the Board's disciplinary authority.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners is a permanent regulatory board whose disciplinary powers over licensees are specifically restricted by the provisions of this bill.
The bill pertains to disciplinary hearings for veterinary licenses; the OAH is the central agency responsible for adjudicating contested cases involving such state board actions.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners and would be responsible for advising the Board on the implementation of these new statutory restrictions.
The bill defines cannabis based on the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article and involves the recommendation of products regulated by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

Synopsis: Establishing the Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund to provide grants to low-income unit owners of condominiums with insufficient reserve accounts to enable a low-income unit owner to pay increased assessments necessary for a condominium association to meet reserve account funding requirements; requiring that the Fund prioritize certain older adults; requiring the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development to establish certain procedures, publicize the Fund and prioritize older owners; etc.
Title: Real Property - Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund - Establishment
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund within the Department of Housing and Community Development. The fund's purpose is to provide grants to low-income unit owners (those with household incomes not exceeding 80% of the area median income) to help them pay increased assessments required for their condominium associations to meet statutory reserve account funding requirements. The bill requires the Secretary of Housing and Community Development to administer the fund and prioritize grants for owners who are at least 65 years old.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income condominium unit owners, especially those aged 65 and older, and Maryland condominium associations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a special fund that will receive money through State budget appropriations and interest earnings. It exempts the fund from the requirement that interest earnings accrue to the General Fund. However, because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific dollar estimates for the State appropriation, administrative costs, or interest revenue impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly designates the Department of Housing and Community Development to administer the Insufficient Condominium Reserve Account Grant Fund, establish application procedures, publicize the fund, and receive annual reports from grant recipients.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the new special fund separately and invest the money of the fund in the same manner as other state money.

The Secretary of State is responsible for the registration and oversight of condominiums in Maryland. This bill creates a financial support mechanism for low-income unit owners to comply with reserve funding requirements related to those condominiums.
The bill requires that priority for grants be given to low-income unit owners who are at least 65 years old, which directly impacts the demographic served by the Department of Aging.

The bill amends the State Finance and Procurement Article regarding how interest on special funds is accounted for by the Comptroller and ensures interest from this new fund stays within the fund rather than accruing to the General Fund.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the budget execution and oversight of the new special, nonlapsing fund created by this bill.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget, which must include the appropriations and expenditures for this new grant fund.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Administrator of Elections to enroll the State in the federal Systematic Alien Verification of Entitlement (SAVE) Program for a certain purpose; requiring the State Board of Elections to establish a process to verify the U.S. citizenship of certain individuals applying to or who have registered to vote in the State; and requiring the State Board to establish a certain appeal process for certain individuals who dispute a certain report that the individual lacks U.S. citizenship.
Title: Election Law - Voter Registration Eligibility - U.S. Citizenship Verification (SAVE Our Elections Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: The SAVE Our Elections Act of 2026 requires the Maryland State Administrator of Elections to enroll the state in the federal Systematic Alien Verification of Entitlement (SAVE) Program. This program will be used to verify the U.S. citizenship status of individuals who are applying to register to vote or are already registered in Maryland. The bill also mandates that the State Board of Elections establish regulations for this verification process and create an appeal process for individuals whose citizenship status is disputed based on reports from the SAVE program.
stakeholders: Individuals applying for voter registration and currently registered voters in Maryland whose citizenship status may be subject to verification.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill's requirements for enrolling in the federal SAVE program and establishing verification and appeal procedures will result in administrative expenditures for the State Board of Elections and local boards of elections, potentially including federal program query fees and personnel costs for processing notices and hearings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates the State Administrator and State Board of Elections to enroll in the federal SAVE program, verify U.S. citizenship for all voter registration applicants and current registrants, and establish a new appeals process for those flagged as non-citizens.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the State Board of Elections during the development of new regulations and the creation of the citizenship verification appeal process, and would likely represent the state in any legal challenges resulting from the implementation of this Act.
DoIT may be required to provide technical assistance in integrating the federal SAVE program's verification system with the state's existing statewide voter registration database.

DBM would oversee the fiscal impact of enrolling in the federal SAVE program, including any per-query fees paid to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security and potential personnel costs for managing the verification and appeals processes.

As a public honors college and independent unit of state government, the college is directly impacted by the bill and must implement the requirement in its student health center.

MCEC's mission is to advance clean energy technologies. Legislative restrictions on solar facility construction in specific land-use zones directly impact their objective to expand solar adoption in Maryland.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates sustainable growth and land preservation efforts (including agriculture and the environment). The bill's focus on land use in preservation areas falls directly under its strategic mission.

DNR is responsible for conserving state lands and managing natural resources. Restrictions on construction in preservation areas align with the department's conservation and land management interests.
The OPC represents utility consumers. Limiting the development of solar generation can impact utility resource planning, energy supply, and potentially long-term consumer costs.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and signs bills into law. This legislation aligns with executive-level policy balancing renewable energy goals with land preservation.

The bill impacts the business environment for solar developers and the broader renewable energy industry in Maryland, which falls under the department's economic development interests.

The Council is required to submit an annual report on the grants made through the Rural Maryland Capacity Building Fund to the Governor.
The bill's primary objective is to enhance capacity for economic development in rural communities, which directly aligns with the Department of Commerce's mission and statutory programs.

As a public institution of higher education, Saint Mary's College is an eligible applicant for the Rural Readiness Program and associated capacity building grants.
The commission oversees postsecondary institutions, including community colleges and private institutions, which are eligible applicants for the newly established rural development grants.
The commission oversees the institutions of higher education that are eligible to apply for the Rural Readiness Program and capacity building grants.

Regional planning agencies are eligible applicants under the bill, and the grants support collaborative planning initiatives that overlap with the Department of Planning's mission for sustainable growth and land use.
The bill allows grant funds to be used for workforce initiatives and economic development, and workforce development organizations are listed as eligible applicants.
The bill targets workforce development as a key area for capacity building grants in rural communities, aligning with the Board's policy-making and strategy duties.

Transportation infrastructure is a designated eligible use for the grants established by the bill to address disparities in rural access.
The bill allows grant funds to be used for health-related initiatives in rural communities to address disparities in healthcare access mentioned in the legislative findings.
The bill designates broadband services as an eligible use for the capacity building grants, supporting DoIT's role in statewide telecommunications strategy and infrastructure.
The bill identifies energy as a sector eligible for collaborative planning and capacity building grants in rural areas.
The bill allows for grants to be used for rural infrastructure development, which frequently involves water and wastewater projects overseen by MDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.

The bill highlights disparities in educational attainment in rural communities as a justification for the program, and MSDE oversees the systems that may benefit from enhanced community capacity.

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland voters to provide proof of identity when voting in person, either through a government-issued photo ID or a combination of a non-government photo ID and a supporting document such as a utility bill, bank statement, or paycheck. Voters who cannot provide identification must be referred to vote using a provisional ballot. The bill also establishes criminal penalties for voting or attempting to vote using false identification.
stakeholders: Maryland voters, election judges, and state and local election officials
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text. The bill is expected to increase administrative expenditures for the State Board of Elections and local boards related to voter education, election judge training, and the processing of an increased volume of provisional ballots. Potential fine revenue may increase from new misdemeanor penalties related to the use of false identification.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for the supervision and administration of elections. It will be required to develop new procedures for identity verification, update training for election judges, and manage the logistics of increased provisional ballot usage.

The MVA is the primary issuer of government photo identification in Maryland. Because the bill requires voters to present valid photo ID (or specific secondary documentation), the MVA would likely see a notable increase in requests for state identification cards.

This office investigates and prosecutes offenses related to the integrity of the electoral process. The bill creates a new criminal offense for knowingly voting or attempting to vote under a false form of identification, which falls directly under the jurisdiction of the State Prosecutor.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the State Board of Elections and will likely be tasked with interpreting the new requirements, providing implementation guidance, and defending the law against potential legal challenges.

The Judicial Branch will handle any criminal cases resulting from the new misdemeanor offenses created by the bill, as well as any civil litigation related to the enforcement of voter identification requirements.

DBM is responsible for state budget planning and execution. The implementation of this bill will have fiscal impacts on the SBE (training and printing) and the MVA (increased ID issuance) that DBM must manage.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved in implementing this law (SBE, MVA, and DBM) and will be responsible for proposing the necessary funding for these activities in the annual budget.

DoIT manages the state's IT infrastructure and strategy. They may be required to support the SBE in updating electronic poll book software or other data systems to accommodate the new identity verification workflows.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be involved in investigating instances of fraudulent identification use or election-related crimes as specified in the updated criminal section of the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law relating to no-knock search warrants; providing that a search warrant may not authorize a law enforcement officer to enter a building, apartment, premises, place, or thing to be searched without first giving notice of the officer's authority and purpose; and providing that an officer executing a search warrant, under certain circumstances, may not enter the building, apartment, premises, place, or thing to be searched unless reasonable notice of the officer's authority and purpose is given to any individual inside.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the authority for judges to issue no-knock search warrants and prohibits law enforcement from entering a premises without first announcing their authority and purpose. It requires officers to wait at least 20 seconds for a response from occupants before entering, unless exigent circumstances exist, and removes specific reporting and training requirements related to no-knock warrants.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Maryland State and local law enforcement agencies, Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, and the Governor’s Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: Maryland residents, law enforcement officers, and the state's judicial system
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. However, the bill's repeal of specific reporting and training requirements for no-knock warrants likely results in a minor reduction in administrative costs for state and local law enforcement agencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is the leading entity responsible for executing search warrants and performing high-risk entries; the repeal of no-knock warrants fundamentally alters their operational tactics and SWAT protocols.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly modifies the reporting requirements for search warrants and SWAT deployments that law enforcement agencies must submit to the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy annually.

The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch by repealing the authority of Circuit Court and District Court judges to issue no-knock search warrants and establishes new statutory requirements for warrant notice and entry procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The repeal of no-knock warrants significantly impacts criminal defense strategies, providing the Office of the Public Defender with new statutory grounds for filing motions to suppress evidence obtained through non-compliant warrant executions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and law enforcement on the implementation of new laws and represents the state in criminal appeals where the legality of a search or the execution of a warrant is at issue.
This independent agency investigates and prosecutes crimes related to public integrity and often utilizes search warrants; the new restrictions on no-knock entries will apply to their investigations.

The Maryland Natural Resources Police, a unit of this department, possesses full law enforcement authority and frequently executes search warrants, making them subject to the bill's new notice and response time requirements.
MDOT oversees several modal administrations with law enforcement components, most notably the MDTA Police, who will be required to change their warrant execution procedures under this bill.

The MDTA maintains a nationally accredited police force that executes search warrants on state highways and bridges; they will be directly affected by the repeal of no-knock authority and the new 20-second notice rule.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, who are responsible for security and law enforcement on state property and must comply with the modified warrant execution standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the duties of the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (which falls under this category) regarding the development of standards for SWAT team deployment and warrant service training.
The Comptroller's Office employs sworn agents who enforce tax, alcohol, and tobacco laws; these agents have the power to execute search warrants and will be subject to the bill's procedural changes.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the various law enforcement agencies impacted by this change and is responsible for broad public safety policy coordination.

Synopsis: Establishing an immunity from liability for a person who discloses information about allegations of sexually assaultive behavior if the person acts in good faith; establishing a presumption of good faith unless it is shown by a preponderance of the evidence that the person acted with actual malice or intentionally or recklessly disclosed false information; providing for the award of attorney's fees and costs in certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Civil Actions - Immunity - Disclosure of Allegations of Sexually Assaultive Behavior (Stop Silencing Survivors Act)

bill_summary: The Stop Silencing Survivors Act establishes that a person who in good faith discloses information about allegations of sexually assaultive behavior is immune from civil liability for that disclosure. The bill creates a legal presumption that such disclosures are made in good faith unless a preponderance of evidence proves actual malice or the intentional/reckless disclosure of false information, and it requires courts to award reasonable attorney's fees and costs to individuals who successfully defend against claims of bad faith.
stakeholders: Individuals reporting or disclosing sexual assault allegations, persons accused of sexually assaultive behavior, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. While it mandates the awarding of attorney's fees and costs in certain civil litigation, these represent transfers between private parties rather than State expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial proceedings by establishing a new immunity standard, a presumption of good faith in civil cases, and a requirement for courts to award attorney’s fees and costs in specific circumstances related to disclosures of sexually assaultive behavior.

The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund and handles liability claims against the state. The establishment of civil immunity for certain disclosures could impact the defense and outcome of liability claims involving state employees or agencies.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG provides counsel to all state agencies and would be responsible for interpreting this immunity and representing state entities or employees who may invoke this immunity in civil litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD was a contributor to the fiscal note and has a vested interest in the legal definitions of sexually assaultive behavior and the intersection between civil disclosures and criminal law proceedings.

The Commission enforces anti-discrimination laws where sexually assaultive behavior often intersects with sexual harassment in employment and public accommodations. Immunity for those disclosing such behavior supports the reporting mechanisms central to the Commission's work.

Synopsis: Prohibiting recovery by a certain plaintiff from being barred in a certain civil action due to the plaintiff's negligence, except under certain circumstances; requiring any damages awarded under the Act to be diminished in proportion to the amount of negligence attributed to the plaintiff; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Civil Actions - Motor Vehicle Accidents Involving Vulnerable Individuals - Comparative Negligence
Status: In the House - Referred to interim study by Judiciary

bill_summary: This bill establishes a modified comparative negligence standard for civil lawsuits involving motor vehicle accidents where the plaintiff is a 'vulnerable individual' (such as a pedestrian, bicyclist, or person on a motorcycle). Under this standard, a plaintiff is not barred from recovering damages unless their own negligence was a proximate cause of the injury and was greater than the combined negligence of all defendants. Any damages awarded are reduced in proportion to the plaintiff's own degree of negligence.
stakeholders: Vulnerable individuals involved in motor vehicle accidents (pedestrians, cyclists, etc.), motor vehicle operators, the Maryland Transit Administration, and State and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may lead to a significant increase in State and local expenditures due to higher tort claim payments, settlements, and insurance premiums. Because the bill replaces the contributory negligence bar with a comparative negligence standard for vulnerable individuals, the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF) may see increased payouts for claims previously barred. The Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is particularly impacted as it does not have a statutory limit on liability. Additionally, the State Treasurer’s Office and the Office of the Attorney General may require additional personnel to handle increased claim volumes and litigation, with one estimate for a claims employee starting at $86,100 in fiscal 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which pays out tort claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. The bill is expected to significantly increase SITF expenditures and requires additional staffing for the agency's Insurance Division to process increased claims.

The MTA is specifically identified as being significantly impacted because its tort liability is not capped under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. As a major operator of motor vehicles (buses and trains) that interact with vulnerable individuals, it faces a high risk of increased claim payouts and litigation costs.

The judicial branch is responsible for adjudicating the civil actions affected by this bill. The shift from contributory negligence to a comparative negligence standard for a specific class of plaintiffs represents a fundamental change in how motor vehicle negligence cases are handled in Maryland courts.

The OAG provides legal representation for the State and its agencies in civil litigation. The bill is expected to increase the volume and complexity of tort cases, requiring additional legal and administrative personnel to defend the State's interests.

As the parent agency for modal administrations like the MTA and SHA, MDOT oversees the state's transportation network and safety policies. The change in liability standards for accidents involving vulnerable road users directly impacts MDOT's operational and fiscal planning.

The MIA regulates the state's insurance industry. A change from contributory to comparative negligence for a significant portion of motor vehicle accidents will necessitate regulatory oversight of how insurance companies adjust their policies, rate-setting, and claims handling.

As the insurer of last resort for Maryland drivers, MAIF is directly impacted by changes in liability rules. The shift to comparative negligence will likely increase the number of claims for which the fund must pay damages and affect its overall fiscal stability.

MSP operates a large fleet of patrol vehicles and frequently interacts with vulnerable road users and emergency responders on highways. The agency is subject to tort claims that would now be evaluated under the new comparative negligence standard.

SHA is responsible for the design and maintenance of the state's non-toll highways where vulnerable individuals (including pedestrians and workers) are present. The agency's highway safety initiatives and its own vehicle operations are directly relevant to the bill's focus.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal agency. It oversees the budget execution and premium assessments for state agencies that pay into the SITF, which are expected to rise as a result of the bill's impact on tort payouts.

MDTA operates toll facilities and maintains a police force. Its operations involve significant interaction with motor vehicles and vulnerable individuals on bridges and tunnels, exposing the agency to potential tort claims under the revised negligence standard.

MVA houses the Highway Safety Office and regulates the operation of motor vehicles. The bill's specific focus on motor vehicle accidents and the definitions of vulnerable individuals is highly relevant to the agency's safety mission and regulatory scope.

DGS manages the state's vehicle fleet and provides security through the Capitol Police. The change in liability standards increases the potential fiscal impact of accidents involving state-owned vehicles operated by various departments.

The bill's definition of 'vulnerable individual' specifically includes individuals using wheelchairs and electric personal assistive mobility devices, groups for whom this department advocates and coordinates services.

The Department of Aging represents older adults, who are frequently pedestrians and thus categorized as 'vulnerable individuals' under the bill. The agency has an interest in policy changes that affect the legal recovery rights of this demographic.

The bill's definition of 'vulnerable individual' specifically includes individuals lawfully operating farm tractors or farm equipment on highways, which falls under the regulatory and support scope of the Department of Agriculture.

The definition of 'vulnerable individual' includes persons providing emergency services on a highway. MDEM coordinates such personnel, and the bill provides enhanced legal protections for these individuals in the event of a motor vehicle accident.

Synopsis: Requiring the annual report of the Maryland Parole Commission to include certain information; altering a certain provision of law to require the Commission to provide certain documents to an incarcerated individual and the incarcerated individual's representative at a certain time; requiring the Commission to document, state on the record, provide to an incarcerated individual, and make available to the public certain information; applying the Act retroactively; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases transparency and equity in Maryland's parole system by requiring the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC) to provide incarcerated individuals and their representatives with copies of all documents used in parole suitability determinations. It establishes that the MPC cannot permanently deny parole and entitles incarcerated individuals to subsequent hearings at specific intervals based on their sentence length. Additionally, the bill requires the MPC to record all parole hearings, provide recordings at no cost to the incarcerated person, and include race-disaggregated data in its annual reports. It also prohibits counties from participating as parties in administrative proceedings for compensation for erroneously convicted individuals.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, legal representatives of incarcerated individuals, crime victims, the Maryland Parole Commission, and erroneously convicted individuals seeking state compensation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least 346,800 in FY 2027 to hire four office secretaries and cover costs for audio recordings of hearings. Ongoing annual expenditures are estimated to reach 456,000 by FY 2031. There is also an indeterminate decrease in general fund revenue because the MPC will no longer collect the 30 dollar fee for audio recording requests. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Board of Public Works is responsible for compensating individuals found eligible for compensation and benefits due to erroneous conviction, a process modified by the bill's changes to party designations in such proceedings.
The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works, which is the body responsible for overseeing and approving the fiscal payouts for erroneously convicted individuals.

As the primary personnel and budget agency, DBM will be involved in the creation of the four new staff positions and the allocation of additional general funds required by the Maryland Parole Commission to implement the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Parole Commission (MPC), which is the primary agency impacted by the bill, is administratively housed within DPSCS. The bill significantly alters MPC's hearing procedures, reporting requirements, and staffing needs.

The Maryland Parole Commission is required to submit an expanded annual report to the Governor containing detailed statistics disaggregated by race, and the Governor oversees the executive functions related to correctional services and parole.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and policy development, which includes the transparency and equity improvements in the parole process established by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill's provisions regarding increased transparency, access to documents, and the right to subsequent parole hearings directly impact the legal rights and representation of indigent individuals in the parole system.
The State Treasurer is a member of the Board of Public Works, which manages the fiscal aspects of compensation for erroneously convicted individuals.

Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) within the OAH are responsible for adjudicating petitions for eligibility for compensation and benefits for erroneously convicted individuals, a process affected by the bill's changes to eligible parties.
The OAG represents the State in proceedings regarding the wrongful conviction of individuals before an Administrative Law Judge, and the bill clarifies the parties involved in these proceedings.

bill_summary: House Bill 468 establishes the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth and imposes a tiered gross revenues tax on digital social media services provided in Maryland. The tax rates range from 5% to 10% based on a provider's global annual gross revenues, specifically targeting entities with more than $500 million in global revenue and at least $1 million in Maryland-derived revenue. The proceeds, after administrative costs are deducted, are dedicated to the new fund to improve mental health care access for children and youth in the state.
responsible_party: Maryland Comptroller, Secretary of Health, and State Treasurer
stakeholders: Digital social media service providers with significant global and state revenue, and Maryland children and youth requiring mental health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a new revenue source by taxing digital social media services at tiered rates of 5%, 7.5%, or 10% of gross revenues derived from Maryland, depending on the provider's global gross income. Revenues are distributed to the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth after the Comptroller's administrative expenses are covered. Specific financial estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering, collecting, and accounting for the new Digital Social Media Gross Revenues Tax established by the bill. The agency must also manage the distribution of these funds to the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth.

The Secretary of Health is specifically charged with administering the newly created Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth, which is dedicated to improving access to mental health services for youth in Maryland.
The bill explicitly tasks the State Treasurer with holding the Mental Health Care Fund for Children and Youth separately and investing its money in the same manner as other State funds.

As the agency responsible for budget development and revenue estimation, DBM will oversee the inclusion of this new special fund and its tax revenues within the state's fiscal planning and budget execution.
The bill's focus on improving access to health services for children and youth aligns directly with the mission of this office to promote the well-being of Maryland's children.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the policy implementation of new taxes and special funds and is responsible for proposing the budget that will include the Fund's expenditures.
The Tax Court is the administrative body that would hear appeals regarding the newly established Digital Social Media Gross Revenues Tax.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Comptroller and the Department of Health regarding the implementation of the new tax and fund, and would represent the State in potential legal challenges.
OAH may be required to adjudicate administrative disputes arising from the Department of Health's or Comptroller's decisions related to the new fund or tax regulations.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain condominium unit owner to obtain a condominium unit owner insurance policy or a substantially similar property insurance policy for the unit; requiring a certain insurance policy to include certain provisions; and authorizing a council of unit owners to acquire an insurance policy on behalf of a unit owner who does not maintain a certain required insurance policy and charge the insurance premium as an assessment to the unit owner.

bill_summary: This bill requires owners of residential condominium units, excluding detached units, to maintain a specific insurance policy for their unit that includes coverage for the council of unit owners' property insurance deductible, personal property replacement, loss of use for at least 12 months, personal liability of at least $500,000, and loss assessment of at least $25,000. Unit owners must provide annual evidence of this insurance to the council of unit owners, which is authorized to purchase a policy on the owner's behalf and charge the premium as an assessment if the owner fails to maintain the required coverage.
stakeholders: Residential condominium unit owners and condominium councils of unit owners
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. No specific dollar estimates for State revenue or expenditures are provided as the impact is considered negligible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates specific types of insurance coverage and minimum limits (such as personal liability, loss of use, and loss assessment) for condominium unit owners. As the state's insurance regulator, the MIA is responsible for reviewing and approving the policy forms and ensuring insurance carriers comply with these new statutory requirements.

The Secretary of State is tasked with the registration and oversight of condominiums in Maryland. This bill directly amends the Maryland Condominium Act to establish mandatory insurance standards for residential units, falling within the agency's primary administrative purview.

The Office of the Attorney General, particularly its Consumer Protection Division, was identified as a source for the fiscal analysis. The bill affects the rights and financial obligations of condominium homeowners, and the OAG would be involved in providing legal counsel on the Act's implementation or handling consumer disputes related to the new mandates.

The bill establishes new mandatory costs for condominium owners to ensure property protection and personal liability. This intersects with the agency's mission to ensure safe and secure housing and its role in monitoring housing policy impacts on Maryland residents.
