bill_summary: This bill establishes the Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force to study and make recommendations regarding the use and regulation of blockchain technology and cryptocurrency in Maryland. The task force is required to analyze the benefits and risks of these technologies for state and local government and private businesses, as well as their impact on state revenue and energy consumption, with a report of findings due by October 1, 2027.
responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation in the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Financial services industry representatives, the Maryland Blockchain Association, state and local government agencies, higher education faculty, and the Office of Financial Regulation.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State special fund expenditures increase by $49,400 in FY 2027 and $53,500 in FY 2028 to cover the costs of one contractual administrative specialist to staff the task force. Travel reimbursements for task force members are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. The bill has no effect on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Office of Financial Regulation within the Maryland Department of Labor to provide staff for the Task Force and includes the Secretary of Labor as a member. The fiscal note indicates specific special fund expenditures for this department to hire a contractual administrative specialist.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly establishes a new Digital Asset and Blockchain Technology Task Force, which is a temporary body tasked with conducting a study and providing recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly.
The Comptroller, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force. Additionally, the task force is required to assess the impact of the cryptocurrency industry on state revenues.
The State Treasurer, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force, reflecting the office's role as the state's chief financial agency.
The Secretary of Commerce, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force, as the study involves economic development and private business impacts in the State.

The Secretary of Information Technology, or their designee, is a named member of the Task Force. The subject matter—blockchain and digital assets—falls directly within the department's strategy and infrastructure oversight.
The Securities Commissioner (part of the OAG's Securities Division) is a named member of the Task Force. The OAG also provides legal counsel to such task forces.

The Governor is responsible for appointing five members of the Task Force (representing industry, faculty, and the Blockchain Association) and will receive the final report on findings and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments will likely assist the Governor in recruiting and vetting the five specific members of the task force appointed by the Governor.
The Task Force is specifically required to assess the impact of the cryptocurrency industry on energy consumption in the State, which relates to the department's environmental protection mission.
DBM is the principal personnel agency and will be involved in the creation of the contractual position required for staffing the Task Force as outlined in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Providing that certain evidence obtained through the use of an unmanned aircraft is inadmissible in a criminal, civil, or administrative proceeding; prohibiting a unit of State government or a political subdivision of the State from deploying or operating an unmanned aircraft subject to certain exceptions; and prohibiting a unit of State government or a political subdivision of the State from using certain information acquired through the use of an unmanned aircraft.
Title: Public Safety - State and Local Governments - Use of Unmanned Aircraft
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland state and local government agencies from deploying or operating unmanned aircraft (drones) for surveillance, evidence collection, or other purposes except in specific circumstances, such as with a valid search warrant, during search and rescue operations, or in fresh pursuit of a suspect. It also establishes that any evidence gathered through the use of drones in violation of these rules is inadmissible in criminal, civil, or administrative proceedings.
responsible_party: Maryland State government units, political subdivisions, and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: State and local government agencies, law enforcement officials, and individuals subject to legal proceedings where drone-captured evidence might be used
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill may result in operational impacts for law enforcement agencies and potentially affect the administrative efficiency of evidence collection and court proceedings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary law enforcement agency, MSP is directly prohibited from deploying drones for surveillance or evidence collection except under specific warrant-based or emergency exceptions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill restricts surveillance at correctional facilities and specifically addresses drone use for locating escaped prisoners.
The Natural Resources Police use drones for environmental enforcement and search and rescue missions, the latter of which is an allowed exception.
The MDTA's police force is restricted in its use of drones, and its operational units are prohibited from using them for toll facility inspections.
The OAG will need to provide legal counsel to all state agencies regarding compliance and will handle litigation regarding the admissibility of drone-obtained evidence.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Public defenders will utilize the new statutory restrictions to challenge the admissibility of evidence in criminal and juvenile cases.
The bill mandates new evidence standards for the Judiciary and requires judges to issue search warrants for most drone operations.
The State Highway Administration and other modal units are prohibited from using drones for infrastructure inspections and other non-excepted purposes.
The agency coordinates emergency responses where drones are used for disaster assessment and search and rescue operations.
Administrative Law Judges will be required to exclude unauthorized drone evidence in the administrative proceedings they adjudicate.
The bill contains an exception for drone use to counter terrorist risks, a determination involving federal and state homeland security coordination.
The bill impacts executive branch oversight of state law enforcement technology and surveillance policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on public safety strategy and coordinates funding for law enforcement agencies impacted by these drone restrictions.
The Maryland Capitol Police are restricted by the bill, and the agency's facility maintenance units are prohibited from using drones for building inspections.
DJS is restricted in its use of drones for facility security, though an exception exists for locating individuals who have escaped custody.
The head of the military department must oversee the restricted use of drones by state military forces during domestic responses.
The Guard's ability to use drones during domestic emergencies or civil unrest is limited to the bill's specific exceptions.
The agency is prohibited from using drones for environmental surveillance and pollution source inspections without a warrant.
MDA is prohibited from using drones for crop monitoring and environmental stewardship activities without specific judicial authorization.
The Maryland Occupational Safety and Health (MOSH) unit is restricted from using drones for workplace safety inspections.
The agency's enforcement units are prohibited from using drones to monitor licensed or illicit grow operations.
School systems and state educational units are restricted from using drones for campus security or facility management.
University police and administrative staff are prohibited from using drones for campus surveillance or infrastructure maintenance.
Public health surveillance and facility inspections by the department are impacted by the general prohibition on drone deployment.
The agency's land use planning and historical preservation work frequently involves mapping and photography that is restricted by the bill.
The agency must manage state IT strategy and data governance for unmanned systems within the new restrictive legal framework.

Synopsis: Limiting the excess amount of tax credit certificates to $20,000,000, that the Department of Commerce may carry forward and issue in subsequent taxable years for a credit against the State income tax for certain costs related to certain theatrical productions in the State; prohibiting the Secretary from issuing tax credit certificates for credit amounts totaling more than $2,000,00 in the aggregate for a single theatrical production;  and extending the termination date of the credit to June 30, 2032.
Title: Income Tax - Theatrical Production Tax Credit - Alterations and Sunset Extension
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 18

bill_summary: This bill extends the Maryland theatrical production tax credit for five years, through tax year 2031, with a final sunset date of June 30, 2032. Additionally, it imposes a $20,000,000 cap on the aggregate amount of unissued tax credits that the Maryland Department of Commerce may carry forward from prior fiscal years to be issued in subsequent taxable years.
stakeholders: Qualified theatrical production entities, including for-profit national touring or pre-Broadway live stage theatrical productions, and qualified theatrical production facilities located in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund revenues are projected to decrease by approximately $500,000 annually from FY 2028 through FY 2032 based on recent program activity. There is no fiscal impact in FY 2027. If credits are claimed against the corporate income tax, revenues for the Higher Education Investment Fund and Transportation Trust Fund will decrease, which would also result in a decrease in local highway user revenues. Expenditures are not otherwise affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for administering the theatrical production tax credit, including issuing tax credit certificates and managing the new $20 million aggregate carry-forward limit.

The Comptroller's Office is responsible for processing the income tax credits and managing the resulting impacts on State tax revenues, including collections for the General Fund and other special funds.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact on the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and local highway user revenues, which are funded through tax collections managed in part by the Department of Transportation.
The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and managing the state's budget, which will be impacted by the projected revenue decrease through fiscal year 2032.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Commerce, and the Governor is responsible for proposing the annual state budget which will be affected by the revenue loss.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on a public school employer negotiating the maximum number of students assigned to a class.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the prohibition that prevents public school employers from negotiating the maximum number of students assigned to a class during collective bargaining with certificated employees.
stakeholders: Certificated public school employees, local boards of education, and public school students
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill allows class size to be a subject of collective bargaining, which may result in increased expenditures for local school systems if agreements require smaller class sizes, necessitating additional teachers and classroom space. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the 24 local school systems that would be directly affected by the change in collective bargaining laws. Allowing class size to be a subject of negotiation directly impacts the operational and educational standards managed by MSDE.

The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is responsible for administering and overseeing collective bargaining for local public school system personnel. This bill expands the scope of negotiable items under their jurisdiction to include class size.

Negotiating maximum class sizes has a direct impact on school facility requirements. If collective bargaining results in lower student-to-teacher ratios, the state may need to fund and construct additional classrooms to accommodate the same number of students, affecting the IAC's capital planning and funding allocations.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM assesses the long-term fiscal impact of legislation. This bill could lead to significantly higher personnel costs for local school systems, which may in turn pressure state funding formulas and the overall state budget for education.

The Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives and proposes the annual state budget. Changes to labor laws for public school employees represent a significant policy shift that impacts the Governor's education and labor priorities.

bill_summary: This bill, known as the Clear Before You Drive Act, prohibits a person from operating or towing a vehicle without first making reasonable efforts to remove accumulated snow and ice from exposed surfaces such as the roof, hood, and windows if the accumulation poses a threat to persons or property. The bill establishes a schedule of fines for violations, which differ for commercial and noncommercial vehicles, and allows for secondary enforcement by police unless the violation contributes to an accident involving property damage, injury, or death.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police, the District Court of Maryland, and the Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Commercial and noncommercial vehicle operators, law enforcement agencies, and Maryland motorists
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a minimal increase in State general fund revenues due to the imposition of fines ranging from $25 to $1,500 depending on the vehicle type and the severity of the offense. Enforcement and administrative costs for the District Court and State Police are expected to be manageable within existing resources. There is no significant fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing traffic laws and would be the principal entity issuing citations for failure to remove snow and ice from vehicles on state highways.
The bill amends the Transportation Article and directly impacts the state's transportation network and safety regulations, which fall under the oversight of MDOT.
The AOC oversees the District Court of Maryland, which will process the citations and collect fine revenue generated by violations of this new law.
An agency within MDOT, the MVA maintains driver records and would be responsible for tracking violations and potentially assessing points associated with traffic offenses under this act.
The MDTA operates its own police force and manages state toll facilities, including bridges and tunnels where falling snow and ice pose significant safety risks, necessitating direct enforcement.
As the agency responsible for highway safety and maintenance, SHA has a direct interest in regulations that mitigate hazards like falling snow and ice on state-numbered roads.
MTA operates a large fleet of buses and transit vehicles that must comply with the bill's requirements regarding snow and ice removal from roofs and cabs.
DGS manages the state's vehicle fleet; it would be responsible for ensuring state-owned vehicles are equipped for compliance and that state drivers follow these safety protocols.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MDOT and MSP regarding the interpretation and enforcement of new traffic statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on public safety strategies and may coordinate with law enforcement regarding the implementation of the new safety-related traffic regulations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Department of Juvenile Services from hiring or retaining an individual convicted of certain crimes.

Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Known as the Juvenile Offender Protection Act, this bill prohibits the Maryland Department of Juvenile Services from hiring or retaining any employee who has been convicted of specific serious crimes, including murder, rape, kidnapping, child abuse, and certain degrees of assault, unless the conviction was reversed or vacated.
stakeholders: Current and prospective employees of the Department of Juvenile Services, and juvenile offenders in the custody or care of the Department.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. The Department of Juvenile Services may experience indeterminate administrative costs related to auditing employee records and potential personnel turnover costs for replacing staff who are disqualified under the new requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Department of Juvenile Services, prohibiting it from hiring or retaining employees with certain criminal convictions.

As the principal personnel agency for the State of Maryland, DBM manages state employee policies and would oversee the implementation of these new hiring and retention restrictions within the executive branch.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Juvenile Services and would be responsible for advising on the implementation of the law and defending against potential litigation related to employee terminations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency coordinates public safety policy and criminal justice strategies, including policies focused on the juvenile justice system and the protection of youth.
PERB oversees collective bargaining for state employees; mandatory termination of current employees ('retaining') could lead to labor disputes or unfair labor practice charges handled by this board.
Employees terminated under the 'retention' clause of this bill may appeal their dismissal through the impartial hearing process provided by the OAH.

Synopsis: Repealing certain limitations on noneconomic damages in civil actions for personal injury or wrongful death; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Civil Actions - Noneconomic Damages - Personal Injury and Wrongful Death
Status: In the House - Referred to interim study by Judiciary

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill repeals the statutory limitations, or caps, on noneconomic damages awarded in civil actions for personal injury or wrongful death. The bill does not affect caps on damages in medical malpractice cases and applies prospectively to causes of action arising on or after October 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Plaintiffs and defendants in personal injury and wrongful death lawsuits, the Maryland Transit Administration, insurance providers, and law firms.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund may increase significantly because the Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) is not covered by the Maryland Tort Claims Act's liability limits and would face higher damage awards. Local governments remain largely protected by the Local Government Tort Claims Act. The bill may also have an operational impact on the Judiciary and circuit courts due to potentially more complex or frequent litigation. Small businesses may see an increase in insurance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill has a significant fiscal impact on the Maryland Department of Transportation because its Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) unit is not covered by the liability limits of the Maryland Tort Claims Act. Repealing the noneconomic damages cap will likely lead to much higher settlement and award costs for MTA, potentially increasing Transportation Trust Fund expenditures.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch, which the fiscal note identifies as being operationally impacted. Repealing damage caps is expected to increase the complexity and duration of personal injury and wrongful death litigation in circuit courts.

As the chief legal representative for the state, the Office of the Attorney General defends state agencies in civil litigation. The removal of noneconomic damage caps directly impacts the legal strategy, financial exposure, and workload of the office in personal injury and wrongful death cases.

As the state's insurer of last resort for drivers, the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund is directly impacted by the removal of damage caps, which will likely increase the size of payouts for claims related to personal injury and wrongful death from vehicle accidents.

The State Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund, which covers tort claims against most state agencies. While protected by the Maryland Tort Claims Act, the office oversees the state's fiscal liability and insurance protection, both of which are affected by shifts in damage award trends.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the state's insurance market. The repeal of caps on noneconomic damages is expected to impact insurance premiums and market stability, requiring oversight and monitoring by the administration.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. Significant potential increases in state expenditures, such as those within the Transportation Trust Fund, fall under its budgetary oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals language in the Maryland Code that specifically references awards by the health claims arbitration panel, which is administered by this office. Additionally, the office was identified as a primary information source regarding the impact on injury claims.

Synopsis: Providing that during the trial of a criminal case in which a defendant is charged with an assault in the second degree, a certain statement is not excluded by the hearsay rule if the statement is offered against a party that has engaged in, directed, or conspired to commit wrongdoing that was intended to and did procure the unavailibility of the declarant of the statement, under certain circumstances.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Admission of Out-of-Court Statements - Assault in the Second Degree
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Judicial Proceedings
bill_summary: This bill expands an exception to the hearsay rule in criminal cases to include trials for second-degree assault. Under the bill, out-of-court statements from an unavailable declarant may be admitted into evidence if the defendant engaged in or conspired to commit wrongdoing intended to make the witness unavailable.
stakeholders: Defendants charged with second-degree assault, victims and witnesses of second-degree assault, Maryland State's Attorneys, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Specific dollar estimates for any minor administrative impacts are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the state's judicial branch. This bill directly alters the rules of evidence (hearsay exceptions) that must be applied by judges in criminal trials involving second-degree assault.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal representation for indigent defendants. Expanding the admissibility of out-of-court statements in second-degree assault cases directly impacts their defense strategies and the outcomes of their clients' cases.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Attorney General represents the state in criminal appeals. This change in evidentiary procedure will affect appellate litigation and the legal guidance provided to state prosecutorial entities.

The Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating criminal law violations, including second-degree assault. The bill affects the legal standard for using witness statements collected during their investigations when a witness is made unavailable by a defendant.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies. The bill represents a legislative policy change in criminal procedure that falls under their advisory and policy-development scope.

The Department of Juvenile Services manages youth in the justice system. Since second-degree assault is a common charge in juvenile proceedings, changes to the rules of evidence regarding such charges are relevant to their cases and the youth they supervise.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees correctional facilities and community supervision. While the bill is procedural, changes to evidence admissibility that could affect conviction rates for assault have a downstream impact on the population management of their facilities.

The Office of the State Prosecutor investigates and prosecutes specific criminal offenses. As an independent prosecutorial agency within the executive branch, they are relevant to any changes in the state's criminal procedure laws.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The Governor is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation that impacts criminal justice procedures.

Synopsis: Altering a subtraction modification under the Maryland income tax for unreimbursed expenses paid or incurred by eligible teachers during a taxable year for the purchase of certain classroom supplies to include prekindergarten classroom teachers employed in publicly funded prekindergarten programs at eligible public providers or lead teachers or consulting teachers employed in a publicly funded prekindergarten program at an eligible private provider in the State; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Income Tax - Subtraction Modification for Classroom Supplies Purchased by Teachers - Alteration
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 61

bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility for a Maryland income tax subtraction modification for classroom supplies to include full-time prekindergarten teachers in publicly funded programs, including those at eligible public and private providers. The modification allows eligible teachers to subtract up to $250 of unreimbursed classroom supply expenses from their federal adjusted gross income for State tax purposes.
stakeholders: Full-time prekindergarten teachers in publicly funded programs in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by approximately $80,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2027. Local income tax revenues are projected to decrease by about $50,000 annually starting in the same year. The Comptroller’s Office can implement the change using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's income tax laws and collecting revenue. This bill directly alters a tax subtraction modification, requiring the Comptroller to update tax forms, instructions, and processing systems to accommodate the expanded eligibility for prekindergarten teachers.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the public education system and the prekindergarten programs impacted by this bill. The bill's definition of an 'eligible teacher' relies on providers defined within the Education Article, which is administered by MSDE.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for fiscal planning and revenue estimation. The bill is projected to decrease state general fund revenues by $80,000 annually, requiring the agency to account for this fiscal impact in state budget planning.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. As the bill modifies state revenue and touches on education policy (a primary focus for the executive branch), the office has a high-level administrative interest in its fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Requiring the University System of Maryland to develop, in consultation with the State Department of Education and the Maryland Higher Education Commission, certain recommendations for a Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program and a teacher preparation pathway in a certain manner; establishing the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup; requiring, the Governor to include an appropriation of $125,000 in fiscal years 2028 and 2029, to support the Workgroup's recommendations; etc.
Title: Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup - Establishment
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program and a corresponding workgroup. This pilot program is designed to create a structured, tuition-free, and credit-bearing early college pathway for high school students in Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary’s counties to prepare for careers in primary and secondary education. The University System of Maryland is tasked with developing the program and recommendations, while the Maryland State Department of Education is responsible for its administration and implementation.
responsible_party: The University System of Maryland and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: High school students in Southern Maryland (Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary’s counties), specifically those from rural areas or historically underrepresented backgrounds; local school systems; and public institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures will increase by $352,100 in FY 2028 and $349,200 in FY 2029 (a total of $701,300) to support mandated appropriations for program development and administrative staff at the Maryland State Department of Education. Local school systems in Calvert, Charles, and St. Mary’s counties may incur additional costs for dual enrollment tuition if the program expands participation beyond existing levels. Higher education revenues and expenditures for the University System of Maryland may also increase starting in FY 2030.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates USM as the lead agency to develop recommendations for the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program, convene and staff the program workgroup, and report on implementation. It also receives a mandated appropriation for these duties.

MSDE is responsible for the administration and implementation of the Program, adopting regulations, and the State Superintendent serves on the Program Workgroup. The fiscal note indicates MSDE will require new contractual staff to manage these responsibilities.
MHEC is a mandated consultant for the program's development and implementation, and the Secretary of Higher Education serves as a member of the Program Workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Southern Maryland Early College Teacher Pathway Program Workgroup, a temporary body tasked with developing policy recommendations and an implementation plan.
The Governor is required to include a mandated appropriation in the annual budget for the program and appoints a representative to the Program Workgroup.
DBM is responsible for supervising the state budget, which includes the mandated appropriations for the program, and oversees personnel policies relevant to MSDE's projected staffing needs.
The President of Saint Mary's College of Maryland is a designated member of the Program Workgroup, and the college is a primary higher education institution in the targeted region.
OAG provides legal counsel to the implementing agencies (MSDE, USM, and MHEC) and would likely review the regulations required to be adopted by MSDE under the bill.
This office assists the Governor in fulfilling the responsibility to appoint a representative to the newly established Program Workgroup.
MLDS links and analyzes student and workforce data from MSDE and MHEC; the data collection and reporting requirements for the new teacher pathway would fall within its analytical scope.
The program specifically targets rural areas of the state and Southern Maryland's unique geographic needs, aligning with the Council's mission to address challenges in rural counties.
The bill addresses the critical shortage of qualified teachers and creates a new workforce pipeline, which relates to the Board's role in statewide workforce development strategy.

The board oversees collective bargaining for public sector employees; the workgroup established by the bill includes representatives from local education associations (unions) for school-based employees.

Synopsis: Requiring a transportation network company to maintain a deactivation policy that provides the policies and procedures for the deactivation of operators; prohibiting a transportation network company from deactivating an operator for certain violations: authorizing a transportation network company to rely solely on a passenger report as the basis for deactivation under certain circumstances; requiring a transportation network company to allow an operator whose account is deactivated to withdraw certain earnings; etc.
Title: Transportation Network Companies - Deactivation of Operators
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

bill_summary: This bill requires transportation network companies (TNCs) to establish, maintain, and provide access to written deactivation policies for their operators. TNCs are prohibited from deactivating operators except for violations clearly defined in their policies and must provide written notice, specific reasons for deactivation, and an internal appeals process. Additionally, the bill allows operators to withdraw accrued earnings following deactivation unless criminal conduct is suspected.
stakeholders: Transportation network companies (TNCs), transportation network operators (drivers), and passengers using digital network applications.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no material impact on State or local finances. There are no state revenue changes or expenditure mandates identified. However, there is a potential meaningful impact on small businesses, specifically transportation network operators, who gain new appeal rights and procedural protections regarding their account status.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulatory body for transportation network companies (TNCs). The bill explicitly requires the Commission to adopt regulations regarding deactivation policies, receive quarterly reports on deactivations, and define certain types of misconduct.
The bill includes the Insurance Commissioner in its definitions and deals with the regulation of TNCs, which are subject to specific insurance requirements managed by this agency.
The bill defines 'egregious misconduct' based on moving violations and traffic collisions, which are recorded and monitored by the Motor Vehicle Administration within MDOT.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and would be involved in the enforcement of the new regulatory requirements and any resulting litigation.

The bill classifies discriminatory acts, including refusal of service to passengers with disabilities, as 'serious misconduct,' overlapping with the Commission's mandate to enforce anti-discrimination laws in public accommodations.
The bill establishes the right for TNC operators to bring a civil action for violations of the deactivation and appeal procedures, which may impact the state's judicial system.
The bill includes specific protections for passengers with disabilities, making refusal of service based on disability or use of a service animal a ground for 'serious misconduct' and deactivation.

Synopsis: Requiring, rather than authorizing, a court to order visitation to be rescheduled, in a manner consistent with the best interests of the child, when the court finds that a party to a custody or visitation order has unjustifiably denied or interfered with visitation granted by the custody or visitation order.
Title: Family Law - Denial or Interference With Visitation Rights
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Family Law -see also- Adoption; Alimony; Annulment; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires a court to order additional makeup visitation when a party to a custody or visitation order has unjustifiably denied or interfered with visitation rights. The court must schedule additional visitation that is of the same type as the denied visitation (such as weekends, holidays, or summer sessions), double the duration of the missed time, and scheduled at a time chosen by the aggrieved party within two years, provided the arrangement is in the best interests of the child.
stakeholders: Parents and children involved in legal custody or visitation proceedings in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill authorizes the court to assess costs or counsel fees against a party who has unjustifiably interfered with visitation rights, representing a potential financial transfer between private parties. Because no formal Fiscal Note is present, specific dollar estimates for state or local expenditures are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Judicial Branch by requiring courts to mandate specific visitation rescheduling and duration penalties when visitation rights are unjustifiably denied. The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for operationalizing these statutory mandates and ensuring judges are trained on the new requirements.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and provides counsel to the General Assembly and Judiciary. Changes to mandatory court procedures in Family Law may require the OAG to provide legal interpretation, policy guidance, or representation in appellate cases concerning the new mandates.

DHS is the primary social service provider for families and children. While visitation disputes are often private civil matters, the department's role in child welfare and support services often intersects with custody and visitation legal frameworks, particularly in cases involving local departments of social services.

This office coordinates statewide efforts to improve the well-being of children and families. Policies that mandate remedies for denied visitation affect child-parent relationships and household stability, which are central to the agency's mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The OPD provides legal representation in parental defense and juvenile cases. New mandatory penalties for interfering with visitation rights would directly influence the defense strategy and legal advice provided to indigent clients involved in family law litigation.

Synopsis: Altering certain standards for the drawing of legislative districts; establishing standards for the drawing of congressional districts; establishing the Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Commission as an independent unit of State government to divide the State into certain legislative districts and congressional districts subject to certain requirements and procedures; etc.
Title: Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Commission (Fair Districts for Maryland Act)

Article.Title: XX - Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to establish an independent Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Commission. The commission would be responsible for redrawing Maryland's legislative and congressional district boundaries every ten years following the census. The bill sets specific standards for redistricting, requiring districts to be compact, contiguous, and respectful of natural and political boundaries, while prohibiting the consideration of political party affiliation, past voting behavior, or the residence of incumbents.
responsible_party: Legislative and Congressional Redistricting and Apportionment Commission
stakeholders: Maryland voters, candidates for office, incumbent officeholders, and political parties.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by approximately $1,750,000 in each of FY 2031 and 2032 (totaling $3,500,000) for the decennial redistricting cycle, and every 10 years thereafter. These costs include staffing, legal services, software for map-drawing, and the administration of public hearings. There is no impact on state revenue or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill fundamentally alters the Governor's role in redistricting by transferring the authority to prepare plans to an independent commission and requiring the Governor to include specific funding for the commission in the state budget.

The bill specifically limits the Attorney General's authority to represent the State in redistricting litigation, instead designating the new commission as the State's representative in these proceedings.

The bill grants the Supreme Court of Maryland exclusive original jurisdiction over redistricting plans and challenges, significantly impacting the workload and jurisdictional responsibilities of the judicial branch.
MDP is responsible for managing the census data and population adjustments required for redistricting, including the geocoding of incarcerated individuals as mentioned in the fiscal note.
The Board of Elections is responsible for implementing the new district boundaries into the state's voting systems and managing the election process based on the commission's plans.
As the state's budget agency, DBM will be responsible for implementing the bill's mandate that the Governor include funding for the commission and related litigation in the annual budget.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in the recruitment and vetting of candidates for the newly established commission.
The commission is required to maintain a computerized population database and specialized map-drawing software, tasks that will likely require support or oversight from DoIT.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates that DPSCS must coordinate with the redistricting process to provide address data for incarcerated individuals to ensure accurate population counts.
The bill explicitly provides for the referral of possible criminal violations by commission members or staff to the State Prosecutor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new independent commission to address a specific government issue (redistricting), fitting the definition of this collective entity.
Members and employees of the new commission will be subject to state ethics laws and disclosure requirements managed by this agency.
OLA is expected to conduct fiscal compliance and performance audits of the new independent commission as noted in the fiscal note.
The Secretary of State is responsible for administrative records related to constitutional amendments and is involved in the process of submitting the amendment to voters.
DGS may be required to provide operational support, such as securing office space or managing procurement, for the new independent commission.

Synopsis: Increasing the minimum gross income amounts from charitable contributions at which a charitable organization must include a certain audit or a certain review with a registration statement; increasing the amount of cash receipts from charitable contributions the Secretary of State may accept an affidavit attesting to under certain circumstances; increasing the maximum amount of gross income of a charitable organization at which the Secretary of State may require an audit or review from $750,000 to $1,000,000; etc.
Title: Business Regulation - Charitable Organizations - Audit and Review Thresholds
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

bill_summary: This bill increases the gross income thresholds that determine whether a charitable organization must submit an audit or a financial review when registering with the Secretary of State. The threshold for requiring an audit is raised from $750,000 to $1,000,000, and the threshold for a financial review is raised from $300,000 to $400,000. It also adjusts the threshold for submitting alternative documentation to $400,000.
stakeholders: Charitable organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State expenditures to update online filing systems and implement the bill are minimal and can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary agency responsible for the registration and oversight of charitable organizations in Maryland. The bill directly affects the agency's operations by changing the financial thresholds for audits and reviews that the agency must collect and verify in registration statements.

The fiscal note indicates that implementing the bill will require updates to the Secretary of State's online filing systems. As the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for overseeing budget execution and ensuring that such costs are properly absorbed within budgeted resources.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Secretary of State regarding the enforcement of state laws. This bill modifies the regulatory requirements for charitable organizations under the Business Regulation Article, which may require legal interpretation or updated guidance from the OAG.

Synopsis: Providing an addition modification under the corporate income tax for the amount of certain direct-to-consumer advertising expenses for certain covered drugs paid or incurred during the taxable year that are deducted under the Internal Revenue Code; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Corporate Income Tax - Addition Modification - Direct-to-Consumer Pharmaceutical Advertising
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill requires a corporate income tax addition modification for expenses related to direct-to-consumer pharmaceutical advertising. This prevents corporations from deducting these advertising costs from their Maryland taxable income, effectively requiring companies to add back the cost of advertising for prescription and compounded drugs to their federal taxable income when determining state tax liability.
stakeholders: Pharmaceutical corporations, sponsors of prescription drug products, and owners of drug outsourcing facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in an indeterminate increase in state corporate income tax revenue by disallowing deductions for direct-to-consumer advertising expenses for certain drugs. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief financial officer and primary tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing and enforcing the new corporate income tax addition modification, updating tax forms, and auditing pharmaceutical companies to ensure compliance with the advertising expense add-back.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning. This bill directly impacts corporate income tax revenues by requiring certain advertising expenses to be added back to modified income, necessitating updated fiscal projections for the state budget.

The Department of Commerce is Maryland's primary economic development agency. This bill targets the pharmaceutical industry—a major economic sector in the state—by altering the tax treatment of their advertising expenses, which may impact the business climate for those companies.

The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes. The implementation of a new addition modification for corporate income tax could lead to factual or legal disputes between corporations and the state, which the Tax Court would adjudicate.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller and the General Assembly. It would be responsible for defending the state's interpretation of this tax law in court and providing guidance on the intersection of state tax policy and federal definitions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. This policy change affects state revenue and aligns with specific policy priorities regarding pharmaceutical industry regulation and corporate taxation.

Synopsis: Altering the name of the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects to be the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects; altering the definition of "licensed landscape architects" to be "professional landscape architects"; altering certain qualifications for membership on the Board; altering certain duties of the Board; altering certain educational and experience requirements of applicants for a license to practice landscape architecture; etc.

bill_summary: This bill renames the State Board of Examiners of Landscape Architects to the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects, updates related terminology, and modifies board membership qualifications, educational requirements, and examination procedures. It also establishes an emeritus status license and updates business permit requirements for firms practicing landscape architecture.
responsible_party: State Board of Professional Landscape Architects
stakeholders: Licensed landscape architects, applicants for landscape architectural licensure, and business entities (corporations, partnerships, and LLCs) offering landscape architectural services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects can implement the bill's changes with existing resources and that revenues are not expected to be materially affected. There is no impact on local government finances. The bill modifies how examination fees are paid and authorizes the board to set fees for emeritus status licenses and license reinstatements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Landscape Architects is an entity within the Maryland Department of Labor. This bill renames the board, alters its membership qualifications, and modifies its licensing, permit, and fee-collection duties.

The bill updates statutory references in the Environment Article to use the new term 'professional landscape architect' specifically in the context of certifying silt and erosion control plans in the Severn River Watershed.

The bill updates references in the Natural Resources Article to use the new term 'professional landscape architect' for professionals authorized to prepare forest stand delineations and forest conservation plans.

The bill amends the Public Utilities Article to update the definition of 'Designer' to include 'professional landscape architects,' which is relevant to the commission's oversight of excavation and demolition safety regulations.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article to update the definition of 'Licensed professional' to include the renamed 'professional landscape architect,' which impacts civil proceedings and professional liability cases.

The bill alters the qualifications for members of the State Board of Professional Landscape Architects, requiring the Office of Appointments to vet candidates based on these new criteria for the Governor's consideration.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and its regulatory boards; this bill's changes to board duties, code of ethics procedures, and licensing status (including emeritus status) require legal review and guidance.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members to the board. The bill modifies the qualifications for these appointees and changes the name of the board within the executive department's oversight.
As the state's principal revenue collector, the Comptroller is responsible for the General Fund, into which the board's licensing fees and penalties are deposited.

bill_summary: This bill designates November 14th as Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day in Maryland public schools to honor Ruby Bridges, the first African American student to integrate an all-white elementary school in 1960. The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is required to provide local school systems with educational resources, such as lesson plans and multimedia materials, to facilitate student discussions regarding civil rights and social justice.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, teachers, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources, though some resources may be temporarily diverted from current priorities. There is no mandatory fiscal impact on local school systems, as the implementation of educational programs remains at their discretion.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the oversight of Maryland's public education system, MSDE is explicitly mandated by the bill to create and make resource materials publicly available for local school systems regarding Ruby Bridges Walk to School Day and pedestrian safety.

The Governor's Office is responsible for overseeing the executive branch and coordinating policy initiatives. This bill designates a specific commemorative day, which often involves executive proclamations or support from the Governor's administration.

MDOT, specifically through the State Highway Administration (SHA) and Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), handles pedestrian safety and 'Safe Routes to School' initiatives. The bill's requirement for pedestrian safety resources directly aligns with MDOT's mission.

As an independent unit within MSDE, the Center focuses on comprehensive school safety. A 'Walk to School Day' involves student safety outside the school building, falling within their broader interest in supportive and safe learning environments.

The bill mandates that educational resources include materials to help teachers engage students in discussions about civil rights and social justice. These topics are central to the mission of the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Technology Development Corporation to adopt certain regulations regarding the consideration of remedies for investments in certain businesses that no longer meet the definition of a qualified business for purposes of provisions of law governing the Corporation; authorizing, rather than requiring, the Corporation to divest itself of an interest under certain circumstances; and authorizing the Corporation to pursue certain other remedies under those circumstances.

bill_summary: The bill modifies the investment and divestment procedures for the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO). It requires TEDCO to adopt regulations for handling businesses that no longer meet the definition of a qualified business and changes the requirement that TEDCO must divest from equity investments within 15 years to an authorization, allowing the corporation to instead pursue other remedies in its best interest.
stakeholders: Businesses receiving equity investments from TEDCO, the TEDCO investment committee, and venture or private equity firms in which TEDCO invests.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances, although financial investment returns to TEDCO may increase due to the added flexibility in managing its investment portfolio. There is no local fiscal impact, and the effect on small businesses is expected to be minimal. Specific dollar estimates for potential increases in investment returns are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly alters the statutory requirements and operational procedures of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO). It mandates that TEDCO adopt new regulations for its investment committee and provides the corporation with greater flexibility in managing its equity investments and divestment strategies.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce works in tandem with TEDCO to foster business growth. The fiscal note identifies Commerce as an information source for this legislation, indicating their involvement in the policy area of technology transfer and business investment.

The OAG provides legal counsel and represents state agencies and instrumentalities. They would be responsible for advising TEDCO on the drafting of the required regulations and ensuring that the new 'remedies' for investments comply with state law and contractual obligations.

bill_summary: House Bill 488 redraws Maryland's eight congressional districts for the 2026 election and proposes a constitutional amendment. This amendment clarifies that state constitutional requirements for legislative districts (such as compactness and population equality) apply only to the General Assembly districts. It also empowers the General Assembly to grant the Supreme Court of Maryland original jurisdiction to review congressional districting and embeds the newly drawn districts into the state constitution until a new plan is adopted following the 2030 census.
stakeholders: Qualified voters in Maryland and candidates for the U.S. House of Representatives
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase State general fund expenditures by at least $3,000,000 in FY 2026 for the State Board of Elections to update mapping software, print and mail new voter identification cards, hire temporary staff, and conduct public outreach. Local boards of elections will also experience significant operational impacts and increased costs, including estimated expenditures of $300,000 per large county for overtime and precinct adjustments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for implementing the new congressional districting plan. The fiscal note identifies a significant impact exceeding $3 million for printing voter identification cards, procuring mapping software, hiring temporary staff, and conducting public outreach for the 2026 elections.

The bill explicitly requires that precinct boundaries used in the districting plan be reviewed and corrected by the Maryland Department of Planning. The agency also serves as the state's technical expert for census data (P.L. 94-171) referenced in the legislation.

The proposed constitutional amendment authorizes the General Assembly to grant original jurisdiction to the Supreme Court of Maryland to review congressional districting. The AOC provides operational and legal support to implement such judicial policy changes.

The Governor is responsible for proclaiming the results of the constitutional amendment referendum. Additionally, the office oversees the executive branch departments implementing the new district boundaries.
As the chief legal officer, the OAG provides legal counsel regarding the constitutional amendments and represents the state in the event of legal challenges to the congressional districting plan.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget and personnel. The bill's fiscal note indicates a significant general fund expenditure increase of approximately $3.5 million in FY 2026 to implement the changes.
The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of the state's official records, including the laws and constitutional amendments passed by the General Assembly and ratified by voters.

Synopsis: Repealing a provision of law prohibiting an electronic health network or electronic medical record vendor from charging a fee for the release of certain patient records or transactions.
Title: Electronic Health Networks and Electronic Medical Record Vendors of Nursing Homes - Release of Records - Fees
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: The bill repeals the provision of law that prohibited electronic health networks and electronic medical record vendors from charging a fee for releasing patient medical records or electronic health care transactions to a nursing home's business associate.
stakeholders: Nursing homes, electronic health networks, electronic medical record (EMR) vendors, and business associates of nursing homes
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill allows electronic health networks and EMR vendors to charge fees for releasing records, which were previously prohibited. This change is expected to increase expenditures for nursing homes or their business associates who must pay these fees. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the text provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for regulating healthcare facilities, including nursing homes, and overseeing the Health-General Article of the Maryland Code, the Department of Health is directly responsible for the implementation and oversight of policies related to patient medical records and the conduct of health record vendors.

The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is an independent regulatory agency within the Department of Health that specifically oversees electronic health networks (EHNs) and health information technology standards in Maryland. The bill directly affects EHN fee structures and data exchange protocols which fall under MHCC's regulatory purview.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission regarding the enforcement of health laws and the regulation of business entities like electronic medical record vendors. They would be involved in interpreting the legal implications of allowing fees for records access.

The Department of Aging advocates for the rights and quality of care for older adults in nursing homes. While not the primary regulator of IT vendors, the department has a vested interest in policies that impact the administrative efficiency and data transparency of long-term care facilities.

Synopsis: Extending the time period during which a certain method is used to calculate compensatory education enrollment through fiscal year 2027;  altering the qualifications for an initial teacher certificate; requiring the State Department of Education to suspend operation of the Expert Review Team Program during the 2026-2027 school year; requiring the Accountability and Implementation Board and the Department to identify a methodology for counting low-income students for purposes of certain funding formulas; etc.

bill_summary: This bill makes several revisions to the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future. Key changes include extending the methodology for counting students from low-income households (compensatory education enrollment) through fiscal 2029, allowing greater flexibility in using Concentration of Poverty Grant funds for programs like fine arts, and updating teacher certification requirements to include apprenticeships. It also delays the National Board Certification requirement for principals until 2034, restructures the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee, and suspends the Expert Review Team Program for the 2026-2027 school year to reallocate funds for other Blueprint purposes.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) and the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB)
stakeholders: Public school students, especially those from low-income households and in Career and Technical Education (CTE) programs; teachers seeking certification; school principals; local boards of education; and county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by $228.5 million in FY 2027, primarily from the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund, with continued increases through FY 2029 due to changes in compensatory aid and Concentration of Poverty grants. Special fund revenues from interest earnings are projected to decrease by $4.7 million in FY 2027. Local school systems will experience an increase in revenues and expenditures, while some county governments will see significant increases in required local appropriations to meet funding mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementer of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future. The bill mandates MSDE to suspend the Expert Review Team Program, determine teacher certification qualifications including portfolio assessments, and collaborate on a new methodology for counting low-income students for funding formulas.

The bill restructures the Career and Technical Education (CTE) Committee as a unit within the Governor's Workforce Development Board. The Board is responsible for approving the list of priority occupations and adopting career pathway information that will guide state curriculum and credentialing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This entry covers the Accountability and Implementation Board (AIB), which requested the bill and is tasked with identifying the methodology for counting low-income students. It also encompasses the restructured CTE Committee which has expanded duties regarding the state's workforce systems.

The Department of Labor staffs the CTE Committee and oversees registered apprenticeship programs, which the bill establishes as a valid pathway for initial teacher certification. The agency is also required to use the new priority occupations list for its workforce programs.

The commission is required to align postsecondary programs with the new career pathway standards. The fiscal note explicitly identifies that the agency will require additional staff and funding to fulfill its expanded role in directing the postsecondary CTE framework.

The Governor oversees the executive agencies implementing these reforms, appoints members to the CTE Committee, and is a recipient of several mandatory reports regarding the Expert Review Team Program and low-income student counting methodology.

The department must be consulted in the development of the new low-income student counting methodology. Furthermore, the bill has a massive fiscal impact on the state budget and special funds, which the department manages.

The Secretary of Commerce is a member of the CTE Committee. The agency is also mandated to use the state's priority occupations list and career pathway information as a guideline for its workforce development initiatives.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller monitors the impact on state revenues and the execution of the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, which is subject to multi-million dollar changes under this legislation.
The Treasurer's Office manages the state's funds and investments, including the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, which the bill utilizes and impacts via altered spending and interest earnings.
As a major provider of postsecondary education, the system is impacted by the requirements to align programs with the new CTE standards and the bill's provisions regarding dual enrollment pathways.
The university must align its career and technical education offerings and teacher preparation programs with the new standards and occupational priority lists established in the bill.
The college is affected by state-level shifts in teacher preparation standards and the requirement to align certain programs with the state's career pathway information.

The bill's focus on creating an accurate methodology for counting low-income students for compensatory education funding directly supports the office's mission to address child poverty and support underinvested communities.

The bill's emphasis on data-driven student counting methodologies and the oversight of Blueprint implementation aligns with the office's role in enhancing government responsiveness and measurable results.
The team is tasked with addressing the Governor's priorities of child poverty and economic mobility, both of which are central to the bill's changes to education funding and career pathway alignment.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a law enforcement agency from making a certain request for verbal acknowledgement in an interaction with a person suspected to have been subjected to sexually assaultive behavior or who claims to have been subjected to sexually assaultive behavior.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Victims of Sexually Assaultive Behavior - Request for Verbal Acknowledgement
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
