bill_summary: This bill prohibits law enforcement agencies from requesting verbal acknowledgments from victims of sexually assaultive behavior that would waive their rights, limit investigation or prosecution, or relieve the agency of its legal obligations.
stakeholders: Victims of sexually assaultive behavior and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances, and no specific dollar estimates are provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly impacted by the bill's prohibition on certain verbal requests to victims and is required to adopt and report a policy for enforcing these provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and oversees the Maryland Sexual Assault Evidence Kit Policy and Funding Committee, which is the designated recipient of the enforcement policies required by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is responsible for public safety and standard-setting; the bill specifically requires law enforcement to follow follow-up practices recommended by the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which operates under this department.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the implementation of new criminal procedure laws and would represent state law enforcement agencies in any injunctive or declaratory relief actions brought by victims under the bill.
MDOT operates the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) Police, a state law enforcement agency that must comply with the bill's interaction prohibitions and policy adoption requirements.

The Department of Natural Resources operates the Natural Resources Police, which is a state law enforcement agency required to comply with the bill's mandates regarding interactions with victims of sexually assaultive behavior.
DGS operates the Maryland Capitol Police, a law enforcement agency that must comply with the bill's requirements regarding victim interactions and policy reporting.

The bill creates a specific cause of action allowing victims to seek injunctive or declaratory relief in court if a law enforcement agency violates the act, which impacts judicial operations and policy support.
The University System of Maryland institutions maintain campus police departments that qualify as law enforcement agencies and must adhere to the bill's prohibitions and policy requirements.
Morgan State University maintains its own police force as a state agency, which must comply with the bill's requirements for law enforcement interactions with victims.
As a state institution with a campus security or police presence, it must ensure compliance with state law enforcement standards and the specific prohibitions established by this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing minimum adequate security standards for courtroom security at all courthouse facilities; requiring a court security officer to meet the qualifications for a special police officer; and requiring a minimum number of court security officers be present for certain types of proceedings.
Title: Courtroom Security - Minimum Adequate Security Standard
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill establishes minimum adequate security standards for courthouse facilities in Maryland. It requires entities responsible for courthouse security to use best efforts to meet specific staffing levels: at least one officer for criminal, family, or juvenile proceedings (starting July 2027) and all proceedings (starting July 2029); two officers for proceedings involving incarcerated or potentially remanded individuals; and additional officers based on the number of courtrooms per floor. Security officers must meet the qualifications of a special peace police officer.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and local entities responsible for providing courthouse security (typically county sheriffs' offices)
stakeholders: Maryland Judiciary, county sheriffs' offices, local governments, and individuals participating in court proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Judiciary can comply using existing resources. However, local government expenditures are expected to increase significantly beginning in FY 2027 to hire additional security personnel. The FY 2027 State budget includes $5,600,000 to assist local jurisdictions, but total local costs are estimated to be much higher; for instance, Prince George's County estimates a $10,000,000 impact and Baltimore City estimates over $4,500,000 for additional security officers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Judicial Conference and the Administrative Office of the Courts (AOC) staffed the task force that developed these standards. The AOC is responsible for the operational and financial support of the Judicial Branch, which must implement these security standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes specific staffing requirements for proceedings involving incarcerated individuals or those who may be remanded to custody. DPSCS is responsible for the supervision and transportation of these individuals and works closely with court security.
The bill specifically mandates security staffing standards for juvenile proceedings, which are directly managed and attended by DJS personnel.

The Register of Wills serves as the Clerk to the Orphans' Court. The bill's standards apply to all courthouse facilities and specifically to all types of proceedings by 2029, which includes the probate matters overseen by this agency.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is involved because the fiscal note indicates the FY 2027 budget includes $5.6 million to assist local jurisdictions in meeting these new security mandates.
The Governor's Office proposes the annual state budget, which currently includes the funding necessary to support the implementation of these security standards across the state.
DHS caseworkers are frequently involved in family and juvenile proceedings, which are two of the categories specifically prioritized for mandatory security staffing under the bill.

The bill requires court security officers to meet the qualifications of a special peace police officer as defined in the Public Safety Article, which aligns with law enforcement standards overseen or influenced by the State Police.

The requirement for local jurisdictions and the state to hire and manage significant numbers of new security personnel may involve collective bargaining and labor relations issues under the board's jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Increasing from five to six the number of associate judges in the District Court in District 11 by increasing from two to three the number of associate judges appointed from Washington County.
Title: Washington County - Judgeships - District Court
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled
bill_summary: This bill increases the number of judges in Maryland by adding one associate judge to the District Court in Washington County and one resident judge to the Circuit Court in St. Mary’s County.
stakeholders: Residents of Washington County and St. Mary's County, judicial staff, and the legal community.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $786,900 in FY 2027 for two new judgeships and associated staff, including courtroom clerks, a law clerk, and contractual bailiffs. Expenditures are projected to increase to approximately $1,051,300 by FY 2031. St. Mary’s County expenditures are expected to increase by $85,500 in FY 2027 and $114,000 annually thereafter for local staff and operating costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the AOC is responsible for the operational, financial, and technological implementation of the new judgeships and associated support staff positions created by this bill.
This office assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for judicial vacancies, including the new judgeships established by this legislation.
The Governor is the constitutional authority responsible for appointing judges to the District and Circuit Courts, and this bill expands the number of appointments the Governor must make.

DBM is responsible for the state's budget development and supervision. The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in general fund expenditures ($786,900 in FY 2027) to fund the new positions, which DBM must manage.
The Comptroller's office is responsible for paying state employees and managing state revenues; it will handle the payroll for the additional judges and staff authorized by the bill.
The Treasurer's Office manages the distribution of state funds and provides insurance protection for state property and employees, including the new personnel and positions established here.
The SRA administers retirement benefits for judges and state employees; the additional judges and clerks will become members of the State Retirement and Pension System managed by this agency.

Synopsis: Requiring certain entities to provide reimbursement to health care providers in a manner that meets the annual primary care investment targets established by the State on or after February 1, 2026; and requiring certain entities to provide a description of the entity's progress in meeting the annual primary care investment targets to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner when filing a premium rate or premium rate change with the Commissioner.
Title: Health Insurance - Primary Care Investment Targets - Reimbursement and Reporting
Status: In the Senate - Favorable Report by Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers to align their provider reimbursements with annual primary care investment targets established by the State. Carriers are also required to report their progress in meeting these targets to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner when filing premium rates or rate changes.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, primary care providers, and participants in the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill using existing resources. State expenditures for the employee health plan may increase by an indeterminate but likely minimal amount starting in FY 2027, including an estimated 3% rate increase for the Kaiser fully insured plan. There is no expected impact on revenues or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires health insurance carriers to report progress on primary care investment targets to the Insurance Commissioner during premium rate filings, making MIA the primary regulatory body for compliance and enforcement.

MHCC is responsible for the Primary Care Investment Workgroup and annual reporting on primary care spending; the bill implements recommendations for legislative accountability that emerged from the Commission's workgroup and analysis.

DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note indicates that the bill will increase expenditures for the state's fully insured health plan option (Kaiser).
The bill's primary care investment targets were formally established via a 2025 Executive Order signed by the Governor, who also oversees the strategic policy initiatives for the executive branch.
MDH sets health policy, regulates Health Maintenance Organizations (HMOs) affected by the bill, and manages Medicaid, which is a component of the all-payer investment model.

Synopsis: Providing that a certain individual duly and in good faith attending a certain court proceeding is immune from a certain immigration arrest in connection with attendance at a court proceeding under certain circumstances; and prohibiting a person from making an arrest in violation of the Act.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Immigration Arrest - Immunity in Connection With Court Proceeding
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: This bill provides immunity from civil immigration arrests for individuals who are parties or witnesses in a court proceeding, as well as their family or household members, while they are traveling to, attending, or returning from court. This immunity applies unless the arrest is authorized by a valid judicial warrant. The bill establishes criminal penalties for violations—misdemeanors for standard violations and felonies if the arrest results in serious bodily injury—and authorizes the Attorney General or affected individuals to seek declaratory or injunctive relief through civil actions.
stakeholders: Individuals attending court proceedings (including parties, witnesses, and their families or household members), law enforcement officers, and court personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal impact on State and local revenues and expenditures through its criminal penalty provisions (fines and incarceration costs). State general fund expenditures may increase by an estimated $272,000 annually for the Office of the Attorney General to hire one assistant Attorney General and one paralegal to handle litigation authorized by the bill, though the actual necessity for additional staff will depend on the volume of cases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes immunity from immigration arrest for individuals attending, going to, or returning from court proceedings. As the central support agency for the Maryland Judicial Branch, the Administrative Office of the Courts is directly responsible for the operations and policies within court locations where these protections apply.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions for declaratory and injunctive relief on behalf of the State or residents. Additionally, the fiscal note indicates a direct impact on the agency, necessitating additional personnel to handle potential litigation resulting from the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants, who are 'parties' specifically protected from immigration arrest under the bill. The agency's clients and witnesses are direct beneficiaries of the immunity established by this legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal offenses (misdemeanors and felonies) for violating the prohibition on immigration arrests. This leads to a potential fiscal impact on the department regarding incarceration costs for individuals convicted under these new provisions.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing the motor vehicle and criminal laws of the state, including the new criminal penalties established for illegal immigration arrests at court proceedings.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. This bill relates to the Governor's role in enforcing state laws and overseeing the state's stance on civil immigration enforcement and judicial accessibility.

Synopsis: Authorizing a voter unaffiliated with a political party to vote the ballot for unaffiliated voters or the ballot of the political party of the voter's choice in a primary election; and prohibiting a voter unaffiliated with a political party who votes the ballot of a political party in a primary election from automatically becoming affiliated with the political party whose ballot the voter voted.
Title: Election Law - Unaffiliated Voters - Open Primary Elections
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill authorizes voters not affiliated with a political party to participate in primary elections by choosing to vote either a party-specific ballot or an unaffiliated voter ballot without automatically changing their registration status. It also allows political parties to permit voters affiliated with different parties to participate in their primaries and requires the State Board of Elections to update voter registration applications and absentee ballot processes to accommodate these changes.
stakeholders: Unaffiliated voters in Maryland, affiliated party members, political parties, and state and local election officials
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The legislation does not explicitly state funding amounts or mandates, though implementation would require the State Board of Elections to update the statewide voter registration system, application forms, and absentee ballot materials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary authority for supervising and administering elections in Maryland, the State Board of Elections is directly responsible for implementing the bill's requirements to allow unaffiliated voters to participate in party primaries, managing the logistics of ballot distribution, and updating the statewide voter registration system.

The bill mandates changes to the disclosures and processes within automatic voter registration systems, which are primarily operated by the MVA, requiring them to update how they inform applicants about party affiliation and voting eligibility in primary elections.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections and the General Assembly regarding the implementation of the new law and ensures the provisions comply with state and federal constitutional and statutory requirements.

The department is responsible for the fiscal oversight and budget management of the state agencies, including the State Board of Elections, which will require additional funding for ballot printing, software updates, and public education campaigns necessitated by this bill.

DoIT manages the state's IT strategy and infrastructure; they would likely be involved in the technical modifications to the statewide voter registration database and automatic registration interfaces to support the new primary voting options for unaffiliated voters.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives, including election reform, and will be responsible for the overall execution and enforcement of these law changes.

Synopsis: Altering from not more than 7 to not more than 14 days after issuance, the time period during which a temporary protective order is effective: and altering the time period during which a final protective order hearing is to be held to not later than 14 days after the temporary protective order is issued.
Title: Family Law - Temporary and Final Protective Orders - Duration
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the duration and timing of protective orders by extending the effective period of a temporary protective order from 7 days after service to 14 days after issuance. It also requires that a final protective order hearing be held no later than 14 days after the temporary protective order is issued, rather than 7 days after it is served.
stakeholders: Individuals seeking protective orders (petitioners), individuals against whom protective orders are filed (respondents), and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures and timelines for domestic violence proceedings, specifically altering the duration of temporary protective orders and the mandatory scheduling of final protective order hearings. The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for the operational and administrative support of the judicial branch to implement these statutory changes.

State and local law enforcement are responsible for serving and enforcing protective orders. The bill shifts the timing for temporary protective orders from a duration based on the 'date of service' to the 'date of issuance,' which impacts the operational window for police to locate and serve respondents before the order expires or the final hearing occurs.

As the primary state agency for social services and protection against abuse, DHS works with victims who utilize the protective order process. Changes to the duration and timing of these orders impact the safety planning and case management services provided by local departments of social services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates state strategies for public safety and victim services. Since protective orders are a critical tool in reducing domestic violence and recidivism, the policy change regarding the timing of legal protections is relevant to their public safety mission.

The OAG serves as the primary legal representative for the state and provides counsel to state agencies, including the Judiciary and the Department of Human Services, regarding the interpretation and implementation of family law statutes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in various legal proceedings. While protective orders are civil, the respondents represented by OPD in related criminal or juvenile matters are directly impacted by the accelerated or altered timelines for final protective order hearings.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the enforcement of state laws and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Governor's approval and involves interagency coordination between law enforcement and social services.

Synopsis: Repealing the exemption from the certificate of need requirement for a change in bed capacity for intermediate care facilities that offer substance use disorder treatment services; providing a certificate of need is not required for a change in bed capacity at certain facilities offering certain treatment services if a written notice is filed with the Commission 45 days before the facility's establishment, the facility is consistent with the State Health Plan, will result in more efficient service delivery, and is in the public interest; etc.
Title: Certificate of Need - Intermediate Health Care Facilities

bill_summary: This bill repeals the existing certificate of need (CON) exemption for changes in bed capacity at intermediate care facilities offering residential or intensive substance-related disorder treatment services. It establishes a new exemption for establishing, operating, or changing the bed capacity of intermediate care facilities that offer medically managed residential substance use disorder treatment services, provided the facility notifies the Maryland Health Care Commission and the Commission finds the proposal consistent with the State health plan and in the public interest.
stakeholders: Intermediate health care facilities, providers of medically managed residential substance use disorder treatment services (ASAM Level 3.7 programs), and patients seeking substance use disorder treatment.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no effect on State revenues. Any additional workload for the Maryland Health Care Commission to review notices and make findings regarding intermediate care facilities can be managed with existing budgeted resources. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Health Care Commission (MHCC) is the primary agency responsible for the Certificate of Need (CON) program. The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Maryland Health Care Commission, advising on the interpretation and enforcement of the Certificate of Need statutes and the State Health Plan.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates state health policy initiatives, including efforts to address substance use disorders and improve health care facility efficiency.
As the state's fiscal and personnel agency, DBM monitors the fiscal impact and resource allocation for MDH and MHCC as they implement the modified regulatory requirements described in the bill.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases from state agencies; decisions made by the Commission regarding Certificate of Need applications or licensing may potentially be appealed to an Administrative Law Judge.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises on public safety and behavioral health strategies; substance use disorder treatment is a critical component of state policy aimed at reducing crime and recidivism.

The bill modifies signature validation requirements to allow for name derivatives if identity can be confirmed, permits the correction of technical deficiencies in invalidated signatures by the signer, and updates timelines for judicial review and sponsor notification regarding petition deficiencies.
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, petition sponsors, petition circulators, the State Board of Elections, and local boards of elections.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures increase by up to $10,000 in fiscal 2027 only for the State Board of Elections to hire a consultant to assist with developing electronic signature standards. State revenues and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is entirely focused on election law, specifically the registration voter list and the petition process. SBE is the primary agency responsible for adopting regulations for secure voter data storage, electronic signature procedures, and managing the petition validation process.
The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations that specify requirements for the accessibility of electronic signature pages for people with disabilities.
The bill alters the timeline and procedures for judicial review of petition determinations, which impacts the administration of the judicial branch and court proceedings.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will provide legal counsel to the State Board of Elections regarding the new regulations and represent the state in judicial reviews of petition determinations.
The fiscal note indicates a general fund expenditure increase of $10,000 for a consultant to assist with electronic signature standards, which falls under DBM's budget oversight.

bill_summary: This bill expands the State sales and use tax exemption for precious metal bullion or coins by removing the requirement that the sale must take place at the Baltimore Convention Center to qualify for the exemption. fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $2,500,000 in FY 2027 and by $2,800,000 in FY 2031. Additionally, revenues for the Blueprint for Maryland’s Future Fund are projected to decrease by $300,000 in FY 2027 and by $400,000 in FY 2031. The total estimated revenue loss in FY 2027 is $2,800,000. There is no impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and is responsible for collecting and enforcing the sales and use tax. This bill directly changes the taxability of precious metals, which the Comptroller must implement and manage.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. The bill's projected reduction in General Fund revenues (estimated at $2.5 million in FY 2027) directly impacts the state's budget development and fiscal outlook.
The bill reduces revenues directed to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund, which is the primary funding source for the educational policies and leadership overseen by MSDE.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. Changes to tax law and the resulting impacts on the General Fund and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund affect executive policy priorities and budget planning.

As the state's chief financial agency responsible for managing state funds and serving on the Board of Public Works, the Treasurer's Office is relevant to significant changes in state revenue streams and fiscal integrity.

bill_summary: This bill reclassifies and increases the criminal penalties for sexual offenses committed by individuals in positions of authority, such as teachers or coaches, against minors. It establishes a new felony offense for such acts involving victims under the age of 13, increases sentences for repeat offenders, mandates Tier III sex offender registration for these felonies, and includes these crimes as predicate offenses for the charge of sexual solicitation of a minor.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary, Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services, Office of the Public Defender, and the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy
stakeholders: Minors in schools and youth programs, individuals working in positions of authority (such as teachers, coaches, and volunteers), and the Maryland criminal justice and correctional systems
fiscal_impact_summary: The formal Fiscal Note states that the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. While the bill increases penalties and creates new felonies, which may shift caseloads from the District Court to circuit courts and lead to longer incarceration periods, no specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditures are provided as the fiscal impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and signs bills into law. This bill involves significant changes to criminal law policy and public safety enforcement, which are core policy areas for the Governor.

The bill's definition of 'person in a position of authority' specifically includes employees and volunteers of public and private preschools, elementary schools, and secondary schools. MSDE oversees these school systems and educational policies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new felonies, increases terms of imprisonment for certain sexual offenses, and modifies the Tier III sex offender registry requirements. DPSCS is responsible for managing correctional facilities and the supervision of justice-involved individuals, including those on the registry.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies in Maryland. This bill directly impacts criminal justice policy and sexual offense statutes.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police are involved in the investigation of criminal law violations and the administration or enforcement of the sex offender registry requirements mentioned in the bill.

The fiscal note indicates that the bill will likely shift cases from the District Court to the Circuit Courts due to the reclassification of certain offenses from misdemeanors to felonies. The AOC provides the operational and financial support for these court systems.

MCSS is responsible for coordinating school safety and provides training and resources to schools. Since the bill targets sexual offenses by school personnel and volunteers (positions of authority), it is highly relevant to their mission of fostering safe learning environments.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent defendants. Changes to criminal penalties, the creation of new felonies, and the expansion of the sex offender registry directly impact the legal defense services they provide and their overall caseload complexity.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state and represents the state in criminal appeals. This bill modifies the Criminal Law and Criminal Procedure articles, which requires legal oversight and potential enforcement by the OAG.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. stakeholders: Full-time sworn law enforcement officers at the rank of lieutenant or below and court security officers in the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Baltimore City expenditures may increase due to the establishment of collective bargaining rights for salaries and wages; however, specific dollar estimates are unavailable because Baltimore City did not provide requested information on fiscal and operational impacts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts court security officers and deputy sheriffs in Baltimore City. As the state's chief financial officer and paymaster, the Comptroller is responsible for processing payroll and managing state employee accounts. Changes to the compensation structures (including salary and wages) for the Baltimore City Sheriff's Office employees, who are technically state employees, would involve the Comptroller's financial administration.

As the principal personnel and budget agency for the State, DBM manages state employee benefits and policies. Since deputy sheriffs are state employees, the expansion of their collective bargaining rights to include wages and salary involves DBM's oversight of state personnel regulations.

The bill allows for collective bargaining over salary, wages, and merit step increases. Because these officers are members of the State Retirement and Pension System, negotiated changes to their compensation will directly impact the calculation of pension benefits and long-term liabilities managed by the agency.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as legal counsel to all state agencies and constitutional officers, including the Sheriff's Office. The OAG would be responsible for providing legal guidance on the collective bargaining process and representing the Sheriff in legal matters related to labor agreements.

This bill directly expands the scope of matters subject to collective bargaining and changes the bargaining partners, which falls under PERB's regulatory and adjudicatory jurisdiction.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Transformational Project Financing Program within the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO) to support large-scale 'transformational' development projects. Political subdivisions may apply to have certain development districts designated as State-supported, allowing for the diversion of 'net-new' State tax revenues—including income and sales taxes, adjusted for displacement—into a special fund to pay for bond financing and project implementation for up to 30 years.
stakeholders: Maryland political subdivisions (counties and Baltimore City), economic developers, and communities within or surrounding designated development districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a mechanism to divert State General Fund revenues (specifically income, sales, and use taxes) generated within approved development districts to the Transformational Project Financing Fund for project-related costs and debt service. While the program requires that projects demonstrate a net positive fiscal benefit to the State using displacement adjustments (10% to 60% reductions based on sector), it results in a redirection of tax revenue that would otherwise be collected by the State. Local governments must also pledge property tax increments to these districts. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note were unavailable in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Transformational Project Financing Program specifically within the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (MEDCO). MEDCO is responsible for administering the program, approving State-supported development districts, determining if improvement plans are 'transformational,' and managing the application process.

The Comptroller is responsible for certifying the amount of net-new State revenue (income, sales, and other taxes) attributable to each district, transferring these funds to the Transformational Project Financing Fund, and evaluating the displacement adjustment percentages every two years.
The State Treasurer is required to hold the Transformational Project Financing Fund separately and is responsible for investing the money within the fund.

The bill defines 'Priority Areas' based on designations managed by DHCD, including Sustainable Communities and Main Street Maryland communities. Portions of districts in these areas are exempt from displacement adjustments, directly affecting the amount of State revenue diverted to the project.

The bill identifies Enterprise Zones and Arts and Entertainment Districts—both managed by the Department of Commerce—as 'Priority Areas' which are exempt from displacement adjustments in the revenue calculation.
As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees the impact of diverting State income and sales tax revenues from the General Fund into the new Transformational Project Financing Fund.
The bill includes 'Priority Funding Areas,' which are designated and managed by the Department of Planning, as 'Priority Areas' that qualify for a waiver of displacement adjustments.
The bill includes 'Transit-Oriented Developments' (TOD), defined under the Transportation Article, as 'Priority Areas' for the purposes of the financing program.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and economic development policy; this program represents a significant new mechanism for State-supported economic development projects.

The Board oversees significant State fiscal matters and expenditures. While the bonds are issued by MEDCO or political subdivisions, the diversion of State tax revenue and the fiscal integrity of the program fall under the Board's general interest in State financial obligations.

The OAG would provide legal counsel regarding the implementation of the new program, the drafting of regulations by MEDCO, and the legal review of the multi-jurisdictional agreements required for State-supported development districts.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to coordinate with Virginia authorities to identify Maryland residents who improperly register their vehicles in Virginia and to maintain a searchable database of this information for state and local law enforcement. It also significantly increases the civil penalties for speed camera and work zone violations involving these specific vehicles, with fines ranging from $250 to $1,250 depending on the recorded speed.
stakeholders: Maryland residents with vehicles improperly registered in Virginia, drivers and owners of such vehicles, state and local law enforcement agencies, the Maryland Department of Transportation, and the Maryland Judiciary.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues will increase from significantly higher civil penalties for speeding violations by Maryland residents with Virginia-registered cars. These funds are allocated for highway safety and police equipment. The MVA can implement the database with existing resources, but the Judiciary identifies a potential $1,400,000 cost for IT upgrades to manage automated citations, though this is not exclusively attributable to this bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for the operations of the District Court, which must prescribe the uniform citation forms for the new penalty structure and process contested citations. The fiscal note also indicates that the bill's expansion of automated enforcement systems may necessitate upgrades to the Judiciary's case management systems.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and estimating revenues, which will be affected by the increased civil penalties distributed to the General Fund and the Transportation Trust Fund.

MDOT is the parent department for the MVA, SHA, and MDTA. It oversees the state's transportation network and the modal administrations directly tasked with implementing the database and managing the speed monitoring systems affected by the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the primary coordinating body for public safety and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies. The bill's changes to automated speed enforcement penalties and the creation of a cross-border registration database fall within its public safety policy purview.

The Maryland State Police is involved in work zone speed enforcement and receives a portion of the penalty revenues from work zone speed control systems to purchase replacement vehicles and equipment.

The MDTA operates toll facilities equipped with speed monitoring systems. It will utilize the MVA's new database to identify improperly registered vehicles and issue citations with the increased penalties established by the bill.

The MVA is specifically mandated by the bill to enter into an agreement with Virginia to obtain registration data, compile a searchable database of improperly registered vehicles, and make that data available to other agencies for enforcement.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and will likely be involved in reviewing the interstate agreement between Maryland and the Commonwealth of Virginia required by the bill.

The SHA operates speed monitoring and work zone speed control systems on state highways. It will be a primary user of the new database and a recipient of the increased fine revenues for highway safety and system preservation.

bill_summary: This bill expands the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit by broadening the definition of eligible projects to include historic, privately owned commercial properties that are substantially vacant or functionally obsolescent. It expands the geographic areas where projects may qualify to include Arts and Entertainment Districts, Main Street Maryland communities, and Priority Funding Areas. The bill increases the tax credit from 20% to 25% of eligible costs and significantly raises the annual aggregate cap for tax credit certificates from $15,000,000 every two years to $35,000,000 every year, with future annual adjustments for inflation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Individuals, nonprofit organizations, and business entities developing historic or vacant commercial properties; financial institutions; and residents of Arts and Entertainment Districts, Main Street Maryland communities, and Priority Funding Areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the maximum aggregate amount of tax credit certificates that the Department of Housing and Community Development may award from $15,000,000 every two years to $35,000,000 every year. This represents a potential annual State revenue decrease of up to $35,000,000. Additionally, the maximum aggregate amount will be adjusted annually starting July 1, 2027, based on the Consumer Price Index for the Washington Metropolitan Area. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note were not provided, but the bill text explicitly establishes these new limits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for the Catalytic Revitalization Project Tax Credit, the Secretary of Housing and Community Development is responsible for issuing tax credit certificates, defining eligible costs, publishing guidance, and adopting regulations.
The Comptroller is the state's principal tax collector and will be responsible for administering the income tax credits claimed by taxpayers and managing the resulting impact on state tax revenues.

The bill explicitly requires the Secretary of DHCD to consult with the Department of Commerce when adopting regulations. The credit also targets Arts and Entertainment districts, which fall under the scope of the Department of Commerce.

The bill defines projects based on their location within Priority Funding Areas and their status as historic properties, both of which involve data and oversight managed by the Department of Planning and the Maryland Historical Trust.

The bill significantly increases the aggregate limit for tax credit certificates from $15 million every two years to $35 million annually, necessitating oversight from the state's principal fiscal agency regarding long-term revenue impact.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, and will be responsible for reviewing the new regulations and statutory alterations mandated by the bill.

bill_summary: This bill updates the definition of 'sexual orientation' within Maryland's hate crime statutes to mean an individual's identity, or perception of identity, in relation to the gender or genders to which they are attracted, while clarifying it does not include gender identity. Additionally, it defines 'hate bias incident' as a non-criminal act of hostility or aggression motivated by a protected class status and mandates the Maryland Department of State Police to collect, analyze, and report data on these incidents and hate crimes to the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.
stakeholders: Individuals within protected classes (including sexual orientation, race, religion, disability, etc.), Maryland Department of State Police, local law enforcement agencies, the State Fire Marshal, and the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to collect, analyze, and disseminate information regarding hate crimes and hate bias incidents from local law enforcement agencies and the State Fire Marshal.
The Maryland State Police are required to make quarterly reports to the Commission on Civil Rights regarding the information collected on hate crimes and hate bias incidents.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the definition of 'sexual orientation' within the hate crime statutes. This directly impacts the legal defense strategies and case evaluations for indigent defendants represented by the Office of the Public Defender.

As the support agency for the judicial branch, the AOC is impacted by changes to criminal definitions that will be adjudicated in the state's courts. The AOC also provided data for the bill's fiscal note.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The GOCPP coordinates statewide public safety strategies and manages funds for law enforcement and victim services. The data collected on hate bias incidents is critical to their policy development and crime reduction missions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of State Police and the Commission on Civil Rights, who are the primary agencies responsible for implementing the reporting and definitions mandated by this bill.
Disability is a protected class specifically named in the bill's reporting and hate crime mandates. The department tracks policies affecting residents with disabilities.

Homelessness is a protected class under the hate crime and hate bias reporting statutes. The department, which administers homeless solutions, has a secondary interest in the protection and safety data related to this population.

Hate bias incidents, including online slurs and name-calling, frequently impact school environments. This agency coordinates school safety training and resources that may be informed by the new reporting requirements.

bill_summary: This emergency bill prohibits charitable organizations from participating in or intervening in political campaigns for or against candidates for public office. It authorizes the Secretary of State and the Attorney General to jointly order the revocation of an organization's state tax-exempt status (including income, sales and use, and property tax exemptions) for two years if the organization is found to have willfully violated this prohibition. The bill also establishes civil penalties and requires charitable registration statements to include a pledge of non-intervention in political campaigns. Implementation is contingent upon federal actions that weaken or nullify the federal Johnson Amendment.
responsible_party: The Secretary of State, the Attorney General, the Comptroller, and the Director of the State Department of Assessments and Taxation.
stakeholders: Maryland charitable organizations, donors to those organizations, political candidates, and state and local tax authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates an indeterminate increase in state and local revenue. Specific impacts include civil penalties of up to $5,000 per violation (with each 5-day period of non-compliance counting as a separate violation) and the potential for increased tax revenue from income, sales and use, and property taxes if a charitable organization's exemptions are revoked for a two-year period. A formal Fiscal Note with specific aggregate dollar estimates was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State is the primary regulator of charitable organizations in Maryland. This bill grants the Secretary direct authority to investigate violations of nonpartisanship, issue cease and desist orders, and jointly order the revocation of a charity's tax-exempt status.

The Attorney General is granted joint authority with the Secretary of State to enforce the act, litigate for restraining orders, and monitor federal legal changes regarding the 'Johnson Amendment' to trigger the act's provisions.
The Comptroller is explicitly mandated by the bill to revoke income tax and sales and use tax exemptions for any charitable organization found in violation of the nonpartisanship requirements.

The bill provides for administrative hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act for organizations contesting civil penalties or the revocation of tax-exempt status, which are typically adjudicated by OAH judges.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Secretary of State and coordinates the significant policy shift regarding the tax-exempt requirements of state-regulated charities.
The department oversees state fiscal health; the bill's provisions regarding the revocation of tax exemptions and the collection of civil penalties will impact general fund revenues.
The Tax Court is the administrative body responsible for hearing appeals from final decisions of the Comptroller and other taxing authorities regarding tax assessments and exemptions.
The board would handle initial administrative appeals for organizations whose property tax exemptions are revoked under the provisions of this bill.
The bill authorizes the Attorney General to seek restraining orders in circuit court and provides for judicial review of administrative actions, impacting the judicial system's operations.

Law enforcement officers are statutory members of the drug overdose fatality review teams; MSP often coordinates with or serves as the law enforcement representative on these boards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The OAG provides legal counsel to state health agencies and boards on statutory implementation and regulatory compliance related to public health and multidisciplinary review teams.

bill_summary: The Worksite Enforcement Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Department of Labor to establish formal procedures for receiving and investigating complaints regarding mismanagement, fraud, safety threats, wage theft, and worker misclassification. The bill mandates specific response timelines for complainants, ranging from 7 to 30 days depending on the severity of the allegation, and requires the Department to hire five investigators to cover specific geographical regions of the state.
stakeholders: Maryland employees, employers, licensed professionals, the Maryland Department of Labor, and the Office of the Attorney General's Division of Consumer Protection
fiscal_impact_summary: Starting in fiscal year 2027, the bill creates a mandated annual appropriation of $500,000 for the Maryland Department of Labor to employ five regional investigators. Additionally, the State must provide for travel expense reimbursements for these investigators under standard State travel regulations. A formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, but the bill text explicitly mandates these expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department of Labor is mandated to establish procedures for investigating complaints, meet specific response timelines for issues like wage theft and worker misclassification, hire five regional investigators, and coordinate with the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of Labor to cooperate and coordinate investigative efforts with the OAG's Division of Consumer Protection, including mandatory referrals when preliminary investigations warrant them.

The bill mandates that the Governor include a specific $500,000 annual appropriation in the state budget beginning in Fiscal Year 2027 to fund the new investigator positions within the Executive Branch.

As the state's personnel and budget agency, DBM will be responsible for managing the mandated appropriation and the creation, classification, and oversight of the five new investigator positions and their travel reimbursements.

The OLA will be responsible for conducting fiscal and performance audits of the Department of Labor's new complaint-handling operations and the management of the specifically mandated funds to ensure legal compliance and efficiency.

bill_summary: This bill affirms and clarifies the authority of Maryland's political subdivisions to adopt local laws and regulations regarding air emission standards, ambient air quality, and solid waste management, provided these local standards are at least as stringent as state requirements. It also specifies that the state's approval of county water and sewerage plans does not restrict local contracting or regulatory authority, and requires the Department of the Environment to publicize these authorities on its website.
stakeholders: Maryland political subdivisions (counties and municipalities), regulated entities such as industrial facilities and waste management systems, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill creates an administrative requirement for the Maryland Department of the Environment to update its website by October 1, 2026. There may be indirect fiscal impacts on local governments that choose to implement and enforce more stringent standards and on regulated entities required to comply with them.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for setting state emission and solid waste standards. The bill modifies the Environment Article of the Maryland Code, requires MDE to approve county water and sewer plans with new local-authority caveats, and mandates MDE to publish specific information on its website regarding the legal authority of political subdivisions.

The bill addresses legal conflicts and judicial interpretations regarding the authority of local governments versus state law. The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to MDE and other agencies and representing the state in litigation concerning the stringency and 'technical possibility' of complying with concurrent standards.

MES provides operational and technical services for water, wastewater, and solid waste management. Changes in local authority to set more stringent standards than the state baseline would directly impact MES operations, facility compliance requirements, and existing contracts with local jurisdictions.

The bill references county water and sewerage plans, which are central to land use planning. MDP provides data analysis and policy guidance to local governments to ensure infrastructure plans align with sustainable growth and environmental preservation.

Air quality and solid waste management are critical components of public health. The bill explicitly mentions local laws providing 'greater protection to the public health, safety, or welfare,' which intersects with MDH's mission to protect and improve the health of Maryland residents.

Local emission and waste standards can impact agricultural operations, such as animal waste management and farm equipment emissions. MDA oversees programs related to pesticide regulation and soil conservation that may overlap with more restrictive local environmental rules.

The bill's expansion of local regulatory authority could create a varied landscape of environmental standards across the state, which affects the business climate and economic development efforts to attract and retain companies.

The Governor oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires a state agency (MDE) to formally recognize and publish information on local authority, which reflects a shift in statewide environmental policy and intergovernmental relations.

OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including MDE. Disputes regarding the enforcement of local versus state environmental regulations or the 'technical possibility' of complying with both sets of standards may result in hearings overseen by OAH.

The PSC regulates utilities and power plants that are significant sources of emissions. Local standards for air quality or refuse disposal (including waste-to-energy) could potentially overlap or conflict with facilities under the PSC's regulatory jurisdiction.

Additionally, sports wagering licensees must provide anonymized transactional and metrics data to Morgan State University, Bowie State University, and the University of Maryland School of Medicine for research purposes.
responsible_party: State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission
stakeholders: Sports wagering licensees, fantasy competition operators, collegiate athletes, individuals with gambling problems, Morgan State University, Bowie State University, and the University of Maryland School of Medicine.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect gaming revenues. Although Bowie State University estimated an annual cost of $700,000 for data analysis, the Fiscal Note indicates that such analysis is not mandated by the bill. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency

The bill requires the sharing of voluntary exclusion list contact information with this center and may increase demand for the treatment services MDH manages.
The bill explicitly requires sports wagering licensees to provide quarterly transactional data and metrics to Morgan State University for the purpose of conducting research and prevalence studies.

The bill requires data sharing with the University of Maryland School of Medicine and Bowie State University (both USM institutions) for research purposes. The OAG serves as the primary legal counsel to the State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission and would be responsible for advising the agency on the development and legal implementation of the mandatory regulations and enforcement mechanisms described in the bill.
