The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) centralizes the administration of collective bargaining for public sector employees. Since the bill establishes grievance rights linked to collective bargaining agreements and exclusive representatives, PERB is relevant to the labor relations aspects of the mandate.

The Comptroller functions as the state's chief financial officer and paymaster. For state-employed firefighters, the Comptroller's office would need to ensure that physical or digital pay stubs meet the new specific reporting requirements for hours worked and pay rates.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like MDOT and DBM regarding the implementation of new labor laws and would represent the state in legal disputes or complex grievance proceedings arising from the bill.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies (such as MDOT and MD Labor) that must implement these changes and coordinates the policy initiatives related to labor standards and state personnel management.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to include in an annual report to certain committees of the General Assembly the amount of proceeds from a certain agricultural land transfer tax that are attributable to the taxation of certain instruments of writing that transfer title to parcels of land that are entirely woodland that were distributed to the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund during the immediately preceding fiscal year; and requiring the Department to report any uncertainties regarding certain amounts.
Title: Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund - Reporting
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Department of Natural Resources to include specific details in its annual report regarding the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund. Specifically, the department must report the amount of agricultural land transfer tax proceeds distributed to the fund from the preceding fiscal year and disclose any uncertainties related to those distributions along with plans to resolve them.
stakeholders: Owners of woodland property, students seeking careers in natural resources, and the Department of Natural Resources.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Natural Resources can fulfill the new reporting requirements using existing resources. The underlying agricultural land transfer tax distribution to the fund remains capped at $200,000 annually under existing law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) is the primary agency impacted by this bill. It manages the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund and is directly responsible for the new annual reporting requirement regarding the distribution of agricultural land transfer tax proceeds and any related uncertainties.

The Comptroller of Maryland is the state's chief tax collector and is responsible for remitting the agricultural land transfer tax proceeds to the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund. DNR's reporting on the amounts distributed and any uncertainties would likely involve coordination with the Comptroller's Office.

The Office of Legislative Audits conducts fiscal compliance audits and performance evaluations of state agencies. A new statutory requirement for DNR to report on specific fund distributions and 'uncertainties' would likely fall under OLA's oversight during future financial audits of the Department.

The Department of Budget and Management (DBM) is the principal fiscal agency for the state. As the agency responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning, DBM oversees the management of state funds like the Mel Noland Woodland Incentives and Fellowship Fund.

The Smart, Green & Growing initiative coordinates multi-agency efforts, including those of DNR, to promote sustainable development and land preservation. The woodland incentives and fellowships supported by this fund align with the initiative's mission to preserve natural resources.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for proposing the annual state budget and overseeing policy initiatives. As DNR is an executive department, the Governor's Office has general administrative relevance to the implementation of new reporting requirements.

Synopsis: Prohibiting nonpublic schools that participate in State-funded education programs from refusing to provide a current or former student or the student's parent or guardian with a transcript or taking other punitive measures regarding a student's transcript request because the student owes a debt to the nonpublic school.
Title: Nonpublic Schools - Transcripts - Prohibition on Punitive Measures Related to Student Debt
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/01 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Private Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill prohibits nonpublic schools that participate in State-funded education programs from withholding a student's transcript or taking other punitive measures because the student owes a debt to the school. Schools are specifically barred from conditioning transcript issuance on debt payment, charging higher fees for transcripts to students with debt, or using transcripts as a collection tool.
stakeholders: Current and former students of nonpublic schools, parents or guardians of these students, and nonpublic schools participating in State-funded education programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact. However, revenue for approximately 374 nonpublic schools participating in State-funded programs may decrease because they will no longer be able to use the withholding of transcripts as a debt collection tool.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the four state-funded programs (Nonpublic Textbook, Nonpublic School Health and Security, Nonpublic Aging Schools, and BOOST) that determine which nonpublic schools are subject to this bill. MSDE also tracks complaints related to the withholding of transcripts for debt.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies like MSDE and enforces consumer protection laws. This bill creates a new legal prohibition on certain debt collection practices by schools, which may fall under the OAG's enforcement or advisory purview.

The Department of Budget and Management was consulted in the development of the fiscal note to assess the bill's impact on state finances and operations. While it does not implement the policy, it oversees the fiscal health of the programs providing the state funding mentioned in the bill.

Synopsis: Increasing from $50,000 to $100,000 the maximum amount of annual revenue a business may generate from the sale of cottage food products to be considered a cottage food business.
Title: Food Establishments - Cottage Food Businesses - Maximum Annual Revenue
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Food -see also- Meat, Poultry, & Seafood; Milk; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum annual revenue limit for a cottage food business from $50,000 to $100,000, allowing more small-scale food producers to operate from residential kitchens without a food manufacturing license.
stakeholders: Cottage food business owners, residential food producers, the Maryland Department of Health, local health departments, and consumers of cottage food products.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $52,400 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Health to hire a part-time registered sanitarian to manage increased cottage food business registrations and inquiries. These costs are projected to rise to approximately $67,700 by FY 2031. General fund revenues may see a minimal, indeterminate decrease if businesses choose to operate as cottage food businesses rather than paying for food manufacturing licenses. Local health departments can likely manage any associated increase in workload with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary regulatory agency for cottage food businesses. The bill amends the Health - General Article, and the fiscal note indicates MDH will require additional staff and funding to manage an increase in requests for unique identification numbers, label reviews, and food safety certifications resulting from the increased revenue cap.

The Department of Agriculture supports the marketing of local agricultural products and the viability of farming. Since cottage food products are frequently sold at farmer's markets, and the agency was consulted in the fiscal analysis, this bill impacts the micro-businesses within the agricultural ecosystem they support.

The bill has a direct fiscal impact on the state's general fund, specifically requiring the creation of a new part-time registered sanitarian position. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and managing state personnel resources.

The bill doubles the annual revenue threshold for cottage food businesses, which acts as an economic stimulus for small, home-based entrepreneurs by allowing them to expand operations before being subject to more stringent commercial licensing requirements.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the Department of Health and is responsible for signing the bill into law and ensuring its implementation aligns with broader state policy priorities regarding small business and public health.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Department of Health and will be involved in advising the agency on regulatory updates needed to comply with the new statutory definition of a cottage food business.

As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller monitors business revenues. The shift of businesses from licensed manufacturers to cottage food businesses may impact tax reporting and revenue streams overseen by this agency.

Synopsis: Expanding certain protections against employment discrimination to apply to temporary disabilities caused or contributed to by childbirth, menopause, or a related medical condition; and authorizing an employer to consider the operational impact of any staffing gap in determining an undue burden imposed by a certain transfer request by an employee.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Reasonable Accommodations - Disabilities Due to Childbirth, Menopause, and Related Medical Conditions
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/25 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands employment discrimination protections to include temporary disabilities caused by childbirth, menopause, and related medical conditions, such as lactation or managing menopause-related symptoms. It requires employers to provide reasonable accommodations—such as modified duties, adjusted work hours, or transfers to less strenuous positions—unless doing so would cause an undue hardship. The legislation also allows employers to consider the operational impact of staffing gaps when determining if a transfer request constitutes an undue burden.
stakeholders: Employees experiencing temporary disabilities due to childbirth, menopause, or related medical conditions; Maryland employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances. The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights, the Judiciary, and the Office of Administrative Hearings are anticipated to handle any increase in complaints using existing resources. While Garrett County noted a potential local expenditure of $60,000 annually if additional staffing is needed to cover transfers, the overall impact on local governments and small businesses is categorized as minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MCCR is the primary agency responsible for enforcing Maryland's anti-discrimination laws in employment. This bill expands the scope of disabilities requiring reasonable accommodation to include childbirth and menopause, requiring MCCR to investigate and resolve new types of complaints.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM manages state employee resources and policies. This bill requires updates to state employee handbooks and employment policies regarding reasonable accommodations and leave across the executive branch.

The OAH provides a hearing process for contested administrative cases. The fiscal note indicates OAH will handle an increase in complaints arising from the bill's expansion of employment discrimination protections.

The AOC supports the Maryland Judicial Branch. The bill's expansion of civil rights protections is expected to result in additional civil actions and appeals within the state court system, as noted in the fiscal analysis.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for the state, providing counsel to all agencies. It will be tasked with advising state entities on compliance with the new accommodation requirements and defending against any related legal challenges.

Synopsis: Establishing a bill of rights for unit owners of a condominium, members of a cooperative housing corporation, and lot owners of a homeowners association.
Title: Residential Owners in Common Ownership Communities - Bill of Rights
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Bill of Rights for residential owners in common ownership communities, including condominiums, cooperative housing corporations, and homeowners associations. It outlines specific rights for owners, such as the right to participate in and receive notice of meetings, vote by secret ballot, access community records, and receive due process during the enforcement of community rules. The bill also authorizes the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to investigate alleged violations and take enforcement actions.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Residential owners (condominium unit owners, cooperative members, and homeowners association lot owners) and the governing bodies of common ownership communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill may result in an indeterminate increase in state expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General to handle the review and enforcement of alleged violations. There is also a potential for an increase in state revenue through the imposition of penalties. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General review alleged violations of laws governing common ownership communities and take direct enforcement actions, including court adjudication and the imposition of penalties.

The Secretary of State is the principal custodian of state records and specifically manages the registration and oversight of condominiums, which are one of the primary types of common ownership communities governed by this Bill of Rights.

The Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various professions; this includes the Board of Common Ownership Community Managers. The bill establishes rights regarding the conduct and training of community managers.

The bill provides for the adjudication of disputes and enforcement actions before a court, which would increase the volume of civil litigation related to common ownership communities managed by the judicial branch.

As the agency responsible for ensuring safe, secure housing and community revitalization, the establishment of a Bill of Rights for residents in common ownership communities directly aligns with their mission to improve the quality of life in Maryland neighborhoods.

The bill establishes a right to nondiscriminatory service from the staff and governing bodies of common ownership communities, which overlaps with the Commission's mandate to enforce anti-discrimination laws in housing.

While the bill mentions court adjudication, many enforcement actions by state agencies like the OAG are initially heard by Administrative Law Judges at the OAH, particularly regarding regulatory violations.

A significant portion of older adults live in common ownership communities (such as condominiums or co-ops with age restrictions). The Department advocates for the rights of older adults in these housing settings.
The bill's provisions regarding the use of community facilities and equal protection may impact residents with disabilities living within these communities.

Synopsis: Requiring each 4-year institution of higher education in the State, by July 1, 2027, that admits first-time undergraduate students to prominently display on its publicly accessible prospective student website a link to the U.S. Department of Education College Scorecard website and share related information in a certain manner; and requiring the Secretary of Higher Education to notify the Department of Legislative Services within 10 days of making a determination that the College Scorecard has been terminated by a federal agency.
Title: 4-Year Institutions of Higher Education - Mandatory Disclosures for New and Prospective Students (Informed Enrollment Act)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Education, Energy, and the Environment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: The Informed Enrollment Act requires four-year institutions of higher education in Maryland that admit first-time undergraduate students to prominently display a link to the U.S. Department of Education's College Scorecard on their websites. Institutions must provide explanations of the scorecard data relating to cost of attendance, graduation rates, salary outcomes, and debt outcomes. This information must be shared during recruitment and orientation, through social media, and with prospective and current students, parents, academic advisors, and career counselors.
responsible_party: Maryland four-year institutions of higher education and the Secretary of Higher Education
stakeholders: Prospective, incoming, and current undergraduate students; parents and guardians; academic advisors; and campus career counselors at Maryland institutions of higher education.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, public four-year institutions, Baltimore City Community College, and local community colleges can comply with the bill's disclosure requirements using existing resources. The Maryland Higher Education Commission can also handle its administrative monitoring duties using existing resources. There is no impact on state or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission oversees policy for both public and private institutions. Furthermore, the Secretary of Higher Education is explicitly tasked with monitoring the federal College Scorecard resource and notifying the Department of Legislative Services if it is discontinued.

USM governs 12 public institutions, many of which are 4-year undergraduate institutions directly impacted by the bill's mandatory disclosure and sharing requirements regarding cost, debt, and salary outcomes.

As an independent 4-year public university, Morgan State must comply with the bill's requirements to display federal scorecard data and share information during student orientation and recruitment events.
As an independent public 4-year honors college, Saint Mary's is directly required to implement the disclosure and information-sharing mandates for its prospective and new students.

The MLDS Center is the state's repository for student and workforce data. While this bill utilizes a federal data resource (College Scorecard), the subject matter of student outcomes, salary, and debt is central to the MLDS mission and the agency was identified as an information source in the fiscal note.
The bill requires institutions to share disclosure information with 'prospective students,' who are primarily high school students within the public education system overseen by MSDE.

The GWDB aligns workforce development with economic goals. Transparency regarding salary outcomes for higher education graduates is relevant to the board's strategy for ensuring pathways to prosperity for Maryland residents.

The team's mission includes enhancing economic mobility and reducing child poverty; the provision of clear information regarding college debt and potential earnings is a key tool for improving economic mobility for Maryland families.

The office focuses on economic opportunities and poverty reduction. Ensuring prospective students have data-driven insights into graduation and salary outcomes supports the office's mission to improve long-term economic stability for Maryland's youth.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Education to provide a pathway for  individuals who are qualified to be child care teachers, but lack proof of necessary educational attainment, to attest to qualifying educational credentials to be a child care teacher teaching in a child care center.
Title: Child Care Centers - Teacher Qualifications - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Board of Education to establish a pathway for individuals to attest to their educational qualifications for child care teacher positions if they lack physical documentation of those credentials. It mandates that the Maryland State Department of Education develop a process for this attestation.
stakeholders: Individuals seeking employment as child care teachers, child care centers, and the Maryland State Department of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The Maryland State Department of Education will likely incur administrative costs to develop and implement the required attestation process for child care teacher credentials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Education to adopt regulations and the Department (MSDE) to establish a process for child care teachers to attest to their educational credentials. MSDE is the primary agency responsible for child care center licensing and oversight of early childhood education programs.

The bill identifies specific academic degrees (such as Early Childhood Education and Child Development) as qualifying credentials. The Commission is responsible for setting policies and standards for the colleges and universities that grant these degrees.

The Department of Labor oversees workforce development and the licensing of various professions. Altering the qualification pathway for child care teachers impacts the state's professional certification and labor supply strategies within the early childhood sector.

The MLDS Center tracks student and workforce data. The creation of a new attestation pathway for educational attainment will require the agency to adjust its data collection and analysis regarding teacher credentials and workforce outcomes.

The Governor's Office for Children coordinates policies to improve the well-being of children and families. Staffing standards and teacher qualifications in child care centers are critical factors in the quality and accessibility of services for Maryland children.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain electric, gas, and gas and electric companies from initiating a proceeding that may lead to a rate change unless the company provides customers with a certain notice; requiring certain electric, gas, and gas and electric companies to include a certain statement in each customer bill and automatic payment e-mail and distribute a certain annual rate report in a certain manner; requiring the Public Service Commission, in consultation with the Office of People's Counsel, to develop a certain report; etc.
Title: Investor-Owned Electric, Gas, and Gas and Electric Companies - Utility Rate Changes (Public Service Company Transparency Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill requires investor-owned electric and gas companies to provide customer notice and a 10-year rate trend report before initiating rate change proceedings. It also mandates that the Public Service Commission (PSC) and the Office of People's Counsel (OPC) develop annual rate reports and that utilities include transparency statements in customer bills.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel
stakeholders: Retail customers of investor-owned electric and gas companies and the companies themselves; municipal electric utilities and electric cooperatives are excluded.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission and the Office of People's Counsel can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Public Service Commission to develop, publish, and manage annual rate reports for investor-owned utilities, consult with the Office of the People’s Counsel, and oversee new transparency requirements for utility companies.

The bill explicitly requires the Office of the People's Counsel to consult with the Public Service Commission on annual rate reports and mandates that the office bring legal cases before the Commission if it determines that a report contains incorrect or misleading information.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and the Office of the People's Counsel regarding the implementation and enforcement of the bill's new regulatory requirements.

The bill's requirements for utility rate transparency and 10-year rate trend reporting provide critical data relevant to the Maryland Energy Administration's role in advising on state energy policy and coordinating long-term energy planning.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the fiscal resources of the implementing agencies; although the fiscal note indicates the bill can be implemented with existing resources, the department remains relevant as the state's principal fiscal agency.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Public Service Commission; this bill represents a significant change in transparency policy for regulated utilities under the Governor's administration.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education to ensure that each public school regularly restock dispensers in the women's restrooms at the school with menstrual hygiene products.
Title: Public Schools - Restocking Menstrual Hygiene Products - Requirement
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Reproductive Matters -see also- Abortion; BrthCntr; Preg
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland county boards of education to ensure that every public school regularly restocks menstrual hygiene product dispensers in women's restrooms to ensure products are available to students at no charge.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students and local county boards of education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates that local county boards of education regularly restock menstrual hygiene products in all public school women's restrooms. While the bill text notes a previous state appropriation of $500,000 in fiscal 2023 for the initial purchase and installation of dispensers, it does not specify a new funding amount or state reimbursement for the ongoing restocking costs. Consequently, these costs will likely result in an increase in local school board expenditures. Specific dollar estimates for the restocking mandate are not provided in the bill text, and the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the source material.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of Maryland's 24 public school systems, MSDE is the primary entity tasked with implementing and enforcing education laws. The bill requires county boards to report to and potentially seek oversight from MSDE regarding the provision and restocking of menstrual hygiene products.

As a state-operated public school, the Maryland School for the Deaf is directly impacted by requirements concerning the provision of hygiene products in school restrooms and the mandate to ensure availability through regular restocking.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget, which includes mandated appropriations for school health initiatives and state reimbursements to county boards for health-related infrastructure like product dispensers.

DBM is responsible for state budget development and supervision of budget execution. This bill involves state mandates on county boards and has fiscal implications for the education budget, specifically regarding the ongoing state reimbursement mechanisms for school restroom equipment.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller's agency is responsible for paying state bills, which would include the reimbursements to county boards mandated under the Education Article for the installation of menstrual hygiene dispensers.

The Governor's Office for Children focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and the reduction of child poverty. Addressing 'period poverty'—the lack of access to menstrual products—is directly aligned with their mission to improve health services and economic opportunities for historically underinvested communities.

The Maryland Department of Health is responsible for protecting and improving public health. The provision of sanitary products in schools is a public health and hygiene matter that falls under the broader scope of health policies for residents.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Department of Education and the Governor's Office. They may be called upon to provide legal interpretations of the 'regular restocking' mandate to ensure compliance with state law.

The Innovation Team is tasked with piloting initiatives to address child poverty and enhance economic mobility. Improving access to essential hygiene products in schools is an evidence-based strategy to improve educational outcomes and health for students in need.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for the Maryland earned income tax credit for  individuals without qualifying children by altering the income thresholds at which the credit phases out; providing that, after the 2025 tax year, the income threshold and phase-out amounts are adjusted annually for inflation; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.
Title: Earned Income Tax Credit - Individuals Without Qualifying Children - Eligibility
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/12 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the Maryland earned income tax credit for individuals without qualifying children by increasing the income threshold at which the credit begins to phase out and providing for annual cost-of-living adjustments starting after tax year 2025.
stakeholders: Low-to-moderate income Maryland residents without qualifying children and Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues are estimated to decrease by $101,300,000 in FY 2027, with projected annual decreases growing to $117,900,000 by FY 2031. While local revenues are not affected, Montgomery County may experience increased expenditures for its local earned income credit supplement program starting in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is the primary agency responsible for tax collection and the administration of tax laws. The bill directly requires the Comptroller to implement the expanded Earned Income Tax Credit formulas and calculate annual inflation-based adjustments for the income thresholds.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning. This bill is projected to decrease general fund revenues by more than $100 million annually, which has a significant impact on the state budget and revenue forecasts managed by this department.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual state budget. The significant revenue impact and the policy shift regarding poverty reduction and economic mobility are central to the Governor's executive and budgetary responsibilities.

As the chief financial agency responsible for the management and protection of state funds, the Treasurer's Office is impacted by major changes in state revenue streams and serves on the Board of Public Works, which oversees fiscal integrity.

The Department of Human Services assists Marylanders in economic need. The expansion of the Earned Income Tax Credit aligns with the agency's mission to provide financial support and aid to vulnerable and low-income populations.

The Maryland Tax Court adjudicates disputes regarding income tax and tax credit determinations. Changes to eligibility and phase-out thresholds for the EITC may lead to new cases or appeals within its jurisdiction.

The Innovation Team is tasked with developing strategies for economic mobility. Expanding the EITC for individuals without qualifying children is a key policy mechanism for enhancing economic mobility for low-income workers.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of state tax laws and any potential litigation resulting from changes to the tax code.

Synopsis: Authorizing a landlord to impose an increased security deposit if a tenant operates or plans to operate a family child care home on the leased premises; prohibiting a landlord of certain residential rental property from prohibiting or unreasonably limiting the operation of a family child care home on the property; providing that landlords of certain residential rental property are immune from civil liability; authorizing a landlord to require a certain tenant to purchase a liability insurance policy; applying the Act prospectively; etc.
Title: Real Property - Landlord and Tenant - Family Child Care Homes
Status: In the House - Laid Over (Delegate Hartman) Adopted

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins

bill_summary: This bill prohibits landlords of single-family dwellings from refusing to lease to or unreasonably restricting tenants who operate or plan to operate a registered family child care home. It allows landlords to charge an increased security deposit of up to two months' rent, requires tenants to provide 60 days' notice and liability insurance naming the landlord as an additional insured, and grants landlords immunity from civil liability related to the child care operations.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Residential landlords, tenants, family child care home operators, and families seeking child care services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect Maryland State or local government operations or finances. It may have a potential meaningful impact on small businesses by increasing opportunities for family child care home operations. Specific financial impacts include the authorization of higher security deposits for landlords and insurance requirements for tenants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines 'family child care home' by referencing the Education Article and requires tenants to provide the landlord with a registration issued by the Department under Title 9.5, Subtitle 3 to operate on the premises.

The bill requires tenants to provide certificates of insurance naming landlords as additional insureds and allows landlords to mandate liability insurance policies with specific coverage limits ($1,000,000).
The OAG's Consumer Protection Division often handles landlord-tenant disputes and provides guidance on the enforcement of residential lease laws, which this bill substantively amends.

The bill creates new statutory requirements for residential leases and security deposits, and explicitly mentions that tenants may recover up to three times the extra amount charged in a court action for security deposit violations.

The bill's provisions regarding increased security deposits for child care homes are added into a section of the Real Property Article that already references tenant eligibility for utility assistance through DHS.

The bill explicitly states that its provisions do not limit or preempt the local zoning authority of counties or municipalities, a subject area where the Department of Planning provides data analysis and policy guidance.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an individual from smoking, vaping, or consuming cannabis in the passenger area of a motor vehicle in which a minor is an occupant.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Cannabis Use in Motor Vehicle With Minor Occupant - Prohibition
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/11 at 2:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits individuals from smoking, vaping, or consuming cannabis in the passenger area of a motor vehicle if a minor is an occupant. Violators are guilty of a misdemeanor and face penalties of up to one year in prison, a fine of up to $1,000, or both.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Motor vehicle operators, passengers, and minors in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a misdemeanor penalty with a fine of up to $1,000 and possible imprisonment. While a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, the bill likely results in an indeterminate increase in State general fund revenues from fines and potentially increased expenditures related to law enforcement and court proceedings. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As Maryland's primary law enforcement agency for motor vehicle and criminal laws, the State Police would be the primary body responsible for enforcing this new prohibition on state roadways.

The bill adds a new section to the Transportation Article and involves motor vehicle law; the MVA oversees highway safety initiatives and maintains driving records that may be affected by convictions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Since the bill establishes a new misdemeanor offense punishable by up to one year in jail, the Office of the Public Defender would be responsible for representing indigent individuals charged under this section.
As the agency responsible for regulating the cannabis industry and public health regulations related to cannabis, the MCA has a direct interest in policies governing cannabis consumption.
The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial system, which will handle the adjudication and processing of these new misdemeanor criminal cases.
The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and represents the state in appeals; they would be involved in legal interpretations of the new law and any subsequent criminal appeals.

MDOT is the parent agency for the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the state's transportation network, which is directly impacted by changes to the Transportation Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department oversees parole and probation; individuals convicted of this misdemeanor could be sentenced to community supervision managed by this agency.
The Maryland Department of Health manages public health policy related to cannabis and behavioral health, including the protection of minors from environmental health hazards like secondhand smoke.
The Governor's Office for Children is focused on the well-being of children and reducing child-related risks, which is the primary intent of this legislation.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates the policy initiatives and state laws that this bill would establish.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes licensed real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons to act as transaction brokers in residential real estate transactions. In this nonagency relationship, the licensee facilitates the sale or lease of residential property for both parties without representing either party as an agent. The bill defines the limited fiduciary duties of transaction brokers, requires written informed consent from all parties involved, and mandates the State Real Estate Commission to develop a standard consent form for these transactions.
stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and real estate salespersons; residential property buyers, sellers, lessors, and lessees.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not included in the provided text, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The bill requires the State Real Estate Commission to develop and provide a standard consent form to all licensees, which may result in minor administrative expenditures. Additionally, the bill allows for disciplinary actions against licensees who fail to provide required disclosures, which could theoretically result in fine revenue, though no specific amounts are stated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates licensed real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons, all of whom are overseen by the State Real Estate Commission, a regulatory board within the Department of Labor. The bill specifically tasks the Commission with developing and providing a standard consent form for transaction brokerage.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state boards and commissions, including the State Real Estate Commission. Additionally, its Consumer Protection Division may be involved in overseeing or enforcing consumer rights related to the new nonagency 'transaction broker' relationships established by this bill.

The bill amends the grounds for disciplinary action against real estate licensees. The Office of Administrative Hearings is responsible for conducting the impartial hearings required when the State Real Estate Commission seeks to reprimand, suspend, or revoke a license for violations of these regulations.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to make a professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing available to all school personnel and administrators by July 1, 2027. The course must cover eight specific dimensions of well-being—social, environmental, physical, emotional, spiritual, occupational, intellectual, and financial—as identified by the federal Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. MSDE may develop its own course or utilize a third-party course, provided the implementation is at no cost or at a cost comparable to existing similar professional development courses.
stakeholders: Maryland school personnel, school administrators, and the Maryland State Department of Education
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are not expected to be materially affected because the Maryland State Department of Education can fulfill the bill's requirements using existing resources, specifically an established course from the Georgetown University Center for Child and Human Development. The bill includes a cost-constraint provision stating that MSDE is only required to offer the course if it is free or costs a comparable amount to existing similar courses. Local school systems face no fiscal impact as the bill does not mandate participation or local development of the course.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) make a professional development course on educator well-being and flourishing available to all school personnel and administrators, including developing or procuring the course content.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and estimates. While the fiscal note suggests MSDE can implement this within existing resources, DBM remains relevant for overseeing potential future expenditure increases if internal resources are diverted for curriculum development.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and MSDE. The Governor must also sign the bill into law and oversees the administration of state policies regarding education and employee well-being.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to MSDE and would likely review any third-party contracts or licenses required to make the course available, ensuring compliance with the 'comparable cost' provisions in the bill.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Secretary of Agriculture to submit an annual report identifying additional agricultural equipment that should qualify for an income tax subtraction modification. Additionally, the bill establishes a $1,000 refundable income tax credit for parents who experience a stillbirth, with the credit amount phasing out for individuals with a federal adjusted gross income over $100,000 and for joint filers over $150,000.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland agricultural producers (farmers) and parents of stillborn children.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement the bill's reporting requirements with existing budgeted resources and State revenues are not affected. However, the bill text also creates a $1,000 refundable income tax credit for parents of stillborn children for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026, which would likely result in a future reduction of State income tax revenue not reflected in the provided Fiscal Note's specific figures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's tax laws. This bill creates a new refundable income tax credit for parents of stillborn children and modifies an existing subtraction modification for agricultural equipment, both of which require the Comptroller to update tax forms, process claims, and manage the resulting revenue impacts.

The bill mandates that the Secretary of Agriculture report annually to the Governor and General Assembly with recommendations for new equipment to qualify for tax subtractions. Furthermore, the agency is responsible for certifying that taxpayers are in compliance with requirements to receive these tax modifications.

The bill's new $1,000 tax credit is contingent upon the issuance of a 'Certificate of Birth Resulting in Stillbirth' under the Health – General Article. The Department of Health oversees the Vital Statistics Administration, which handles the issuance of such certificates.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and budget supervision. The implementation of a new refundable tax credit and expanded subtraction modifications will affect the state's general fund revenues, requiring DBM's oversight.

The Secretary of Agriculture is required by the bill to submit an annual report specifically to the Governor regarding recommended agricultural equipment for tax modifications. Additionally, the Governor oversees the executive agencies implementing the bill's provisions.

The Maryland Tax Court hears appeals regarding final decisions made by taxing authorities. Disputed claims for the new stillborn child credit or the agricultural equipment subtraction would eventually be adjudicated by this court.

bill_summary: The Maryland Housing Certainty Act requires that local approvals for housing development projects be governed by the laws and regulations in effect at the time a complete application is submitted. It grants developers vested rights for at least five years and prohibits local governments from collecting development impact fees or excise taxes until construction is finished and occupancy requirements are met, with certain exceptions for debt incurred before 2026.
responsible_party: Local regulatory authorities (including county or municipal governing bodies, boards, and planning departments) and the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission (M-NCPPC).
stakeholders: Housing developers, residential construction businesses, local government jurisdictions, and the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not directly affected. Local governments will experience a delay in revenue collection from development impact fees and excise taxes, which are projected to total approximately 148798435 across jurisdictions in fiscal 2026. This delay may lead to increased capital borrowing or deferred infrastructure spending. Additionally, local governments may incur increased administrative costs for personnel and tracking systems to comply with the bill's application and vesting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Land Use Article and alters the procedures for local regulatory authorities. The Department of Planning is the principal agency for sustainable growth and land use policy, providing technical assistance to local governments on the implementation of such laws, a role specifically highlighted in the fiscal note.

As the 'Maryland Housing Certainty Act,' the bill specifically targets residential real estate projects and housing development. The agency is responsible for ensuring access to safe and affordable housing, which is directly impacted by changes to development permitting and the timing of impact fees.

This multi-agency initiative coordinates land use, community revitalization, and state planning visions. Because the bill modifies local land use procedures and growth management mechanisms, it is highly relevant to this initiative's mission.
The bill establishes a significant new framework for development rights (the Maryland Housing Certainty Act) and relates to executive priorities regarding housing supply and economic stability.

The bill impacts the construction and development industry by providing regulatory certainty (vesting) and delaying the payment of development impact fees, which affects the economic viability and cash flow of residential businesses.

The bill creates statutory 'vested rights' and specific legal timelines for application completeness, which requires legal interpretation and counsel for the state agencies (Planning, DHCD) that interact with local jurisdictions and developers.

Additionally, the bill requires state officials and candidates for office to include a detailed schedule of any virtual currency interests valued over $1,000 in their financial disclosure statements, specifying the type, amount, and details of any acquisition or transfer.
stakeholders: Maryland State officials, candidates for State office, members of the General Assembly, regulated lobbyists, and their domestic partners.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill's implementation will likely result in minimal administrative costs for the State Ethics Commission and the Joint Ethics Committee to update financial disclosure forms and reporting systems to accommodate new virtual currency schedules and the inclusion of domestic partners.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for administering and enforcing the Maryland Public Ethics Law, the State Ethics Commission is directly responsible for implementing the new virtual currency disclosure requirements and updating financial disclosure forms to include domestic partners and registered domestic partners.

The bill explicitly expands ethics restrictions and financial disclosure requirements for the Governor and the Governor's spouse, domestic partner, or registered domestic partner. The Governor is also a 'State official' required to file disclosures under this law.

The Attorney General is specifically named as an official subject to the reporting requirements and lobbyist transaction restrictions. Additionally, the OAG provides legal counsel on the interpretation and enforcement of the Public Ethics Law.
The Comptroller is explicitly named as an official subject to the bill's expanded ethics reporting requirements and restrictions on business transactions with lobbyists.
The State Treasurer is explicitly named as an official subject to the bill's expanded ethics reporting requirements and restrictions on business transactions with lobbyists.
The Lieutenant Governor is explicitly named as an official subject to the bill's expanded ethics reporting requirements and restrictions on business transactions with lobbyists.
The Secretary of State is explicitly named as an official subject to the bill's expanded ethics reporting requirements and restrictions on business transactions with lobbyists.

The Secretary of DBM, as a secretary of a principal State department, is subject to the lobbyist transaction reporting requirements. Furthermore, as the central personnel agency, DBM may be involved in coordinating ethics compliance policies for executive branch employees.

The bill applies to 'each official and candidate for office as a State official,' which includes the Judiciary. The AOC provides operational and legal support to the judicial branch regarding compliance with state mandates and policies.

The OLA conducts fiscal compliance audits of state agencies. Changes to the Public Ethics Law regarding financial disclosures and lobbyist reporting would be subject to their audit and compliance monitoring functions.
The bill directly impacts all three members of the Board of Public Works (Governor, Comptroller, Treasurer) regarding their personal financial disclosures and regulated interactions with lobbyists.

Synopsis: Establishing certain civil liability for a federal law enforcement officer who, under color of law, deprives another of a right, a privilege, or an immunity secured by the U.S. Constitution; and applying the Act retroactively to a cause of action arising on or after March 1, 2025.

bill_summary: The No Kings Act establishes civil liability for federal law enforcement officers who, while acting under color of law, deprive individuals of rights, privileges, or immunities secured by the U.S. Constitution. The bill allows for the recovery of reasonable attorney's fees and expert witness fees by prevailing plaintiffs, sets a five-year statute of limitations for filing claims, and applies retroactively to causes of action arising on or after March 1, 2025.
stakeholders: Federal law enforcement officers and individuals in Maryland whose constitutional rights are allegedly violated by those officers.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, so specific revenue and expenditure estimates are unavailable. The bill establishes a new civil cause of action against federal law enforcement officers, which could increase the caseload and associated administrative costs for the Maryland court system. The bill also explicitly allows courts to award attorney's fees and expert witness fees to prevailing plaintiffs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new civil cause of action within the Maryland judiciary's jurisdiction, directly impacting the caseload and operational procedures of the state court system by adding Subtitle 27 to the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article.

The OAG is responsible for providing legal counsel to state agencies and would likely handle constitutional challenges, provide interpretive guidance, and analyze the interplay between state and federal law regarding the liability of federal officers.

Maryland State Police frequently collaborate with federal agencies on joint task forces; this legislation alters the legal liability of federal partners in such operations, which could impact interagency cooperation and operational procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department frequently collaborates with federal law enforcement, particularly for fugitive apprehension and task force activities; this bill introduces new state-court litigation risks for those federal partners.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the criminal prohibitions, associated penalties, and statutory definitions related to drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia in Maryland. Specifically, it eliminates the offenses of using, possessing, delivering, selling, or advertising drug and controlled paraphernalia, which were previously classified as misdemeanors with varying fines and terms of imprisonment.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals who use or possess drug-related paraphernalia, law enforcement agencies, the Maryland court system, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill will result in a minimal decrease in State general fund revenues due to the loss of fines previously imposed in the District Court. State expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Office of the Public Defender are expected to remain stable, as resources will likely be reallocated. Local governments may see a minimal decrease in expenditures due to a reduction in reincarceration, while local revenues are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for enforcing the criminal laws that this bill proposes to repeal. The removal of drug and controlled paraphernalia prohibitions will directly change their enforcement protocols and training requirements.

The bill will significantly reduce the number of criminal cases related to drug and controlled paraphernalia processed by the Maryland Judicial Branch. The fiscal note explicitly mentions a reduction in caseloads for the courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals charged with the criminal offenses being repealed. The bill will result in a direct reduction in the agency's caseload for these specific charges.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages the incarceration, parole, and probation of individuals involved in the justice system. The repeal of these offenses will lead to a reduction in the number of individuals entering the state's correctional and supervision systems.

DJS is responsible for youth involved in the juvenile justice system. Since youth are subject to the criminal laws being repealed, this bill will decrease the number of juveniles entering supervision or residential facilities for paraphernalia-related offenses.

The bill modifies Title 5 of the Criminal Law Article, which defines the Department of Health as the primary oversight agency. The decriminalization of paraphernalia, which includes hypodermic needles and syringes, is a major public health policy shift relevant to the department's mission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office advises the Governor on criminal justice strategy and coordinates public safety policies. The total repeal of paraphernalia-related criminal penalties is a major shift in state criminal justice policy that falls within their strategic planning and coordination scope.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly on the interpretation of the Maryland Criminal Law Article and will oversee the legal implications of these repeals for state agencies.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates state policy. This bill represents a significant change in the state's approach to drug-related criminal law, aligning with broader executive policy initiatives.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Commission on the House of Reformation and Instruction for Colored Children to research the history and operations of the former reformatory institution in Prince George’s County. The commission is responsible for identifying and accounting for children buried in unmarked graves, investigating institutional policies and causes of death, and making recommendations for systemic reform, memorialization, and reparative measures for descendants.
stakeholders: Descendants of children buried at the site, former residents of the House of Reformation, justice-involved youth, African American communities in Maryland, and the Prince George's County community.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures are estimated to increase by $250,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2029 to fund the commission’s investigative contracts and operational needs. The Office of the Attorney General is expected to staff the commission using existing resources. The FY 2027 budget already includes $250,000 for related efforts, and the commission may seek federal grants to supplement State appropriations. No significant impact on local government finances is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General is the primary agency responsible for the Commission. The Attorney General serves as the Chair, appoints several members, provides the staffing, administers all funding, and handles procurement for the project.

The Department of Juvenile Services is a member of the Commission. Furthermore, it operates the Cheltenham Youth Detention Center, which is the successor to the historical House of Reformation, and holds records essential to the investigation.
The State Archivist is a designated member of the Commission. The agency is a primary source of the historical and institutional records needed to identify the children buried at the site.

The Director of the Maryland Historical Trust, which is within the Department of Planning, is a member of the Commission. The Commission is specifically required to consult with the Trust regarding archaeological methods and site preservation.

The Commission is required to consult with the Maryland Department of Health regarding safety protocols for the disinterment of remains. The agency also provides access to historical medical and death records.

The State Superintendent of Schools is a member of the Commission. The Commission is tasked with making recommendations to incorporate the history of the House of Reformation into the State's educational curriculum.

The Secretary of General Services is a member of the Commission. As the agency responsible for managing state-owned facilities and real estate, DGS is involved due to the state's ownership of the historical grounds.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families is a member of the Commission. The agency is also identified as a collaborator in developing a cemetery conservation plan for the site.
The Chair of the Maryland Commission on African American History and Culture—an entity overseen by GOCI—is a designated member of the Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new Commission within the State Government, fitting the criteria for this collective entity of permanent and temporary advisory bodies.
The Chief Archaeologist of the State Highway Administration (part of MDOT) is a designated member of the Commission, providing technical expertise for the forensic and archaeological work.
The Secretary of Human Services is a designated member of the Commission, given the facility's historical role in child welfare and state custody.

The Commission includes a member from the University of Maryland Carey School of Law. Additionally, the Attorney General is encouraged to procure services from Maryland institutions such as state universities.
The Governor receives the Commission's initial and final reports and maintains executive oversight over the Commission as established under the State Government Article.
The bill grants the Commission full access to sealed and confidential juvenile records, which are managed by the Maryland Judicial Branch supported by the AOC.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for the oversight and execution of the funding provided in the state budget for this Commission.

However, if the department's current data-sharing methods do not meet the bill's 'user-friendly' standard, a one-time general fund expenditure of approximately $75,000 may be required for a new database module. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Commissioner of Labor and Industry, a division of the Maryland Department of Labor, to establish and maintain a user-friendly, searchable database of active elevator inspection certificates on the department's website.

bill_summary: This bill revises, restates, and recodifies the laws governing the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP). While primarily a technical and stylistic revision, the bill modifies eligibility requirements for certain professionals: it limits lawyer eligibility to graduates of Maryland law schools, removes certain degree requirements for specified licensed clinical counselors, and narrows teacher eligibility to those who qualify for the Nancy Grasmick Public School Professional Award.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance
stakeholders: Graduates of Maryland colleges and law schools, public school teachers, nurses, mental health professionals, licensed clinical counselors, and veterinary practitioners and technicians.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program are budgeted at 4,100,000 for fiscal 2027. Although the bill modifies eligibility criteria for certain professional categories, it is not expected to alter total program spending, as applicants may be placed on a waiting list if funds are exhausted. The Maryland Higher Education Commission may incur a minimal, one-time increase in general fund expenditures in fiscal 2027 for computer programming updates. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) is the primary agency responsible for administering the Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program (LARP) through its Office of Student Financial Assistance. The bill recodifies the program's laws and alters eligibility criteria for various professional categories.
The bill mandates that the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) determines the 'high-need geographic areas' where clinical counselors must practice to qualify for the loan repayment program.

The bill outlines eligibility for education-related professionals, including public school teachers, nurses, and mental health professionals. It references teaching licenses issued by the Department and alternative preparation programs approved by the State Superintendent.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is impacted because the fiscal note indicates a likely increase in general fund expenditures for MHEC to update programming for eligibility changes.
The bill includes specific loan repayment provisions for veterinary practitioners and technicians; MDA is the primary state agency overseeing the agricultural and animal health community.
Graduates of Maryland's public universities are primary beneficiaries of the LARP. The bill specifically revises eligibility requirements for graduates of colleges and universities in the State.

As a state-funded institution, Morgan State's graduates are eligible participants in the loan assistance program, and the university has a vested interest in financial support for its alumni in high-need fields.
Graduates of St. Mary's College of Maryland who enter public service fields covered by the bill are eligible for the Janet L. Hoffman LARP.
The OAG provides legal counsel to MHEC and other state agencies, and would be responsible for ensuring that the code revisions and resulting regulations are legally sound.

The MLDS links student and workforce data; changes to loan repayment eligibility for graduates in specific workforce sectors relate to the system's role in analyzing student performance and workforce outcomes.

bill_summary: The Maryland Family Utility Tax Relief Act authorizes local governments, including Baltimore City, counties, and municipalities, to establish a property tax credit for homeowners who spend 25% or more of their net household income on utility services such as electricity, gas, water, and internet.
responsible_party: Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation
stakeholders: Homeowners paying significant portions of their income on utilities and local Maryland government taxing authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill permits local jurisdictions to grant property tax credits, which would lead to an indeterminate reduction in local property tax revenues if adopted. Because the implementation of the credit is optional for local governments and no formal Fiscal Note was provided in the text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new local property tax credit. The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is the independent agency responsible for hearing appeals regarding property tax assessments, exemptions, and various property tax credits.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes in the state, including factual determinations and adjudications involving property tax credits and assessments.

The bill establishes a tax credit based on the percentage of income spent on utility services (electricity, gas, water, and internet). The Office of the People's Counsel is the primary advocate for the interests of residential utility consumers regarding the affordability and reliability of these services.

The bill defines eligibility based on 'household net income,' which refers to earnings after legally required withholdings. Verification of an applicant's income for this tax credit would likely require data or verification from the Comptroller, who serves as the state's chief tax collector and manager of income tax records.
The bill's tax credit is triggered by expenses for utility services, including electricity, gas, and water, all of which are industries regulated by the Public Service Commission.

The Department of Human Services administers energy assistance and aid to residents in economic need. The population targeted by this bill (households spending over 25% of income on utilities) overlaps significantly with the demographic served by the department's Office of Home Energy Programs.

Synopsis: Providing that "department" does not include the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services for purposes of certain provisions prohibiting a department from refusing to issue an occupational license or certificate based on a certain conviction under certain circumstances; establishing a predetermination review process for occupational licenses and certificates in certain departments of State government; authorizing a department to charge a criminal history review fee of up to $100; etc.
Title: Occupational Licensing and Certification - Criminal History - Predetermination Review Process
Status: In the House - Returned Passed
