bill_summary: This bill enhances privacy protections for Maryland residents by prohibiting data controllers from selling personal data to government units involved in civil immigration enforcement. It requires custodians of public records to take reasonable steps to ensure records are not accessed for immigration enforcement purposes without a warrant and extends these protections to law enforcement message switching systems. Additionally, it expands the definition of sensitive data and requires state and local government entities to update their data protection and disclosure procedures.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Motor Vehicle Administration, Department of State Police, and Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Maryland residents, data controllers and processors, state and local government agencies, law enforcement agencies, and individuals or entities requesting public records.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary may increase significantly to implement new procedures for determining the intent of every data request. While most other state and local agencies are expected to manage the requirements within existing resources, some local governments may experience significant operational impacts due to the increased scrutiny required for public record requests. The bill has no direct impact on revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies that the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts will experience a significant operational impact and increased general fund expenditures to implement new procedures for determining the purpose of data requests across all courthouse kiosks and records.

As a major collector of sensitive personal and financial data, the Comptroller is subject to the bill's expanded Public Information Act restrictions and the requirement to develop procedures to prevent the sale or redisclosure of sensitive data.

DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and personnel oversight; it will need to manage the budgetary impact of the bill, including potential staffing or programming costs for agencies like the Judiciary and DPSCS.

Mentioned in the fiscal note as being affected, MSDE will need to ensure its data management and public record disclosure policies comply with the bill's new sensitive data protections and immigration enforcement inquiries.

As an agency handling sensitive health and personal data, MDH is impacted by the bill's new restrictions on data disclosure for immigration enforcement and the requirement to develop privacy procedures in consultation with DoIT.
The bill explicitly requires every Maryland governmental entity to consult with DoIT to develop and publish procedures that prevent the sale and redisclosure of sensitive data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically names DPSCS to adopt regulations regarding message switching systems and reporting requirements for immigration-related data requests. It is a primary implementing agency for the public safety provisions.

The bill specifically tasks the Motor Vehicle Administration (a unit of MDOT) with adopting regulations to ensure compliance with data disclosure restrictions and mandates annual reporting on immigration enforcement data requests.

The bill explicitly requires the Department of State Police to adopt regulations to enforce data privacy compliance and to report annually on requests for personal information or facial recognition searches for immigration purposes.

The OAG oversees the Public Information Act Manual and website and will provide legal guidance to all state agencies on implementing the bill's new restrictions on data sharing and immigration enforcement inquiries.

bill_summary: This bill establishes product liability standards for developers and deployers of high-impact and generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems. It allows individuals and the Maryland Attorney General to bring civil actions for harms resulting from defective design, failure to warn, or breach of express warranty. The bill incorporates a comparative negligence standard and provides a rebuttable presumption of safety for entities that follow industry-best testing and risk-management protocols.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Developers and deployers of artificial intelligence systems, individuals potentially harmed by AI, and the Maryland Attorney General.
fiscal_impact_summary: The state may see an increase in revenue from civil penalties and the recovery of litigation costs by the Attorney General. There may also be increased state expenditures for the Judiciary and the Office of the Attorney General to manage and litigate new AI-related product liability cases. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions against developers or deployers of artificial intelligence systems for harm caused, seeking injunctive relief, civil penalties, and damages on behalf of individuals.

The bill establishes new civil causes of action and rebuttable presumptions within the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, directly impacting court operations and the adjudication of product liability cases.

As the state's principal agency for IT strategy and security, DoIT would be responsible for establishing the risk management policies required for state agencies to meet the rebuttable presumption criteria if they are sued as deployers.
The bill creates significant liability and regulatory frameworks for AI developers and deployers, which directly impacts Maryland's technology business sector and economic development.
The bill specifically defines 'high-impact artificial intelligence systems' to include those used in vehicles or vehicle safety systems, impacting automotive and transportation technology regulation.
The bill defines 'high-impact AI' to include systems used in medical devices and healthcare-related 'consequential decisions,' which falls under the regulatory purview of the Department of Health.
The bill targets AI systems used in 'consequential decisions' regarding employment and credit, directly affecting areas regulated by the Department of Labor.
The bill addresses AI systems used to categorize groups by protected characteristics (race, ethnicity, religion), which overlaps with the Commission's mission to enforce anti-discrimination laws.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill covers AI systems used in 'consequential decisions' regarding access to the criminal justice system, which is a core function of this department.
AI systems making 'consequential decisions' regarding housing are subject to the new liability standards, impacting the department's oversight of housing access and security.
The bill includes AI systems used in 'consequential decisions' regarding insurance, making the legislation highly relevant to the regulation of the insurance industry.
The bill includes AI systems used in 'consequential decisions' regarding education, and establishes specific considerations for AI designed for or likely used by minors.
The bill's definition of 'high-impact AI' includes systems used in the management or operation of critical infrastructure, which is overseen by the PSC.

Because the bill defines 'person' to include governmental entities, the state could be liable as a 'deployer.' The Treasurer's Office manages the State Insurance Trust Fund which handles claims against the state.
DBM would be impacted by the fiscal requirements for state agencies to implement risk management policies and the potential costs associated with state liability under the Act.

fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on state finances. Cecil County expenditures will increase by at least $4,813 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $8,250 annually starting in fiscal 2028. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills serves as the Clerk to the Orphans' Court in each jurisdiction. While the salary increase is funded by Cecil County, the AOC oversees the broader judicial system in which the Orphans' Courts operate.

The Governor's Office is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the constitutional process of appointing individuals to judicial vacancies, including positions on the Orphans' Court should they become open.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is designated as the primary administrator of the Algorithmic Addiction Fund and is responsible for developing goals, performance indicators, managing the grant program for political subdivisions, and reporting annually on the fund's activities.

The Baltimore City Police Department can manage the issuance of raffle permits using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency

The Maryland Stadium Authority plans, builds, and manages the Camden Yards Sports Complex, which includes Oriole Park and M&T Bank Stadium. The bill's provisions regarding raffle geofencing and timing are directly tied to these physical locations and the professional teams (Orioles and Ravens) that use them.

The Comptroller is the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector. The agency was consulted for the fiscal note and has an interest in the tracking of state revenues, including potential impacts on lottery funds or tax implications from gaming proceeds.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly. They may be involved in interpreting the interaction between this local authorization and broader state criminal laws regarding gaming.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires the Governor's signature to become law and impacts gaming policy in the state's largest city.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law governing information technology plans apply to certain public institutions of higher education; establishing a policy of the State that State and higher education employee e-mail systems and resources are intended to support State business and may not serve as a public forum; requiring certain policies, plans, and standards to include provisions to implement systems that automatically filter spam e-mail from certain email accounts; etc.
Title: Information Technology – State and Higher Education E–Mail – Requirements
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that email systems for State and public higher education employees are intended to support State business and are not public forums. It requires State IT policies and standards to include protections against spam and other unauthorized uses, such as automated filtering, while permitting incidental personal use that has a minimal impact on resources and follows professional norms.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Information Technology and the governing boards of public institutions of higher education
stakeholders: State and higher education employees, State agencies, and public institutions of higher education
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances as it generally codifies existing practices regarding email usage and security. There is no direct impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency for state information technology strategy and policy, the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) is responsible for overseeing the IT plans and standards that this bill modifies, including the new email and spam filtering requirements.

The bill explicitly requires the governing boards of public institutions of higher education, such as USM, to develop and submit IT policies and plans that comply with the new email security and usage standards.

As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State's governing board is specifically required by the bill to submit IT policies and plans regarding employee email systems and anti-spam measures.

The bill mandates that governing boards of public institutions of higher education, including St. Mary's College, develop IT policies and plans that incorporate the specified email usage and security requirements.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the implementation of policies. This bill involves legal definitions of 'State Business' and 'public forums,' which may require legal interpretation and defense of state personnel communication policies.
As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM is affected by policies regarding state employee resources and the regulation of 'incidental personal use' of information technology by employees.

The bill's definition of 'spam email' specifically excludes bulk communications from 'exclusive representatives' (unions), which falls under the jurisdiction of PERB regarding collective bargaining and labor-management communication.

MHEC serves as the coordinating board for the state's higher education institutions, which are directly impacted by the bill's requirements for higher education employee email systems and IT planning.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch units that must comply with these new IT policies and receives the final approved plans through the Secretary of Information Technology.

OLA conducts fiscal and compliance audits of state agencies and will be responsible for ensuring that agencies have correctly implemented and documented the mandated IT email policies and spam filters.
As the oversight body for the state's public education system, MSDE is identified in the fiscal note as a relevant stakeholder and must ensure its own IT plans align with the bill's requirements.
MDOT is a major executive department with a large employee base that will be subject to the new email usage policies and anti-spam technical standards required by the bill.
The Comptroller's Office is a significant executive unit that must update its IT policies and standards to comply with the bill's provisions regarding state business email use.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits Maryland State and local government entities from adopting sanctuary policies that restrict cooperation with federal immigration authorities. It requires these entities to comply with immigration detainers and share information regarding the immigration status of individuals in custody, while repealing several existing state laws that limited such cooperation.
responsible_party: Maryland State and local government units, county sheriffs, and law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: State and local law enforcement, correctional facilities, federal immigration agencies, and individuals in custody subject to immigration enforcement
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable. The bill's requirement for State and local agencies to cooperate with federal immigration authorities may result in increased administrative and operational costs related to the detention and processing of individuals for federal agencies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the department in the repeal of reporting requirements related to facial recognition and immigration enforcement. It also impacts the department's operation of correctional facilities by prohibiting policies that impede cooperation with federal immigration agencies, such as providing access to incarcerated individuals and complying with detainers.

The bill repeals specific reporting requirements for the Maryland State Police regarding immigration-related information requests and facial recognition searches. It also removes existing restrictions on state police officers' ability to inquire about citizenship or immigration status during regular police functions.

The bill repeals specific sections of the General Provisions Article that required the MVA to report to the General Assembly regarding federal agency requests for personal information, photographs, and facial recognition searches for the purpose of immigration enforcement.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the OAG will be responsible for advising all state agencies on the implementation of this Act, the legality of 'sanctuary policies,' and the interaction between state law and federal immigration enforcement mandates.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, and the bill prohibits any unit of the Executive Branch from adopting or maintaining sanctuary policies. This represents a significant shift in executive policy regarding intergovernmental relations with federal immigration authorities.

The department operates residential and detention facilities for youth; the bill's requirements for cooperating with federal immigration agencies and complying with detainers would apply to individuals in the custody of DJS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy in Maryland. This bill fundamentally alters state strategy regarding law enforcement cooperation with federal agencies, which falls under GOCPP's policy development purview.

The bill repeals provisions that designated public schools as 'sensitive locations' where access for immigration enforcement was restricted. This change directly affects the policy environment for the state's public education system.
As an independent unit within MSDE responsible for school safety, the removal of 'sensitive location' protections for public schools affects the safety and security protocols the center coordinates.

The bill repeals provisions related to 'sensitive locations' which included courthouses and restricts the ability of state entities to require judicial warrants before cooperating with federal immigration authorities.

The USM and its constituent institutions operate campus police forces and are units of the State. The bill's prohibition on sanctuary policies and the repeal of restrictions on inquiring about immigration status apply to USM law enforcement and administrative units.

The bill repeals 'sensitive location' protections that previously applied to executive branch units, including state-run health facilities. Additionally, the department's Office of Controlled Substances Administration and other regulatory units are prohibited from having sanctuary policies.

DGS manages state-owned facilities and oversees the Maryland Capitol Police. The bill's repeal of 'sensitive location' protections and the prohibition on sanctuary policies impact how these facilities are managed and policed.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition on awarding the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship after June 30, 2030; and repealing the limitation on renewing the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship if the scholarship recipient received an initial scholarship before June 30, 2030.

Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 58

bill_summary: This bill repeals the June 30, 2030, termination date for awarding initial scholarships under the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship program and removes the limitation on renewing scholarships for recipients after that date, effectively making the program permanent.
stakeholders: Maryland residents who are veterans, active service members, or activated reservists who served in the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, as well as their spouses and children.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures will increase by an estimated $750,000 annually beginning in fiscal 2031 to maintain the scholarship program beyond its previous sunset date. There is no fiscal impact through fiscal 2030 as the program is already funded at approximately $750,000 annually. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for administering state financial aid programs, the Maryland Higher Education Commission (through its Office of Student Financial Assistance) is responsible for awarding the scholarships, managing the program's special fund, and submitting annual reports to the General Assembly.

The scholarship specifically benefits Maryland veterans and active-duty service members who served in the Afghanistan and Iraq conflicts, as well as their families. This aligns with the agency's mission to assist these groups in securing benefits and services.

The Governor's Office is responsible for proposing the annual state budget, which includes the $750,000 appropriation for this scholarship program. Additionally, the Governor appoints members to various boards and oversees the executive departments involved.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for developing the state's budget and long-term fiscal planning. The bill has a notable fiscal impact by maintaining $750,000 in general fund expenditures indefinitely beyond FY 2030.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer shall hold the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund separately.
The bill explicitly mandates that the Comptroller shall account for the Douglas J. J. Peters Veterans of the Afghanistan and Iraq Conflicts Scholarship Fund.

The scholarship is available to active service members and members of reserve components who were activated for the Afghanistan or Iraq conflicts, all of whom fall under the senior military advisory and readiness purview of the Adjutant General.
The scholarship is specifically available to active service members and reserve members who served in the specified conflicts, many of whom are members of the Maryland Army or Air National Guard.

The scholarship amount is capped based on the average tuition, fees, and room and board at institutions within the University System of Maryland, and these institutions serve as eligible locations for scholarship recipients to use their awards.
As a state public university and eligible institution, Morgan State University is a site where scholarship recipients may enroll and apply their awards.
As a state public college and eligible institution, St. Mary's College of Maryland is a site where scholarship recipients may enroll and apply their awards.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law regarding priority registration at public institutions of higher education, resources and support at community colleges, senatorial and Delegate scholarships, and preferences in hiring by the Public Service Commission to the spouses of active service members and veterans; etc.
Title: Uniformed Services Spouses Act
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.

bill_summary: The Uniformed Services Spouses Act extends various state-level benefits to the spouses of active duty service members and veterans. Key provisions include granting priority course registration at public institutions of higher education, extending specialized advising and resource center support at community colleges to veterans' spouses, and expanding eligibility for senatorial and delegate scholarships to spouses of active duty members. The bill also broadens the definition of an 'eligible veteran' to include those with an 'other than dishonorable' discharge for the purpose of hiring and promotion preferences in state and local government positions.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission, Maryland Department of Budget and Management, and Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Spouses of active duty service members and veterans, veterans with other than dishonorable discharges, and members of the PHS and NOAA Commissioned Corps.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have no effect on State revenues, and its requirements can be handled with existing budgeted resources. While the bill expands eligibility for certain scholarships and hiring preferences, it does not increase the total funding allocated for these programs. Minor administrative costs for updating state personnel systems are considered minimal and absorbable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the principal personnel agency for the state. The bill requires updates to the JobAps system and personnel guides to account for the expanded definition of 'eligible veteran' and the application of selection test credits for spouses.
The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article regarding hiring and promotion preferences that private employers and local governments may grant to veterans and their spouses.

As the primary agency for assisting veterans and military families, this bill directly impacts their constituents by expanding access to higher education benefits, scholarships, and hiring preferences for spouses and veterans with other than dishonorable discharges.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies affected by this legislation and is responsible for final approval of the bill.

MHEC is the central regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education. It is responsible for the oversight of scholarship programs (Senatorial and Delegate) and higher education policies, including priority registration and community college resource centers, all of which are altered by the bill.
As a public institution of higher education, Morgan State University is required to implement the bill's provisions regarding priority registration for eligible service members and their spouses.
The bill's preamble explicitly mentions preferences in hiring by the Public Service Commission for spouses of active service members and veterans.
As a public honors college and state agency, St. Mary's College must comply with the bill's requirements for granting priority course registration to service members and their spouses.

The University System of Maryland's constituent institutions are required to implement priority registration for eligible service members and spouses and are involved in the administration of scholarships affected by the bill.

Synopsis: Abrogating the doctrine of charitable immunity as a defense to an action for damages arising out of a claim of child sexual abuse; and applying the Act retroactively.
Title: Child Sexual Abuse Claims - Doctrine of Charitable Immunity - Abrogation
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill abrogates the doctrine of charitable immunity as a defense in civil actions for damages arising from child sexual abuse claims. It allows such actions to be brought against charitable organizations regardless of when the abuse occurred and applies retroactively to cases that were previously pending, concluded, or dismissed. The bill also maintains specific caps on noneconomic damages and limits on attorney fees for such actions.
stakeholders: Survivors of child sexual abuse, charitable organizations, legal professionals, and the Maryland court system
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates for state or local fiscal impact are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. The bill's removal of charitable immunity for child sexual abuse claims and its retroactive application are expected to increase the volume of civil litigation, which may increase the administrative workload and expenditures for the Maryland Judiciary. The bill specifies noneconomic damage caps of $700,000 for actions filed on or after June 1, 2025.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial proceedings by abrogating the doctrine of charitable immunity as a defense in child sexual abuse cases. It also establishes specific caps on noneconomic damages and limitations on attorney fees for these cases, which the courts must apply in civil litigation.

The Secretary of State manages the registration and oversight of charitable organizations in Maryland. This bill fundamentally changes the legal liability and defense protections for these regulated entities.

The removal of charitable immunity for child sexual abuse claims is likely to have a significant impact on the liability insurance market for non-profit and charitable organizations, requiring MIA oversight regarding rate changes and policy coverage.

As the primary liaison to faith-based and community non-profit organizations, this office is relevant because the bill directly affects the legal protections and operational risks of its key stakeholders.
The bill's focus on child sexual abuse claims aligns with the GOC's mission to promote the well-being of Maryland's children and families and address systemic issues affecting youth.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates statewide strategies for public safety and manages victim services funding. This bill impacts policy related to justice for victims of sexual abuse.

DHS oversees child welfare and works extensively with charitable and non-profit organizations to provide foster care and other social services. Changes in liability for these partners could impact service delivery and contracting.

As the state's chief legal officer, the OAG provides counsel on matters of civil litigation policy and may represent the state's interests in related judicial interpretations of the abrogation of immunity.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI connects residents with service opportunities through non-profits. The increased liability risk for these partner charitable organizations could affect the placement and management of service programs.

MCSS interacts with private and non-public schools, many of which are operated by charitable or religious organizations. The removal of charitable immunity would apply to these educational entities in cases of alleged abuse.

Synopsis: Requiring electric companies to submit to the Public Service Commission cost containment plans for electric distribution and transmission system planning on or before January 1, 2027, and every 3 years thereafter; requiring the plans to combine to reduce peak electric system loads in a certain manner; and requiring electric companies to submit certain progress reports on the implementation of the plan.
Title: Electric Companies - Cost Containment Plans - Requirement (Securing Affordable, Valuable Investments in Next Generation Grid Solutions (SAVINGS) Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: The bill requires electric companies to develop and submit cost containment plans to the Public Service Commission (PSC) aimed at reducing peak electric system loads. These plans must incorporate various advanced technologies and nonwires solutions, such as grid-enhancing technologies, demand flexibility, and virtual power plants, to minimize capital expenditures while improving system reliability and resilience. The bill mandates that these plans combined must reduce the utility's peak electric system load by at least 20% from 2025 levels by 2030.
stakeholders: Electric companies (including municipal utilities), Maryland electricity ratepayers, the Department of Natural Resources, and the Office of People’s Counsel.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Public Service Commission (PSC) expects special fund expenditures to increase by $1,699,796 in FY 2027 for new staff and consultants, with costs continuing at approximately $1.9 million annually. These costs are offset by corresponding increases in special fund revenues from assessments on public service companies. The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) expects expenditures of approximately $50,000 annually for consultants. General fund revenues may increase starting in FY 2030 from potential penalties for non-compliance. Local municipal electric utilities may face significant financial impacts to meet the bill's requirements. While ratepayer costs may decrease long-term due to optimized grid planning, the exact impact is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of electric companies, the PSC is responsible for reviewing, approving, and enforcing the cost containment plans required by the bill. The fiscal note indicates a significant expenditure of $1.7 million for the PSC to hire engineers, economists, and legal staff to implement this program.

The OPC is the statutory advocate for residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC. The fiscal note anticipates an increased workload and potential consultant costs for the OPC to participate in the new regulatory proceedings established by this bill.
The fiscal note specifically identifies a $50,000 annual impact for DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) to assist the PSC with the technical review of utility cost containment plans.

The MEA coordinates state energy policy and efficiency initiatives. This bill's focus on demand flexibility, building electrification, and grid efficiency directly aligns with the MEA's mission to maximize energy efficiency and coordinate energy planning.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for state agencies, including providing counsel to the PSC. They would be involved in the legal framework of these new regulations and represent the state in any appeals of PSC decisions related to this bill.

The bill's objectives include reducing environmental impacts and integrating increased renewable energy supply, which are core components of MDE's mission to enforce environmental laws and meet state greenhouse gas reduction goals.

DGS manages state-owned facilities and leads sustainability and energy conservation initiatives. As a major consumer of electricity, the state government (via DGS) is impacted by changes in utility rates and grid management strategies that arise from these cost containment plans.

Synopsis: Prohibiting employment discrimination based on an individual's caregiver status.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Caregiver Status
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits employment discrimination on the basis of an individual's caregiver status. Caregiver status is defined as the status of providing direct and ongoing care for a minor child or an individual with a disability who is a family member or resides in the same household. The bill extends these protections to hiring, discharge, compensation, conditions of employment, harassment, labor organization membership, and internships.
stakeholders: Employers, employees, job applicants, labor organizations, employment agencies, interns, and individuals providing care for minor children or disabled family members.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text; therefore, specific dollar estimates for expenditures or revenue changes are unavailable. The bill may result in an increased administrative workload for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights as it would be responsible for investigating and adjudicating new claims of discrimination based on caregiver status.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Commission on Civil Rights is the primary agency responsible for enforcing Maryland's anti-discrimination laws in employment. This bill adds 'caregiver status' as a new protected class, directly expanding the Commission's investigative and enforcement mandate. Furthermore, the bill explicitly empowers the Commission to recognize additional familial relationships for the purpose of defining caregiver status.

As the state's central personnel agency, the Department of Budget and Management is responsible for managing state employee policies and ensuring compliance with labor laws. DBM will need to update state hiring practices, personnel manuals, and training programs for all executive branch agencies to include caregiver status as a protected class.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Commission on Civil Rights and DBM. It will be responsible for providing legal advice on the interpretation and implementation of the new caregiver discrimination standards and representing the state in related litigation.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including the Commission on Civil Rights. This bill is likely to increase the agency's caseload as it handles disputes and appeals arising from alleged employment discrimination based on caregiver status.

The Department of Labor's mission includes protecting workers and enforcing labor laws. While the Commission on Civil Rights is the primary enforcer for civil rights, this change in employment law fundamentally alters the legal landscape for workers and employers overseen by the Department of Labor.

The bill's definition of caregiver status specifically includes individuals providing care for people with disabilities. These protections help ensure the economic stability of caregivers, which indirectly supports the Department's mission of improving the quality of life for Marylanders with disabilities who rely on those caregivers.

The Department of Aging supports the rights and welfare of older adults and their caregivers. This bill provides new employment protections for family members who provide ongoing care for elderly individuals, directly aligning with the Department's advocacy for caregiver support.

Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill requires employees or agents of State or local correctional facilities to provide at least 48 hours notice to federal immigration authorities before the release of an individual, if requested. It also mandates the transfer of the individual to federal immigration authorities, provided that the transfer does not extend the individual's time in custody beyond their scheduled release.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, State and local correctional facility employees, and federal immigration authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill establishes new notification and transfer protocols for State and local correctional facilities, which may result in indeterminate administrative expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary agency responsible for state correctional facilities and pretrial detention centers. The bill's requirements for releasing individuals and transferring them to federal immigration authorities directly impact their operational protocols and mandate.

The OAG would be responsible for providing legal counsel to state agencies on the implementation of this mandate and representing the state in potential litigation related to immigration enforcement and the legality of the release/transfer requirements.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, this office would be involved in the policy development and interagency collaboration required to implement the bill's immigration enforcement provisions.

While primarily focused on youth, DJS operates secure residential facilities for youth that may be classified as correctional facilities under certain statutory definitions, potentially requiring them to comply with the notice and transfer mandates.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. The bill involves a significant shift in state policy regarding cooperation with federal immigration authorities.

The bill may have fiscal impacts regarding the administrative workload of state correctional facility employees. DBM would be responsible for overseeing any budgetary adjustments or personnel allocations required to comply with the new notice and transfer protocols.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Transportation Authority to name the replacement bridge for the collapsed Francis Scott Key Bridge the 'Francis Scott Key Memorial Bridge' upon its completion.

fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. Potential fiscal impacts include the costs associated with signage for the new bridge and administrative updates to existing laws and regulations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Transportation Authority to name the replacement bridge the 'Francis Scott Key Memorial Bridge' and requires the Authority to notify the Department of Legislative Services within five days of the bridge opening to vehicle traffic.

As the department responsible for building and operating the state's transportation network, MDOT oversees its modal administrations, including the Maryland Transportation Authority. This bill impacts the official designation and statutory classification of a major piece of the state's transportation infrastructure.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 6-209 of the Transportation Article, which regulates gaming on vessels based on their geographical location relative to the bridge. The agency will need to ensure its regulatory references align with the new official name of the bridge used as a boundary marker.

The naming of a major state landmark and infrastructure project is a significant executive and policy matter. The Governor oversees the Maryland Transportation Authority and the broader executive branch responsible for the bridge's reconstruction.

As the central depository for government records and the entity that maintains the Maryland Manual On-Line, the Archives will be responsible for reflecting the official name change in the state's historical and administrative records.

Synopsis: Altering membership criteria for a Class C (veterans' organization) alcoholic beverages license in Anne Arundel County by including certain members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service, and repealing a requirement that members of the veterans' organization served in a war; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands the eligibility criteria for Class C (veterans' organization) alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County by replacing the requirement that members must have served in the 'armed forces of the United States in a war' with a requirement for service in the 'uniformed services.' This change allows organizations with members who served in the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and the Public Health Service (PHS) to qualify and removes the requirement that service must have occurred specifically during a period of war.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Veterans' organizations in Anne Arundel County and individuals who served in the uniformed services, including the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County's finances or operations. While the annual fee for a Class C (veterans' organization) license is $300, the bill's changes to membership criteria are not anticipated to significantly alter the number of licenses issued or the revenue generated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the membership criteria for veterans' organization alcoholic beverages licenses by replacing 'armed forces' with 'uniformed services' and removing the requirement for wartime service. This directly affects the definition and recognition of veterans and their organizations, which is central to the agency's mission of advocating for and assisting Maryland's veterans and military families.

The Comptroller is the state's principal regulator of the alcohol industry. While local boards of license commissioners in Anne Arundel County handle the specific issuance and enforcement of these licenses, the bill amends the statewide Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, which falls under the Comptroller's general regulatory and oversight authority.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of General Services, Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Maryland Department of Planning, Maryland Department of Transportation, and Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations focused on historic preservation, archaeology, and conservation; state agencies (DGS, DHCD, MDP, MDOT, DNR); and Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is indeterminate as the provided text does not include a formal Fiscal Note or specific dollar estimates. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly adds the Department of General Services to the list of agencies exempt from standard state procurement requirements for projects involving historic preservation, archaeology, or conservation services with nonprofit entities. As the state's central procurement authority, DGS is also responsible for managing state-owned facilities, many of which are historic.

bill_summary: This bill makes it a crime to tamper with gift cards or their packaging to defraud others, creating a misdemeanor known as gift card forgery. stakeholders: Consumers, retail businesses, law enforcement agencies, and individuals involved in criminal proceedings related to gift card theft or fraud.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

Synopsis: Requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to develop a process to allow a homeowner to designate a family member or another representative of the homeowner to communicate and work with the Ombudsman on the homeowner's behalf; requiring the dwelling of a homeowner to be withheld from tax sale if the homeowner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship; increasing the maximum value of a dwelling that a homeowner may reside in and be eligible for the Homeowner Protection Program to $450,000; etc.

bill_summary: This bill enhances protections for homeowners at risk of tax sale by requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to allow homeowners to designate representatives to work on their behalf. It mandates that local governments withhold dwellings from tax sale if the homeowner has a documented terminal illness or medical hardship. Additionally, the bill increases the eligibility for the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) by raising the maximum dwelling assessed value from $300,000 to $450,000 and grants priority enrollment in the program to homeowners experiencing medical hardships or terminal illnesses.
responsible_party: State Tax Sale Ombudsman, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT), and local county tax collectors.
stakeholders: Homeowners with delinquent taxes, specifically those with terminal illnesses or medical hardships; their designated representatives; the Maryland Department of Health; and local government tax authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to increase special fund expenditures as the expansion of eligibility for the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) will allow currently appropriated funds (approximately $750,000 annually) to be more fully utilized to assist homeowners. There may also be a corresponding increase in future special fund revenues from homeowner repayments. Local government revenues may experience minimal delays or reductions due to the mandatory withholding of certain properties from tax sales.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the State Tax Sale Ombudsman and the Department of Assessments and Taxation to consult with the Maryland Department of Health to define 'terminal illness' and 'medical hardship' by regulation.

The bill expands eligibility for the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP) by increasing the assessed value limit. The fiscal note indicates this will result in increased special fund expenditures from the Homeowner Protection Fund, which DBM oversees.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Health and the Department of Assessments and Taxation. They will likely be involved in drafting and reviewing the regulations and processes mandated by the bill.

The bill addresses housing stability and mandates that the Ombudsman refer homeowners to housing counseling. The Department of Housing and Community Development is the state's lead agency for ensuring access to secure housing and managing community revitalization investments.
The bill includes specific protections for homeowners who are at least 65 years old and sets priority enrollment for the Homeowner Protection Program for those who are at least 60 years old.
The Ombudsman is required to refer vulnerable homeowners to social services. DHS is the state's primary provider of social services and aid to residents in economic need.
The bill provides protections for disabled homeowners and prioritizes individuals receiving federal Social Security Disability insurance for the Homeowner Protection Program.

As the state's chief financial officer and tax collector, the Comptroller oversees tax law enforcement and revenue collection. Changes to tax sale eligibility and homeowner protections impact the state's overall tax administration landscape.
The bill increases the assessed value threshold for HPP eligibility from $300,000 to $450,000. Homeowners may appeal their property valuations to the PTAAB to qualify for these protections.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the department where the State Tax Sale Ombudsman is located, and is responsible for coordinating policy initiatives and signing the bill into law.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest level of administrative review for tax disputes. Legal challenges regarding tax sale withholding or eligibility determinations under this bill may eventually be adjudicated here.

stakeholders: Holders of Class B beer, wine, and liquor golf course licenses in Wicomico County and patrons of these facilities.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies regarding the implementation and legality of state laws, including the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article.

Synopsis: Requiring each county board of education to develop and implement, not later than the 2026-2027 school year, a policy prohibiting the use of a personal electronic device by a student during school day hours; providing the policy may not prohibit a student from using a personal electronic device for any purpose related to an individualized program or 504 plan; providing that any disciplinary measures adopted as part of the policy may not include suspension or expulsion solely for violation of the policy; etc.

bill_summary: This bill, known as the 'Phones Away for the School Day Act,' requires each Maryland county board of education to develop and implement a policy by the 2026-2027 school year that prohibits students from using or carrying personal electronic devices during school hours. Students must store their devices in a manner determined by the board. Exceptions are provided for instructional devices, medical devices, and purposes documented in a student's Individualized Education Program (IEP) or 504 Plan. Schools are also required to provide designated telephones for students to contact parents or guardians if necessary.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents and legal guardians, teachers, and local school board administrators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances. Local boards of education can likely develop and implement the required personal electronic device policies using existing resources. No impact on local revenues is expected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the public education system by requiring county boards of education to implement specific student policies. The fiscal note also confirms that MSDE and the State Board of Education previously convened a task force on this specific issue.

As an independent unit within the Department of Education responsible for coordinating school safety, MCSS is relevant because policies regarding the use and storage of electronic devices significantly impact school environment safety, emergency communication protocols, and the development of safe learning environments.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland State Department of Education and the General Assembly. They would be responsible for reviewing the legality and constitutionality of the mandate on local boards and advising on potential liability issues related to the storage of student property.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the theft of mail or packages as a felony offense, punishable by up to five years in prison. stakeholders: Victims of mail and package theft, the U.S. Postal Service, private delivery companies, and individuals prosecuted for theft.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. Additionally, the mandatory victim notification requirements impose an administrative mandate on local State's Attorneys' offices.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony related to the theft of mail and packages and mandates specific victim notification requirements within court proceedings. agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes mail and package theft as a felony subject to up to 5 years of imprisonment, which directly impacts the state's correctional system. agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

DBM oversees the state's fiscal planning and personnel. The creation of a new felony and the mandate for proactive victim notification by prosecuting attorneys may have a fiscal impact on state resources and agency workloads (such as DPSCS and the Judiciary).

The bill references the MDEC (Maryland Electronic Courts) system protocols for victim notification and confidentiality. DoIT oversees the state's IT strategy and coordination, which supports the infrastructure for these inter-agency digital notification systems.

The Maryland State Treasurer's Office is statutorily mandated to invest and reinvest money within the Problem Gambling Fund, ensuring interest and earnings accrue to the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

Synopsis: Repealing the sentencing date limitation of October 1, 2021, for an individual convicted as an adult of an offense committed when the individual was a minor to file a motion to reduce the duration of the sentence.

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for sentencing relief under the Juvenile Restoration Act by repealing the requirement that an individual convicted as an adult for an offense committed as a minor must have been sentenced before October 1, 2021. Under the bill, such individuals may file a motion to reduce their sentence duration regardless of their sentencing date, provided they have been imprisoned for at least 20 years.
stakeholders: Individuals convicted as adults for offenses committed as minors, crime victims and their representatives, State's Attorneys' offices, and the Office of the Public Defender.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill is unlikely to have a state or local fiscal impact within the five-year period from fiscal 2027 to 2031. Because individuals must serve at least 20 years before becoming eligible to file a motion for sentence reduction, those sentenced after the original October 1, 2021 deadline would not be eligible to apply for relief until 2041 at the earliest.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the court to conduct hearings on motions to reduce sentences, and the Administrative Office of the Courts is responsible for providing operational support and implementing policies for the Maryland Judicial Branch.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender is responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants; this bill expands eligibility for sentence reduction motions, which directly impacts the agency's caseload and duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees state correctional facilities and the supervision of incarcerated individuals; the bill's expansion of eligibility for sentence reductions directly affects the population of justice-involved individuals under their management.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The Governor's Office coordinates policy initiatives and oversees the executive branch; this bill represents a modification to criminal justice policy and the Juvenile Restoration Act.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

Synopsis: Increasing to $40,000 over a 2-year period the amount of a certain subtraction modification under the State income tax for certain military retirement income received by an individual, regardless of age, during a taxable year for certain military service.

bill_summary: The 'Keep Our Heroes Home Act' increases the Maryland income tax subtraction modification for military retirement income. fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in a decrease in State general fund revenues and local income tax revenues by expanding the income tax subtraction modification for military retirement income. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for implementing changes to the Maryland income tax code, including the administration and enforcement of the proposed increase to the military retirement income subtraction modification.

Emergency medical services surcharge revenues will follow a similar pattern of initial increase followed by decrease. Local fiscal impact is expected to be negligible.

In cases where the Office of the State Prosecutor acts as the prosecuting attorney for offenses involving theft, they would be legally required to perform the specific victim notifications mandated by this bill.

The department would be responsible for assessing and managing the fiscal impact and personnel needs resulting from the increased administrative workload for state agencies implementing the new notification requirements.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to adopt regulations that prohibit police officers from affiliating with, supporting, or advocating for white supremacist groups, ideologies, or causes. It also prohibits officers from participating in or promoting any domestic or international extremist group that the FBI identifies as supporting or encouraging illegal violent conduct.
responsible_party: Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission
stakeholders: Maryland police officers and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. Implementation of the bill likely results in indeterminate administrative costs for the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to update standards and ensure compliance.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission is an independent body housed within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. This bill specifically mandates the Commission to establish and enforce new standards prohibiting police officers from affiliating with or supporting White supremacist or extremist groups.

As the state's primary law enforcement agency, all Maryland State Police officers will be directly subject to the new conduct standards and prohibitions regarding extremist and white supremacist affiliations.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new regulations and advising on potential constitutional issues related to the First Amendment.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases; it would be the forum for appeals and hearings if police officers face disciplinary action or decertification based on the new prohibitions established under this bill.
The Department of Natural Resources operates the Natural Resources Police; its officers are defined as police officers under state law and would be subject to the new standards and prohibitions.

The Maryland Transportation Authority maintains its own nationally accredited police force, whose members would be subject to the conduct and affiliation standards established by the Commission under this bill.
The Department of General Services oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, whose officers would be required to comply with the new standards prohibiting extremist group affiliations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office is the primary coordinating body for public safety policy and advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies, including the professional standards and accountability of law enforcement officers.

The Commission on Civil Rights enforces anti-discrimination laws; the bill's intent to remove white supremacist ideologies from law enforcement aligns with the agency's mission to protect residents from bigotry and bias.

Synopsis: Requiring that a carrier's internal grievance process provide for human review of grievances resulting from adverse decisions made using artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools; requiring carriers to report certain information on grievances resulting from adverse decisions made using artificial intelligence, algorithm, or other software tools; requiring a carrier to provide a model review process under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Artificial Intelligence - Grievance Process and Reporting (AI Health Insurance Accountability Act of 2026)
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Racial Matters -see also- Ethnic Affairs; Minorities
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers to provide for a human review of any adverse decisions or grievances resulting from the use of artificial intelligence, algorithms, or software tools. It mandates quarterly reporting to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner regarding the use of such tools, including the number of decisions overturned and demographic data of the members involved. Furthermore, if AI-driven adverse decisions result in a high frequency of grievances, the carrier must perform a model review process. The bill establishes standards for AI use in utilization reviews, prohibiting determinations based solely on group datasets and ensuring that these tools do not replace healthcare providers or cause harm to enrollees.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, health maintenance organizations (HMOs), nonprofit health service plans, dental plan organizations, pharmacy benefits managers, healthcare providers, and insured Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in an indeterminate increase in state expenditures for the Maryland Insurance Administration to oversee the new reporting requirements and model review processes. Health insurance carriers will likely face increased administrative and operational costs due to the human review mandate and the complexity of the required quarterly reports. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulator responsible for overseeing the health insurance carriers subject to this bill. The Insurance Commissioner is tasked with receiving quarterly reports, compiling annual summaries, determining the percentage thresholds for model reviews of AI tools, and enforcing compliance through audits and examinations.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) co-regulates various aspects of health policy and HMOs. The bill specifically references the Secretary of Health's reporting requirements under the Health – General Article, and the regulations regarding adverse decisions directly impact the delivery of healthcare services overseen by MDH.

The bill requires carriers to report grievance data aggregated by whether the policy was purchased on the Health Benefit Exchange, which is the marketplace administered by this agency. Changes to AI-driven decision-making and human review processes will directly affect the plans offered through the Exchange.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for health system planning and improving access to care. The implementation of AI in utilization reviews and the potential for increased grievances or denials directly relate to the commission's mission of ensuring accountability and transparency in health services.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and is responsible for enforcing consumer protection laws. The use of AI in insurance determinations and the legal requirements for human review and non-discrimination are significant areas for legal oversight and consumer advocacy.

The bill explicitly prohibits AI tools from resulting in 'unfair discrimination' and requires reporting of grievance outcomes aggregated by race and gender. The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights is the primary agency for enforcing anti-discrimination laws and investigating complaints of bias.

The Governor's Office receives the mandatory annual summary reports compiled by the Insurance Commissioner regarding carrier activities, AI-driven adverse decisions, and grievance outcomes. The office also oversees the executive branch agencies implementing these regulations.

As the agency responsible for managing the State Employee Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM has a fiscal interest in the regulatory requirements and grievance processes of health insurance carriers that provide services to state employees and their families.

The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) oversees the state's strategic approach to technology, including AI governance and data standards. The regulatory framework for inspecting and auditing AI models used by private carriers aligns with DoIT's role in cybersecurity and information technology policy.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies. If the Maryland Insurance Administration takes enforcement action against a carrier for non-compliance with the new AI grievance and reporting requirements, the carrier may appeal those decisions through the OAH.

The Health Services Cost Review Commission regulates hospital rates and quality outcomes. AI-driven adverse decisions and service denials by carriers can have a significant impact on hospital revenues, patient length-of-stay, and the financial stability of the state's all-payer system.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of recycling to exclude certain chemical conversion processes, pyrolysis, hydropyrolysis, methanolysis, gasification, enzymatic breakdown, or similar processes as determined by the Department of the Environment; and prohibiting a person from building in the State a facility that converts plastic to fuel or feedstock through a chemical conversion process.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the construction of facilities in Maryland that convert plastic into fuel or feedstock using chemical processes such as pyrolysis, gasification, or enzymatic breakdown. It also narrows the state's legal definition of 'recycling' to specifically exclude these chemical conversion methods.
stakeholders: Plastic processing and waste management industries, environmental organizations, and local government recycling coordinators.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill may have an indeterminate fiscal impact by preventing the development of new chemical conversion facilities, which could affect potential tax revenue and business investment, as well as influencing how local governments calculate and report recycling metrics.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for environmental protection and enforcing the Environment Article, MDE is the chief implementer of this bill. The department is specifically tasked with defining 'similar chemical conversion processes' and adopting regulations to enforce the prohibition on building chemical conversion facilities.

The bill's prohibition on the construction of certain plastic-to-fuel facilities directly impacts the state's economic development and industrial landscape. Commerce would need to account for this restriction when attracting or advising businesses in the waste management and chemical manufacturing sectors.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of the Environment and would be responsible for representing the state in any legal challenges to the definitions or the prohibition of facility construction.

MES provides technical environmental services and manages waste and recycling for state and local governments. The exclusion of chemical conversion from the definition of recycling and the ban on such facilities would affect MES's long-term waste management planning and operational strategy.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy. This bill touches on significant environmental and industrial policy that coordinates with the Governor's environmental priorities and legislative agenda.

MDP's role in land use planning and promoting sustainable growth through visions for resource management makes the prohibition of specific industrial facilities relevant to their long-term infrastructure and development guidance.

As a multi-agency initiative focused on environmental protection and sustainable development, this change in recycling definitions and plastic waste processing limits directly aligns with the initiative's scope of reducing the state's carbon footprint and protecting the Chesapeake Bay.

Synopsis: Prohibiting an employer from taking certain discriminatory employment actions against a fire and rescue public safety employee based on the employee's use of medical cannabis, subject to certain conditions; and requiring an employer to report an incident of a fire and rescue public safety employee reporting for work while impaired by cannabis to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
Title: Employment Discrimination - Fire and Rescue Public Safety Employees - Use of Medical Cannabis
Status: In the Senate - Favorable Report by Finance

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv

bill_summary: This bill prohibits employers from discriminating against fire and rescue public safety employees—including firefighters, emergency medical technicians, cardiac rescue technicians, and paramedics—based on their possession of a medical cannabis certification or a positive test for cannabis. While protecting employees with valid certifications, the bill allows employers to maintain policies against on-duty use or impairment and requires reporting incidents of on-duty impairment to the State Emergency Medical Services Board.
stakeholders: Fire and rescue public safety employees (firefighters, EMTs, paramedics) and their employers (State, county, and municipal governments).
fiscal_impact_summary: General fund expenditures for the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights increase by $67,800 in fiscal 2027 to hire a civil rights officer to handle an anticipated increase in discrimination complaints. Annual costs are projected to reach $89,400 by fiscal 2031. State and local governments may also face indeterminate cost increases related to potential litigation and the administrative updates of human resources policies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights (MCCR) is the primary agency responsible for enforcing anti-discrimination laws in employment. This bill creates a new protected status regarding medical cannabis use for specific public safety employees, and the fiscal note explicitly details a $67,800 expenditure increase for MCCR to handle the resulting increase in complaints.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that if a fire and rescue public safety employee reports to work while impaired by cannabis, the employer must report the incident to the State Emergency Medical Services Board, which is overseen and supported by MIEMSS.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM is responsible for managing state employee policies and benefits. DBM noted fiscal and operational impacts regarding the State's role as an employer of fire and rescue personnel and the challenges of managing impairment policies.

The bill explicitly names the 'State Airport Authority' as an employer subject to these rules. The MAA owns and operates BWI and Martin State Airport, which employ fire and rescue personnel covered by the bill's protections.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Maryland Aviation Administration. The bill's specific inclusion of airport-based fire and rescue personnel makes MDOT a relevant employing agency.

The bill's protections are predicated on the 'written certification' and status as a 'qualifying patient' within the medical cannabis program, which is regulated and overseen by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

The Maryland State Police employs paramedics and emergency medical technicians, particularly within its Aviation Command. As a state agency employing individuals defined as fire and rescue public safety employees, MSP is impacted as an employer.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and will be responsible for advising them on the intersection of this state law and federal drug-free workplace requirements, as well as defending agencies in potential litigation mentioned in the fiscal note.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for state agencies. Disputes regarding employment discrimination or professional reports to the EMS Board could result in hearings before an Administrative Law Judge.
The Governor oversees the executive branch agencies affected by this policy shift and is responsible for the final approval of the legislation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of Commerce to authorize an eligible fund manager to receive, use, and retain a certain management fee; and authorizing the Department to set an annual cap on the cumulative amount of certain management fees an eligible fund manager may receive.
Title: Economic Development - Small, Minority, and Women-Owned Business Accounts - Management Fees (Small Business Increased Access to Capital Act)
