bill_summary: This bill allows the Talbot County Board of Education to implement a school scheduling model that eliminates early dismissal days and reduces the total number of school days below 180, provided the required 1,080 school hours are maintained. The bill also mandates that the board provide hourly employees with opportunities to make up any wages lost because of the shortened schedule.
stakeholders: Public school students, teachers, and hourly employees in Talbot County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Talbot County Board of Education to offer hourly school employees opportunities to make up lost wages resulting from a reduced number of school days. Specific dollar estimates for the state or local fiscal impact are unavailable as a formal fiscal note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of Maryland's public education system, MSDE (and the State Board of Education) is directly responsible for enforcing the school attendance requirements modified by this bill. The bill specifically requires the Talbot County Board of Education to report its scheduling operations to the State Board of Education.

The bill includes a specific labor mandate requiring the county board to offer hourly employees an opportunity to make up wages lost due to scheduling changes. The PERB has jurisdiction over labor relations and disputes involving local public school system personnel.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Education and the Department of Education regarding the implementation of changes to the Education Article of the Maryland Code.

Synopsis: Regulating commercial financing transactions, including by establishing requirements related to certain disclosures, calculations of annual percentage rates, terms of repayments, and other related items, and the extension of specific offers.
Title: Commercial Financing - Small Business Truth in Lending Act
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.

bill_summary: The Small Business Truth in Lending Act regulates commercial financing transactions by requiring providers to provide clear disclosures to recipients. Key disclosures include the total financing amount, disbursement amounts, finance charges, annual percentage rates (APR), and repayment terms. The act covers various financing types—including sales-based, closed-end, and open-end financing and factoring transactions—while exempting traditional banks, credit unions, and transactions exceeding 2500000 dollars. The Commissioner of Financial Institutions is responsible for oversight, regulation, and enforcement.
stakeholders: Small businesses and other entities seeking commercial financing, non-exempt commercial financing providers, and the Maryland Commissioner of Financial Institutions.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes civil penalties of up to 2000 dollars per violation and up to 10000 dollars for each willful violation, which would contribute to state revenue. The Commissioner of Financial Institutions will incur administrative and enforcement costs to implement the regulatory framework and investigate complaints; however, specific dollar estimates for the total fiscal impact are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Financial Institutions Article, which is primarily regulated by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation under the Department of Labor. The bill explicitly tasks 'The Commissioner' with adopting regulations, investigating complaints, and enforcing civil penalties against commercial financing providers.

The bill empowers the Commissioner of Financial Regulation to investigate complaints and impose civil penalties. Such administrative enforcement actions are typically subject to adjudication by Administrative Law Judges within the Office of Administrative Hearings if contested by a provider.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency serves as a primary advocate and connector for Maryland's small business community. Since the bill regulates 'commercial financing' specifically for 'recipients' (small businesses), the office would be a key stakeholder in monitoring how these Truth in Lending protections affect their target demographic.

As the state's primary economic development agency, the Department of Commerce is concerned with the regulatory environment for small businesses. The bill's requirements for commercial financing disclosures directly impact the cost and transparency of capital for the businesses the department seeks to attract and retain.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies, including the Department of Labor. They would be responsible for advising the Commissioner on the development of regulations and representing the state in any civil enforcement actions or appeals stemming from the new law.

MEDCO provides financing and advisory services to private businesses and non-profits. Depending on the structure of its financing products, it may qualify as a 'provider' under the bill and would need to ensure its disclosure forms and APR calculations comply with the new standards.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides targeted financial services and low-interest loans to rural businesses. As a quasi-public entity extending commercial financing, it must comply with the disclosure requirements unless specifically exempted, and it would be impacted by the new regulatory framework for its lending activities.

TEDCO provides funding and resources to early-stage technology businesses. While often involved in equity, any debt-based or sales-based commercial financing offers they provide to entrepreneurs would fall under the regulatory and disclosure requirements established by this bill.

The Council is tasked with advocating for the interests of rural counties and their businesses. Because the bill impacts the accessibility and transparency of commercial lending, the Council would be concerned with its specific impact on the economic viability of rural small businesses.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. This bill implements a significant consumer protection policy for small businesses, requiring high-level coordination and alignment with the Governor's economic priorities.

Synopsis: Authorizing a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to delay or deny a disbursement from the account of a certain individual or the account on which a certain individual is a beneficiary; requiring a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to provide certain financial records to certain entities; authorizing a fiduciary institution, under certain circumstances, to contact certain individuals; and providing certain fiduciary institutions immunity from certain liability.
Title: Fiduciary Institutions - Exploitation of Seniors and Vulnerable Adults - Protections and Required Referral (Vulnerable Adult Banking Protection Act)
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

bill_summary: The Vulnerable Adult Banking Protection Act authorizes fiduciary institutions to delay or deny disbursements from the accounts of seniors (aged 65+) and vulnerable adults if financial exploitation is reasonably suspected. The bill requires institutions to notify local Adult Protective Services, law enforcement, or the State's Attorney within four business days of a disbursement request and provides for the sharing of relevant financial records. It also grants fiduciary institutions immunity from civil or administrative liability for actions taken in good faith and exercising reasonable care under these provisions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services (local Adult Protective Services agencies) and the Office of the Commissioner of Financial Regulation.
stakeholders: Seniors aged 65 and older, vulnerable adults, fiduciary institutions (including national and state banks, credit unions, and savings and loan associations), and local law enforcement and social service agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local social service agencies and law enforcement agencies are expected to manage the notification and investigation requirements within existing resources. No impact on state or local revenues is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires fiduciary institutions to notify the Adult Protective Services (APS) program in local departments of social services, which are overseen by the Department of Human Services. DHS is responsible for delivering services to vulnerable adults requiring protection from abuse and neglect.

The bill governs 'fiduciary institutions,' including those subject to the supervision of the Commissioner of the Office of Financial Regulation within the Department of Labor. The department regulates the financial institutions that are authorized to delay or deny disbursements under this act.

The bill requires fiduciary institutions to notify law enforcement agencies when they suspect financial exploitation. As the primary law enforcement agency for the state, the Maryland State Police would receive and potentially investigate these reports.

The bill authorizes courts of competent jurisdiction to issue orders that terminate or extend the delay of disbursements. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides support to the state's courts that will handle these requests.

The bill specifically targets 'eligible adults,' defined as individuals at least 65 years old. The Department of Aging is the cabinet-level agency dedicated to protecting the rights and improving the quality of life for older adults in Maryland.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for the state agencies involved in implementing this bill and enforces consumer protection laws, which are relevant to the prevention of financial exploitation.

The bill applies to 'vulnerable adults' who lack the physical or mental capacity to provide for their daily needs, a population that often includes individuals with disabilities served by this department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates Maryland's public safety strategies and manages funds for victim services. The bill's focus on reporting and preventing the financial exploitation of seniors aligns with the office's mission to reduce crime and assist victims.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a clerk of the circuit court from recording an instrument that effects a change of ownership of real property from the United States to another person unless the instrument is accompanied by a Certificate of Compliance; requiring the Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation to review certain changes of ownership of real property and issue a Certificate of Compliance following a determination of legal compliance; etc.
Title: Transfer of Real Property - Recordation Certification and State Transfer Tax (Land Transfer Accountability Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/26 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: The Land Transfer Accountability Act requires a Certificate of Compliance from the Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation before a clerk of the circuit court can record a property transfer from the U.S. government to a private party. The bill also increases the State transfer tax rate from 0.5% to 2% for these specific transactions and directs the resulting revenue to Program Open Space.
responsible_party: The Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Parties involved in real property transfers from the United States government, the Office of the Attorney General, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and the Administrative Office of the Courts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill increases the State transfer tax rate from 0.5% to 2% for property formerly held by the U.S. government, with the revenue from this increase dedicated to Program Open Space. Additionally, the Office of the Attorney General and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation are required to establish fees for the review and issuance of Certificates of Compliance to cover administrative costs, with those fees deposited into the General Fund. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the source text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Office of the Attorney General to review real property instruments for compliance with state and federal laws and, in collaboration with the Department of Assessments and Taxation, issue certificates of compliance.

The bill mandates that the Administrative Office of the Courts work with circuit court clerks to establish uniform statewide procedures for receiving and recording the newly required certificates of compliance.
The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state revenues and is specifically directed by the bill to credit transfer tax revenue from the new 2% rate to Program Open Space.

The bill establishes a 2% transfer tax rate for certain property transfers, with the resulting revenue directed to Program Open Space, a program governed by the Natural Resources Article and managed by the Department of Natural Resources.

As the chief financial agency, the Treasurer's Office manages state funds and oversees the issuance of bonds that are secured by the State transfer tax revenue mentioned in the bill's distribution section.
The bill requires fees for certificates to be deposited into the General Fund, which DBM manages, and the agency oversees the personnel and fiscal resources required for the implementing departments.
The bill references the distribution of transfer tax revenue to the Agricultural Land Preservation Fund, which supports the department's mission of rural land preservation.
The Tax Court would have jurisdiction over appeals regarding the assessment or calculation of the new 2% transfer tax established by the bill.
The new transfer tax is based on property values determined at the date of finality; disputes regarding these valuations, which form the basis of the tax, are heard by this board.
The Board of Public Works oversees the fiscal integrity of the state and approves bond issuances, including those supported by the transfer tax revenue streams modified by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations for the review, certification, and decertification of election-supporting technology and to review and evaluate election-supporting technology on or before January 1 each year; and requiring that the regulations be adopted by December 1, 2026.
Title: Election Law - Certification of Election-Supporting Technology - Regulations, Review, and Evaluation

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations for the review, certification, and decertification of election-supporting technology, such as electronic pollbooks and audit tools, and to conduct annual evaluations of this technology beginning in 2027.
stakeholders: State Board of Elections, local boards of elections, and election technology vendors
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text; therefore, specific dollar estimates for expenditures or revenues are unavailable. The bill requires the State Board of Elections to develop regulations and perform annual technology evaluations, which likely involves indeterminate administrative costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland State Board of Elections to adopt regulations for the certification and decertification of election-supporting technology and conduct annual evaluations of such equipment.

As the chief legal officer for state agencies, the OAG will provide legal counsel to the State Board of Elections in the drafting and adoption of the mandated regulations and ensure compliance with existing laws.

DoIT is the principal agency for state IT strategy and cybersecurity; its expertise is directly relevant to the review, certification, and security evaluation of the software and equipment defined as election-supporting technology.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency and would be responsible for overseeing any budgetary changes or personnel requirements necessary to implement the board's new annual technology review mandate.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state expenditures and procurement contracts; any selection or purchase of certified election-supporting technology would likely require their administrative approval.
DGS serves as the central procurement authority for the state and would be involved in the acquisition processes for technology that is reviewed and certified under the new regulations.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch agencies, including the State Board of Elections, and coordinates state policy regarding election integrity and administrative efficiency.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup on Supporting Transgender and Gender Diverse Students to study ways to support transgender and gender diverse students and, on or before December 1, 2026, make recommendations regarding statewide statutory and regulatory policies.
Title: Workgroup on Supporting Transgender and Gender Diverse Students - Established
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/04 at 1:00 p.m.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Workgroup on Supporting Transgender and Gender Diverse Students to study methods for supporting these students in public schools and to make recommendations for statewide statutory and regulatory policies.
stakeholders: Transgender and gender diverse students in Maryland public schools, the State Department of Education, county boards of education, and various state education and teacher associations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland State Department of Education is required to provide staff for the workgroup. Members of the workgroup receive no compensation but are entitled to reimbursement for travel expenses under Standard State Travel Regulations. Specific fiscal estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Education is the primary agency impacted as it is responsible for providing staff for the workgroup, appointing a representative, and receiving the final report. The workgroup's focus on public school students directly aligns with the department's oversight of the state's public education system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill establishes a new temporary body (a Workgroup) to conduct studies and make policy recommendations, which falls under this collective entity.
The Governor's Office is responsible for appointing two executive branch members to the workgroup and is one of the primary recipients of the final report and recommendations.
The Office of Appointments within the Executive Department is responsible for vetting and recommending candidates for the Governor's appointments to state task forces and commissions.
The Attorney General is required to appoint an advisory member to the workgroup, likely to provide legal counsel on statutory and regulatory policy recommendations.
The bill entitles workgroup members to travel reimbursement as provided in the state budget, which is overseen by the Department of Budget and Management as the state's principal fiscal agency.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes Maryland counties and municipalities to establish multidisciplinary local suicide fatality review teams. These teams are tasked with reviewing suicide deaths to identify systemic risk factors, improving coordination among prevention and crisis response entities, and developing recommendations to prevent future suicides. The bill also establishes protocols for membership, data confidentiality, and immunity from liability for team members.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and local health departments
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local health officers, law enforcement, behavioral health professionals, social service agencies, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) may increase by approximately $163,289 starting in fiscal 2027 for a data analyst and program administrator, though the Department of Legislative Services suggests these costs might be absorbed within existing resources. Local health department expenditures are estimated to increase by $30,000 to $50,000 for each jurisdiction that chooses to establish a team. Penalty provisions for confidentiality violations are not expected to materially affect finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary state agency for health policy and oversees local health departments and behavioral health authorities, both of which are mandated members of the local review teams. Additionally, the department is authorized to adopt regulations to carry out the subtitle.

The bill requires local departments of social services, which are part of DHS, to be represented on the suicide fatality review teams. The agency also coordinates child fatality review teams mentioned in the bill.
The bill requires local superintendents of schools to be represented on the local review teams, and the Department of Education oversees these local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires local teams to coordinate with the State Suicide Fatality Review Committee, which is a state-level committee tasked with identifying suicide trends and prevention strategies.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Emergency medical services providers are designated members of the local suicide fatality review teams. MIEMSS is the state agency responsible for overseeing and regulating the EMS network.
State law enforcement officers are listed as potential members of the multidisciplinary local teams. The Maryland State Police is the primary state-level law enforcement agency.
The bill contains significant legal provisions regarding confidentiality, Open Meetings Act exemptions, and immunity from liability, requiring legal counsel and interpretation from the OAG.

The bill establishes rules regarding the use of records as evidence, subpoenas, and discovery in judicial proceedings, as well as providing immunity from liability for team members, which impacts the court system.

As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for assessing the fiscal impact of the bill on state agencies, including the Maryland Department of Health's potential need for additional resources.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch agencies involved in these review teams and coordinates the policy initiatives related to public health and suicide prevention.

Synopsis: Requiring the Prince George's County Board of Education and County Superintendent, beginning in the 2027-2028 school year, to include certain funds in their annual budget to certain individuals hired as one-to-one student aides; requiring the County Superintendent, or the County Superintendent's designee, to provide certain quarterly updates to the county board and the State Department of Education; etc.

bill_summary: This emergency bill requires the Prince George’s County Board of Education and the County Superintendent to provide full-time salaries and benefits to all individuals employed as one-to-one student aides beginning in the 2027-2028 school year. It mandates quarterly reporting on special education services, requires annual professional development for special education staff, and directs the Maryland State Department of Education to hire a third-party auditor to conduct a comprehensive performance and financial audit of the county's special education department for fiscal years 2021 through 2025.
responsible_party: Prince George’s County Board of Education, Prince George’s County Superintendent, and the Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Students with special needs in Prince George's County Public Schools, one-to-one student aides, and special education employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a significant new spending mandate for Prince George's County by requiring full-time salaries and benefits for one-to-one student aides. The Maryland State Department of Education will incur costs to contract with a third-party auditor for a multi-year audit. Specific dollar estimates for these expenditures are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Department is responsible for hiring a third-party auditor to evaluate Prince George's County Public Schools, receiving and publishing quarterly special education updates, and certifying compliance. Additionally, the State Superintendent of Schools is authorized to withhold funds from the local school system for non-compliance with the act's record production requirements.

The bill requires a comprehensive audit of special education due process filings and resolution timelines; the OAH is the independent agency responsible for adjudicating these contested cases, which includes special education disputes, via its Administrative Law Judges.

The bill mandates that one-to-one student aides in Prince George's County receive full-time salary and benefits equivalent to other employees, which directly impacts the administration of collective bargaining and labor relations for public school personnel overseen by this board.

The Department of Disabilities is the principal agency for coordinating and improving the delivery of services to residents with disabilities; the bill's focus on the delivery of Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) and the provision of one-to-one aides for students with disabilities is a core policy focus for this agency.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts; the requirement for the Department of Education to hire a third-party auditor to conduct a performance and financial audit would involve a contract that likely requires the Board's approval.

The OLA conducts performance and fiscal compliance audits of local school systems; the scope of the third-party audit mandated by this bill regarding special education services, financial data, and staffing within Prince George's County Public Schools is highly relevant to OLA's statutory oversight role.

The audit required by the bill includes analysis of student outcomes such as graduation rates, chronic absenteeism, and discipline; the MLDS Center is the state's repository for linking and analyzing the student performance data necessary for these longitudinal evaluations.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Education and the State Superintendent; they would likely be involved in drafting the audit contract and providing legal guidance on the enforcement mechanisms and fund withholding provisions of the bill.

DBM is the principal fiscal agency for the state; it would oversee the budget execution related to the Department of Education's new oversight duties and the fiscal implications of withholding state funds from the local school system.

This office utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to enhance the responsiveness of state government; the bill's requirements for transparency dashboards, objective performance thresholds, and a corrective action plan based on audit metrics align with GOPI's mission.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the Department of Education; this bill represents a significant policy initiative concerning educational accountability and equity, and involves the appointment of various reporting requirements within the executive branch.

The office focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and improving access to education and health services; this bill's aim to ensure accountability and service delivery for students with special needs directly impacts the children and families supported by this agency.

Synopsis: Defining "danger to the life or safety of the individual or of others" for purposes of the involuntary admission of individuals with mental disorders to a facility or Veterans' Administration hospital and the emergency evaluation of individuals with mental disorders.
Title: Mental Health Law - Danger to the Life or Safety of the Individual or of Others - Definition (Right to Treatment)
Status: In the Senate - First Reading Senate Rules

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill establishes a specific definition for 'danger to the life or safety of the individual or of others' in the context of involuntary admissions and emergency evaluations for mental disorders. The definition includes a substantial risk of serious bodily harm, an inability to provide for basic needs such as food or medical care, or a substantial deterioration in judgment or reasoning, regardless of whether the risk is imminent, based on recent and relevant conduct.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Individuals with mental disorders, peace officers, healthcare professionals, the Maryland Judiciary, and the Office of the Public Defender
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by at least $414,000 in FY 2027 for the Office of the Public Defender (OPD) to hire three attorneys and support staff to manage an estimated increase of 1,000 involuntary admission cases. These expenditures are projected to reach $553,900 by FY 2031. The Judiciary may also face an indeterminate increase in general fund expenditures due to a higher volume of emergency evaluation petitions. No significant fiscal impact is expected for Maryland Department of Health hospital facilities. Local jurisdictions may see impacts on police activities and circuit court caseloads.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary executive agency responsible for overseeing behavioral health services and the mental health laws amended by this bill. It is responsible for receiving and evaluating individuals for involuntary admission to state facilities and setting regulatory policy for these clinical interventions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in involuntary admission proceedings. The fiscal note indicates this bill will increase their caseload by an estimated 1,000 cases per year, requiring a significant increase in general fund expenditures to hire additional attorneys and support staff.

The Judiciary, supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, processes petitions for emergency evaluations. The bill's expanded definition of 'danger' is expected to increase the volume of these petitions in both District and Circuit courts, impacting judicial and clerical workloads.

The Maryland State Police serve as peace officers who have the authority to petition for emergency evaluations. The change in the legal definition of 'danger' directly affects the standards by which state troopers assess and intervene with individuals suffering from mental disorders.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Judiciary regarding the enforcement of state laws. They will be responsible for providing guidance on the new legal threshold for involuntary admissions and representing state interests in related litigation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services frequently manages individuals with mental health needs within the justice system. Revisions to the criteria for involuntary admission affect the coordination of care and legal standards for justice-involved individuals requiring psychiatric intervention.

The bill explicitly applies the new definition of 'danger' to the involuntary admission of individuals to Veterans’ Administration hospitals, making this directly relevant to the department's role in assisting veterans with health benefits and advocacy.

As the principal agency for coordinating services for Marylanders with disabilities, including mental health conditions, this department is impacted by changes to legal standards that affect the rights and treatment of its target population.

The Department of Human Services manages protective services for vulnerable adults. The bill's inclusion of a person's inability to provide for basic needs (food, clothing, shelter) as a criterion for 'danger' intersects with the department's mission to assist those at risk of self-neglect due to mental impairment.

The Department of Aging advocates for older adults, who are a demographic frequently subject to emergency evaluations and involuntary admissions related to cognitive and mental health disorders. The revised standards will affect the legal protections and treatment pathways for this population.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP advises on public safety and criminal justice strategies. While a specific provision regarding criminal justice involvement was removed during amendments, the bill remains a significant public safety policy regarding the detention and treatment of potentially dangerous individuals.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive departments impacted by this bill, proposes the state budget that must account for the bill's fiscal impact on the Public Defender and the Judiciary, and is responsible for signing the legislation into law.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for developmental disabilities services to individuals who received certain services in another state and relocated to the State; and requiring the Department to begin the determination process before an individual establishes residency in the State under certain circumstances.
Title: Developmental Disabilities Services - Expedited Eligibility Determinations for Recently Relocated Individuals (Ralph's Act)
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

Home Care Services -see also- Respite Care

bill_summary: Known as Ralph's Act, this bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to provide an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for developmental disabilities services to individuals who move to Maryland after receiving similar services in another state for at least 10 years. To qualify, the individual must be a dependent of an immediate family member who has lived in Maryland for at least two years and moved because their caretaker died or became incapacitated. The department must complete the determination within 60 business days and may begin the process before the individual has established residency in the State.
stakeholders: Individuals with developmental disabilities relocating to Maryland and their immediate family members who are Maryland residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can likely handle the bill's requirements using existing resources, as the number of eligible individuals is expected to be very limited. However, if application volume increases significantly, an additional position costing approximately $80,000 annually (shared between general and federal funds) might be required. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), the Department is tasked with establishing and implementing the expedited Medicaid eligibility determination process and providing services to individuals who meet the new criteria.

This agency is the principal state entity for coordinating services for residents with disabilities and works with other departments to ensure inclusive services, making the streamlining of eligibility for disabled residents highly relevant to its mission.

The Exchange administers the state's health insurance marketplace and determines eligibility for Medicaid; since the bill requires an expedited Medicaid eligibility determination for these specific services, coordination with the Exchange's systems and protocols may be necessary.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases for state agencies including the Department of Health; any appeals or disputes regarding the new expedited eligibility determinations or service priority assignments would likely be heard by this office.

The fiscal note indicates potential administrative burdens and staffing needs at MDH to manage the expedited process, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget, personnel, and fiscal planning.

The OAG provides legal counsel to MDH and would likely be involved in ensuring the new expedited process complies with federal Medicaid waiver requirements and assisting with any necessary CMS approvals mentioned in the fiscal note.

This office focuses on the well-being of Maryland's children and families, particularly those in vulnerable situations; the bill specifically addresses families where a caretaker has died or become incapacitated, requiring support for their dependents.

The bill mandates a specific timeline for eligibility determinations (60 business days), making the tracking and oversight of this new performance metric relevant to GOPI's mission of enhancing government responsiveness.

The team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and address child poverty; the bill's focus on helping vulnerable relocated families access services aligns with the team's multidisciplinary mission.

Military families relocate frequently, and the provisions for expedited eligibility for dependents of residents relocating to Maryland may impact military families moving into the state who have dependents with developmental disabilities.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy coordination; the bill is presented for the Governor's approval and involves significant policy changes regarding the prioritization of state services.

The Department of Aging supports caregivers and older adults; the bill addresses situations where a caretaker's death or incapacitation (often an aging parent or relative) necessitates a move, which intersects with the department's long-term care advocacy.

bill_summary: The bill establishes that noncompete and conflict of interest clauses in employment contracts for licensed architects are null and void if the employer relocates its principal place of business outside of Maryland or if the majority of its employees no longer work from Maryland-based sites. This rule applies to employers who had more than 30 Maryland-based employees at the time the architect was hired and targets contracts executed on or after the bill's effective date.
stakeholders: Licensed architects and architectural firms or other employers with more than 30 employees that relocate their operations outside of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. There is a potential meaningful impact on small businesses (those with 30 to 50 employees) that relocate their headquarters or the majority of their workforce outside of Maryland, as they will be prohibited from enforcing existing noncompete provisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Labor and Employment Article and falls under the jurisdiction of the Maryland Department of Labor. Additionally, the department oversees the Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing, which is responsible for the 'licensed architects' specifically mentioned and protected by the bill's provisions.

The bill defines legal standards for 'judicial enforcement' and declares certain contract provisions 'null and void as being against the public policy of the State.' This directly impacts how state courts adjudicate employment contract disputes and noncompete enforcement actions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and represents the state in matters concerning the enforcement of labor laws and public policy. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal implications of these new contract restrictions.

The bill specifically addresses employers that relocate their principal place of business or the majority of their workforce outside of Maryland. As the state's primary economic development agency, this policy regarding business relocation and the retention of skilled professionals (architects) is relevant to their mission.

bill_summary: This emergency bill prohibits the State and local governments from approving the use of any building or property as a detention facility, including immigration detention facilities, by a private entity. It authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions to enforce the prohibition and establishes a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per day for each violation. The bill also includes contingent provisions that would impose strict zoning and public notice requirements for private detention facilities if the absolute prohibition is ever ruled unenforceable by a court.
responsible_party: Maryland Attorney General, State government, and units of local government
stakeholders: Private entities operating detention facilities, individuals detained for civil or criminal violations, and State and local government units involved in zoning and corrections.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It establishes a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per day for violations, which would provide indeterminate revenue to the State only in the event of noncompliance by private entities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill specifically authorizes the Attorney General to bring civil actions to enforce the prohibition against private detention facilities and to seek temporary or permanent injunctive relief.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Correctional Services Article, which is the primary regulatory domain of the department, and establishes new standards for what constitutes a detention facility in Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategy, this office is relevant to the bill's policy shift regarding the management and privatization of detention facilities.
The bill authorizes the Judiciary to hear civil actions brought by the Attorney General and to issue injunctions and civil penalties of up to $10,000 per day.

Section 2 of the bill introduces specific land use and zoning requirements for private detention facilities, areas where the Department of Planning provides technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments.

The bill provides specific exclusions for health care facilities licensed by the Department of Health, requiring the agency to ensure its licensed facilities are not misclassified under the new detention facility criteria.

The bill provides specific exclusions for residential child care programs and child placement agencies licensed by the Department of Human Services, requiring coordination to ensure these programs are not affected by the detention facility prohibition.

The department manages and supervises youth in detention; the bill's restrictions on private detention facilities intersect with the department's oversight of residential facilities and rehabilitative services.
As the agency responsible for state real estate management and facilities, DGS is impacted by the prohibition on the state approving the use of real property for private detention facilities.

The Board oversees significant state contracts and the transfer or lease of state property, which is directly relevant to the bill's prohibition on the state approving real property for use as a private detention facility.
The State Police were identified as a contributing agency in the fiscal note and may be involved in issues regarding involuntary custody and the secure confinement features described in the bill.
As the state's principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for supervising the fiscal impacts of the bill, including the collection of any civil penalties generated by violations.

bill_summary: This emergency bill establishes minimum mandatory safety and care standards for immigration detention facilities in Maryland and expands the oversight authority of the Maryland Commission on Correctional Standards to include these facilities. The bill mandates that certain facility staff report violations, requires annual facility certifications regarding safety and utilities, and authorizes the Attorney General to take legal action and seek civil penalties against private operators for noncompliance.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Civil detainees in immigration detention facilities, incarcerated individuals in correctional facilities, private and public facility operators, and health care and security professionals working within these facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill will lead to a potential significant increase in State general fund expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to manage expanded inspection, certification, and oversight duties. While a specific dollar estimate is currently unavailable, the impact is expected to be significant. The bill also authorizes civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, though State revenues and local government finances are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department is the primary implementing agency. Its Secretary is required to adopt regulations for immigration detention facilities, and the Maryland Commission on Correctional Standards (MCCS), which is housed within the Department, is responsible for inspections, compliance, and enforcement of the new standards.

The Attorney General is an ex officio member of the Commission on Correctional Standards. The bill specifically authorizes the Attorney General to bring legal actions against private entities for violations of reporting requirements, certification failures, or non-compliance with audit findings.

The bill authorizes the Commission to conduct joint inspections with the Maryland Department of Health. Furthermore, licensed health care practitioners are mandatory reporters of violations under the bill, and their respective licensing boards (housed within MDH) are required to take disciplinary action for failures to report.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is an ex officio member of the Commission on Correctional Standards. Additionally, the fiscal note indicates a potentially significant increase in general fund expenditures to support the staffing needs of the Commission for expanded inspection and certification duties.

The Secretary of General Services is an ex officio member of the Commission on Correctional Standards. The bill also establishes new requirements for facility certifications regarding utilities, physical plant maintenance, and emergency power systems.

The bill requires certified security guards to report violations, and the Maryland State Police is the agency responsible for such certifications under Title 19. Additionally, joint inspections of facilities may involve the State Fire Marshal, which is a unit within the State Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that licensed emergency medical technicians (EMTs) report violations and requires facilities to maintain coordination protocols with emergency medical services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the statutory duties of an existing commission (MCCS) and explicitly authorizes the creation of a new advisory board specifically focused on immigration detention facilities.

The bill allows the Commission, in conjunction with the Attorney General, to petition circuit courts for compliance orders. The fiscal note recognizes potential impacts on the Judiciary resulting from these new enforcement actions.

Facilities are required to maintain emergency operations plans and establish coordination protocols with emergency management units, which falls under the broader scope of MDEM's coordination mission.

The Commission is required to submit an annual report on its activities and compliance issues at correctional and immigration facilities to the Governor. The bill also impacts high-level executive branch regulatory policy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice policy in Maryland. This bill creates a new regulatory framework for detention facilities that falls within their advisory and policy oversight domain.

As the liaison to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, GOHS is relevant because the bill regulates facilities housing federal civil immigration detainees (ICE detainees) and requires coordination with federal entities.
The bill standardizes the process for reporting and reviewing violations, which could result in contested administrative hearings requiring impartial adjudication by OAH.

OLA is responsible for fiscal and performance audits of state agencies. The expansion of MCCS duties and the associated significant expenditure of state funds will likely be subject to OLA oversight and compliance auditing.

bill_summary: The bill expands Maryland's school bus transition program to include propane-powered school buses alongside zero-emission vehicles. It renames the state's transition grant program and fund, directs the Department of the Environment and Department of Transportation to provide technical assistance, and allows county boards of education to enter into contracts for propane-powered school buses starting in fiscal year 2030.
stakeholders: Maryland county boards of education, private school bus contractors, and public school students.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill expands the scope of the Zero-Emission Vehicle School Bus Transition Fund to include propane-powered buses, utilizing funding from state appropriations, interest earnings, and legal settlements. Although the bill enables grants and alters school board contracting options, specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Department of the Environment as the lead agency responsible for implementing and administering the Zero-Emission Vehicle and Propane-Powered School Bus Transition Grant Program and Fund.

The Maryland State Department of Education is explicitly required to consult on the administration of the program and fund, and it oversees the county school boards directly impacted by the bus procurement changes.

The bill explicitly tasks the Department of Transportation with jointly providing technical assistance to county boards of education and contractors for the transition to propane-powered school buses.
The State Treasurer is specifically mandated to hold the Zero-Emission Vehicle and Propane-Powered School Bus Transition Fund and manage its investments and interest earnings.
The bill requires the Comptroller to account for the newly renamed and expanded Zero-Emission Vehicle and Propane-Powered School Bus Transition Fund.
The department is responsible for supervising the state's budget and will oversee the fiscal management and appropriations for the expanded grant program and special fund.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the primary implementing agencies (MDE, MSDE, and MDOT) regarding the new regulations and the management of legal settlements that may fund the program.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures and contracts, which may include large-scale procurement or grants related to school bus transitions.
The OLA is responsible for conducting fiscal compliance audits of the state agencies and the special fund created or altered by this legislation.

bill_summary: This bill increases the mandatory retirement age for members of the State Police Retirement System from 60 to 62 years and adjusts the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) eligibility and participation limits to reflect this change. It also allows certain current DROP participants to extend their participation until they reach age 62 or complete seven years in the program.

stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS)
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State pension liabilities decrease by $2,110,000, and the normal cost decreases by $60,000. This is expected to result in a $290,000 decrease in State general fund expenditures for pension contributions in fiscal 2028, with savings continuing to accrue in subsequent years. There is no fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland State Police by increasing the mandatory retirement age for its members and the Secretary of State Police from 60 to 62. It also alters the eligibility and participation requirements for the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) specifically for members of the State Police Retirement System.

As the administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), which includes the State Police Retirement System, this agency is responsible for implementing the bill's changes to retirement ages, processing extension requests for the DROP, and providing the necessary forms and support to affected members.

DBM is the principal personnel and fiscal agency for the state. This bill changes state personnel policy regarding retirement age for a specific class of employees and results in a reduction of state pension liabilities and general fund expenditures for employer contributions.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the Maryland State Police, and is responsible for signing the legislation into law. The bill also explicitly mentions the Governor's signature and the role of the Secretary of State Police, who is an appointee of the Governor.

The Comptroller is a member of the Board of Public Works and typically serves on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, which is responsible for approving retirement orders and managing the system affected by this bill.

The State Treasurer acts as the state's chief financial agency and typically sits on the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System. The Treasurer's office is also responsible for the management and protection of the state funds that will see a fiscal impact from reduced pension liabilities.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Maryland State Police and the State Retirement Agency, regarding the implementation of legislative changes to retirement and pension laws.

OLA conducts fiscal and performance audits of executive branch agencies and would be responsible for ensuring the State Retirement Agency and Maryland State Police properly implement the adjusted retirement ages and DROP extensions in compliance with the updated law.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists to certify licensed psychologists to use prescriptive authority, allowing them to prescribe and administer medications for mental health and behavioral disorders. It establishes rigorous qualification requirements, including a doctoral degree, specialized education, a postdoctoral fellowship, and a national examination, while creating the Prescriptive Authority Advisory Committee to oversee implementation.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners of Psychologists
stakeholders: Licensed psychologists seeking prescriptive authority, patients with psychiatric or behavioral disorders, the State Board of Physicians, and the State Board of Pharmacy.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note is not included in the provided text. The bill creates administrative costs for the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists related to the certification process, oversight, and the operation of the Prescriptive Authority Advisory Committee, which would likely be offset by revenue from certification and renewal fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, which is a unit within the Department of Health. The Department will be responsible for implementing the certification process, oversight of prescribing psychologists, and managing the Prescription Drug Monitoring Program (PDMP) which the bill requires psychologists to use.

The bill requires prescribing psychologists to file their Maryland State Controlled Dangerous Substance registration number with the Board. As the agency responsible for issuing these permits and enforcing the Controlled Dangerous Substance Act, the OCSA will oversee the registration and regulation of these new prescribers.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the State Board of Examiners of Psychologists, the State Board of Physicians, and the State Board of Pharmacy, all of which are involved in the new advisory committee and regulatory framework created by this bill.

The bill sets rigorous educational and postdoctoral training requirements for certification, which involves coordination with the state's regulatory body for higher education to ensure programs meet the required standards.

The bill sets rigorous educational and postdoctoral training requirements for certification, which involves coordination with the state's regulatory body for higher education to ensure programs meet the required standards.

As the agency that adjudicates contested cases for state regulatory boards, the OAH would handle hearings related to the denial, suspension, or revocation of the new prescriptive authority certifications.

The expansion of prescriptive authority to licensed psychologists affects health insurance regulation, including provider scope of practice, rate-setting, and compliance with state insurance laws regarding covered services.

The Council is dedicated to improving healthcare access in rural areas; authorizing psychologists to prescribe medications is a key policy often aimed at addressing the shortage of psychiatrists in underserved rural communities.

DJS manages the treatment of youth in the juvenile justice system, many of whom require mental health services and medication. The authorization of psychologists to prescribe could impact how these services are delivered within DJS facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is responsible for the rehabilitation and medical care of incarcerated individuals. Expanding the pool of authorized prescribers to include psychologists could change mental health treatment protocols within state correctional facilities.

DHS provides services to vulnerable children and adults who may require psychiatric medication; psychologists with prescriptive authority could play a larger role in the care of individuals served by DHS programs.

The Department oversees long-term care and mental health advocacy for older adults. The ability of psychologists to prescribe medication would impact the delivery of behavioral health services to Maryland's aging population.

The department coordinates services for residents with disabilities, including mental health conditions. Changing the scope of practice for psychologists impacts the delivery and integration of these services.

The Commission adjudicates claims that include psychiatric treatment. Authorizing psychologists to prescribe medication would change the scope of authorized medical treatment and the types of providers whose treatment plans and testimony are evaluated in claims.

As the administrator for state employee workers' compensation claims, this entity would be impacted by the expansion of providers authorized to prescribe medication for mental health conditions related to workplace injuries.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office handles medical malpractice claims. By granting prescriptive authority to psychologists, the bill creates a new class of healthcare providers subject to potential malpractice claims related to medication management.

The MHCC is responsible for health system planning and improving access to care. Changes in the scope of practice for health professionals like psychologists are relevant to their planning and accountability mandates.

USM institutions provide the doctoral and postdoctoral training in psychology and clinical pharmacology that would be required for practitioners to meet the certification standards established in the bill.
Morgan State University offers graduate programs in psychology and would be involved in providing the specialized training and clinical education required for the new certification.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and boards, and the Governor appoints the members of the Board of Examiners of Psychologists who will implement the bill.

The Office of Appointments assists in recruiting and vetting candidates for the state boards, including the Board of Examiners of Psychologists, which is tasked with new regulatory duties under this bill.

bill_summary: This bill phases out the sale and distribution of various products containing intentionally added PFAS chemicals in Maryland, with bans starting in 2028 and 2029. It requires manufacturers of PFAS-containing products to register with the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) and pay registration fees. The bill also establishes the Maryland PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund to support contamination assessment, prevention, and remediation through grants and loans, funded by registration fees and penalties.
stakeholders: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers of products containing PFAS (such as cookware, cosmetics, and textiles); consumers; and State and local agencies involved in public health and environmental protection.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, MDE expenditures increase by $201,400 in FY 2027, rising to over $677,800 in future years to cover staffing and grant/loan awards ($250,000 annually). Special fund revenues from manufacturer registration fees and penalties will increase, while general fund revenues will decrease as existing penalties are redirected to the new special fund. Local governments may face higher procurement costs but gain access to remediation grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, MDE is responsible for adopting regulations, managing product registrations, collecting fees, enforcing product bans, and administering the Maryland PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund.

MDE is required to consult with the Department of Health to identify unavoidable uses of PFAS chemicals and to administer the PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund and its grant/loan criteria.

MDE is required to consult with the Department of Agriculture on the administration of the PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund and the development of grant and loan criteria, particularly regarding impacts on farm operations.

MDE is required to consult with DNR on the administration of the PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund and the development of grant and loan criteria, specifically concerning contamination of ecosystems and fish tissue.
The OAG is responsible for prosecuting violations, representing the state in civil actions for penalties, and pursuing cost recovery from PFAS polluters for the remediation fund.
MDE must consult with the Chesapeake Bay Trust on the administration of the PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund and the development of criteria for project applications.
The State Treasurer is responsible for holding the Maryland PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund separately and investing its funds.
The Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the Maryland PFAS Chemicals Protection and Remediation Fund and managing interest earnings distributions.
DBM oversees the fiscal impact on the state budget, including the creation of multiple new positions at MDE and the management of a significant new special fund.
As the state's central procurement authority, DGS will be impacted by prohibitions on various products (cleaning supplies, paint, textiles) commonly purchased for state facilities.

The bill provides funding for research and projects involving the removal of PFAS from wastewater and landfill leachate, areas where MES provides technical and operational services to state and local governments.
MDOT is impacted by regulations on fire-fighting foam at airports and ports, and as a major consumer of restricted products like industrial cleaners and highway-related paints.
Member institutions are eligible for grants/loans from the PFAS fund and are impacted as consumers of various restricted products like cleaning supplies and scientific materials.
As a state institution and researcher, MSU is impacted as a consumer of regulated products and is an eligible recipient for grants or loans from the PFAS fund.
The college is impacted as a consumer of various regulated products and is an eligible recipient for grants or loans from the PFAS fund.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the sale, distribution, and manufacturing of lab-grown meat for human consumption in Maryland. It defines lab-grown meat as animal tissue cultured from cells outside the source animal and establishes a civil penalty of up to $5,000 for violations. The Secretary of Health is also authorized to seize or condemn any lab-grown meat produced or sold in violation of the law.
stakeholders: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers of meat products; Maryland consumers; and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided. The bill establishes a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per violation, which would result in an indeterminate revenue increase for the state. The Maryland Department of Health will incur administrative and enforcement costs, including the potential seizure of prohibited products, though specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Health – General Article. The Secretary of Health is responsible for enforcement, including the authority to seize or condemn prohibited lab-grown meat products.

This bill directly impacts the meat industry and agricultural policy in Maryland. The Department of Agriculture regulates food quality and is tasked with promoting the economic viability of traditional farming and agribusiness, which this ban supports.

The bill prohibits the manufacturing and sale of a specific food-technology product, which affects the state's economic development strategies, particularly within the biotechnology and food manufacturing sectors.

TEDCO supports early-stage technology-based businesses and the commercialization of technology. A ban on lab-grown meat would restrict innovation and investment in this emerging biotechnology sector in Maryland.
The bill establishes civil penalties to be collected via civil actions in the District Court, impacting court operations and the judiciary's administrative functions.
The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Department of Health and Department of Agriculture regarding the enforcement of this ban and would represent the state in civil penalty actions.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, coordinates policy initiatives, and would be responsible for signing this legislation and overseeing its implementation across departments.
DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and oversight. This bill has potential fiscal impacts related to enforcement costs and revenue from civil penalties.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the State or any of its instrumentalities or political subdivisions from taking certain property that is subject to a perpetual agricultural or conservation easement.
Title: Eminent Domain - Agricultural and Conservation Easements - Prohibited Taking
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/05 at 1:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Agriculture -see also- Agritourism; Cannabis Prd; Farm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the State of Maryland, its instrumentalities, and its political subdivisions from using the power of eminent domain to acquire privately owned property that is subject to a perpetual agricultural or conservation easement.
responsible_party: The State of Maryland, its instrumentalities, and its political subdivisions
stakeholders: Owners of private property under perpetual agricultural or conservation easements, state and local government agencies involved in infrastructure and land acquisition, and land conservation organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text; however, the bill explicitly prohibits certain land acquisitions, which may increase the cost of public projects by requiring more expensive alternative routes or sites to avoid protected properties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF), which manages perpetual agricultural easements. This bill directly protects land subject to these easements from being taken via eminent domain.

The Department of Natural Resources manages various conservation easements, including those under Program Open Space and the Rural Legacy Program. The bill directly prohibits the use of eminent domain on property subject to these perpetual conservation easements.

The Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) frequently utilizes eminent domain for the expansion of highways, transit lines, and other infrastructure. This bill would restrict the agency's ability to acquire land protected by perpetual agricultural or conservation easements.

As a modal administration within MDOT, SHA is responsible for the construction and maintenance of state roads. It is a primary user of eminent domain power, and this legislation would prohibit its use on easement-protected properties.

The MDTA is an instrumentality responsible for toll facilities and has the power to finance and build transportation projects, which often requires land acquisition through eminent domain. This bill would limit that authority.

The Department of General Services is the state's central real estate and procurement agency, responsible for land acquisition for state-owned facilities. This bill restricts the agency's capacity to acquire specific types of property for public use.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding property law and represents the state in eminent domain proceedings. This bill creates a significant new legal prohibition that the OAG would need to enforce and interpret.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures, including the acquisition of state property and the creation of easements. This bill restricts the Board's authority to approve certain types of condemnation.

The Department of Planning oversees the Maryland Historical Trust and promotes sustainable growth and resource management. It has a significant interest in the preservation of agricultural and conservation lands affected by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO provides financial services to support rural land preservation and agricultural viability. The bill reinforces the permanent nature of the easements MARBIDCO helps facilitate.

The Maryland Stadium Authority is a state instrumentality that plans and builds large-scale facilities, which sometimes involves land acquisition. This bill would restrict its eminent domain powers relative to easement-protected lands.
DBM is responsible for fiscal planning and the state budget. Restrictions on eminent domain can impact the costs, timelines, and feasibility of major state capital projects.

MEDCO is a state instrumentality involved in real estate development to promote economic prosperity. This bill would limit its ability to acquire property for development if that property is under a perpetual easement.
As a state instrumentality that manages environmental infrastructure projects, MES might be impacted if a project requires land acquisition currently protected by a conservation easement.
The Governor oversees the executive branch and its instrumentalities, all of which are subject to this new prohibition on the use of eminent domain.
The State Treasurer serves on the Board of Public Works, which must approve state property acquisitions and easements, and the office manages the protection of state property.

Synopsis: Repealing the option for an applicant for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services to pass a practical and written examination administered by the State Board of Cosmetology in order to be licensed; etc.
Title: State Board of Cosmetologists - Licensing - Eyelash Extensions
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Age -see also- Age of Maj; Children; Elderly; Inf&Tod.; etc
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill repeals the option for an applicant for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services to qualify for the license by passing a practical and written examination without completing specific training. Applicants must now meet alternative requirements, which include either serving as a registered apprentice for at least three months or successfully completing 100 hours of instruction in an approved cosmetology school, in addition to passing the board-administered examination.
stakeholders: Applicants for a limited license to provide eyelash extension services, registered apprentices, and approved cosmetology schools in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the State Board of Cosmetologists can implement the licensing changes with existing resources. State revenues are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact. Small businesses are expected to experience a minimal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the licensing and regulation of various professions, including the State Board of Cosmetologists, which is the primary body responsible for implementing the licensing changes for eyelash extension services mandated by this bill.

The bill explicitly mentions that the instruction required for an eyelash extension license must be completed in a cosmetology school approved by the State Department of Education. By removing the examination-only path, this agency's role in approving and overseeing these educational programs becomes a mandatory part of the licensing process.

The bill specifies that the required instruction for eyelash extension services can be completed in schools approved by the Maryland Higher Education Commission. The removal of the exam-only qualification option makes the commission's oversight of these vocational training programs more central to the licensing requirements.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state boards and commissions, including the State Board of Cosmetologists. They would be responsible for advising the board on the regulatory updates and legal implications of changing license qualification requirements.

Synopsis: Authorizing a merchant to round the portion of the price of a certain  transactions for which a customer pays using cash in a certain manner or round the amount of change due to a customer in a certain manner; providing that certain provisions of the Act shall preempt existing regulations, rules, and ordinances that conflict with certain provisions of the Act; and altering the definition of "taxable price" for certain purposes to clarify the exclusion from tax of a certain amount collected due to rounding the price.
Title: Business Regulation - Rounding Cash Transactions - Authorization
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Laws and Ordinances -see also- Pub Local Laws; Uniform Laws
