bill_summary: This bill establishes a five-year pilot program in Howard County that authorizes the county to use surveillance cameras at designated dumping sites to enforce laws against illegal dumping. It allows the Howard County Police Department or a designated department to issue civil citations of up to $1,000 to the owners of motor vehicles recorded by the surveillance systems, provides for a trial process in District Court, and authorizes the Motor Vehicle Administration to suspend vehicle registrations for unpaid fines.
responsible_party: Howard County Police Department or other department designated by the Howard County Executive
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners in Howard County, the Howard County government, the Howard County Police Department, and the Maryland District Court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $10,300 in fiscal 2027 for one-time computer programming by the Judiciary. Starting in fiscal 2028, the State Highway Administration may see an expenditure decrease of up to $250,000 annually due to reduced litter removal costs if the program deter dumping. Howard County revenues will increase from the collection of civil penalties (up to $1,000 per violation), although the county will also incur costs for system installation and operation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the District Court, which must consult with Howard County on citation forms, schedule trials for contested violations, and adopt procedures for the issuance of citations and collection of penalties. The fiscal note identifies a specific general fund expenditure for computer programming within the Judiciary.

The bill explicitly requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to refuse or suspend the registration of vehicles involved in illegal dumping violations if the owner fails to pay the fine or appear for trial.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and the State Highway Administration (SHA), MDOT is highly relevant. The bill mandates MVA enforcement actions, and the fiscal note indicates that SHA may see a decrease in litter removal expenditures as a result of the pilot program.
The bill references the Comptroller's existing role in the system for remitting costs, fines, and penalties collected by the District Court to the State.

The bill concerns the enforcement of illegal dumping and litter control laws, which falls under the broader mission of the Department of the Environment to protect land quality and enforce environmental laws.
As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies involved in implementing the bill and the Governor must sign the legislation into law.

The Office of the Attorney General may be required to provide legal counsel to the state agencies (MVA and Judiciary) regarding the implementation and enforcement of the new surveillance and registration-suspension provisions.

stakeholders: Individuals with Alzheimer’s disease, related dementias, or autism at risk of elopement, as well as their families and caregivers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, there is no state or local fiscal impact because the bill only authorizes specific groups to make recommendations and does not substantively change state operations or create new insurance or program mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council, which is explicitly authorized by this bill to recommend elopement response devices for individuals with dementia.
The Department of Disabilities houses the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs, which is authorized by this bill to recommend elopement response devices for individuals with autism.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the authorized activities and scope of recommendations for two specific state bodies: the Virginia I. Jones Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias Council and the Advisory Stakeholder Group on Autism-Related Needs.

The Department of Aging focuses on the quality of life for older adults and individuals with Alzheimer's; the authorization of elopement response device recommendations directly aligns with their mission to support long-term care and safety for these populations.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch departments (MDH and MDOD) and the councils/boards that are granted new recommendatory authority under this bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies and boards impacted by this legislation and was consulted as an information source during the fiscal analysis of the bill.

While the mandatory insurance coverage requirements were stricken from the final bill, the MIA remains a relevant stakeholder as an information source regarding health-related devices and potential future policy recommendations regarding medical safety technology.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) to provide coverage for perinatal behavioral health screenings during a child's first year of life. It mandates that health care providers perform these screenings at specific well-child visits and provide educational information to pregnant and postpartum patients. The bill also requires carriers to provide standing referrals to behavioral health care providers for pregnant and postpartum members, establishes a $1,000 refundable State income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child, and directs health occupations boards to grant double continuing education credits for perinatal behavioral health training.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Insurance Administration, Maryland Health Care Commission, and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Pregnant and postpartum individuals, parents of stillborn children, health care providers, and health insurance carriers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will decrease by an indeterminate amount beginning in fiscal 2027 due to the establishment of a $1,000 refundable income tax credit for parents of stillborn children. Special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in fiscal 2027 from $125 rate and form filing fees. The Maryland Department of Health, Medicaid, and the Maryland Health Care Commission can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency. It is responsible for identifying perinatal behavioral health screening tools, developing provider training programs, administering Medicaid coverage for these screenings, and disseminating information to local WIC agencies.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission conduct an analysis and report on the impact of requiring coverage for perinatal behavioral health screenings and prohibiting certain cost-sharing practices.

The bill establishes a $1,000 refundable State income tax credit for parents of a stillborn child, which the Comptroller is responsible for administering and overseeing as the state's principal tax collector.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for regulating health insurance carriers and ensuring they comply with the bill's requirements for mandatory screenings, coverage, and standing referrals to behavioral health providers.
The bill impacts the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which is managed by DBM. The agency reviewed the bill for potential fiscal impacts on the state plan.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the various state agencies and boards tasked with implementing the new health regulations and tax provisions.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the agencies implementing this bill, and the bill requires a report to be submitted to legislative committees regarding health care impacts.

bill_summary: This bill redefines and updates the scopes of practice for licensed social workers in Maryland, including bachelor, master, and certified clinical social workers. It outlines the specific activities authorized for each license level, details supervision requirements for clinical duties such as psychotherapy and diagnosis, and clarifies the standards for independent practice within the profession.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Social Work Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed bachelor, master, and clinical social workers; the State Board of Social Work Examiners; and individuals and communities in Maryland receiving social work services.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text. The legislation focuses on regulatory definitions and professional scopes of practice and does not explicitly state any financial implications, fee changes, or specific spending mandates. Consequently, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and is responsible for the final approval of legislation. While not the primary implementer, the office manages the policy coordination that affects the state's workforce regulations.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Board of Social Work Examiners and the Department of Health. They would be responsible for interpreting these scope-of-practice changes and defending them in legal challenges.

The Department of Aging relies on social workers for long-term care advocacy and nutrition programs. Changes to the professional scope and supervision of social workers directly impact the workforce available for elder care services.
As the state's central personnel agency, DBM is affected by changes to the professional qualifications and practice standards of state-employed social workers.
Social workers are primary service providers and case managers for individuals with disabilities. Scope changes impact how these integrated services are delivered.

MSDE oversees school social workers. Changes to clinical diagnosis authority and supervision requirements for social workers directly affect the delivery of behavioral health services in public schools.

The Maryland Department of Health houses the State Board of Social Work Examiners and regulates health care professionals. This bill directly amends the Health Occupations Article governing a profession MDH oversees.

DHS is a major employer of social workers who handle foster care, adoption, and protective services. Changes to social work practice standards and the ability of staff to practice independently are critical to their operational model.

DJS employs social workers for the rehabilitation and assessment of youth in the justice system. The bill's changes to clinical assessment and treatment authorizations affect their internal staffing and service provision.
The Department of Labor is involved in professional licensing and workforce development generally, making them relevant to broad changes in health occupation scopes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS utilizes social workers for inmate rehabilitation and community supervision. New scope-of-practice definitions will dictate what their clinical staff can perform within correctional facilities.
Social work is a core component of veteran advocacy and family support services. Changes to licensing categories affect the department's outreach and support capabilities.

MHEC oversees the educational institutions that train social workers. The bill's updated definitions of required professional preparation and practice must align with the academic standards MHEC coordinates.
The Office of Appointments vets members for the State Board of Social Work Examiners, which is the primary entity impacted by this legislation.
The office coordinates support networks for children and families, where social workers are the primary service delivery professionals. Changes to their scope impact child well-being initiatives.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office manages youth programs and victim services that frequently utilize social work professionals for crisis intervention and safety planning.
The board sets the strategy for the state's workforce; social work is a critical and regulated sector of that workforce.

Social workers interact frequently with the judicial system in family, criminal, and juvenile law matters. Scope changes, particularly around clinical diagnosis, impact their role as expert witnesses and court-appointed professionals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Clinical social workers are health care providers. Alterations to their scope of practice could impact the types of medical malpractice claims that go through this office's arbitration system.
The MHCC plans for the state's health system needs. The bill affects the professional capabilities of a large portion of the behavioral health workforce.
MLDS tracks workforce outcomes for student graduates. Changes to licensing categories are relevant to how the state tracks social work career paths and workforce supply.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD uses social workers for mitigation and psychosocial assessment in criminal defense. The bill's specific language regarding psychosocial evaluations and clinical diagnosis is highly relevant to their practice.
MSD employs social workers to support its students. The updated scopes of practice will define the service limits of these staff members.
The team focuses on child poverty and economic mobility. Since social workers are key to these efforts, the team would be concerned with the regulatory framework governing that profession.
Morgan State has a major Social Work department and is a state agency. Changes to licensing categories and practice scopes require updates to their curricula and student preparation.

OAH adjudicates contested cases involving licensing boards. ALJs would hear cases related to the newly defined scopes of practice if a social worker is charged with practicing outside of their category.
The board oversees collective bargaining for state and higher education employees, many of whom are social workers impacted by these professional changes.
As a state agency that provides professional preparation in the arts and sciences, SMCM has an interest in ensuring their graduates meet these updated professional practice standards.
The Commission handles claims that involve psychological injuries where social workers may perform assessments or provide treatment.

Multiple USM institutions host social work degree programs. The bill's redefinition of 'Practice Social Work' based on degree levels and the specific scope of each license category is critical for USM academic planning and professional certification alignment.

bill_summary: This bill allows U.S. Foreign Service members and their spouses who relocate to Maryland on official assignment to practice their profession using a valid occupational or professional license from another state. Eligible individuals are exempt from Maryland's standard licensing requirements for the duration of their assignment, provided they meet specific criteria such as remaining in good standing with their original licensing authority and complying with Maryland's standards of practice and continuing education.
responsible_party: Maryland State licensing authorities (including the Department of Agriculture, Department of Labor, State Department of Education, and Department of Health)
stakeholders: U.S. Foreign Service members and their spouses relocating to Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general and special fund expenditures will increase by an estimated $45,000 in FY 2027 for one-time software updates to licensing platforms ($30,000 for the Maryland State Department of Education and $15,000 for the State Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners). Local government finances are not significantly affected.

The bill specifically modifies requirements for transient vendor licenses, which are administered by the State Comptroller.

The bill affects a vast range of health professional boards under the Department of Health's jurisdiction, including nursing, pharmacy, dentistry, and medicine.
The Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing oversees many of the boards and commissions impacted by this bill, including public accountancy, architects, and barbers.
The bill modifies licensing requirements for professions regulated by the DNR, specifically taxidermists and tree experts.

The bill impacts several licenses managed by the Motor Vehicle Administration (a modal administration of MDOT), including vehicle salesmen and driving instructors.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency

The bill modifies licensing requirements for several automotive-related professions, such as title service agents and driving instructors, which are directly regulated by the MVA.
The OAH may be required to adjudicate disputes or appeals related to the recognition of out-of-state licenses under these new provisions.
The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and boards that will be required to update their regulations and procedures to comply with this bill.
The bill modifies registration requirements for rehabilitation counselors and vocational evaluators, which fall under the purview of this commission.

bill_summary: This bill addresses perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal health conditions by expanding the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness and requiring health occupations boards to grant double continuing education credits for related training. It further mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission, the Maryland Commission for Women, and the Maryland Department of Health evaluate and report on health insurance coverage barriers, state policy initiatives, and clinical education opportunities for these conditions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Health Care Commission, Maryland Commission for Women, and Maryland Health Occupations Boards
stakeholders: Healthcare providers, patients experiencing menopausal conditions, and Maryland state health and regulatory agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not provided in the text. However, the bill creates administrative mandates for the Maryland Department of Health, the Maryland Health Care Commission, and the Maryland Commission for Women to conduct evaluations and produce reports, which will likely lead to increased operational costs. Additionally, health occupations boards will incur administrative impacts to implement new continuing education standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department of Health (MDH) evaluate clinical education methods, develop an action plan for community health workers, and consult with the Maryland Health Care Commission on insurance coverage evaluations. Furthermore, MDH oversees the health occupations boards that must now grant specific continuing education credits for menopause-related training.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to evaluate insurance coverage and barriers for perimenopausal, menopausal, and postmenopausal conditions and submit a report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness. It also assigns specific evaluation and reporting duties to the Maryland Commission for Women and requires consultation with the State Community Health Worker Advisory Committee.

The Maryland Insurance Administration is named as a required consultee for the Maryland Health Care Commission's evaluation of insurance coverage, hormone replacement therapy, and preauthorization barriers.

The Department of Health must consult with institutions of higher education to evaluate methods for increasing clinical and postgraduate education opportunities regarding menopausal evaluation and treatment.

As a primary provider of medical and clinical education in the state, USM institutions are likely to be consulted by the Department of Health regarding the expansion of clinical education for perimenopausal and menopausal conditions.

The Secretary of Aging is a permanent member of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, which is being expanded and modified by this bill. Additionally, the subject matter is highly relevant to the older adult population served by the department.
The Secretary of Disabilities is a permanent member of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, the membership of which is altered by this bill.
The State Superintendent of Schools is a permanent member of the State Advisory Council on Health and Wellness, the membership of which is altered by this bill.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the various health occupations boards and the Department of Health as they implement new regulatory requirements for continuing education and council membership.

As an institution of higher education with public health and medical programs, Morgan State University may be consulted by the Department of Health regarding clinical education methods for menopausal conditions.

Synopsis: Establishing for a Sheriff of Anne Arundel County vesting rights in the Employees' Pension System after accruing at least 8 years of eligibility service; and establishing that a Sheriff of Anne Arundel County elected or appointed on or after July 1, 2026, may retire with a normal service retirement allowance from the Employees' Pension System if the individual is at least 65 years old and has at least 8 years of eligibility service.

bill_summary: This bill establishes vesting rights for the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County in the Employees' Pension System after eight years of eligibility service. It also allows an individual elected or appointed as the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County on or after July 1, 2026, to retire with a normal service retirement allowance at age 65 with at least 8 years of service or when the sum of their age and service years equals at least 90.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency and the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: The Sheriff of Anne Arundel County
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill results in a negligible increase in State pension liabilities and has no discernible effect on State pension contributions because the provisions apply to a very limited number of cases. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary agency responsible for the administration and management of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), including the Employees’ Pension System (EPS). This bill directly alters the vesting and retirement eligibility requirements for the Sheriff of Anne Arundel County, a specific member within the system they manage.

The Department of Budget and Management is the state's principal personnel and fiscal agency, overseeing state employee benefits and policies. As the agency responsible for long-term fiscal planning and managing state personnel resources, the bill's changes to pension vesting rules fall under its broad personnel policy and fiscal oversight mandate.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Retirement Agency. They would be responsible for ensuring the legislative changes to the State Personnel and Pensions Article are correctly interpreted and implemented in accordance with state and constitutional law.

The Board of Public Works, composed of the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees the state’s fiscal integrity. While the fiscal impact is negligible, changes to state pension liabilities and benefit structures are matters of fiscal policy relevant to the Board’s oversight of state expenditures.

As the state's chief financial officer and a member of the Board of Public Works, the Comptroller is relevant to any legislation impacting state financial obligations, including pension benefits and the administrative processes of the state's financial agencies.

The State Treasurer acts as the chief financial agency and is a member of the Board of Public Works. The office is involved in the management of state funds and the protection of state property, making pension-related financial changes relevant to its broad fiscal responsibilities.

The Governor oversees the executive branch, proposes the state budget, and signs legislation into law. Changes to the pension system for constitutional officers like a County Sheriff require executive approval and affect the administration of state-mandated benefits.

Synopsis: Altering the penalty for storing or leaving a loaded firearm in a location where the person knew or should have known that an unsupervised minor has access to the firearm to include the possibility of imprisonment not exceeding 5 years.

Status: In the House - Hearing 3/11 at 2:00 p.m.

Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth

bill_summary: This bill increases the penalty for storing or leaving a loaded firearm in a location where the owner knew or should have known an unsupervised minor could gain access. It changes the existing penalty from a maximum fine of $1,000 to a misdemeanor punishable by up to five years in prison, a fine of up to $1,000, or both.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Firearm owners in Maryland, unsupervised minors, law enforcement agencies, and the Maryland judicial and correctional systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates a potential minimal increase in State general fund expenditures due to the new five-year maximum incarceration penalty. Local governments may also experience a minimal increase in revenues from fines and expenditures for incarceration, though specific dollar estimates were not provided as the impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees the implementation of criminal law changes and policy initiatives related to public safety and child welfare.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state and represents Maryland in criminal appeals, which may increase if more severe penalties for firearm storage result in contested convictions.
DBM is responsible for the state's fiscal planning and budget execution; it would monitor the potential increase in general fund expenditures identified in the fiscal note.
The bill includes an exception for minors who possess a certificate of firearm and hunter safety issued under the Natural Resources Article, which is managed by this department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill significantly increases the penalty from a fine to a possible five-year prison sentence. DPSCS would be responsible for the incarceration and supervision (parole/probation) of individuals convicted under the revised law.
As the primary state law enforcement agency, MSP is responsible for enforcing firearm-related criminal laws and protecting public safety.
The office is dedicated to the well-being of Maryland's children; this bill directly addresses policy regarding the safety of minors in the presence of loaded firearms.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, advising the Governor on policies like those addressed in this bill.
The Judiciary is responsible for the adjudication of these misdemeanor cases. Increasing the penalty to include jail time may increase the complexity and duration of court proceedings.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The introduction of a possible five-year prison sentence triggers the requirement for OPD to provide legal representation for indigent defendants, whereas a fine-only penalty might not have required their involvement in the same way.

Synopsis: Establishing consumer protections related to health care financing, including disclosure and refund requirements; prohibiting health care providers and certain agents of health care providers from offering, obtaining, applying for, or assisting in applying for certain financing; prohibiting a health care provider from promoting certain financing to certain patients or billing a certain financier before a certain number of days prior to a procedure; etc.
Title: Commercial Law - Consumer Protections - Health Care Financing
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Economic Matters; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes consumer protections for patients using third-party financing for health care services. It requires health care providers (excluding hospitals) and veterinarians to provide patients with written disclosures and treatment plans before discussing financing options and mandates refunds for unprovided services within 15 days. The bill prohibits providers from applying for financing on a patient's behalf, promoting financing to patients while they are under the influence of substances or undergoing treatment, or billing financiers more than 30 days before services are rendered. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Health care providers (excluding hospitals), licensed veterinarians, and patients seeking or using third-party financing for medical or veterinary services.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text. The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General is responsible for preparing disclosure forms and enforcing the provisions of the bill, which may increase administrative expenditures. State revenue may increase indeterminately through civil penalties assessed for violations under the Consumer Protection Act.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General to prepare and publish a mandatory health care financing disclosure form. Additionally, the Attorney General is authorized to adopt regulations to carry out the subtitle, and violations of the bill are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act enforced by the OAG.

The bill regulates 'health care providers' defined as individuals licensed under the Health Occupations Article, which is overseen by the Department. It also requires providers to disclose whether treatment is covered by Maryland Medicaid (the Maryland Health Care Assistance Program), which is administered by the Department of Health.

The bill's definition of 'health care provider' explicitly includes veterinarians licensed under Title 2, Subtitle 3 of the Agriculture Article, placing them under the new consumer protection and financing disclosure requirements.

As an agency responsible for promoting informed decision-making and providing accurate information regarding the cost of health services to the public, the MHCC is relevant to the bill's requirements for written treatment plans and cost transparency in financing.

The bill establishes new consumer rights, disclosure requirements, and refund mandates. Violations create grounds for civil litigation and the application of Consumer Protection Act penalties, which would be processed through the Maryland Judicial Branch.

Violations of the health care financing subtitle may lead to administrative enforcement actions or contested cases regarding professional licenses for health care providers and veterinarians, which are typically adjudicated by the OAH.

Synopsis: Requiring units of State government proposing certain capital projects to complete a certain community engagement plan and certain community outreach activities and submit a certain report to the Department of Budget and Management; and requiring the Department to annually submit a compiled report, beginning December 1, 2027, of the community engagement and outreach reports submitted by each unit of State government proposing a covered project to certain governing bodies, the General Assembly, and the Legislative Policy Committee.
Title: State Capital Program - Covered Projects - Public Engagement and Community Outreach Requirements (Community Engagement and Outreach Act of 2026)

bill_summary: The Community Engagement and Outreach Act of 2026 requires Maryland State agencies proposing capital projects exceeding $2,000,000 in cost or 75 feet in height to conduct specific community engagement and outreach. Agencies must create engagement plans, provide mailed notices to all residents and businesses within a one-mile radius, hold public meetings with virtual options, and offer a 30-day public comment period. The bill also mandates annual reporting on these activities to the Department of Budget and Management, which will compile the data for the General Assembly and local governments.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Budget and Management and State units proposing capital projects
stakeholders: Residents, businesses, and community organizations located within one mile of a State capital project footprint; State agencies; and local governing bodies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures across all funds may increase significantly, potentially exceeding $20,000,000 annually starting in FY 2027. This impact includes estimated costs of $10,600,000 for the State Highway Administration and $10,000,000 for the Maryland Transportation Authority to manage consultant services and outreach requirements. Individual project costs may also increase due to delays and inflation, though total capital expenditure limits remain fixed by the state budget. Local government expenditures may increase for projects requiring local matching funds if delays occur.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates DBM as the central oversight agency, requiring it to adopt regulations, receive community engagement reports from all other state units, and submit a compiled annual report to the General Assembly and local governing bodies.

As the state's primary operational support agency for the construction and maintenance of state-owned facilities, DGS will be responsible for implementing these engagement and outreach requirements for the numerous capital projects it manages.

MDOT oversees several modal administrations that propose massive capital projects (transportation facilities) that meet the criteria of 'covered projects,' including roads, transit centers, and port improvements.
The fiscal note explicitly identifies SHA as being significantly impacted, estimating $10.6 million in annual costs to manage community outreach for approximately 106 covered projects per year.

The MDTA is identified in the fiscal note as potentially incurring up to $10 million in annual non-budgeted expenditures to satisfy the bill's community outreach requirements for its toll facility projects.
The fiscal note identifies the MSA as needing to hire additional program managers and incurring significant mailing and consultant costs to coordinate community meetings for its capital projects.

The fiscal note mentions that USM institutions will face increased expenditures because the bill's requirements are more extensive than their current community notification policies for capital projects.
BPW approves significant state capital projects and contracts; the community engagement reports required by this bill would likely inform or be part of the documentation for project approval.
MDH proposes and manages significant capital projects for health facilities and hospitals that would qualify as 'covered projects' under the bill's cost and impact criteria.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees correctional facilities and pretrial centers, many of which involve capital projects exceeding $2 million that would require the new outreach procedures.
DNR manages extensive public lands and state parks, and its capital projects for environmental facilities or infrastructure would be subject to the bill's community outreach mandates.
MSP proposes capital projects for police barracks and aviation command centers that frequently meet the $2 million threshold for covered projects.
As a state agency that proposes its own capital projects independently, Morgan State would be required to perform community outreach and reporting for any project exceeding the bill's thresholds.
As an independent state agency, the college would be subject to the bill's requirements for any major capital projects on its campus that exceed the specified cost or height thresholds.
DJS operates residential facilities and secure centers that involve significant capital projects requiring community engagement under the bill's guidelines.
The bill explicitly includes 'environmental facilities' in the definition of covered projects, making MDE responsible for the new outreach requirements for its major infrastructure projects.
MES manages and operates water, wastewater, and solid waste capital projects for various clients, many of which would qualify as 'covered projects' requiring outreach and reporting.
IAC oversees state-funded public school construction projects; while some grants are excluded, major 'public building' projects overseen by IAC may be subject to the bill's requirements.
MTA's development of transportation facilities, such as rail lines and transit stations, are specifically named as covered projects in the bill.
MAA's infrastructure projects at BWI and Martin State Airport would likely meet the criteria for covered projects based on cost, height, and potential community impact.
MPA's capital projects related to marine terminals and port infrastructure are transportation facilities that fall under the scope of this legislation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain carriers and managed care organizations from prohibiting an enrollee from selecting, or limiting the ability of an enrollee to select, a laboratory; prohibiting certain carriers and managed care organizations from denying a laboratory the right to participate in the health benefit plan if the laboratory agrees to comply with certain terms; and prohibiting certain carriers and managed care organizations from imposing additional copayments, fees, or conditions for laboratory services provided to an enrollee.
Title: Health Insurance and Managed Care Organizations - Laboratory Services - Contract Providers
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/19 at 2:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: This bill prohibits health insurance carriers and Medicaid managed care organizations from restricting an enrollee's choice of laboratory if the laboratory is a contract provider. It requires carriers to allow any laboratory to participate in their network if the laboratory agrees to the plan's terms, conditions, and reimbursement rates. Additionally, the bill prohibits carriers from imposing extra copayments, fees, or conditions on enrollees for laboratory services provided by a contract provider.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Health insurance enrollees, Medicaid recipients, health insurance carriers, Medicaid managed care organizations, and laboratory service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2027 due to $125 rate and form filing fees. Medicaid expenditures (50% general funds, 50% federal funds) may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2027, as the requirement to accept any willing laboratory provider may necessitate an increase in managed care organization capitation rates. Federal fund revenues would increase to match the 50% federal share of Medicaid costs. The State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and local governments are not expected to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Insurance Article (15-112(y)) prohibiting carriers from limiting an enrollee's choice of laboratory and requiring an 'any willing provider' standard for laboratory contracts. As the primary regulator of Maryland's insurance market, the MIA is responsible for enforcing these provisions and reviewing the rate and form filings mentioned in the fiscal note.

The bill specifically amends the Health-General Article to apply the new laboratory provider requirements to Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs). The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Medicaid program and oversees MCOs, and the fiscal note indicates a potential indeterminate increase in Medicaid expenditures due to impacts on MCO capitation rates.

As the administrator of Maryland's health insurance marketplace (Maryland Health Connection), the Exchange oversees the private health plans (qualified health plans) offered to residents. These plans must comply with the bill's new contracting and coverage requirements for laboratory services.

DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Although the fiscal note suggests the impact may not be material, the bill's changes to provider network rules for carriers could potentially affect the administration and costs of the state's health insurance plans.

The MHCC is responsible for health system planning and improving access to care. The bill's mandate to allow any willing laboratory to join a provider network directly impacts health system dynamics, provider access, and the analysis of healthcare costs and quality which the Commission monitors.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel for the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health. They would be responsible for providing legal advice on the implementation and enforcement of the new laboratory service regulations and defending against any potential legal challenges from carriers.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note identifies a potential meaningful impact on small businesses. Small laboratory providers in Maryland may benefit from the 'any willing provider' provision, which prohibits carriers and MCOs from denying them the right to participate in networks if they meet standard terms.

bill_summary: This bill expands eligibility for the Homestead Property Tax Credit in Washington County to include 'additional residences' that do not serve as the homeowner's principal residence. It removes the 'only one' dwelling limitation and strikes provisions that previously disqualified homeowners from claiming the credit on multiple properties, provided the additional residences are located in Washington County.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Homeowners in Washington County with additional residential properties, the Washington County government, and municipal governments within Washington County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The expansion of the Homestead Property Tax Credit to non-principal residences in Washington County is expected to result in a decrease in property tax revenues for the State, Washington County, and local municipalities. By capping the growth of taxable assessments on a larger pool of properties, the bill reduces the potential property tax base. Specific dollar estimates of the revenue loss are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included with the provided bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board is the primary body responsible for hearing disputes regarding property tax assessments and credits. This bill creates a new eligibility category for the homestead property tax credit in Washington County, which will directly impact the volume and nature of appeals handled by the local boards.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court adjudicates appeals from the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board. The expansion of the homestead property tax credit in Washington County will involve the Court in resolving complex disputes regarding the new 'additional residence' definition.

As the state's chief financial officer, the Comptroller is responsible for the oversight of state revenues and enforcement of tax laws. Changes to property tax credits affect the overall state revenue structure, specifically the state portion of the property tax which supports the State Annuity Bond Fund.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for revenue estimation and fiscal planning. Expanding tax credit eligibility results in a fiscal impact that must be accounted for in state revenue projections and budget execution.

The bill includes specific provisions and definitions regarding agricultural ownership entities and homesites on land receiving agricultural use assessments. These changes directly affect how agricultural property owners in Washington County manage their residences and tax liabilities.

The Rural Maryland Council addresses the unique economic and quality-of-life challenges in rural counties. This bill is geographically targeted at Washington County, a rural jurisdiction, and modifies its property tax landscape to provide relief to residents.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies on the implementation of new laws. They would be involved in interpreting the statutory expansion of the Homestead Property Tax Credit and ensuring new definitions meet constitutional and legal standards.

The bill specifies procedures involving the recordation of deeds with the Clerk of the Circuit Court and sets deadlines for these recordings to qualify for the tax credit. The Judiciary's administrative arm oversees these local court functions.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the annual budget. This bill modifies state tax policy and has a fiscal impact on state revenues, requiring coordination with the Governor's policy and budget priorities.

Synopsis: Allowing a credit against the State income tax for 25% of an investment made in qualified Maryland companies up to $1,000,000; providing that investments in companies engaging in certain emergent technology may qualify for the tax credit subject to certain requirements; providing that a qualified investor shall make an investment in a qualified Maryland company within a certain amount of time after the Department issues an initial tax credit certificate; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Angel Investor Tax Credit to incentivize investments in early-stage Maryland companies specializing in emergent technologies, specifically artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and cybersecurity. It creates the Angel Investor Tax Credit Reserve Fund and allows qualified investors to claim a state income tax credit equal to 25% of their investment, up to $1,000,000 per investment.
stakeholders: Individual and entity investors, early-stage technology companies in Maryland specializing in AI, quantum computing, or cybersecurity, and the Maryland Department of Commerce.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation of at least $25,000,000 to the Angel Investor Tax Credit Reserve Fund in the annual budget bill. As tax credits are certified, the Comptroller transfers funds from the Reserve Fund to the General Fund to offset revenue losses. Administrative costs for the Department of Commerce are also paid from the Reserve Fund. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are unavailable, but the bill text explicitly establishes this $25,000,000 annual spending mandate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the primary agency responsible for administering the Angel Investor Tax Credit program, including reviewing and approving applications from both investors and companies, issuing tax credit certificates, and conducting outreach to stakeholders.

The Comptroller is responsible for processing the tax credits, receiving notifications of certificates, managing the transfer of funds from the Reserve Fund to the General Fund, and jointly adopting regulations with the Department of Commerce.
The Treasurer is mandated to manage, invest, and reinvest the money within the newly established Angel Investor Tax Credit Reserve Fund, ensuring that interest earnings accrue back to the Fund.
DBM is responsible for state budget development and revenue estimation. This bill requires a mandatory annual budget appropriation of at least $25 million for the tax credit reserve fund.
The bill requires the Governor to include a specific minimum appropriation in the annual budget bill and oversees the executive department (Commerce) tasked with the program's implementation.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Commerce and the Comptroller, particularly in the drafting and adoption of regulations required to implement and monitor the tax credit program.

As a major network of institutions of higher education, the University System of Maryland is a designated target for outreach by the Department of Commerce regarding the investment opportunities in emergent technologies.
Morgan State University is an institution of higher education explicitly identified as a target for outreach to connect emergent technology research and development with angel investors.
Saint Mary's College is an institution of higher education identified as a target for Department of Commerce outreach efforts related to the new tax credit program.
The Tax Court may be involved in adjudicating appeals from investors or companies regarding the revocation of tax credit certifications or disputes over recaptured credits.

Synopsis: Requiring provider agencies to pay at least $17 per hour to personal care aides and to provide a certain notice regarding the wage to personal care aides; and requiring provider agencies to provide personal care aides with a certain minimum amount of earned sick and safe leave.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program - Provider Agencies - Wages and Leave for Personal Care Aides

Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires provider agencies that receive reimbursement from the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) to pay personal care aides a minimum wage of $17 per hour and provide at least 24 hours of paid earned sick and safe leave annually. It also mandates that the Maryland Department of Health monitor compliance and report on the feasibility of increasing the minimum wage to $20 per hour and ensuring that 80% of Medicaid payments are directed toward aide compensation.
stakeholders: Personal care aides, provider agencies reimbursed by the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (excluding those under the Developmental Disabilities Administration), and the Maryland Department of Health.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill mandates a $17 per hour minimum wage and paid sick leave for personal care aides, which will likely result in increased expenditures for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program. However, specific total dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) as it mandates new wage and leave requirements for provider agencies reimbursed by the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which MDH administers. MDH is responsible for monitoring compliance, taking enforcement actions such as program suspension or termination, and submitting a report to the General Assembly regarding Medicaid payment allocations and future wage increases.

The bill establishes specific wage floors and sick and safe leave requirements for personal care aides, which are matters typically regulated by the Department of Labor. Furthermore, the bill explicitly amends the Labor and Employment Article to resolve potential conflicts between these new requirements and existing state sick and safe leave laws.

The requirement for provider agencies to pay a minimum wage of $17 per hour for Medicaid-reimbursable services will likely necessitate an increase in Medicaid provider reimbursement rates. As the principal fiscal agency, DBM will be responsible for managing the significant budgetary impact and fiscal planning required to fund these state-mandated wage increases.

The personal care services impacted by this bill (such as Community First Choice and Community Options) are essential for Maryland's older adults. The Department of Aging oversees long-term care advocacy and support for this population, and changes to the workforce and reimbursement structure for these services directly affect their mission and the quality of care for their constituents.

The bill affects the delivery of home- and community-based services that are vital to individuals with disabilities. bill_summary: The Pregnancy Outcome Protection Act prohibits the investigation, civil liability, or criminal prosecution of individuals for experiencing a pregnancy loss, including miscarriages, stillbirths, and self-managed abortions. It also protects healthcare providers from liability for supporting patients in these circumstances and restricts the disclosure of medical records related to pregnancy loss. Additionally, the bill establishes that pregnancy loss does not constitute probable cause for a search warrant and allows for a private right of action and criminal penalties against those who violate these protections.
stakeholders: Individuals who experience pregnancy loss, healthcare providers, doulas, and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not available. As a primary law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police is considered an 'investigating entity' under the bill. The legislation explicitly restricts law enforcement's ability to investigate pregnancy loss, obtain search warrants related to it, and subjects them to civil liability and criminal penalties for violations.

It would be responsible for advising investigating entities (such as DHS and DJS) on compliance with this act and representing the state in civil or criminal appeals related to pregnancy loss investigations.

MDH is responsible for setting health policy and overseeing the conduct of health care institutions and practitioners impacted by these new reporting and liability prohibitions.

It places specific legal prohibitions on their ability to investigate individuals for pregnancy loss, impacting their operational procedures in cases of potential neglect or abuse.

bill_summary: This emergency bill establishes a methodology for determining the Consumer Price Index (CPI) value for October 2025, which was not published by the federal government due to a shutdown. No effect on revenues is expected.

As the oversight body for Maryland's public education system, the Department of Education has a regulatory interest in the governance and membership structure of local boards of education.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references the Baltimore County School Board Nominating Commission, which is tasked with providing the list of nominees to the Governor for the board's appointed positions.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and state agencies regarding the legal framework and implementation of statutory changes to public boards.
The Secretary of State is the custodian of official records and processes the commissions for individuals appointed by the Governor to the board.

Synopsis: Increasing the minimum population threshold for municipal incorporation to 600 residents; requiring a certain organizing committee to make certain determinations and provide a certain report to the county commissioners or county council of a certain county regarding a proposed municipal incorporation; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the minimum population required to incorporate a new municipality from 300 to 600 residents. It requires an organizing committee to provide comprehensive reports to the county government regarding the fiscal effects, expected services, and potential adverse economic impacts of incorporation. If a referendum request is signed by at least 40% of the registered voters in the area proposed for incorporation, the county commissioners or council must approve the request and schedule a vote for the next general election.
responsible_party: County Commissioners, County Councils, Municipal Organizing Committees, and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Residents and registered voters in unincorporated areas, county governments, and organizing committees seeking municipal incorporation.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the text. However, the bill creates administrative impacts for counties, which must verify petitions, host reports on their websites, and potentially conduct mandatory referendums. The bill also requires organizing committees to conduct fiscal analyses comparing projected expenditures to local income tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Office of the Attorney General to create a standard petition form for use by organizing communities seeking municipal incorporation and to provide this form to county boards of elections.

The bill involves county boards of elections in the distribution of incorporation petition forms and requires that mandatory referendums for municipal incorporation be held during the next general election, which is overseen by the State Board of Elections.

As the agency responsible for providing technical assistance and policy guidance to local governments regarding land use and sustainable growth, the Department of Planning is relevant to the processes of forming new municipal boundaries and governance structures.

The bill requires organizing committees to report on projected local income tax revenue as part of the incorporation process; the Comptroller is responsible for the collection and distribution of these tax revenues to local jurisdictions.

The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for government records, including municipal charters; successful incorporations under this bill would result in new legislative records for the Archives to preserve and make accessible.

Synopsis: Establishing a Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures to study and evaluate the revenue structure of the county and municipal governments within the State; and requiring the Task Force to submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures
Status: Approved by the Governor - Chapter 17

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures to evaluate the current revenue-raising capabilities of Maryland's local governments, explore untapped revenue sources, and analyze the impact of potential new revenue streams on the cost of living.
stakeholders: County and municipal governments, Maryland taxpayers, and the Department of Legislative Services
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal state fiscal impact. The Department of Legislative Services (DLS) is responsible for staffing the task force and can likely do so using existing budgeted resources. While significant administrative or research demands could lead to additional general fund expenditures for contractual staff, such costs are not currently estimated. Reimbursements for task force members are assumed to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller or their designee is a named member of the Task Force. As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the agency is central to any study of revenue structures and tax laws.
The Secretary of Budget and Management or their designee is a named member of the Task Force. DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for state budget and revenue estimation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new Task Force to Modernize County and Municipal Revenue Structures, which falls under this collective entity of advisory bodies.
The Task Force is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor, and it involves the participation of executive branch department heads.

Local revenue structures frequently involve development impact fees, excise taxes, and land-use assessments, which are integral to the Department of Planning's mission to promote sustainable growth and infrastructure development.

Property tax is the largest locally generated revenue source for counties and municipalities. The Task Force's evaluation of these revenue structures directly relates to the board's role in reviewing property tax assessment disputes.
Changes to local revenue structures can impact the state's economic competitiveness and business environment, which the Department of Commerce is tasked with monitoring.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the state agencies and officials serving on the Task Force and would advise on the legal authority of local governments to implement new revenue sources.
As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Tax Court is impacted by policy recommendations that could change the structure or implementation of local taxes.
The Council advocates for the interests of Maryland's 18 rural counties, which face unique challenges in their revenue structures and tax bases that the Task Force will evaluate.

The Task Force is specifically required to analyze the impact of revenue sources on the overall affordability of goods and services and the cost of living, which aligns with the Innovation Team's focus on economic mobility.
The Task Force's goal is to modernize and evaluate the efficiency of government revenue structures, aligning with GOPI's mandate to enhance the efficiency and accountability of government operations.

Synopsis: Prohibiting, for a certain period of time, the Chief Medical Examiner, deputy chief medical examiners, assistant medical examiners, and pathologists authorized by the Chief Medical Examiner from using a hydrostatic lung test, also known as a lung float test, if performing a certain perinatal autopsy; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to report, by December 1, 2027, to certain committees of the General Assembly on the usefulness and efficacy of the hydrostatic lung test and certain recommendations.
Title: Public Health - Office of the Chief Medical Examiner - Perinatal Autopsies (Lung Float Test Ban)
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/26 at 1:00 p.m.

Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner from using the hydrostatic lung test, also known as a lung float test, during perinatal autopsies for a period of two years. Additionally, it requires the Maryland Department of Health to conduct a study and report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2027, regarding the efficacy and necessity of the test as an autopsy tool.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner
stakeholders: Parents and legal representatives of deceased infants, medical examiners, and authorized pathologists.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures will increase by $35,700 in FY 2027 and $18,000 in FY 2028. These costs are for hiring a part-time contractual health policy analyst to complete the mandated report on the lung float test's efficacy. The bill has no impact on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primarily affects the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, which is a unit within the Department of Health. Furthermore, the Secretary of Health is responsible for reviewing autopsy findings and referring appeals to the Office of Administrative Hearings. The Department is also mandated to lead a study and submit a report on the efficacy of the lung float test, resulting in a direct fiscal impact of $53,700 over two fiscal years.

The bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to consult with the Office of the Attorney General on the mandated report. Additionally, the Attorney General's Office would be responsible for representing the Chief Medical Examiner and other state pathologists in any civil actions authorized by the bill for violations of the lung float test ban.

The bill updates provisions in the Health - General Article that require the Secretary of Health to refer appeals concerning medical examiner findings and conclusions on cause and manner of death to the Office of Administrative Hearings.

The bill authorizes parents, guardians, or legal representatives to bring civil actions for violations of the lung float test ban and allows for the appeal of administrative decisions to circuit courts of competent jurisdiction, impacting court caseloads and judicial administration.

The bill modifies the Public Safety Article to require law enforcement agencies to reopen or reinvestigate death investigations if a medical examiner's findings are amended to undetermined or homicide, directly impacting the operations of the State's primary law enforcement agency.

As the principal fiscal and personnel agency, the Department of Budget and Management will oversee the allocation of general funds and the creation of the part-time contractual health policy analyst position required by the Maryland Department of Health to fulfill the bill's reporting mandate.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "adjusted actual income" under the State child support guidelines.
Title: Child Support - Adjusted Actual Income - Definition
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/26 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill modifies the definition of adjusted actual income used in the Maryland child support guidelines. It specifies that the allowance for supporting a child living in a parent's home (who is not the subject of the current support order) applies if that child spends more than 25% of their overnights, which must be at least 92 overnights, in that parent's home.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Parents with child support obligations and their children living in the household.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, this bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and legal support to the judicial branch, where judges and magistrates apply the state's child support guidelines to establish and modify awards.

The Department of Human Services is the primary agency responsible for child support services in Maryland, and its local departments must utilize these guidelines for administrative calculations and enforcement actions.
This office leads efforts to reduce child poverty and improve family well-being, goals that are directly influenced by the economic support levels established through child support guidelines.

The Innovation Team is charged with piloting initiatives to reduce child poverty and enhance economic mobility, making the technical adjustment of child support calculations relevant to their policy focus.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Human Services and its Child Support Enforcement Administration regarding the interpretation and enforcement of family law.
The Governor's Office coordinates executive policy initiatives and oversees the agencies responsible for the administration of family law and child support services.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law relating to the confidentiality of juvenile police records and court records do not prohibit access to and confidential use of certain records by the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement, the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Children and Family Success, and the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of African American Male Engagement under certain circumstances; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes three specific Baltimore City Mayor’s offices—the Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement, the Office of Children and Family Success, and the Office of African American Male Engagement—to access and confidentially use juvenile police and court records when providing programs or services to a child. The offices are permitted to use these records for developing treatment plans and are held liable for any unauthorized disclosure of the information.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Mayor's Office (specifically the Office of Neighborhood Safety and Engagement, the Office of Children and Family Success, and the Office of African American Male Engagement)
stakeholders: Juveniles in Baltimore City receiving services, the Baltimore City Mayor's Office, the Department of Juvenile Services, and Maryland law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill establishes potential legal liability for the specified Baltimore City offices in the event of unauthorized record releases, which could result in future expenditures, alongside minor administrative costs for managing record access.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Juvenile Services is the primary state agency responsible for managing juvenile records and providing services to youth in the justice system. The bill specifically authorizes the sharing of juvenile records with Baltimore City offices, often in conjunction with DJS, and mentions DJS liability for certain record releases.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides operational and technological support for the judicial branch. This bill directly modifies access and confidentiality rules for juvenile court records managed by the court system.

The Maryland State Police is the primary law enforcement agency that maintains and regulates access to criminal police records. This bill establishes exceptions to the confidentiality of juvenile police records for specific local government offices.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office serves as the state's coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, including juvenile delinquency. The local Baltimore City offices mentioned in the bill (MONSE) directly overlap with the policy goals and coordination efforts of GOCPP.

The bill focuses on the Baltimore City Mayor's Office of Children and Family Success and the provision of services to youth. The Governor's Office for Children oversees statewide efforts to improve the well-being of children and coordinate support networks, aligning with the bill's subject matter.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies regarding the implementation of state laws. This bill involves complex privacy, confidentiality, and liability issues related to juvenile records that would require legal interpretation and guidance.

The Department of Human Services is currently listed in the statute as having access to juvenile court records for specific treatment and funding purposes. The bill adds new entities to this framework of authorized access.

The Maryland Department of Health is currently authorized to access juvenile records when providing coordinated care with DJS. The bill expands access to local city offices for similar service-delivery purposes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is mentioned in the bill's existing statutory sections regarding the transition of juvenile records and access by the Division of Parole and Probation or the Division of Correction.
The bill references Section 7-303 of the Education Article, which governs the disclosure of criminal and juvenile records to local school systems and officials.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from committing a crime of violence while the person is in a medical facility or a place of worship; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a felony and on conviction is subject to imprisonment of up to 10 years.
Title: Crime of Violence - Medical Facilities and Places of Worship - Penalty (Sacred Places Safety Act)
