bill_summary: This bill requires manufacturers of motor vehicles and farm equipment to provide owners and independent repair facilities with the same diagnostic and repair information, tools, and documentation they provide to authorized dealers. It mandates that motor vehicle manufacturers install standardized open data platforms for telematics systems starting with the 2025 model year and prohibits farm equipment manufacturers from withholding part numbers from customers. Violation of these requirements is classified as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice.
responsible_party: Division of Consumer Protection of the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Motor vehicle and farm equipment manufacturers, authorized dealers, independent repair facilities, and owners of motor vehicles and farm equipment.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Fiscal Note indicates that the bill has no material impact on State or local government finances or operations, as the Office of the Attorney General can implement the requirements using existing resources. While there is no major government fiscal impact, the bill is expected to have a meaningful economic impact on small businesses, specifically benefiting independent repair facilities while potentially increasing competition for authorized dealers.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the Division of Consumer Protection within the Office of the Attorney General to develop a disclosure document explaining telematics systems and consumer rights. Additionally, the OAG is responsible for enforcing the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, under which violations of this bill are categorized.

The bill establishes a new 'Farm Equipment Repair' subtitle, which directly impacts the agricultural community by requiring manufacturers to provide diagnostic tools and documentation to farmers and independent repairers to ensure the economic viability of farming.

The bill defines key terms by referencing the Transportation Article and regulates the relationship between motor vehicle manufacturers, dealers, and owners, all of whom fall under the MVA's regulatory and licensing oversight.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT has a high-level interest in regulations affecting motor vehicle standards, telematics systems, and the maintenance of the state's transportation fleet.

The bill affects the competitive landscape for businesses in Maryland by granting independent repair facilities access to proprietary information and tools, which impacts the economic growth of small businesses and the operations of large manufacturers.

The 'Farm Equipment Repair' provisions are highly relevant to the council's mission to address challenges in rural counties, specifically those related to agricultural sustainability and the ability of rural residents to maintain essential machinery.

Synopsis: Requiring the Interagency Commission on School Construction to distribute funds to public charter schools for capital improvements to public charter school facilities;  beginning in fiscal year 2028, requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill an appropriation for the capital improvements to public charter school facilities that is equal to the total aggregate student enrollment in the Maryland Public Charter School Program for the prior fiscal year multiplied by $200; etc.
Title: Maryland Public Charter School Program - School Facilities - Funding
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Public Debt -see also- County & Balt City Bonds; State Bonds
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires the Interagency Commission on School Construction to distribute state funds directly to public charter schools for facility-related costs, including capital improvements, debt service, rent, or lease payments. To qualify, a charter school must have had an unqualified audit in the previous fiscal year. Beginning in fiscal year 2028, the Governor is required to include a mandated appropriation in the annual budget calculated by multiplying the total charter school enrollment from the prior year (excluding students in districts that have closed more than 50 schools since 2010) by $200.
stakeholders: Public charter schools and their students, particularly those in jurisdictions that have not closed more than 50 schools since 2010.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $116,835 in fiscal 2027 for administrative staffing and by an estimated $2.4 million annually beginning in fiscal 2028 to satisfy the bill's mandated appropriation. Federal fund revenues may potentially increase if the program enables the state to receive competitive federal charter school facility grants. There is no direct local fiscal impact as the funds are disbursed directly to charter schools rather than local school boards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Interagency Commission on School Construction (IAC) as the primary agency responsible for distributing funds to public charter schools, adopting regulations for the program, and receiving mandatory reports on capital improvement projects and expenditures.

As the agency overseeing the state's public education system, including charter schools, MSDE provides the student enrollment data and local school system information required to calculate the mandated per-pupil funding allocations. The bill also impacts educational facility planning.

The bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation beginning in FY 2028 and requires the hiring of additional personnel to manage the new grant program, both of which fall under DBM's oversight of the state budget and personnel resources.
The bill requires the Governor to include a specific mandated appropriation in the annual budget bill for charter school facility maintenance and operation, based on aggregate student enrollment.

The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state expenditures and capital project funding; the distribution of State funds directly to charter schools for capital improvements would fall under their administrative review.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the IAC and would be responsible for reviewing and approving the legal sufficiency of the new regulations required by the bill.

The fiscal note indicates that the establishment of this state funding program may allow Maryland to apply for and receive competitive federal grant funding through the Charter Schools Program, which the GGO helps coordinate.

The bill requires charter schools to have an unqualified audit to receive funds and creates a new state-to-school funding stream; OLA is responsible for auditing the efficiency and fiscal compliance of state programs and school systems.

Synopsis: Requiring the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission, subject to specified limitations, to accept and consider applications for sports wagering facility licenses and mobile sports wagering licenses submitted before January 1, 2028.
Title: Sports Wagering - Licenses - Application Period
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill requires the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission to accept and consider applications for sports wagering facility licenses and mobile sports wagering licenses submitted before January 1, 2028, specifically encouraging applications from minority- and women-owned business entities.
stakeholders: Potential sports wagering facility and mobile sports wagering license applicants, including minority-owned and women-owned business entities and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill extends the application period for sports wagering licenses until January 1, 2028. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text; however, the extension is expected to result in an indeterminate increase in state revenue from license application fees and subsequent sports wagering taxes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency is the primary regulator for all commercial gaming, including sports wagering, and is responsible for ensuring compliance across the industry, making the extension of the license application period highly relevant to its oversight.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Sports Wagering Application Review Commission (SWARC), which is a legislative commission tasked with reviewing license applications, to extend its application window until 2028.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the commission to seek racial, ethnic, and gender diversity and to encourage minority business enterprises (MBEs) to apply for licenses, directly relating to this office's mission of monitoring socioeconomic procurement programs.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to state agencies, boards, and commissions, and would be responsible for advising SWARC and the Lottery & Gaming Control Agency on the legal requirements of the extended application process.

As the agency responsible for supervising budget execution and fiscal planning, DBM is relevant due to the potential administrative costs and revenue implications associated with extending the sports wagering license application timeline.

Synopsis: Authorizing motor vehicles that are registered in the State and were previously registered as Class L (historic) vehicles to be insured by certain specialty insurance policies; exempting motor vehicles that are registered in the State and were previously registered as Class L vehicles from the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program; and establishing a certain recurring fee on motor vehicles registered in the State that were previously registered as Class L vehicles and that are exempt from the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Vehicles Previously Registered as Historic Vehicles - Emissions Inspection and Insurance
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/27 at 1:30 p.m.

Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes motor vehicles with a model year of 2000 or later that were previously registered as Class L (historic) vehicles to be covered by specialty insurance policies (historic, show, or antique). It also exempts these specific vehicles from the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP) and instead requires them to pay a $30 biennial fee to the Motor Vehicle Administration.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation (Motor Vehicle Administration) and the Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners of motor vehicles from model year 2000 or later previously registered as historic vehicles, specialty vehicle insurance providers, and the Motor Vehicle Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are expected to decrease by a few hundred thousand dollars annually starting in FY 2027. This net decrease accounts for an estimated $396,000 annual loss in late fees and lost VEIP testing fees, which are only partially offset by a new $30 biennial fee (estimated at up to $926,700 total, or roughly $463,350 annually). Additionally, TTF expenditures are projected to increase by approximately $21,000 annually for mailing and notification costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and manages the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), which is directly impacted by the bill's revenue changes, including the loss of emissions testing fees and the creation of a new biennial fee.

MVA is the primary agency responsible for vehicle registration and the implementation of the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program (VEIP). The bill explicitly requires MVA to administer a new $30 fee and exempts a specific class of vehicles from its mandatory inspections.

MDE is responsible for jointly establishing and managing the state's emissions control program (VEIP) alongside the MVA to comply with the federal Clean Air Act. The bill's exemption of certain vehicles from emissions testing falls under its regulatory domain.

The bill authorizes certain vehicles to be covered by specialty historic, show, or antique vehicle insurance policies. As the regulator of the state's insurance market, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees the policy forms and compliance related to these types of insurance.

Synopsis: Defining, for purposes of collective bargaining in community colleges, the term "supervisory employee" to mean an employee who is authorized to hire, transfer, suspend, lay off, recall, promote, discharge, assign, reward, or discipline employees, direct employees for 50% of the employee's working hours, and address employee complaints; and excluding from the definition a department head or an employee in a comparable position or any faculty member below the level of assistant dean.
Title: Community Colleges - Collective Bargaining - Definition of Supervisory Employee
Status: In the Senate - Special Order until later today (Senator Hershey) Adopted

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill defines the term "supervisory employee" for the purpose of collective bargaining at Maryland community colleges, including Baltimore City Community College. It specifies that the definition does not include department heads, employees in comparable positions, or any faculty member below the level of assistant dean, thereby clarifying that these individuals are eligible to participate in collective bargaining.
responsible_party: Maryland Community Colleges and the Baltimore City Community College
stakeholders: Community college faculty, department heads, administrative staff, and community college governing boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to have a material fiscal impact on State or local expenditures or revenues. According to the fiscal note, department heads are already permitted to collectively bargain as faculty under current law, so the clarification provided by the bill does not change existing financial obligations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) is the primary agency responsible for overseeing collective bargaining, union elections, and labor disputes for public sector employees, including those at community colleges. The bill's definition of 'supervisory employee' directly affects PERB's determination of which employees are eligible for collective bargaining units.

As the state's regulatory and coordinating board for postsecondary education, the Commission establishes statewide policies for community colleges. Changes to collective bargaining eligibility for faculty and staff at these institutions fall within its policy oversight scope.

DBM is the central personnel agency for the state. Since Baltimore City Community College is a state agency, changes to the definition of employees eligible for collective bargaining impact state personnel policies and potentially the state's fiscal planning regarding employee compensation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Public Employee Relations Board and the Higher Education Commission, regarding the interpretation and enforcement of state labor and education laws.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. As the bill affects labor relations and the administration of state-funded or state-regulated higher education institutions, it aligns with the office's policy coordination role.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish and maintain a centralized caregiver resource webpage to support various types of caregivers in the state. The webpage must provide plain-language, easily accessible information and links to resources concerning children with disabilities, adults with chronic illness or behavioral health needs, and older adults, as well as health and wellness, financial assistance, and safety planning for caregivers.
stakeholders: Caregivers in Maryland, including parents of children with disabilities, individuals caring for family members with chronic illnesses or functional limitations, and minor or dependent caregivers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local governmental operations and finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary implementing agency, the Maryland Department of Health is responsible for developing, hosting, and maintaining the centralized caregiver resource webpage, and coordinating with other state entities as required by the bill.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to coordinate with the Department of Aging in the development of the webpage. The agency also manages related resources like the Maryland Access Point for long-term services and supports for older adults and their caregivers.

The bill explicitly names the State Department of Education as a coordinating partner for the webpage's development, specifically regarding information and school-based supports for children with disabilities and special health care needs.

The department is responsible for improving service delivery to Maryland residents with disabilities and their families. The bill's focus on resources for caregivers of individuals with disabilities directly aligns with this agency's mission and coordination role.

The fiscal note indicates that the Department of Human Services staffs the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which is responsible for coordinating statewide planning and handbooks for family caregiver support services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This category includes the Maryland Commission on Caregiving, which is specifically mentioned in the fiscal note as the entity responsible for coordinating statewide caregiver support and distributing handbooks for current services.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note highlights this agency as a coordinator for the Maryland Access Point (MAP) program. The bill's mandate for caregiver resources for individuals with functional limitations includes the population served by this office.

This agency provides support services to deaf and hard-of-hearing students and their families. It is a relevant resource for the 'educational and school-based supports' section of the caregiver webpage mandated by the bill.

The agency's focus on the well-being of Maryland's children and families, particularly those in underinvested communities, overlaps with the bill's requirement to provide resources for caregivers of children with disabilities and special health care needs.

DoIT is responsible for the state's IT strategy and infrastructure. The bill's requirements for a centralized webpage and specific considerations for data security and privacy when using technology to support caregiving fall under DoIT's technical oversight.

The agency oversees the Maryland State Library for the Blind and Print Disabled, which serves individuals with functional limitations and their caregivers, making it a relevant resource for the mandated webpage.

Caregivers for veterans with disabilities or chronic illnesses are included in the bill's broad definition of caregivers, making this agency a relevant partner for resource links and program information.

Synopsis: Requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to provide certain coverage for hormone-related care, including hormone therapy treatment for perimenopausal and menopausal symptoms; establishing certain requirements and prohibitions related to coverage for hormone-related care; requiring certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations to report to the Maryland Insurance Administration certain data related to hormone-related care; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Required Coverage - Hormone-Related Care
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/13 at 1:30 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers, including insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations, to provide coverage for medically necessary hormone-related care. This specifically includes hormone replacement therapy and related clinical services for perimenopausal and menopausal symptoms. The bill prohibits carriers from denying coverage based on age or specific diagnosis, and it restricts the use of administrative barriers like burdensome prior authorizations, step therapy, or higher cost-sharing for these treatments compared to other medical services. Carriers must also report annual data on claims and denials to the Maryland Insurance Administration.
stakeholders: Perimenopausal and menopausal individuals, Maryland residents requiring hormone-related therapies, health insurance carriers, and healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2027 due to a $125 rate and form filing fee per carrier. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Expenditures for local governments that purchase fully insured medical plans may increase if the mandate leads to higher insurance premiums. Specific total dollar estimates for the aggregate revenue increase or premium changes are not provided, though the impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of Maryland's insurance market, the MIA is responsible for enforcing the mandate, reviewing rate and form filings, adopting regulations, and submitting an annual summary report to the General Assembly regarding hormone-related care claims.

The MHBE administers the state's health insurance marketplace; the bill's fiscal note discusses the potential impact on the benchmark plan and the state's obligation to defray costs if mandates are expanded to the individual and small group markets.

DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; while the fiscal note indicates no immediate fiscal impact, the department monitors all health insurance mandates for their effect on state personnel benefits.

The department is responsible for setting health policy and protecting public health; the mandate for medically necessary hormone therapy for endocrine and reproductive conditions aligns with the department's oversight of healthcare access and quality.

The MHCC is responsible for health system planning and promoting informed decision-making; it frequently reviews and analyzes the impact of mandated health insurance benefits on the state's healthcare landscape.

The OAH adjudicates contested administrative cases for the Maryland Insurance Administration; disputes regarding the enforcement of this new mandate or carrier compliance would be heard by the office's administrative law judges.
The bill specifically addresses perimenopausal and menopausal care, which directly impacts the health and well-being of the older adult population and caregivers served by the department.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and would be involved in the drafting of regulations and any legal enforcement actions related to the new mandate.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and budget; it is relevant because of the potential future requirement for the state to defray the costs of new mandates under the Affordable Care Act.
Some hormone-related treatments, such as testosterone replacement therapy, involve controlled dangerous substances (CDS); the OCSA regulates the prescribing and dispensing of these medications.

Synopsis: Requiring the Office of the Attorney General to investigate certain grievances and mediate certain resolutions between the clients and providers of certain federal- and State-assisted housing programs; establishing procedures for the filing, review, and investigation of certain grievances; requiring the Office to inform a grievant of certain legal services and provide assistance to certain legal service providers in relationship to a grievance; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Office of the Attorney General to establish a grievance and mediation process for residents in federal and State-assisted housing programs. The Office will investigate complaints regarding housing conditions and lease violations, and it is authorized to take legal action against housing providers who violate housing laws or fail to cooperate.
stakeholders: Residents of assisted housing programs, housing providers (including landlords and housing authorities), and the Office of the Attorney General.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not included. However, the bill creates new mandates for the Office of the Attorney General, including investigating grievances, mediating disputes, and maintaining a hotline, which will increase State expenditures for personnel and operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Office of the Attorney General as the primary agency responsible for investigating grievances, mediating resolutions between clients and housing providers, establishing a toll-free hotline, and bringing legal actions for violations or non-cooperation.

The bill adds a new title to the Housing and Community Development Article and applies to state-funded housing programs administered by this department. Additionally, the Attorney General is specifically authorized to coordinate with the department during investigations.
The bill's definition of 'assisted housing program' explicitly includes emergency shelter programs, many of which are overseen or funded by the Department of Human Services and its local departments.
The bill authorizes the Office of the Attorney General to bring actions for injunctive relief and damages in the court system, which may lead to an increase in civil filings and judicial proceedings.

The Commission on Civil Rights enforces anti-discrimination laws in housing; the grievance process established for the Attorney General regarding housing conditions and law violations may overlap with the Commission's jurisdiction.

Synopsis: Altering a limitation on claiming the income tax credit for eligible long-term care insurance premiums for more than 1 year with respect to the same insured individual; altering the amount of the credit from a one-time $500 credit to a maximum of $250 for a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2026; and applying the Act to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland income tax credit for long-term care insurance premiums by reducing the maximum credit from $500 to $250 per insured individual and restricting the credit to insurance policies covering individuals who are at least 45 years old. It also updates eligibility criteria to allow the credit for policies purchased after 2026, provided no credit has been claimed for that individual under the new rules, and clarifies that the credit may only be claimed once per insured individual per taxable year.
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers paying long-term care insurance premiums and Maryland residents aged 45 and older who are beneficiaries of such insurance.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to impact State income tax revenues by halving the maximum credit per individual and adding age-based restrictions, which may increase revenue relative to current law. However, the bill also resets credit eligibility for policies purchased after 2026, which could increase participation. Because the full text of the Fiscal Note with specific revenue projections was not provided, a precise dollar estimate is unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's income tax system, including the processing and auditing of the long-term care tax credit. Furthermore, the bill explicitly mandates the Comptroller to submit an annual report to the Governor and General Assembly regarding the credit's usage and its fiscal impact on the Medical Assistance Program.

The bill requires the reporting of savings to the State’s Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health. The policy objective of incentivizing long-term care insurance is specifically intended to reduce Medicaid expenditures for long-term care services, making the health department a key stakeholder.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates the long-term care insurance market. The agency is responsible for overseeing the contracts and products that would qualify for the tax credit under both federal and state definitions.

The Department of Aging is dedicated to the well-being of older adults and long-term care advocacy. As this bill specifically targets residents aged 45 and older and concerns the financing of future care, it aligns directly with the department's core mission and service population.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state revenue estimates and fiscal planning. Modifying a tax credit directly impacts state income tax revenues and requires coordination for long-term fiscal projections.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and receives the annual report from the Comptroller regarding the effectiveness and savings generated by the tax credit.
The State Treasurer's Office manages the state's financial resources and anticipates monetary needs, meaning the fiscal impact of tax credits on the state's general fund is of institutional interest.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Comptroller and the General Assembly regarding the implementation of tax laws and ensures that statutory changes meet constitutional and legal standards.

As an independent administrative agency that hears appeals regarding tax assessments and credits, the Maryland Tax Court would be the venue for adjudicating any disputes between taxpayers and the state regarding the eligibility or amount of the credit.

The Office of Legislative Audits performs fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive agencies, including the Comptroller's Office, and may be tasked with verifying the accuracy of the data reported regarding the credit's utilization and Medicaid savings.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Education to review graduation requirements for public high school students every 5 years; and requiring implementation of updated graduation requirements for the cohort entering high school in the school year following State Board approval.
Title: State Board of Education - Public High School Graduation Requirements
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/07 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Education to review and update public high school graduation requirements at least once every five years. It also specifies that any changes to these requirements must be implemented for the cohort of students entering high school in the school year immediately following the State Board's approval.
stakeholders: Public high school students, local school systems, the Maryland State Department of Education, and the State Board of Education.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact, as the State Board of Education can handle the periodic review and updating of graduation requirements using existing resources. Local school systems may experience minimal fiscal and operational impacts depending on whether future updates require new course offerings or curriculum adjustments, but specific dollar estimates are unavailable and would depend on future policy decisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill primarily directs the State Board of Education, which is the leadership body for this department, to review and update high school graduation requirements every five years and manage the implementation for student cohorts.

The bill explicitly requires the State Board of Education to coordinate and consult with the Maryland Higher Education Commission when performing its duties regarding graduation requirements and career readiness standards.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Board of Education consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board to align graduation requirements with workforce and career readiness goals.

As the agency overseeing executive branch policy initiatives and the Blueprint for Maryland's Future, the Governor's Office coordinates the high-level policy goals that these graduation requirements are intended to reflect.

The Department of Labor is involved in workforce development and provided input for the fiscal analysis; changes to graduation standards directly impact the state's labor pipeline and workforce training programs.

This agency links student data with workforce outcomes; any changes to graduation requirements will necessitate updates to their data collection models and impact their longitudinal analysis of student success.

Synopsis: Requiring a party to a partition action to timely notify the court of the type and amount of each outstanding lien on the property if the plaintiff does not procure a title report; altering the calculation of the purchase price for the interest of a cotenant by subtracting the amount of outstanding liens owed on the property from the value of the entire parcel; requiring the court to adjust the purchase price for the interest of a cotenant based on certain costs and income from the property; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Real Property - Partition of Property - Liens and Purchase Price Adjustments
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 4/03 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: This bill modifies the legal process for the partition of real property by requiring parties to notify the court of outstanding liens if a title report is not required. It alters the calculation of a cotenant's interest purchase price by subtracting the total value of outstanding liens from the property's value before applying the ownership percentage. Additionally, it mandates that courts adjust the purchase price based on necessary costs incurred by a cotenant (such as taxes, mortgage, or maintenance) or income earned (such as rent) without equitable contribution or distribution from other cotenants.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Cotenants of real property involved in partition actions, legal parties in partition cases, and property owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The fiscal note indicates that the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial operations by establishing new requirements for court-ordered property partitions, including mandatory lien notifications, specific purchase price calculation formulas, and requirements for judges to hold evidentiary hearings on cost adjustments and income distributions.

As the chief legal representative for the state, the OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly regarding changes to the Real Property Article and may be involved in litigation or appeals resulting from the interpretation of these updated partition laws.

The bill relates to real property ownership and equity, particularly in cases involving multiple cotenants. This aligns with the department's mission to ensure access to secure housing and support homeownership stability by ensuring fair equitable contribution and distribution during property sales.
The Governor's Office is responsible for the final review and signing of legislation into law and oversees policy initiatives related to state property laws.

The bill requires parties to notify the court of outstanding tax liens. As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller's office manages the state tax liens that will be reported and documented under these new court procedures.

The Maryland State Archives is the central depository for judicial records. Changes to partition procedures and the resulting court documentation will eventually be part of the permanent state record managed by the agency.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a managed care organization and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from requiring a prior authorization or step therapy or fail-first protocol under certain circumstances for prescription drugs that have been reviewed by the Prescription Drug Affordability Board; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage and Utilization Review - Drugs Reviewed by the Prescription Drug Affordability Board
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Health; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Managed Care Organizations -see also- Health Maint Orgs

bill_summary: The bill prevents Medicaid managed care organizations and private health insurers from using prior authorization, step therapy, or other coverage restrictions on prescription drugs that have been reviewed by the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board, provided the board has not identified specific affordability challenges or has set payment limits.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Medicaid participants, state employees and retirees, private health insurance policyholders, health insurers, and managed care organizations
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are expected to increase significantly beginning in FY 2027. Medicaid costs will likely increase by tens of millions of dollars annually. The State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program expects cost increases of $49.7 million to $65.0 million annually. Local government health insurance costs for fully insured plans will also rise.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Department of Health. It prohibits Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) from requiring prior authorization or limiting coverage for drugs reviewed by the Prescription Drug Affordability Board. The fiscal note indicates a significant increase in Medicaid expenditures (tens of millions) as a result.

The bill adds new requirements to the Insurance Article, prohibiting private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs from imposing step therapy, fail-first protocols, or limiting coverage for drugs reviewed by PDAB. MIA is the primary regulator responsible for enforcing these compliance measures and reviewing rate and form filings.

DBM manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. The fiscal note estimates that removing prior authorization for drugs reviewed by PDAB could increase program costs by $49.7 million to $65.0 million annually, specifically due to increased utilization of high-cost medications.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This category includes the Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB), whose actions—conducting drug reviews, making affordability determinations, and setting upper payment limits—are the primary triggers for the bill's insurance and Medicaid coverage mandates.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill aligns with executive priorities regarding drug affordability and impacts the administration of the executive department's Medicaid and state employee benefit policies.

As the administrator of the state's health insurance marketplace, the Exchange must ensure that plans offered on Maryland Health Connection comply with these new statutory requirements for coverage and utilization review.

The MHCC is responsible for health system planning and quality improvement. The bill's restrictions on utilization management tools for high-cost drugs directly affect the commission's work in monitoring healthcare costs and accessibility.

The OAG serves as the chief legal officer for state agencies, including MDH and MIA. It would provide legal counsel regarding the implementation and enforcement of these regulations and defend the state in potential challenges from pharmaceutical manufacturers or insurance carriers.

Synopsis: Requiring a citation issued for violations relating to public consumption of alcohol and possession of an open container to contain notice that fines for the violation may be prepaid; establishing a maximum fine for public consumption and open container violations and authorizing the Chief Judge of the District Court to establish a schedule for prepayment of the fines; establishing that prepayment of a fine is a plea of guilty; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Public Consumption and Open Container - Prepayment of Citation
Status: In the Senate - Special Order until 4/13 (Senator Hayes) Adopted
bill_summary: This bill allows individuals cited for public consumption of alcohol or possession of an open container to prepay their fines rather than appearing in court, with such prepayment counting as a guilty plea. It requires the Chief Judge of the District Court to establish a prepayment schedule, sets a maximum fine of $100 for these violations, and mandates that citations be updated to notify individuals of the prepayment option.
stakeholders: Adults issued citations for public alcohol consumption or open container violations, law enforcement officers, alcoholic beverages inspectors, and the Maryland District Court.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary will increase by approximately $24,100 in fiscal 2027 only for the purpose of revising and reprinting citations. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect other State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts District Court operations by requiring the Chief Judge of the District Court to establish a prepayment schedule and the court to prescribe specific citation forms. The Judiciary faces a direct fiscal impact for reprinting these forms.

The bill explicitly authorizes forest and park wardens, who operate under the Department of Natural Resources, to issue citations for public consumption and open container violations in state parks and recreation areas.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, Maryland State Police officers are authorized to issue the citations described in the bill and will be responsible for implementing the new notice requirements on citations.

The bill requires the court to notify the Motor Vehicle Administration of code violations involving the use of a driver's license, and tasks the MVA with establishing uniform reporting procedures with the District Court.
The legislation applies to alcohol-related citations issued to minors, which fall under the jurisdiction of the juvenile justice system and the procedures monitored by this agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender provides legal counsel to indigent individuals in proceedings related to code violations and contested hearings as outlined in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This agency advises on criminal justice strategies and manages funds for public safety; changes to citation procedures and fine structures for alcoholic beverage violations fall within their policy scope.
The bill results in general fund expenditures for form revisions and reprints, requiring fiscal oversight by the state's principal budget agency.
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the various state agencies and the District Court as they implement these changes to the Criminal Law Article and citation procedures.

Synopsis: Modifying the definition of "community choice aggregator" for the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program to include residential electric customers served by certain electric cooperatives; expanding the application of the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program to apply to all counties and Baltimore City instead of applying to Montgomery County only; and modifying the membership of the Community Choice Energy Workgroup.
Title: Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program - Definition, Application, and Workgroup - Modifications
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill expands the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program from Montgomery County to all Maryland counties and Baltimore City. It enables local governments to purchase electricity for residential and small commercial customers, updates the definition of a community choice aggregator to include certain electric cooperative customers, and modifies the membership of the Community Choice Energy Workgroup.
stakeholders: Residential and small commercial electric customers, county governments, Baltimore City, electric companies, and competitive electricity suppliers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State: The Public Service Commission will experience an increased administrative workload to oversee the expanded program, adopt regulations, and staff the workgroup. Local: Participating counties and Baltimore City will incur indeterminate costs to develop aggregation plans and notify customers; they are also liable for stranded costs related to electricity contracts or generation ownership. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as no formal Fiscal Note was included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Public Service Commission as the primary regulatory authority for the Community Choice Aggregation Pilot Program, requiring it to approve aggregation plans, establish implementation schedules, adopt regulations, and oversee the Community Choice Energy Workgroup.

The bill explicitly mandates the inclusion of a representative from the Office of People’s Counsel in the Community Choice Energy Workgroup and directly impacts residential utility consumers, whom the office is statutory tasked with representing.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the membership and reporting mandates of the Community Choice Energy Workgroup, an advisory body established to support the pilot program and provide recommendations to the Commission.

The bill requires community choice aggregators to consult with the Department of Housing and Community Development when promoting or providing energy efficiency programs to residential and small commercial customers.

The bill requires the Commission to establish procedures ensuring that customers in community choice aggregation programs receive bill and arrearage assistance administered by the Office of Home Energy Programs, which is part of the Department.

As the state's energy planning agency, the MEA's work in promoting renewable energy and energy efficiency is directly related to the goals of the community choice aggregation program expanded by this legislation.

The bill references the Department's authority to sell energy and the statewide expansion of aggregation programs may impact the Department's role as the central procurement authority for state energy services.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive agencies implementing the pilot program and is a recipient of the Commission's final report on the program's effectiveness and costs.

Synopsis: Repealing certain provisions related to energy salespersons and the marketing and pricing of green power; altering the process of renewing certain electricity supplier and gas supplier licenses; requiring the Public Service Commission to provide a certain licensee with due process before taking certain actions regarding the license; requiring electric and gas suppliers to submit a list of energy vendors to the Commission under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Retail Supply of Electricity and Gas - Regulation and Consumer Protection - Alterations
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Environment and Transportation; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill modifies the regulatory framework for retail electricity and gas suppliers in Maryland by repealing the classification and licensing of 'energy salespersons' and instead regulating 'energy vendors.' It requires the Public Service Commission (PSC) to establish an Energy Choice Multimedia Program for consumer education, updates license renewal procedures for energy suppliers, and mandates new consumer protection notices for automatic renewals and price increases exceeding 10%. Additionally, it grants the PSC authority over energy vendor lists and provides due process protections for licensees.
stakeholders: Residential and small commercial electricity and gas customers, electricity suppliers, gas suppliers, energy vendors, and electric and gas utility companies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has several financial implications: it allows for civil penalties of up to $25,000 per violation to be deposited into the Education and Protection Fund and maintains licensing and renewal fees. It also requires the Public Service Commission to fund and administer a new Energy Choice Multimedia Program, involving annual mailings and bill inserts. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text, specific total dollar estimates for expenditures or revenues are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary agency tasked with implementing and enforcing the bill's provisions, including licensing electricity and gas suppliers, establishing the Energy Choice Multimedia Program, and overseeing the Education and Protection Fund.

The bill explicitly references the People's Counsel as having authority in licensing, complaint, and dispute resolution proceedings and allows them to file complaints against suppliers for just cause.

The bill requires the Public Service Commission to consult with the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General before adopting certain regulations and acknowledges the OAG's role in enforcing consumer protection laws.
The bill requires the State Treasurer to hold the Education and Protection Fund separately and invest its money in the same manner as other State money.
The bill mandates that the Comptroller account for the Education and Protection Fund used for customer education and protection initiatives.

The Department of General Services is explicitly mentioned as an entity that sells energy under the Public Utilities Article and is carved out from certain regulatory definitions and licensing requirements amended by the bill.

The bill's education programs are specifically required to inform customers on energy choices that help meet the State’s climate commitments under statutes administered by the Department of the Environment.

As the state's energy policy agency, the MEA is impacted by shifts in the regulatory landscape for retail electricity and gas supply and the state's strategies for consumer education and climate goals.

The bill requires due process before the suspension or revocation of licenses, which often involves the impartial hearing process provided by the Office of Administrative Hearings for contested executive agency cases.
The bill specifies that expenditures from the Education and Protection Fund may only be made in accordance with the State budget, which is overseen by the Department of Budget and Management.
The Governor's Office oversees the Public Service Commission and the executive branch agencies responsible for the bill's fiscal and policy outcomes.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Washington County Health Department to exempt the owner of a certain residential property from compliance with all or part of a certain on-site sewage disposal system regulation if compliance with the regulation would be unduly burdensome; and establishing requirements for the consideration and issuance of exemptions under the Act.
Title: Washington County - On-Site Sewage Disposal System Regulations - Exemptions
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/11 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Washington County Health Department to exempt residential property owners in Washington County Agricultural (Rural) or Rural Village zoning districts from compliance with specific on-site sewage disposal system regulations. To qualify, an owner must prove that compliance is unduly burdensome due to physical or financial impracticality, supported by a report from a licensed on-site wastewater professional. Exemptions are valid for up to three years or until the property changes ownership and may be renewed.
stakeholders: Residential property owners in rural Washington County zones, the Washington County Health Department, and licensed on-site wastewater professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not provided in the text. The bill creates an application and review process for septic system exemptions which involves administrative duties for the Washington County Health Department and costs for property owners to obtain professional reports. However, property owners could see financial savings by being exempted from expensive septic regulations. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly empowers the Washington County Health Department to grant exemptions for on-site sewage disposal systems. The Department of Health oversees local health departments and sets public health policy regarding sanitation.

The regulations from which owners may be exempted (COMAR 26.04.02) are promulgated by the Department of the Environment, which is responsible for implementing and enforcing state environmental laws regarding water quality and pollution control.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and the Department of the Environment regarding the interpretation and enforcement of regulatory exemptions and the definition of 'unduly burdensome' compliance.

As the independent agency that adjudicates contested cases for state and local agencies, the Office of Administrative Hearings would likely handle appeals regarding the denial of exemption permits under this Act.

The bill requires a report from an individual licensed by the State Board of On-Site Wastewater Professionals; the Department of Labor is responsible for the licensing and regulation of various professions and industries in the state.

The bill specifically addresses septic system challenges for residential property owners in rural and agricultural zoning districts, aligning with the Council's mission to support the unique needs of rural Maryland counties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Council on the Chesapeake Bay
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Septic regulations are a key component of watershed management and bay restoration; changes to these standards in rural areas are relevant to the Council's role in advising the Governor on cleaning up the Chesapeake Bay.

This multi-agency initiative promotes sustainable development and environmental protection, including the management of the state's carbon footprint and the protection of the Chesapeake Bay through resource management.

Synopsis: Repealing the 90-day time limit within which an individual receiving services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration must appeal a loss of eligibility for services; establishing requirements related to eligibility determinations and redeterminations under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; prohibiting the Department from procedurally disenrolling individuals from the Program or home- and community-based services solely on a certain basis except under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Developmental Disabilities Administration - Home- and Community-Based Services Eligibility Determinations (Maryland Protecting People With Disabilities Act)
Status: In the Senate - Second Reading Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Home Care Services -see also- Respite Care
Long-Term Care -see also- Continuing Care; Nursing Homes
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: The Maryland Protecting People With Disabilities Act establishes specific standards and protections regarding eligibility determinations and redeterminations for the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and services provided by the Developmental Disabilities Administration. The bill prohibits the Maryland Department of Health from procedurally disenrolling individuals from home- and community-based services due to missing documentation unless specific verification and notification steps are exhausted, and it requires retroactive reinstatement for those disenrolled due to department delays. Additionally, the department must provide accessible information regarding program eligibility and rights, reserve waiver slots for reinstated individuals, and submit quarterly reports on eligibility statistics through 2029.
stakeholders: Medicaid recipients receiving home- and community-based services, individuals with developmental disabilities, and applicants for disability-related medical assistance programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, the bill generally codifies existing federal mandates and aligns with current practices for waivers administered by the Developmental Disabilities Administration. The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) advises that the administrative requirements, including reporting and application processing, can be handled with existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to affect state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) is the primary implementing agency for this bill. It oversees the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), both of which are central to the bill's requirements regarding eligibility redeterminations, procedural disenrollments, and waiver slot management.

The bill's preamble explicitly references the Department of Disabilities' role in compiling data for the State's Olmstead Plan and its collaborative work with the DDA to address barriers to community placement for individuals with disabilities.

The bill alters appeal procedures for individuals receiving services from the Developmental Disabilities Administration who lose eligibility. The Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH) is the independent agency responsible for conducting these impartial hearings.

The bill requires the Department of Health to ensure that service providers can automatically exchange electronic data through an application program interface (API) with the state's Long Term Services and Supports (LTSS) software system, which involves state-level information technology infrastructure.

As the chief legal officer for the state, the Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and represents the state in matters related to Medicaid eligibility laws and the Americans with Disabilities Act.

The Department of Human Services is involved in the administration of Medicaid eligibility through its local departments, and the bill's changes to eligibility redetermination processes directly intersect with their operations.

Synopsis: Authorizing certain school vehicle driver trainers to administer the commercial driver's instructional permit knowledge test to applicants for a commercial driver's license - school bus endorsement.
Title: Commercial Driver's Instructional Permits - School Vehicles - Knowledge Test
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes school vehicle driver trainers employed by a county school board to administer the commercial driver’s instructional permit knowledge test to applicants seeking a commercial driver’s license with a school bus endorsement.
responsible_party: County school boards and school vehicle driver trainers
stakeholders: Applicants for a commercial driver's license school bus endorsement, county school boards, and school vehicle driver trainers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The bill identifies a shift in the administration of knowledge tests which may result in a decrease in administrative workload for the Motor Vehicle Administration and a corresponding increase in responsibility for local county school boards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The MVA is the primary state agency responsible for driver licensing and testing, including commercial driver's instructional permits. This bill directly impacts MVA operations by authorizing external school vehicle driver trainers to perform knowledge tests previously conducted by MVA staff.

As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), MDOT is responsible for the overall management of state transportation laws and the regulatory framework for driver licensing and endorsements.

The Department of Education oversees Maryland's 24 local school systems. The bill involves employees of county school boards (school vehicle driver trainers) and affects the training and certification process for personnel within the public education system's transportation network.

The Maryland Center for School Safety is tasked with providing a comprehensive approach to safety in schools, which includes the safe transportation of students. Changes to the testing and certification process for school bus drivers fall under their broad mandate for student safety.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to implement a certain system for collecting certain information and determining certain addresses; authorizing the Administration to conduct certain investigations and assess certain penalties; requiring the Administration to provide certain notice; requiring certain penalties to be deposited into the Transportation Trust Fund; authorizing the Administration to enter into contracts with private parties to procure certain services of independent agents; etc.
Title: Motor Vehicle Administration - Improper Registration - Investigation and Penalties
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/05 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to implement a system to collect address information from vehicle insurance contracts to identify Maryland residents who have improperly registered their vehicles in other states. The MVA is authorized to conduct investigations, hire private contractors for assistance, and assess penalties of $150 for noncompliance and an additional $500 if the vehicle remains unregistered 60 days after notice. All penalties are to be deposited into the Transportation Trust Fund.
stakeholders: Maryland residents owning vehicles registered out-of-state, the Motor Vehicle Administration, and private investigative contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates a new revenue stream for the Transportation Trust Fund through penalties of $150 and $500 assessed against residents with improperly registered vehicles. The MVA will incur costs to establish the data collection system and conduct investigations, which may be performed by private agents under contract. Specific aggregate dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are not available in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) is the primary agency tasked with implementing the new system to collect insurance address information, conducting investigations into improper vehicle registration, assessing penalties for noncompliance, and potentially contracting with private parties for these services.

As the parent agency of the MVA, the Department of Transportation oversees motor vehicle registration and manages the Transportation Trust Fund, which is the designated recipient of the penalties collected under this bill.
The Office of Administrative Hearings typically adjudicates contested administrative decisions and penalties assessed by the MVA, such as those authorized by this bill for improper registration.

The Board of Public Works oversees significant state procurement contracts; its approval would likely be required if the MVA enters into substantial contracts with private parties to procure the services of independent agents.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees state agency expenditures and personnel; it would be responsible for managing the fiscal impact on the MVA's budget and the resulting revenue for the Transportation Trust Fund.
The State Treasurer acts as the custodian of state funds, including the receipt and distribution of penalties directed to the Transportation Trust Fund.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the MVA and would likely be involved in drafting or reviewing the new regulations, investigation protocols, and private contracts authorized by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a municipality to submit to the State Board of Elections the qualifications to be a candidate for each office on the ballot in a municipal election, the list of qualified candidates for each office on the ballot in a municipal election, the date of a special election and each office on the special election ballot, and certain information on voting procedures and locations in a municipal election on or before certain dates; requiring the State Board to post the information on the State Board's website immediately on receipt; etc.
Title: Municipal Elections - Reporting of Information to the State Board
Status: In the House - Passed Enrolled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland municipalities to report candidate qualifications, election dates, lists of qualified candidates, and voting procedures to the State Board of Elections (SBE) for publication on the SBE website. Municipalities using ranked-choice voting must also submit their tabulation regulations for publication. The State Board of Elections must post this information immediately upon receipt.
stakeholders: Municipal governments, municipal election candidates, and voters in Maryland municipalities
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Elections can implement the bill with existing resources, resulting in no state fiscal impact. The bill is not expected to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the head of the executive branch, the Governor oversees the State Board of Elections. The bill requires the Governor's signature to become law and impacts the administrative duties of a state executive agency.

The State Board of Elections is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill. It is responsible for receiving election data, candidate qualifications, and voting procedures from municipalities and must immediately publish this information, along with ranked-choice voting regulations, on its official website.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the State Board of Elections. It may be called upon to provide legal guidance regarding the new reporting requirements for municipalities or the publication of municipal ranked-choice voting regulations.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Maryland Office of the Inspector General (OIG) and an Advisory Board to provide oversight and appoint an Inspector General. The OIG is authorized to investigate waste, mismanagement, misconduct, fraud, and corruption within the executive branch of the State government, conduct audits, and issue subpoenas. It also extends whistleblower protections to State employees who report information to the OIG and allows for the transfer of existing staff and funding to the new office.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Inspector General and the Maryland Office of the Inspector General Advisory Board
stakeholders: Maryland State employees, Executive Branch agencies and units, and Maryland residents
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a new state office, resulting in increased state expenditures for salaries, equipment, and operations as provided in the state budget. The Governor is authorized to transfer existing funds and positions from executive agencies to the OIG. While specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note are absent in the provided text, the bill establishes a potential revenue source through misdemeanor fines of up to $2,000 for unauthorized disclosure of confidential investigation records.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor or a designee serves as a member of the Maryland Office of the Inspector General Advisory Board. Additionally, the Governor appoints one professional member to the board, receives annual and final investigative reports, and is authorized to transfer positions and funds from other executive units to the new Office of the Inspector General.

The Comptroller or a designee serves as a member of the Maryland Office of the Inspector General Advisory Board, which is responsible for appointing and overseeing the Inspector General. The board requires the Comptroller's participation for a quorum and a majority vote for leadership decisions.

DBM is the state's principal fiscal and personnel agency. It will be responsible for managing the transfer of funds and positions to the new office and overseeing the implementation of the expanded whistleblower protections in the State Personnel and Pensions Article.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new permanent advisory board, the Maryland Office of the Inspector General Advisory Board, to appoint, oversee, and potentially remove the Inspector General.

The bill establishes legal frameworks for investigations and criminal referrals. It also explicitly includes the Inspector General alongside the Attorney General as a protected recipient of disclosures in the state's whistleblower statute.
The bill requires the Inspector General to obtain approval from a circuit court judge to issue subpoenas. This creates a new administrative interaction between the executive branch and the judiciary.

The bill mandates that the state maintain and equip office space for the Maryland Office of the Inspector General, a core responsibility of DGS. Additionally, the Inspector General's oversight of 'waste and mismanagement' often involves procurement and facility management audits.

The bill requires the Inspector General to take steps to avoid duplicative investigations or audits. As OLA is the primary agency responsible for auditing executive units, the two offices must coordinate closely to ensure oversight efficiency.

The Inspector General is required to establish a toll-free hotline and a public website to receive complaints and post reports, which typically requires coordination with and technical support from DoIT.

The Inspector General is mandated to notify the appropriate law enforcement agency if an investigation discovers evidence of criminal activity. As the primary state-level law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police would likely receive such referrals.
The bill contains specific protections ensuring that employees transferred to the new Maryland Office of the Inspector General do so without diminution of their retirement status or benefits.

Synopsis: Requiring, under certain circumstances, an insurer, a nonprofit health service plan, a health maintenance organization, a dental plan organization, a managed care organization, or any other entity providing health benefit plans in the State to identify primary and secondary payors, the amounts payable by those payors, and to coordinate benefits with those identified payors; and altering the time period in which a carrier may retroactively deny reimbursement subject to coordination of benefits with another carrier.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers to take responsibility for identifying primary and secondary payors, determining payable amounts, and coordinating benefits when a claim involves multiple payors. It also shortens the window for a carrier to retroactively deny reimbursement to a healthcare provider from 18 months to 9 months for claims subject to coordination of benefits with another carrier, while maintaining the 18-month window for Medicare and Medicaid claims.
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, healthcare providers, and the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration will see a minimal increase in special fund revenues from a $125 rate and form filing fee starting in fiscal year 2027. There is a potential indeterminate increase in administrative costs for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Small business healthcare providers may experience a positive impact due to reduced administrative burdens and shorter retroactive denial windows.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Insurance Article and imposes new regulatory requirements on health insurance carriers. The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulator for these entities and is specifically tasked with receiving the newly required annual reports from carriers regarding their coordination of benefits activities.

The fiscal note indicates that the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) anticipates a potential increase in administrative costs for the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program due to the bill's requirements on coordination of benefits and retroactive denials.

The bill specifically defines 'Payor' to include the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and includes Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) under the definition of 'Carrier'. These programs and entities are overseen by the Department of Health, and the bill regulates their reimbursement and coordination of benefits processes.

As the agency responsible for administering the state's health insurance marketplace, the Exchange has a significant interest in regulations affecting the carriers that provide health plans on the platform, particularly regarding claims processing and coordination of benefits.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health, both of which will be responsible for implementing or complying with the changes in insurance law established by this bill.

The Commission is responsible for planning for the state's health system needs and improving access to health care. Regulations concerning reimbursement and coordination of benefits impact the financial stability and operational efficiency of health care providers and the overall health system.
