bill_summary: Known as Tiarra's Law, this bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop a pamphlet providing information on the State and national 9-8-8 Suicide and Crisis Lifelines and the Crisis Response System. Health care providers and representatives from the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner must distribute this pamphlet to individuals upon request or in connection with a death, overdose, or behavioral health crisis. The bill also mandates that the Department review trauma-informed care training for health care providers and report findings and recommendations to the General Assembly.
stakeholders: Individuals and family members impacted by behavioral health crises, overdoses, or deaths; health care providers including facilities, practitioners, and emergency medical services personnel; and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Maryland Department of Health can develop the required pamphlet, conduct the review of trauma-informed care training, and complete the mandated report using existing budgeted resources. The bill has no impact on State revenues and does not affect local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing the crisis response system pamphlet, conducting a review of trauma-informed care training, and reporting findings to the General Assembly. Additionally, the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner, which is responsible for distributing the pamphlet, is a unit within the Department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly includes licensed or certified emergency medical services (EMS) providers in the definition of 'health care provider.' The agency oversees these providers and will be directly involved in the mandated review of trauma-informed care training and post-incident support protocols.

The Office of the Attorney General serves as the primary legal representative for the State and would provide counsel to the Department of Health and the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner regarding the development of public health information materials and the implementation of new regulatory requirements.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates policy initiatives. The bill requires a report to be filed with the General Assembly on findings and recommendations for public health policy changes, which falls under the Governor's administrative and executive oversight.

The bill's underlying statute for the Crisis Response System requires coordination with the police. As a key first responder frequently involved in overdose scenes and death investigations alongside the medical examiner, the agency is impacted by the bill's focus on improving first response practices and survivor support.

The bill requires a review of trauma-informed care training provided to health care practitioners. The Commission establishes statewide policies and standards for public and private colleges and universities that provide this professional education and training.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency advises the Governor on criminal justice strategies and public safety policy. The bill explicitly aims to use evaluation data to formulate recommendations to decrease criminal detention and improve crisis diversion, which aligns with this office's mission.

The Commission is responsible for planning for state health system needs and increasing accountability. The bill's requirement for a comprehensive evaluation of Crisis Response System outcomes and public reporting overlaps with the Commission's regulatory and planning duties.

Synopsis: Requiring that the average weekly wages from employments of a covered employee who, at the time of an accidental personal injury or last injurious exposure to an occupational disease, was concurrently employed by more than one employer be combined for purposes of computing the average weekly wages under certain circumstances; and requiring that the Subsequent Injury Fund reimburse an employer for certain compensation paid by the employer to an employee for permanent partial and total disability under certain circumstances.
Title: Workers' Compensation - Average Weekly Wage - Multiple Employers
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/11 at 1:00 p.m.

Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires that when a worker who holds multiple jobs is injured or develops an occupational disease that prevents them from working any of those jobs, their average weekly wage for workers' compensation purposes must be calculated by combining the wages from all their employers. It also mandates that the Subsequent Injury Fund reimburse the employer or insurer for the extra benefit costs resulting from including wages from other jobs in the calculation for permanent disability cases.
responsible_party: Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission and the Subsequent Injury Fund
stakeholders: Workers with multiple concurrent employers, workers' compensation insurance carriers, self-insured employers, and the Subsequent Injury Fund.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill requires the Subsequent Injury Fund to reimburse employers or insurers for the portion of permanent disability benefits derived from an employee's concurrent employment wages. This is expected to increase expenditures for the Subsequent Injury Fund. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Subsequent Injury Fund to reimburse employers or their insurers for additional weekly compensation resulting from combining a covered employee's wages from multiple concurrent employers for permanent partial and total disability claims.

As the independent agency that administers the state's Workers' Compensation Law and adjudicates claims, the Commission is responsible for implementing the new method of computing average weekly wages for concurrently employed workers and overseeing the reimbursement process from the Subsequent Injury Fund.

The Injured Workers' Insurance Fund (operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company) is the third-party administrator for workers' compensation claims for State of Maryland employees. It will be responsible for calculating combined wages for state employees with concurrent employment and seeking reimbursement from the Subsequent Injury Fund.

The bill specifically amends Section 9-602(c) regarding the computation of the average weekly wage for individuals engaged for fire fighting by the Department of Natural Resources, ensuring their wages from other employment are factored in according to the new subsection.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the State Workers' Compensation Commission and the Subsequent Injury Fund, and represents the state in civil appeals related to workers' compensation claims.

As the central personnel agency for the state, DBM manages state employee benefits and policies; changes to workers' compensation payouts and the resulting fiscal implications for the state as an employer fall under its oversight.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Baltimore City Mobile Infant and Maternal Health Pilot Program (MomMobile) within the Maryland Department of Health to provide mobile postpartum care, mental health screenings, and care coordination directly to underserved communities in Baltimore City. The program aims to reduce transportation barriers, improve postpartum visit attendance, and identify behavioral health risks through culturally competent care provided by health care professionals, including midwives and doulas.
stakeholders: Postpartum individuals and infants in Baltimore City, healthcare providers including midwives and doulas, and the Baltimore City Health Department.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Maryland Department of Health general fund expenditures increase by $71,900 in FY 2027 and $81,700 in FY 2028 for contractual staff to develop the program. The Baltimore City Health Department expenditures are estimated to increase by $39,875 in FY 2027 and $28,325 in FY 2028 for its consultative role in development. Total implementation costs for the pilot program are currently indeterminate but potentially significant, with one estimate for full local implementation reaching approximately 1.9 million dollars.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly establishes the Baltimore City Mobile Infant and Maternal Health Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of Health. The Secretary of Health is responsible for developing, implementing, and reporting on the program.

The bill's focus on infant and maternal health outcomes and improving access to services for underserved communities aligns directly with this office's mission to promote the well-being of children and families and improve access to health services.

This agency functions as a solution incubator for novel initiatives addressing the Governor's priorities, such as enhancing economic mobility and reducing poverty. This pilot program ('MomMobile') is a novel strategy aimed at improving outcomes for Maryland families through data-driven health intervention.
The Secretary of Health is required to report annually to the Governor on the implementation and effectiveness of the pilot program.
The program's purpose includes improving referrals to social services and community programs, which are primarily managed and delivered by the Department of Human Services.
The bill has a notable fiscal impact on general fund expenditures for personnel and program implementation, which falls under DBM's oversight of the state budget and personnel management.

The program utilizes 'mobile health units' (motor vehicles). As the central procurement and fleet management authority for the state, DGS would likely be involved if the Department of Health procures or manages these vehicles.
The commission is responsible for planning for the state's health system needs and improving access to health care, making this pilot program relevant to their regulatory and planning functions.
The bill requires the Secretary to determine 'funding support' for the program. The Grants Office may assist in identifying and managing federal grant funding to support the initiative.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and would likely review the legal frameworks or contracts required to implement the new pilot program.

The OLA is responsible for fiscal compliance and performance audits of state agencies, including the Department of Health, and would eventually audit the expenditures and execution of this new program.
The bill requires the identification of key metrics to assess outcomes and an evaluation plan, which aligns with GOPI's role in using performance metrics to enhance state government responsiveness.
As the program relies on 'mobile health units' defined as motor vehicles, the MVA would be responsible for the titling and registration of any new state-owned vehicles acquired for the program.

Synopsis: Altering terminology in the Maryland Constitution to be gender-neutral.
Title: Constitutional Language - Modernization
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to modernize the Maryland Constitution by replacing gender-specific language with gender-neutral terminology. It replaces terms such as 'man' and 'mankind' with 'person' and 'humanity,' and updates masculine pronouns like 'he,' 'him,' and 'his' with gender-neutral alternatives like 'they,' 'them,' 'their,' or specific role titles such as 'the Governor' or 'the Judge.'
responsible_party: The Maryland General Assembly, the Governor of Maryland, and the State Board of Elections
stakeholders: All citizens and voters of Maryland, as well as state government officials and employees whose roles are defined within the Maryland Constitution.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates for state or local fiscal impacts are unavailable as no formal Fiscal Note is provided in the bill text. The primary financial implication of the bill is the administrative cost to the State Board of Elections for preparing and including the constitutional amendment on the November 2026 general election ballot.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill proposes multiple amendments to Article II (Executive Department) of the Maryland Constitution, which governs the powers, duties, and descriptors of the Governor's office.
Article II, Sections 1A, 1B, 21, and 21A are specifically amended to modernize language and descriptors pertaining to the Lieutenant Governor.
Article VI (Treasury Department) is amended to modernize terminology for the Comptroller, and Article II is amended regarding the Governor's examination of the Comptroller's books.
Article VI (Treasury Department) is specifically amended to modernize terminology and duties for the State Treasurer.
Article V is amended to modernize the title and descriptors for the Attorney General. Additionally, the Attorney General is tasked with approving summaries for referendum petitions in Article XVI.
Article II, Sections 22 and 23 are amended regarding the Secretary of State's appointment and duties. The Secretary is also mentioned in Article XVI regarding ballot titles for referendums.
Article IX, Section 2 is amended to modernize the terminology and gendered language specifically describing the Adjutant General's office and duties.
Article IV, Section 41 is specifically amended to modernize descriptors for the Register of Wills.
The bill significantly amends Article IV (Judiciary Department), affecting constitutional language for judges, the Chief Judge of the District Court, and various court clerks.
The bill amends Article I (Elective Franchise) and requires the State Board of Elections to submit the constitutional amendment to the voters in the 2026 general election.
The bill updates the constitutional titles and descriptions of all three members of the Board of Public Works (Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer).
As the custodian of Maryland's official records and the Constitution, the modernization of constitutional text is directly relevant to their preservation and documentation mission.
Article IX (Militia and Military Affairs) is amended; the National Guard operates under the Adjutant General, whose constitutional description is being modernized.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates terminology for the Governor's Salary Commission (Article II) and the General Assembly Compensation Commission (Article III).
The bill updates language in Article II regarding the Governor's appointment power and the vetting/confirmation of civil and military officers.

bill_summary: The Vincent Anthony Fisher III Act narrows the eligibility for individuals to request a reduction in their prison sentences. It specifically targets individuals who were between the ages of 18 and 24 at the time of their offense and have served at least 20 years. The bill adds a list of serious offenses—including various forms of murder, manslaughter, homicide by vehicle, and child abuse resulting in death—that make an individual ineligible to file a motion for a sentence reduction.
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals who were aged 18 to 24 at the time of their offense, victims of violent crimes and their representatives, State's Attorneys, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. By narrowing eligibility for sentence reduction motions, the bill may prevent potential decreases in state incarceration expenditures and could reduce the volume of sentence modification hearings for the Maryland Judiciary.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new procedural requirements for the judiciary, including conducting hearings, evaluating specific factors for sentence reduction, and issuing written decisions. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides the necessary operational and technological support for these judicial processes.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly impacts the prison population by altering the eligibility for sentence reductions. The department is responsible for managing incarcerated individuals and providing records regarding their compliance with institutional rules and participation in educational or vocational programs, which are factors the court must consider.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals who would be filing these motions. The bill's alteration of eligibility criteria and procedural rules for sentence reductions directly impacts the caseload and legal strategies of public defenders.

The Office of the Attorney General represents the state in criminal appeals and provides legal counsel to state agencies and the judiciary regarding changes to the Criminal Procedure Article. They would be involved in interpreting and defending the new eligibility criteria.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this agency is responsible for advising the Governor on policies related to sentencing and recidivism, which are central themes of this bill.

The bill may have a fiscal impact on the state budget by potentially increasing the duration of incarceration for certain individuals (by making them ineligible for sentence reduction), which affects long-term fiscal planning and correctional expenditures managed by DBM.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the agencies responsible for corrections and public safety, and coordinates the high-level policy initiatives related to criminal justice reform and sentencing.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Department of Human Services from denying an application or reducing or terminating temporary cash assistance from an individual if the individual has good cause or an adequate reason for noncooperation with child support; defining "good cause" as circumstances in which cooperation with child support may be against the best interest of the child; requiring the Family Investment Program to determine that there is good cause for noncooperation with child support using certain criteria; etc.
Title: Family Investment Program - Temporary Cash Assistance - Good Cause and Adequate Reason Exceptions
Status: In the House - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Public Benefits -see also- Housing; MedAsst;  SupplNutrAsstP

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the Department of Human Services from denying, reducing, or terminating Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) for individuals who have 'good cause' or 'adequate reasons' for not cooperating with child support requirements. It establishes specific criteria for these exceptions—such as risks of harm, cases of incest or rape, or pending adoptions—and requires the department to notify applicants of their right to claim them. The bill also simplifies the application process by allowing oral statements to prove good cause and prohibiting the requirement of third-party verification or notarized documents.
stakeholders: Applicants for and recipients of Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA), their children, and the staff of the Family Investment Program and Child Support Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the Department of Human Services can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. There is no projected impact on State revenues or local governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency overseeing the Family Investment Program (FIP) and the Child Support Administration (CSA), DHS is responsible for implementing the new criteria for 'good cause' and 'adequate reason' exceptions and managing the resulting impacts on Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) eligibility and distribution.

The OAH adjudicates contested cases involving state agencies; changes to TCA eligibility, including new criteria for noncooperation exceptions, directly affect the administrative appeals process for residents whose benefits are denied, reduced, or terminated.

The bill's focus on Temporary Cash Assistance and preventing the reduction of benefits for families aligns with the GOC's specific mission to coordinate statewide efforts to reduce child poverty and improve outcomes for vulnerable children.
The Innovation Team is specifically charged with piloting initiatives to address child poverty and enhance economic mobility; this bill's reform of the TCA system directly supports these goals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Human Services and would likely assist in the development of regulations and legal interpretations of the new 'good cause' and 'adequate reason' criteria.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for the state's budget and would oversee the fiscal implications of changes to the Temporary Cash Assistance program managed by DHS.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates major policy initiatives, including the SERVE Act and poverty reduction strategies that this bill supports.

GOPI utilizes performance metrics to oversee the implementation of the state's priorities; reducing child poverty is a top priority, making the performance of the TCA program relevant to their oversight role.

Synopsis: Establishing the Interjurisdictional Safe Pathways Commission to identify, coordinate, and secure funding for safe pathways for students traveling to and from school; and requiring the Commission to report by December 1 annually to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly an assessment of funding opportunities, recommendations for infrastructure improvements, and progress in implementing interjurisdictional coordination.
Title: Education - Interjurisdictional Safe Pathways Commission - Establishment
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.
Public Works -see also- Brg&Tun; Hwys; PublBlgFac; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Interjurisdictional Safe Pathways Commission to coordinate and secure funding for physical infrastructure and educational programs that ensure students can travel safely to and from school. The commission is responsible for identifying gaps in existing infrastructure—such as sidewalks, bike lanes, and school zone signage—and developing a strategic plan to maximize federal, state, and private funding for these safety improvements.
stakeholders: Maryland public school students and their parents, local school systems, municipal management boards, and the State Departments of Transportation, Health, and Disabilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State general fund expenditures increase by $840,600 in fiscal 2027 to cover the costs of a contractual commission coordinator and a $750,000 comprehensive inventory of current safe pathways. Subsequent annual expenditures for staffing and operations are estimated to range between $105,300 and $119,500 through fiscal 2031. Local governments are expected to be able to coordinate with the commission using existing resources without a significant fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education is the primary agency responsible for staffing and supporting the new commission. The State Superintendent is a mandatory member and appoints seven additional members. The agency also carries the primary fiscal impact of $840,600 in the first year for staff and infrastructure inventory.

The Secretary of Transportation is a mandatory member of the commission. The bill directly relates to transportation infrastructure (sidewalks, bike lanes, pedestrian bridges) and involves evaluating State transportation funds.

The Secretary of Disabilities is a mandatory member. The bill specifically includes students and parents of children with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) in the commission membership and addresses the physical accessibility of school pathways.
The Governor is responsible for designating the Chair of the Commission and receives an annual report from the commission detailing funding opportunities and policy recommendations.
As a modal agency of MDOT, SHA is responsible for the design and maintenance of the non-toll roads and sidewalks that would comprise the 'safe pathways' identified by the commission.
The Secretary of Health is a mandatory member of the commission, reflecting the public health and safety dimensions of safe student travel.
The agency provides a coordinated approach to school safety and administers grants. The commission's focus on safe routes to school is an extension of school campus safety.
The MTA manages multi-modal transit systems. Safe pathways for students include the pedestrian and bike infrastructure that connects schools to public transit links.
DBM is responsible for the state budget and personnel. It will oversee the general fund expenditures and the creation of the contractual position required at MSDE to staff the commission.
The commission is explicitly tasked with identifying and securing federal and private grants. GGO assists state agencies in identifying and acquiring federal funding.
The IAC manages state review of school facilities and master plans. The safe pathways infrastructure is closely related to the capital improvement planning for school facilities.
The Office of Appointments will assist the Governor in vetting and recommending individuals for the specified appointed positions on the commission.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new interjurisdictional commission within the executive branch to address a specific government issue regarding student safety.
The commission's work aligns with this initiative's focus on sustainable growth, interagency collaboration, and the integration of land use and transportation planning.
The MVA oversees highway safety initiatives and would be a stakeholder in programs promoting safe pedestrian and bike routes for students.
The office coordinates support networks for the well-being of Maryland's children, and safe travel to school is a key component of youth safety and access to education.
The team incubates novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and child welfare; improvements in school accessibility could impact these priorities.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain certificated and noncertificated public school employees, library system employees, and employer organizations have the right to engage in a strike; repealing the authority of the Public Employee Relations Board to deny or revoke an employee organization's certification as exclusive representative of public employees in State and local government under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Collective Bargaining - Public Employees - Revocation of Certification and School and Library Employees' Right to Strike
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/11 at 1:35 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the right to strike for certificated and noncertificated public school employees and public library employees, prohibiting employers from taking retaliatory actions such as permanent replacement, discrimination, or lockouts. Additionally, it repeals the authority of the Public Employee Relations Board to revoke an employee organization's certification as an exclusive representative for willful failure to comply with collective bargaining laws.
stakeholders: Certificated and noncertificated public school employees, public library employees, employee organizations (unions), local boards of education, and public library systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no impact on State finances as the Public Employee Relations Board can implement it using existing resources. The fiscal impact on local governments is indeterminate; while there is no direct financial mandate, local school and library systems could face significant operational and legal costs if strikes occur, though the timing and frequency of such events cannot be predicted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the authority of the Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) by repealing its power to revoke the certification of employee organizations. PERB is also the primary body responsible for adjudicating the impasse and arbitration processes amended by the bill.

As the agency responsible for leadership and oversight of Maryland's public education system, MSDE is significantly impacted by legislation that grants the right to strike to certificated and noncertificated public school employees across the 24 local school systems.

The Maryland State Library Agency oversees the state's public library systems. The bill establishes the right to strike for library system employees and prohibits library employers from taking retaliatory actions, directly affecting the agency's coordination and leadership responsibilities.

As a state agency providing public education services, its staff likely fall within the scope of public school employees granted the right to strike under this bill, impacting the school's operations and labor relations.

The OAG serves as the legal counsel to the State, the Department of Education, and the Public Employee Relations Board. It would be responsible for interpreting the new strike rights and defending the state in potential litigation involving labor disputes or anti-discrimination claims.

DBM is the central personnel agency for the State. The bill's amendments to Title 22 of the State Government Article regarding strike prohibitions and the removal of the Public Employee Relations Board's certification revocation authority affect the broader state personnel and collective bargaining framework.

The Public Employee Relations Board (PERB) oversees collective bargaining for USM employees. The bill's repeal of PERB's authority to revoke union certification applies to all public sector labor relations under PERB's jurisdiction, including those within the University System.

As a public university whose labor relations are overseen by the Public Employee Relations Board, Morgan State is impacted by the bill's changes to PERB's enforcement powers and the broader public employee collective bargaining statutes.

As a public college whose collective bargaining is governed by the statutes overseen by the Public Employee Relations Board, the college is affected by changes to the Board's authority and the general state policies regarding public employee strikes.

Authorized strikes by public school employees could have significant operational impacts on school security and the implementation of safety protocols, which fall under this agency's coordination and training mandates.

Synopsis: Requiring the Charles County Board of Education to provide at least 10 years' notice and hold a certain public hearing before taking any action that results in a certain displacement of a company that has been providing student bus transportation services in Charles County; and requiring the Board of Education to provide written notice by registered mail at least 2 years before the displacement of a company that has been providing student bus transportation services.
Title: Charles County - Student Bus Transportation Providers - Provider Displacement
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Ways and Means; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Charles County Board of Education to provide written notice and hold a public hearing before displacing any company currently providing student bus transportation services. It further mandates a two-year advance notice period before displacement occurs, or alternatively, requires the board to compensate the displaced company with an amount equal to two years of its gross receipts. The bill excludes displacement for cause, safety violations, or breach of contract.
stakeholders: Charles County Board of Education, private student bus transportation contractors in Charles County, and the Charles County Public School System.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal impact. Local school expenditures in Charles County may increase by a significant but indeterminate amount. By requiring a two-year notice for displacement, the bill could delay the school system's ability to transition to in-house services, which was estimated to save over 1600000 dollars annually. Additionally, bypassing the two-year notice period would require the school system to pay a contractor its gross receipts for the previous 24-month period.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new section to the Education Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland specifically regulating student bus transportation policies. As the agency responsible for the oversight and leadership of the state's public education system, including 24 local school systems, the Department of Education manages pupil transportation standards and reporting.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and the Department of Education. They would be responsible for interpreting the legal definitions of 'displacement' and 'cause' established in this bill and ensuring the new requirements comply with existing state law.

The Office of Legislative Audits conducts performance and compliance audits of local school systems. This bill introduces specific statutory mandates regarding public hearings and notice periods that the Charles County Board of Education must follow, which would be subject to future audit review.

The bill regulates the displacement of private contractors in favor of school board-provided services. Because such a transition would move services 'in-house' and create new public sector positions, the Public Employee Relations Board would have jurisdiction over the resulting labor relations and collective bargaining for those new employees.

The Department of Budget and Management tracks fiscal impacts on local government units and oversees state personnel policy. This bill imposes a local government mandate that may lead to increased school system expenditures, which DBM monitors in the context of state-local fiscal relations.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and local legislation. The Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the Department of Education, which is the primary state entity concerned with the bill's implementation.

Synopsis: Authorizing the offer and use of certain time-of-use rates and products relating to residential electricity supply and residential retail gas supply, including offering the rates for a term greater than a certain number of months; authorizing the sale and purchase of accounts receivable for certain products; authorizing certain energy resource aggregators to act without the direction of an electric company; etc.
Title: Electricity and Retail Gas Supply - Customer Choice, Consumer Protection, and Green Power (Retail Energy Modernization and Consumer Choice Act)
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.
Renewable Energy Sources -see also- Geotherm; Solar; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: The Retail Energy Modernization and Consumer Choice Act authorizes residential electricity and gas suppliers to offer specialized products including time-of-use rates, contracts exceeding 12 months, and energy products bundled with emissions-free certificates or distributed energy resources. It creates exemptions from existing price caps for these specific products and mandates the Public Service Commission to establish regulations for consolidated billing, cybersecurity standards, and expedited interconnection procedures for distributed energy resources.
stakeholders: Residential electricity and gas customers, energy suppliers, electric and gas utility companies, and distributed energy resource aggregators.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as the formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill imposes administrative and regulatory mandates on the Public Service Commission to develop new rules by 2027 and requires electric and gas companies to implement consolidated billing and nondiscriminatory interconnection procedures, which likely involve significant implementation and operational costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body for electricity and retail gas supply in Maryland. The bill explicitly requires the PSC to adopt several sets of regulations, including those for consolidated billing, accounts receivable purchase protocols, cybersecurity standards, and interconnection procedures for distributed energy resources.

The Office of the People's Counsel is the statutory advocate for residential utility consumers in Maryland. Since this bill directly alters the pricing, terms, and consumer protection regulations for residential electricity and gas supply, the agency will be heavily involved in the resulting Public Service Commission proceedings.

The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) advises on state energy policy and manages renewable energy programs. The bill's provisions regarding 'green power' products, emissions-free energy certificates, and distributed energy resources align closely with MEA's mission to promote renewable energy and efficiency.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Public Service Commission and enforces state consumer protection laws. The bill introduces new consumer protection rules and exemptions for energy marketing that may require legal interpretation or enforcement action by the OAG.

The Department of General Services is mentioned specifically in the bill as being exempt from certain regulations regarding residential electricity and green power sales, maintaining its current authority under existing law to manage certain energy sales and procurement.

The bill requires the Public Service Commission to establish cybersecurity standards and information exchange protocols for electricity suppliers and distributed energy resource aggregators, which falls under the broader expertise and strategic mandate of the Department of Information Technology.

The bill defines and regulates 'emissions-free energy' and products related to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. As the agency responsible for environmental protection and air quality, MDE is relevant to the environmental standards applied to 'green' energy products.

Synopsis: Requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to issue a single registration plate to all classes of vehicles; and prohibiting persons who are issued a Class L (historic) registration plate from violating the terms of issuance.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Registration Plates
Status: In the House - Unfavorable Report by Environment and Transportation; Withdrawn

NarrowSubjects.Name: Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
License Plates -see also- Motor Vehicle Registration

bill_summary: House Bill 1495 requires the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration to issue only one registration plate for all classes of vehicles, rather than two. The bill specifies that registration plates must be displayed on the front of tractors and on the rear of all other vehicles. It also prohibits historic vehicle owners from knowingly violating their registration terms, with a warning system established for first-time offenses.
stakeholders: Maryland vehicle owners, the Motor Vehicle Administration, and state and local law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in a decrease in state expenditures for the Motor Vehicle Administration due to reduced costs associated with manufacturing and distributing one registration plate per vehicle instead of two. There may also be an impact on law enforcement efficiency and revenue from automated license plate readers. Specific dollar estimates are not provided in the bill text, and a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided document.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the MVA to change its vehicle registration process by issuing a single registration plate instead of two for all vehicle classes, and requires the MVA to verify compliance for Class L vehicle violations.
As the parent agency of the MVA, MDOT is responsible for the overall management of the state's transportation network and the administrative transition to a single-plate system.

The bill impacts law enforcement's ability to identify vehicles from both the front and rear. It also explicitly requires police officers to report violations of the new registration requirements to the MVA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: License plates in Maryland are typically manufactured by Maryland Correctional Enterprises, a program within DPSCS. Moving from two plates to one for most vehicles would significantly reduce production volume and operational revenue/expenditure for this unit.

The MDTA operates toll facilities that utilize license plate recognition cameras for enforcement and billing; the removal of front license plates on many vehicles may impact the efficiency and accuracy of these systems.
The bill establishes a new violation and warning system for Class L (historic) vehicles, which must be tracked through the state's judicial and administrative hearing systems.

The transition to a single-plate system will have a notable fiscal impact on the state budget, specifically regarding reduced manufacturing costs and potential changes in registration fees or processing costs managed by DBM.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the MDOT and MVA and would be responsible for advising on the regulatory changes required to implement a single-plate system and enforcing the new Class L vehicle terms.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "vulnerable individual" to exclude an individual who is riding a motorcycle for purposes of the prohibition on causing the serious physical injury or death of a vulnerable individual as a result of operating a motor vehicle in violation of certain rules of the road.
Title: Vehicle Laws – Causing Serious Injury or Death of Vulnerable Individual
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/12 at 1:00 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'vulnerable individual' under Maryland's vehicle laws by excluding motorcyclists. By removing motorcycles from this category, the specific criminal and administrative penalties for causing serious physical injury or death to a vulnerable individual while violating traffic laws—which include mandatory court appearances, fines up to $2,000, community service, and driver's license suspensions—will no longer apply to incidents involving motorcyclists.
responsible_party: Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Motorcyclists, motor vehicle operators, the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration, and the Maryland court system
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is not included in the provided text, so specific aggregate dollar estimates are unavailable. However, the bill may result in an indeterminate decrease in State fine revenue (up to $2,000 per violation) and a reduction in administrative expenditures for the Motor Vehicle Administration due to fewer mandatory license suspension proceedings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the agency overseeing the state's transportation network and the Transportation Article of the Maryland Code, MDOT is directly responsible for the policy and implementation of vehicle laws. The bill specifically alters definitions within the rules of the road that MDOT and its administrations manage.

The bill explicitly tasks 'The Administration' (referring to the MVA) with the mandatory suspension of driver's licenses for individuals convicted of causing serious injury or death to a vulnerable individual. The MVA will need to update its systems and procedures to reflect the change in definition for 'vulnerable individual.'

The bill mandates that individuals charged with this violation must appear in court and may not prepay fines. It also outlines specific sentencing options for the court, including fines, community service, and safety courses, directly affecting judicial operations and case processing.

As the primary law enforcement agency for enforcing motor vehicle laws and ensuring traffic safety on state highways, MSP officers would be responsible for charging individuals under this specific section of the Transportation Article. Changes to the definitions of offenses impact enforcement protocols and reporting.

OAH provides an impartial hearing process for contested cases involving state agencies, including driver's license suspensions initiated by the MVA. Mandatory license suspensions resulting from this bill could lead to an increase in administrative hearings.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the MDOT, MVA, and MSP, and would be responsible for advising these agencies on the legal interpretation and enforcement of the revised definition of 'vulnerable individual' and the associated penalties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates public safety strategies and advises the Governor on criminal justice matters. Changes to vehicle laws involving serious injury or death fall under their policy purview regarding public safety and recidivism reduction.

Synopsis: Requiring Charles County to establish a rent increase limit for units occupied by seniors that is no greater than the Consumer Price Index; and defining "senior" as an individual who is at least the age required to receive full Social Security retirement benefits.
Title: Charles County - Rent Stabilization - Seniors
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/12 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect

bill_summary: This bill requires Charles County to establish an annual rent increase limit for rental units occupied by seniors, defined as individuals who have reached the age for full Social Security retirement benefits. The annual increase is limited to the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for the Washington Metropolitan Area.
stakeholders: Senior renters and landlords in Charles County.
fiscal_impact_summary: Charles County is required to implement rent stabilization for seniors, likely resulting in administrative expenditures for the county. Since no formal Fiscal Note was provided with specific figures, the exact financial impact is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This bill directly concerns the economic security and housing stability of Maryland's senior population. As an agency dedicated to protecting the rights and improving the quality of life for older adults, the Department of Aging is heavily impacted by policies that regulate senior-specific housing costs.

The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development is the state's primary agency for affordable housing. While this bill mandates action at the county level, state housing policy and community vitality are directly influenced by rent stabilization measures, making this relevant to the agency's overarching mission.

The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to state agencies and enforces consumer protection laws. Changes to rental property law in the Real Property Article require legal oversight, interpretation, and potentially enforcement by the OAG to ensure compliance with state standards.

Landlord-tenant disputes and eviction proceedings are adjudicated within the state's District Courts. Establishing a specific rent increase limit for a specific demographic in Charles County creates a new legal standard that judges and court personnel must apply during judicial proceedings.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives. As this bill requires the Governor's signature to become law and involves a local mandate that could set a precedent for statewide senior housing policy, it is relevant to the executive's policy coordination role.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County from issuing a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license to a specific establishment with retail floor space of more 3,500 square feet; prohibiting the Board from issuing a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license for use at certain restaurants, subject to certain grandfather provisions; and prohibiting the Board from issuing more than one Class A beer, wine, and liquor license for use in a councilmanic kjdistrict.
Title: Wicomico County - Class A Beer, Wine, and Liquor License - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 2/23 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill modifies the regulations for Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Wicomico County. It prohibits the issuance of these licenses to establishments with more than 3,500 square feet of retail floor space and restricts the issuance of new licenses to restaurants (Class B license holders) beginning July 1, 2026, while allowing existing licenses to be renewed. Furthermore, it limits the distribution of these licenses to no more than one per councilmanic district and maintains a countywide cap of three total licenses.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County
stakeholders: Current and prospective alcoholic beverage license holders in Wicomico County, including restaurant owners and retail establishment operators.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill maintains an annual license fee of $4,400 and keeps the maximum number of Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Wicomico County at three. While it introduces new restrictions on establishment size and eligibility for restaurant owners, the cap on the total number of licenses suggests the overall fiscal impact on license revenue will be negligible. Specific dollar estimates for the net fiscal impact are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller is the primary state agency responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state revenues. This bill directly alters alcoholic beverages licensing requirements, fees, and operational restrictions for Wicomico County, which falls under the Comptroller's regulatory and oversight purview.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to all state agencies, boards, and commissions. This includes the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County, which will require legal guidance on implementing the new prohibitions and grandfathering provisions established by this bill.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in appointing individuals to state boards and commissions, including the Board of License Commissioners for Wicomico County, which is the body tasked with issuing the licenses regulated by this bill.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the state's budget and revenue estimation. As this bill modifies license fees ($4,400 per license) and the number of available licenses, it may have a fiscal impact on state or local revenues that DBM monitors.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch, including the local boards of license commissioners created under state law, and holds the ultimate authority for appointing the members who will enforce these new regulations.

Synopsis: Increasing from one-third to one-half the maximum portion of a home improvement contract price that a person may receive as a deposit before or at the time of execution of the home improvement contract.
Title: Business Regulation - Home Improvement Contracts - Deposits
Status: In the House - Hearing canceled

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the maximum deposit amount a contractor may receive for a home improvement contract from one-third to one-half of the total contract price, payable at or before the time the contract is executed.
responsible_party: Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC) within the Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Home improvement contractors, small business owners in the construction and remodeling industry, and Maryland homeowners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and there is no local fiscal impact. However, it is expected to have a meaningful impact on small businesses by improving their cash flow and working capital through the collection of larger up-front deposits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Home Improvement Commission (MHIC), which is a unit within the Department of Labor, directly licenses and regulates home improvement contractors. This bill modifies the statutory limit on deposits for home improvement contracts, which the MHIC is responsible for enforcing.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Maryland Home Improvement Commission and would be involved in legal interpretations and enforcement actions related to contract deposit violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The fiscal note indicates a meaningful impact on small businesses, many of which are home improvement contractors. This office tracks policies affecting the economic opportunities and cash flow of small, minority, and women-owned businesses.

The Office of Administrative Hearings adjudicates contested cases for state agencies, including the Department of Labor. Disputes or enforcement actions regarding home improvement contract regulations, such as deposit limits, may be heard by Administrative Law Judges.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a unit of State government that is required by law to adopt regulations to implement a program that is authorized or required under State law from collecting any fee or other payment under that program until the unit finalizes adoption of the regulations that implement the program.
Title: State Agencies - Adoption of Regulations - Required
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/11 at 1:35 p.m.

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: This bill prohibits any unit of State government from collecting fees or other payments for a program authorized or required under State law until the agency has finalized the adoption of the regulations necessary to implement that program.
stakeholders: Maryland State agencies and individuals or entities subject to State program fees and payments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues across multiple fund types may decrease beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent that agencies are prohibited from collecting fees until associated regulations are finalized. The exact financial impact is indeterminate as it depends on future programs and the timeline of regulation adoption. There is no anticipated impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief financial officer and revenue collector, the Comptroller is impacted by any bill that affects the timing, legality, and flow of state revenue collection for the programs it regulates.

The agency conducts regulatory activities regarding animal health and food quality that involve fees; the bill requires that the regulations for these programs be finalized before any payments can be collected.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM is responsible for estimating revenues and overseeing budget execution; the bill's potential to decrease or delay state revenues across multiple funds is a major concern.
MSDE oversees educational standards and educator certifications which involve fee-based programs that would be subject to the bill's regulatory adoption requirements.
The department oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and coordinates emergency services; the collection of fees for these programs would be contingent upon finalized regulatory adoption.
The department noted specific concerns regarding the bill's impact on its ability to collect fees established by emergency regulations, as 'finalized' adoption might exclude emergency measures.
DHCD manages community revitalization and energy efficiency programs that may involve fees; the bill ensures these fees cannot be collected until the regulatory framework is fully established.
DHS administers social services and aid programs that may include administrative fees; the bill prohibits such collection until the governing regulations are finalized.

bill_summary: This bill legalizes the purchase, possession, and use of consumer fireworks by individuals at least 18 years old, subject to specific safety and location restrictions, such as distances from structures and livestock. While a specific total revenue estimate is not provided in the bill text, the act creates a new revenue stream for state emergency funds and the general fund. bill_summary: This bill establishes comprehensive requirements for the prevention, detection, and enforcement of unemployment insurance (UI) fraud. It mandates the use of multifactor authentication for the Department of Labor's online UI portals, requires claimants to provide specific forms of identification, and necessitates mandatory reviews of claims involving duplicate bank accounts, addresses, or out-of-state IP addresses. Additionally, the bill increases the monetary penalty for fraud from 15% to 20%, extends UI disqualification for fraudulent claimants to 10 years, allows for the recovery of overpayments through State income tax withholding, and requires the referral of fraud cases to law enforcement. It also mandates the termination of government employees or contractors found to have committed UI fraud.
stakeholders: Unemployment insurance claimants, employers, the Maryland Department of Labor, law enforcement agencies, and government employees or contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to result in an indeterminate increase in State revenue due to the increased fraud penalty (from 15% to 20%) and the authorization to recover overpaid benefits through State income tax refund withholding. State expenditures will increase to implement technological requirements like multifactor authentication, conduct mandated claim reviews, and fulfill new annual reporting obligations. Local fiscal impact may include increased costs for county law enforcement agencies tasked with investigating and prosecuting referred fraud cases. Specific dollar estimates from a formal Fiscal Note were not available in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for administering the state's unemployment insurance program. This bill directly mandates new operational requirements for the department, including multifactor authentication, specific claim review procedures, annual reporting on fraud, and enhanced enforcement and recovery mechanisms.

The bill authorizes the recovery of overpaid unemployment benefits through State income tax withholding and references procedures for withholding tax refunds under the Tax – General Article, which the Comptroller oversees as the state's principal tax collector.

DBM oversees the Central Collection Unit (CCU), which the bill explicitly authorizes to collect unemployment insurance overpayments caused by fraud. Additionally, DBM is the central personnel agency for the state; the bill's mandate to terminate government employees who commit unemployment fraud directly impacts its personnel management and policy duties.

The bill specifies that a final determination of unemployment fraud is grounds for immediate termination of a state employee, notwithstanding any terms of a collective bargaining agreement. As the agency responsible for administering collective bargaining and labor laws for state employees, PERB would be impacted by this statutory override of labor contracts.

The bill requires the use of multifactor authentication for the Department of Labor's publicly accessible websites and online portals. As the agency responsible for the state's information technology strategy and cybersecurity standards, DoIT would likely be involved in the technical implementation and security oversight of these requirements.

The bill discusses 'final determinations' after the exhaustion of administrative appeals. The OAH conducts hearings for contested cases involving state agencies, including the Department of Labor. New fraud review protocols and disqualification criteria would likely result in an increased volume or change in the nature of administrative hearings handled by this agency.

The bill requires the Secretary of Labor to refer final determinations of unemployment fraud to appropriate law enforcement agencies for prosecution. As the primary state law enforcement agency responsible for criminal investigations, MSP is a likely recipient of these referrals.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Comptroller. The bill specifically mentions the Attorney General's role in advising on the validity of debts before they are certified for tax refund withholding.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the Secretary of Labor. The bill requires the Department of Labor to submit an annual report on fraud prevention and enforcement efforts to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP coordinates the state's criminal justice strategies and manages funds for law enforcement. The bill's emphasis on referring fraud for prosecution aligns with GOCPP's mission to reduce crime and recidivism through interagency collaboration.

Synopsis: Renaming and transferring the State Clearinghouse for Missing Children to be the State Clearinghouse for Missing Persons; requiring the Department of State Police to study the Department's capacity to report about persons who have disappeared from, or are thought to be located in, Maryland to the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System; and requiring the Department to submit its findings to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Public Safety - State Clearinghouse for Missing Persons
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: This bill renames the State Clearinghouse for Missing Children to the State Clearinghouse for Missing Persons and expands its scope to include all missing individuals. It requires the Department of State Police to collect and distribute information and statistics on all missing persons and mandates a study and report on the department's ability to provide information to the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System by December 1, 2026.
stakeholders: Missing persons, families of missing persons, Maryland law enforcement agencies, and volunteer search organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, so specific dollar estimates are unavailable. However, the bill's requirements for the Department of State Police to expand the Clearinghouse's scope and conduct a study suggest potential administrative and operational expenditure increases.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Department of State Police to operate the State Clearinghouse for Missing Persons, publish statistics, develop fingerprinting programs, and conduct a study on reporting to the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System.
The Governor's Office is the mandated recipient of the Department of State Police's report regarding the capacity to report to the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System.

The bill moves the clearinghouse's statutory authority from the Family Law Article (traditionally associated with child and adult protective services) to the Public Safety Article and expands its scope from children to all persons, impacting the populations DHS serves.

Expanding the clearinghouse from 'children' to 'persons' includes older adults and seniors, which aligns with the Department's mission to protect and advocate for Maryland's elderly population, particularly those who may go missing due to cognitive conditions.
The expansion of the clearinghouse to include all persons directly involves individuals with disabilities who may be at risk and require coordinated state services for location and recovery.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this office is relevant to the policy shift of expanding the state's missing persons reporting and tracking capabilities.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the Maryland State Police and would provide legal guidance on the transfer of statutory authority and the regulatory requirements of the new State Clearinghouse for Missing Persons.

Synopsis: Requiring, if a merchant rounds up the price of a cash transaction for a good or service in a certain manner, the merchant to remit to the Comptroller the difference between the total price the customer is required to pay after the rounding occurs and the price before the rounding occurs; and requiring the Comptroller to distribute certain revenue to the General Fund of the State.

Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds

bill_summary: This bill requires merchants who round up the total price of a cash transaction to the nearest 5 cents to remit the difference between the rounded price and the original price to the State Comptroller, provided the customer did not consent to the rounding for a donation. The Comptroller is required to distribute this revenue to the State General Fund.
stakeholders: Merchants, cash-paying customers, and the State of Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill will result in an indeterminate increase in State General Fund revenue from remitted cash transaction rounding differences. Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because no formal Fiscal Note was provided with the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief financial officer and principal tax collector, the Comptroller is explicitly tasked by the bill with prescribing the manner of remittance for the rounded amounts and distributing the collected revenue to the General Fund.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Comptroller, and would likely be involved in interpreting the requirements of the bill or representing the state in legal challenges regarding merchant remittance.
DBM is the principal fiscal agency responsible for estimating revenues and overseeing budget execution; this bill introduces a new revenue stream for the General Fund.
The Treasurer's Office is responsible for receiving and distributing state funds; it would manage the funds collected under this bill once remitted to the General Fund.

The bill impacts every 'merchant' engaged in the sale of goods or services in Maryland. The Department of Commerce, as the primary business development agency, may need to coordinate with the Comptroller to inform businesses of the new regulation.

As the administrative body that hears appeals regarding final decisions of taxing authorities, the Maryland Tax Court would have jurisdiction over disputes between merchants and the Comptroller regarding the remittance of rounded cash transaction differences.

Synopsis: Authorizing and empowering the County Commissioners of Calvert County, from time to time, to borrow not more than $80,957,080 to finance the construction, improvement, or development of certain public buildings, roads, and facilities in Calvert County, and to effect such borrowing by the issuance and sale at public or private sale of its general obligation bonds in like par amount; etc.

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Calvert County Commissioners to borrow up to $80,957,080 through the issuance of general obligation bonds to finance the construction, improvement, or development of various public facilities, including public buildings, roads, and storm drainage systems.
stakeholders: Residents and taxpayers of Calvert County, Calvert County Government, and users of local public facilities such as schools and senior centers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Calvert County will receive up to $80,957,080 in bond proceeds for capital projects. The fiscal note estimates that annual debt service expenditures will increase by approximately $6,300,000 (roughly $4.6 million for 15-year bonds and $1.7 million for 25-year bonds). The bill has no impact on Maryland State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law, which provides the necessary legislative authorization for Calvert County to borrow funds and issue general obligation bonds for public facilities.

The bill explicitly exempts the authorized bonds and the interest derived from them from all Maryland state and local taxation, which is relevant to the Comptroller's role as the state's principal tax collector and revenue administrator.

The bond proceeds are specifically intended to fund renovations at the Calvert Pines Senior Center, which aligns with the department's mission to oversee programs and facilities that improve the quality of life for older adults.

The bill authorizes funding for several public school projects, including Northern Middle School and Southern Middle School, which are part of the state's public education system overseen by the department.

The bond authority includes $1.5 million for local health department facilities, which are regulated and overseen by the Maryland Department of Health as part of the state's public health infrastructure.

A significant portion of the bond request (over $26 million) is allocated for wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) upgrades, sewer collection, and landfill projects, all of which fall under the environmental and water quality regulatory authority of the Department of the Environment.

The bill authorizes funding for county road paving and construction projects, including the Prince Frederick Loop Road and Boyd's Turn Road, which connect to the broader state transportation network managed by MDOT.

The bill facilitates the funding and execution of public school capital improvement projects, such as Northern and Southern Middle Schools, which are specifically overseen by the Commission to ensure facility sufficiency.

Synopsis: Altering the salaries of the County Commissioners of Calvert County, the president and members of the Calvert County Board of Education, and the County Treasurer of Calvert County; repealing a provision that the salary of State's Attorneys shall take effect at the beginning of the elected term of office and may not increase during the term of office; altering certain retirement benefits for the County Treasurer of Calvert County; providing that the Act does not apply to the salary or compensation of certain incumbent officials; etc.

bill_summary: This bill increases the annual salaries for several Calvert County officials, including the President and members of the Board of County Commissioners, the President and members of the County Board of Education, and the County Treasurer. It also adjusts retirement health benefits for County Commissioners and aligns the County Treasurer's pension benefits with those of other county employees. Additionally, it repeals a restriction that prevented the State's Attorney's salary from increasing during a term, allowing it to fluctuate with the salary of a circuit court judge.
responsible_party: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners
stakeholders: Calvert County Board of County Commissioners, Calvert County Board of Education, Calvert County Treasurer, Calvert County State's Attorney, and Calvert County taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, Calvert County expenditures are expected to increase by approximately $52,300 in fiscal 2027 and by a minimum of $100,900 annually thereafter. Specifically, the costs are estimated at $106,800 in fiscal 2029 and $112,700 in fiscal 2030. These estimates account for salary increases but do not reflect potential additional costs from increased fringe benefits or specific pension benefit changes.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office is responsible for signing or vetoing legislation passed by the Maryland General Assembly, including this bill which impacts the salaries and benefits of local Calvert County officials.

The bill amends Section 3–303 of the Education Article to alter the annual compensation for the president and members of the Calvert County Board of Education. The Department of Education oversees the state's 24 local school systems, including their leadership structure and compensation standards.

The bill links the salary of the Calvert County State’s Attorney to the salary of a circuit court judge. The Administrative Office of the Courts provides financial and operational support to the judicial branch, including the management of judicial salaries used as the benchmark in this legislation.

The bill modifies the pension benefits for the Calvert County Treasurer to align with those of other county employees. Because many Maryland counties participate in the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) as participating governmental units, the SRA may be responsible for the administration and oversight of these modified benefits.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Governor and the General Assembly, reviewing legislation for constitutionality and legal sufficiency, particularly regarding local government authority and public official compensation.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law establishing that certain noncompete and conflict of interest provisions in certain employment contracts are null and void as being against the public policy of the State to employees of certain employers that relocate majority of its employees or principal place of business outside the State.

bill_summary: This bill expands existing laws regarding noncompete and conflict of interest clauses to include employees of certain large employers that relocate outside of Maryland. Specifically, it renders noncompete and conflict of interest provisions null and void for employees whose employer previously had more than 30 employees in Maryland and, after the employee's departure, relocates the majority of its workforce or its principal place of business to a location outside the state.
stakeholders: Maryland employees, Maryland employers with more than 30 employees that may relocate out of state, and legal practitioners specializing in employment law.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note is absent from the provided text, and specific dollar estimates for revenue or expenditure changes are unavailable. The bill's financial impact is primarily private, affecting the enforceability of employment contracts for relocating businesses. It does not explicitly mandate new State spending or change existing tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for enforcing Maryland's labor and employment laws. This bill directly amends the Labor and Employment Article regarding the validity of noncompete and conflict of interest clauses in employment contracts.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies on the interpretation and enforcement of state laws. It would likely represent the state's interest in defending the public policy regarding voided noncompete clauses.

The Department of Commerce is Maryland's primary economic development agency. The bill's provisions regarding employer relocation outside the state directly impact the business climate and the agency's mission to retain and expand companies within Maryland.

The Maryland Judicial Branch will be responsible for adjudicating civil disputes where employment contracts containing noncompete or conflict of interest clauses are challenged as null and void under this new provision.

The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and legislative initiatives. This bill introduces a significant shift in labor policy by linking the validity of private employment contracts to an employer's relocation status.

The bill amends Section 3-716 of the Labor and Employment Article, which specifically includes noncompete regulations for health care professionals licensed under the Health Occupations Article, a sector regulated by the Department of Health.
The bill modifies the section of the Labor and Employment code that explicitly governs noncompete clauses for veterinary practitioners and technicians licensed under the Agriculture Article.

MEDCO supports the state's economy by providing services for business retention and expansion. The bill's focus on employer relocation and its legal consequences for employment agreements is relevant to their economic mission.

The board coordinates partnerships and strategies to ensure residents have access to employment. Policies that nullify noncompete clauses promote labor mobility, which is a key interest of the state's workforce strategy.
