Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: This bill authorizes the county councils of charter counties, excluding Prince George's County, to exceed property tax rate or revenue limitations set within their county charters through a simple majority vote. Any additional revenue generated by exceeding these limits must be specifically dedicated to funding the county's public safety budget.
responsible_party: County councils of Maryland charter counties (excluding Prince George's County)
stakeholders: Property owners in Maryland charter counties and county public safety agencies including police, fire, and emergency services.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no impact on State finances. Local property tax revenues could increase in charter counties with existing tax limitations (Anne Arundel, Montgomery, Talbot, and Wicomico) if their councils approve rates exceeding charter limits for public safety purposes. Based on fiscal 2027 estimates, a one-cent property tax rate increase across these four eligible counties could generate approximately $37,650,091. Prince George's County is explicitly excluded from the provisions of this bill.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires any charter county that exercises the authority to exceed its property tax limits for public safety to submit an annual report to the Governor by December 31, detailing the tax rate set, revenues generated, and the appropriation of those revenues.

The bill amends Section 5-104 of the Education Article, which currently allows counties to exceed tax limits for education funding. The amendment specifically creates an exception so that excess property tax revenues intended for public safety budgets do not have to be appropriated to the local board of education.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is directly related to the funding of local public safety budgets, which falls under this office's mission to coordinate public safety strategies and advise the Governor on criminal justice policy and resource allocation.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the state on the implementation of laws. This bill involves complex interactions between state law and local charter limitations, which may require legal interpretation or defense.

As the highest level of administrative review for tax-related disputes, the Maryland Tax Court may hear appeals regarding the application or legality of property tax rates set by counties using the new authority granted by this bill.

Synopsis: Requiring certain health systems to comply with certain insurance provisions regarding notice of termination of contracts; altering the notification requirements a carrier is required to provide an enrollee regarding changes to the carrier's provider panel; altering the notice requirements a carrier is required to provide to the Insurance Commissioner for certain material changes to the carrier's provider panel; requiring certain notice if a carrier and health system intend to terminate certain contracts; etc.
Title: Health Insurance - Material Changes to Provider Networks - Notification and Special Enrollment Period
Status: In the Senate - Returned Passed

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires health insurance carriers and health systems to provide advance notice regarding the termination of provider contracts and expands requirements for notifying enrollees when primary care or behavioral health providers are removed from a provider panel. It mandates a 90-day transitional period where providers must continue to serve enrollees under existing contract terms and establishes a 90-day special enrollment period for individuals whose regular providers have been terminated from their health plan's panel.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE)
stakeholders: Health insurance enrollees, primary care and behavioral health providers, health systems and hospitals, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. While the bill allows the Insurance Commissioner to impose a fine of $5,000 per day for carriers that fail to file required access plan updates, these penalties are not expected to have a material impact on State revenues. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is the primary regulatory agency for this legislation. The Insurance Commissioner is responsible for receiving notifications of provider terminations, reviewing access plan updates, developing a new uniform form for transitional care requests, and enforcing daily fines of $5,000 for non-compliance.

The bill establishes a new Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for individuals enrolled in the Individual Exchange who are patients of a provider that is terminated from a plan's provider panel. MHBE is responsible for administering these enrollment periods.

The bill adds requirements to the Health-General Article for health systems (hospitals and their affiliates) regarding contract terminations. It also specifically impacts notification requirements for behavioral health providers and applies to Medicaid Managed Care Organizations (MCOs) which are overseen by the department.

As the agency responsible for managing state employee benefits and personnel policies, DBM is impacted because material changes to carrier provider networks may affect the administration and cost of health plans provided to state employees.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Maryland Insurance Administration and the Department of Health. It would be responsible for representing the state in any legal challenges to the new regulations or enforcement of the bill's penalty provisions.

OAH is relevant because it would likely adjudicate contested cases resulting from the Maryland Insurance Administration's imposition of fines on carriers that fail to file required access plan updates.

The Governor oversees the executive branch departments implementing this bill (MIA, MDH) and signs the legislation into law. The bill also impacts broader health policy initiatives managed by the executive branch.

Synopsis: Altering the annual salary of the Sheriff of Frederick County to be $175,000 for calendar year 2027; and altering the annual salary of the Sheriff of Frederick County to be 82.5% of the State's Attorney for Frederick County's annual salary including any increments and salary adjustments authorized under certain provisions of law for calendar year 2028 and each subsequent calendar year.
Title: Frederick County - Sheriff - Salary
Status: In the House - Hearing 4/01 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill alters the annual salary of the Sheriff of Frederick County. It sets the salary at $125,000 for calendar year 2026, $175,000 for calendar year 2027, and 82.5% of the Frederick County State’s Attorney’s annual salary for calendar year 2028 and thereafter. In accordance with constitutional requirements, the salary changes take effect at the beginning of the next term of office.
stakeholders: The Sheriff of Frederick County and Frederick County residents
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. Frederick County expenditures are projected to increase by approximately $33,750 in fiscal 2027 and by at least $92,011 annually thereafter due to the mandated salary increase and associated fringe benefits. There is no impact on county revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General (OAG) provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and executive branch. The fiscal note for this bill specifically references a legal interpretation from the Counsel to the General Assembly (a unit of the OAG) regarding the constitutionality of mid-term salary adjustments for public officers under Article III, Section 35 of the Maryland Constitution.

The bill amends the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland, which is a core statutory area for the Judicial Branch. Additionally, the Sheriff serves as a constitutional officer of the court, providing security and service of process, while the Administrative Office of the Courts provides central operational and legal support to the state's judicial system.

Synopsis: Repealing the requirement that a private home detention monitoring agency provide notice to the designated law enforcement agency for violating a condition of home detention monitoring under certain circumstances.
Title: Private Home Detention Monitoring Agencies - Notification of Violation
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill modifies the notification requirements for private home detention monitoring agencies. It repeals the requirement that these agencies notify a designated law enforcement agency within 24 hours of a defendant violating a condition of home detention, although the agencies must still notify the court within that timeframe. The bill does not change existing requirements for immediate or one-hour notifications to both the court and law enforcement in cases where equipment is tampered with or the defendant enters a prohibited area.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and private home detention monitoring agencies
stakeholders: Private home detention monitoring agencies, local law enforcement agencies, the Maryland court system, and defendants on pretrial home detention.
fiscal_impact_summary: A formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. The bill reduces reporting requirements for private agencies, which may lead to minor administrative efficiencies for law enforcement agencies, but specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which the Department of Labor is responsible for administering, specifically regarding the regulation and reporting requirements of private home detention monitoring agencies.

The bill modifies requirements for notifying the court of pretrial release violations. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch in implementing policies related to these procedures.

As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police may be a 'designated law enforcement agency' that currently receives these notifications. The bill removes specific 24-hour reporting requirements to law enforcement.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency oversees pretrial detention centers and the supervision of justice-involved individuals. Changes to home detention monitoring protocols directly impact the broader pretrial supervision framework within the state's correctional system.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This office coordinates state public safety and criminal justice strategies, including policies related to pretrial release and home detention monitoring.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office represents indigent defendants who are subject to private home detention monitoring; changes in how violations are reported to law enforcement affect the legal process and due process for their clients.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies, including the Department of Labor and the Judiciary, regarding the enforcement and interpretation of statutes related to criminal procedure and business occupations.

Synopsis: Requiring that a court determine custody before awarding child support under certain circumstances; and establishing a conclusive presumption that the application of the child support guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate if the parents mutually assert that the agreement is in the best interest of the child.
Title: Family Law - Child Support - Determination of Custody and Agreements Between Parents
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/18 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires a Maryland court to determine child custody before awarding child support if a parent requests it and there has been no prior judicial determination of custody. It also establishes a conclusive presumption that the state's child support guidelines are unjust or inappropriate if the parents mutually agree to a departure from the guidelines and assert that the agreement is in the best interest of the child.
stakeholders: Parents and children in Maryland involved in child support and custody legal proceedings
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text. The legislation may result in increased judicial workload by requiring custody determinations prior to awarding child support and could lead to child support awards that deviate from standard state guidelines based on mutual parental agreements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates specific judicial procedures, requiring courts to determine custody before awarding child support in certain cases and establishing a new conclusive presumption for judges to apply when parents agree to depart from standard child support guidelines.

DHS oversees the Child Support Administration, which manages child support services and enforcement. Changes to how support amounts are determined and the recognition of parent agreements directly impact the agency's operations and federal compliance regarding state guidelines.

The OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies like DHS on the interpretation of family law and child support guidelines, and it represents the state in cases where state child support interests are involved.

The Governor's Office for Children is focused on reducing child poverty and enhancing child well-being; child support policies are a critical component of the financial stability of children in the state.

Modifications to child support determination and parent agreements can have fiscal implications for the state budget, particularly concerning federal matching funds and the administration of the Child Support Administration's programs.

Synopsis: Requiring certain facilities to inform individuals of certain rights relating to the participation of a family member or other authorized individual in the individual's plan of treatment; requiring facilities to recognize certain documents as an individual's formal request to allow a certain individual to participate in a certain plan; limiting the reasons for which a treating provider is authorized to withhold information on an individual's plan of treatment from certain third parties; etc.
Title: Mental Health - Treatment Plans for Individuals in Facilities - Participation of Family Members or Other Individuals
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 3/10 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Care Facilities -see also- Clinics; Hospices; etc
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires mental health facilities to inform patients, both verbally and in writing, of their right to have family members or other authorized individuals participate in the development and review of their treatment plans. Facilities must provide plain-language consent forms, offer information on mental health advance directives and supported decision-making, and recognize these legal documents as formal requests for third-party participation. The bill also restricts a provider's ability to withhold information from authorized parties, requiring a specific written finding of demonstrable harm to the patient if participation is denied.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and mental health facilities
stakeholders: Individuals admitted to mental health facilities, family members of patients, authorized patient representatives, and mental health treatment providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text. The bill creates administrative mandates for the Maryland Department of Health to develop model mental health advance directive forms and regulations. Mental health facilities will likely incur internal costs to update patient notification protocols, administrative documentation, and staff procedures for coordinating treatment plan meetings with authorized third parties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary agency responsible for overseeing state psychiatric facilities and behavioral health services. The bill directly impacts MDH by requiring its facilities to modify treatment plan protocols, develop model mental health advance directive forms, and establish an appeal process through the Department's Chief Medical Officer.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and its facilities. The OAG would be responsible for reviewing the model forms and regulations required by the bill to ensure compliance with state and federal laws regarding patient rights and legal instruments like advance directives.

The bill explicitly integrates 'supported decision-making agreements' into treatment planning, which is a key policy priority for the Department of Disabilities. The agency works across departments to ensure that individuals with disabilities have inclusive and autonomous access to services and information.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in involuntary commitment and mental health proceedings. The agency's attorneys advocate for the rights of these individuals within state facilities, and the new requirements for treatment plan participation and information disclosure would be significant to their legal advocacy.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires facilities to inform individuals of their rights 'verbally and using plain language.' This office is responsible for ensuring that state programs and services are accessible and inclusive for the approximately 1.2 million deaf and hard of hearing Marylanders, who require specific communication accommodations to meet this requirement.

Synopsis: Repealing the prohibition against a surrogate authorizing treatment for a mental disorder for a person who has been certified to be incapable of making an informed decision.
Title: Health Care Decisions Act - Surrogate Decision Making - Mental Disorders
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/24 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the legal prohibition that prevents a health care surrogate from authorizing treatment for a mental disorder on behalf of a person who has been certified as incapable of making an informed decision. By amending the Health Care Decisions Act, it allows authorized surrogates to make mental health treatment decisions based on the patient's known wishes or best interests when no health care agent has been appointed.
stakeholders: Patients with mental disorders who lack the capacity to make informed health care decisions, their family members or friends serving as health care surrogates, and health care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided source text. The bill itself does not explicitly state any revenue changes, new spending mandates, or direct financial allocations, focusing instead on policy changes regarding surrogate decision-making authority.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Health - General Article, which is the primary statutory domain of the Maryland Department of Health. Specifically, it repeals the prohibition against a surrogate decision-maker authorizing treatment for a mental disorder for a patient certified as incapable of making an informed decision, directly impacting the department's oversight of behavioral health and clinical standards.

As the agency responsible for coordinating services and protecting the rights of individuals with disabilities, including mental health disorders, this bill's expansion of surrogate decision-making authority for psychiatric treatment significantly impacts their constituency.

The Department of Aging oversees long-term care advocacy and support for older adults, a population that frequently utilizes the Health Care Decisions Act and surrogate decision-makers. Changes to what a surrogate may authorize regarding mental health treatment are highly relevant to their mission.

The bill modifies the authority of surrogates, and the priority list for surrogates begins with court-appointed guardians. Changes to the legal scope of treatment that a guardian or other surrogate can authorize for an incapacitated individual directly affects the judicial branch's oversight of guardianship cases.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Health and other state agencies regarding the implementation of health laws. Repealing a statutory prohibition on authorizing mental health treatment involves complex legal considerations regarding patient rights and surrogate liability.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent individuals in involuntary commitment and parental defense proceedings. Since the bill affects how mental health treatment is authorized for those deemed incapable of informed consent, it impacts the legal rights of the individuals the OPD is tasked with protecting.

DHS serves vulnerable adults through Adult Protective Services and other social services. These individuals often require surrogate decision-makers for health care, making the scope of surrogate authority relevant to DHS operations.

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law related to the Baltimore City Public School Board Community Panel; altering the process for appointments to the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; requiring the Mayor of Baltimore City to hold a public hearing to select qualified candidates for appointment to the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners; requiring that appointed members and members appointed to fill a vacancy of an appointed or elected member are subject to confirmation by the Senate of Maryland; etc.
Title: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners - Appointment Process and Compensation - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 4/01 at 1:00 p.m.

Higher Education -see also- Comm Colleges; Med Schools; etc.
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill alters the appointment process for the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners by repealing the Baltimore City Public School Board Community Panel and requiring the Mayor of Baltimore City to hold public hearings to select candidates. Appointed members are now subject to confirmation by the Senate of Maryland. Furthermore, the bill establishes an annual compensation of $10,000 for all voting members (except the student member) and mandates a $10,000 scholarship for the student member upon the completion of their term, intended for higher education or apprenticeship costs.
stakeholders: Members of the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, students of Baltimore City Public Schools, the Mayor of Baltimore City, and various community and advocacy groups in Baltimore City.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State fiscal impact is negligible, as the Senate can handle the confirmation process within existing resources. Locally, the bill creates a mandate for Baltimore City to pay $10,000 in annual compensation to 11 voting members and a $10,000 scholarship for the student member, totaling an estimated $120,000 per year. The formal Fiscal Note indicates that the bill does not materially affect city finances, though specific compensation figures are detailed in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's 24 local school systems. This bill directly alters the governance, appointment process, and compensation structure for the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, which is one of the local systems under MSDE's leadership.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Baltimore City Public School Board Community Panel, a body authorized by the General Assembly to assist in the school board appointment process. This falls under the category of executive commissions and advisory boards established to address specific government issues.

The Governor's Office oversees policy initiatives and coordinates executive branch actions. The bill makes significant changes to the appointment process of a major state-authorized board, including the addition of a Senate confirmation requirement, which involves intergovernmental and policy coordination.

The bill stipulates that the $10,000 scholarship awarded to the student member of the board shall not be considered compensation for the purpose of calculating taxable income. As the state's principal tax collector, the Comptroller is responsible for enforcing and interpreting state tax laws and exclusions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the General Assembly and state agencies. They may be required to review the legality of the changes to board structure, the compensation mandates, and the specific tax-exempt status of the student scholarship.

The bill mandates that at least one appointed member of the school board possess knowledge or experience in the education of children with disabilities. The Department of Disabilities is the principal agency for coordinating services and policies for Marylanders with disabilities and would have an interest in this board representation.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "own" for purposes of certain provisions of law governing the operation of video lottery facilities and the conduct of sports wagering to exclude certain non-voting interests in the property or business of an applicant or licensee under certain circumstances.
Title: Gaming - Definition of "Own" - Alterations
Status: In the House - Hearing 4/02 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of "own" regarding video lottery facilities and sports wagering. Specifically, it excludes individuals or entities with a beneficial or proprietary interest of 15% or less from the definition of an owner, provided that the interest does not confer voting rights and meets specific disclosure and criminal background check requirements. This change limits the scope of certain regulatory and licensing requirements for passive investors in the gaming industry.
responsible_party: Maryland State Lottery and Gaming Control Commission (SLGCC)
stakeholders: Video lottery facility applicants and licensees, sports wagering licensees, and passive investors with ownership interests of 15% or less.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill has no direct effect on State or local governmental finances. It reduces the workload for State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency investigators by simplifying background check requirements for certain specified interests, but does not result in a change in revenue or expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulatory body for lottery, video lottery facilities, and sports wagering, this agency is directly responsible for implementing the bill's changes to ownership definitions and licensing requirements. The fiscal note specifically identifies a workload reduction for the agency's investigators.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires applicants to submit State and national criminal history records checks, including fingerprints. This department manages the State's criminal record systems and is responsible for processing these background checks.
The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Lottery and Gaming Control Agency and would be involved in interpreting the revised statutory definition of 'own' and ensuring regulatory compliance.

Synopsis: Establishing the Recreational Fishery Data Collection Program in the Department of Natural Resources to develop and implement a data collection system for recreational anglers in the State; and requiring the Department to report on the findings of the Program, including a workplan detailing the proposed development and implementation of a data collection system for recreational anglers, on or before December 31, 2027.
Title: Natural Resources - Recreational Fishery Data Collection Program - Established
Status: In the House - Hearing 4/01 at 1:00 p.m.

Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; FishNets&Dev
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Recreational Fishery Data Collection Program within the Maryland Department of Natural Resources. The program is tasked with developing and implementing a data collection system for recreational anglers in the State. The department must survey reporting programs in other states, enter into a contract for the development of a data collection system (subject to available funding), and submit a report with a detailed workplan to the General Assembly by December 31, 2027.
stakeholders: Maryland recreational anglers, fishing guides, and businesses associated with the recreational fishing industry.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State General Fund expenditures will increase by at least $905,600 in FY 2027 and $621,800 in FY 2028. These costs cover the addition of two staff members, mobile application development ($500,000), and ongoing data management and outreach expenses. Special Fund revenues from the Fisheries Research and Development Fund may decrease if anglers choose not to purchase licenses due to the new requirements. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary agency responsible for establishing the Recreational Fishery Data Collection Program, developing the data collection system for recreational anglers, conducting surveys of other states, and reporting findings to the General Assembly.

The bill requires a significant increase in general fund expenditures (over $900,000 in FY 2027) and the creation of two new state personnel positions, which requires DBM's oversight regarding budget planning and personnel management.

The implementation of the program involves significant IT development, specifically the modification of the MD Outdoors mobile application and the creation of a data collection system, which falls under DoIT's purview for statewide IT strategy and infrastructure.

OAG would provide legal counsel to DNR regarding the implementation of the program, the drafting of any required regulations, and the review of the procurement contract for the data collection system.

As the head of the executive branch, the Governor's Office oversees DNR, proposes the annual budget containing the necessary program funds, and coordinates the interagency policy initiatives described in the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring a provider of a continuing care retirement community to pay any contractual entrance fee refund not later than 2 years after a continuing care agreement is terminated.
Title: Continuing Care Retirement Communities - Refunds
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/27 at 1:00 p.m.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Continuing Care -see also- Long-Term Care; Nursing Homes
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Elderly Persons (65+) -see also- Elder Abuse and Neglect
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: This bill requires providers of continuing care retirement communities (CCRCs) to pay any contractual entrance fee refunds to a subscriber or their beneficiary within two years after a continuing care agreement is terminated, regardless of whether the unit has been reoccupied by a new resident.
stakeholders: Subscribers and residents of continuing care retirement communities, their beneficiaries or estates, and CCRC providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a mandatory two-year deadline for CCRC providers to issue entrance fee refunds, which may impact the cash flow and financial management of private providers. As the formal Fiscal Note was not included in the provided text, specific state and local revenue or expenditure estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Aging is the primary regulatory authority for Continuing Care Retirement Communities (CCRCs) under Title 10, Subtitle 4 of the Human Services Article. This bill directly amends the statutes governing CCRC entrance fee refunds, which the Department oversees and enforces to protect the rights of older adults.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the Department of Aging and represents the state in matters concerning the enforcement of the Human Services Article. Additionally, its Consumer Protection Division may be involved in disputes or complaints regarding CCRC entrance fee refund delays.

CCRCs often include assisted living and comprehensive nursing care components regulated by the Department of Health. Financial regulations affecting the viability or operational requirements of CCRC providers can impact the overall health care delivery system for Maryland's senior population.

The Maryland Health Care Commission is responsible for health system planning, which includes the oversight and approval of health-related beds and services within CCRCs. bill_summary: This bill reduces the ownership and control threshold for social equity cannabis applicants from 65% to 55% and modifies regulations regarding cannabis advertising. It clarifies that advertisements must not directly target individuals under the age of 21 and removes the prohibition against advertisements being 'attractive to' minors. The bill allows standard dispensaries to display limited exterior signage for identification and safety information, subject to specific size constraints. Additionally, it requires the Maryland Cannabis Administration to develop processes for verifying audience composition for advertisements and event sponsorships, and it permits the use of cannabis-related trademarks in non-commercial editorial content like news articles or documentaries.
stakeholders: Cannabis license applicants (specifically social equity applicants), standard cannabis dispensaries, the Maryland Cannabis Administration, media entities, and editorial publishers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) is expected to implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Although the MCA initially requested $85,600 in fiscal 2027 to hire an administrator for compliance and data evaluation, the Department of Legislative Services determined that these duties can be managed by existing staff. There is no projected material impact on State revenues or local government finances. Small businesses in the cannabis industry may see a potential benefit from clarified and expanded advertising and signage options.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulatory body for the cannabis industry, the Maryland Cannabis Administration is responsible for implementing the bill's changes to advertising regulations, approving new exterior signage, accepting audience data, and submitting required reports to the General Assembly.

The bill alters the definition of 'social equity applicant' to include individuals who attended institutions of higher education where at least 40% of students are Pell Grant eligible, a metric relevant to the commission's oversight of postsecondary financial and academic standards.

The bill's criteria for 'social equity applicant' includes attendance at Maryland public schools in disproportionately impacted areas, which falls under the leadership and data oversight of the Department of Education.

The fiscal note discusses the Maryland Cannabis Administration's perceived need for additional personnel to evaluate advertising data, a matter directly overseen by the Department of Budget and Management.
The Comptroller was consulted for the fiscal note and is responsible for collecting the sales and use taxes from adult-use cannabis that fund the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Maryland Cannabis Administration and would be responsible for reviewing the legality of the new advertising regulations required by the bill.

The Maryland Cannabis Administration is an independent unit within the Executive Department, and the Governor is responsible for signing the bill into law and oversees the administration's policy initiatives.
The bill requires dispensary signage to include contact information for the Maryland Poison Center and advice for adverse events, which relates to the department's public health mission.

bill_summary: The bill establishes the Maryland Artificial Intelligence (AI) Partnership within the University System of Maryland to coordinate AI initiatives, develop a strategic plan, and create technology extension hubs. USM costs for the partnership, hubs, and lab may require additional funding beyond the initial appropriation, potentially offset by federal or private grants. MSU may incur costs if research requests exceed current capacities.

The bill explicitly designates Morgan State University's Center for Equitable Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Systems to serve as a statewide resource and hub for ethical AI use and to lead research initiatives requested by the state.
DoIT is mandated to provide policy guidance to the AI Incubation Lab, support its integration into state agencies, and provide funding, while coordinating the broader state AI program.

DBM is required to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding for the establishment of the AI Incubation Lab and must approve the repurposing of funds by state agencies to support the AI Public Service Fellowship.
The Department of Labor is tasked with collaborating with the Maryland AI Partnership to establish Technology Extension Hubs to provide AI skills training and connect businesses with resources.
The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and the AI Subcabinet, which is empowered to request research and must be consulted on the strategic plan and fellowship implementation.

The bill's focus on AI workforce development, literacy, and career pathways aligns with this board's mission to set the statewide vision for workforce solutions.
The bill's goals of advancing economic growth, innovation, and business development through AI initiatives fall within the Department of Commerce's primary mission.

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's sales and use tax by excluding certain information technology and software publishing services from the definition of a 'retail sale' when those services are used as components for other taxable services or are transferred between affiliated business entities. fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues will decrease due to the expansion of sales and use tax exclusions for specific technology services sold for resale or between affiliated companies. Because the formal Fiscal Note was not provided, specific dollar estimates are unavailable, though the nature of the impact is an indeterminate revenue decrease.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the state's chief tax collector and administrator of the sales and use tax, the Comptroller's office is directly responsible for implementing the altered definition of 'retail sale' and managing the resulting tax exclusions for technology and software publishing services.

DBM is responsible for revenue estimation and long-term fiscal planning. This bill alters the tax base for IT services, which would result in a reduction in state general fund revenues that the department must account for in the annual budget.

The bill provides tax relief for companies in the data processing, software publishing, and computer systems design sectors (NAICS 518, 519, 5415, and 5132). This directly relates to Commerce's mission to stimulate the economy and support the growth of the technology industry in Maryland.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and proposes the state budget. A change in sales tax policy impacting the technology sector aligns with the Governor's role in coordinating policy initiatives and fiscal management.

The Maryland Tax Court is the highest administrative review body for tax disputes. It would likely hear appeals regarding the interpretation of 'affiliated groups' or 'incorporation of services' under the new exclusions created by this bill.

TEDCO supports early-stage technology-based businesses. The companies in their portfolio, particularly in software and IT systems design, would be primary beneficiaries of the sales and use tax exclusion for inter-company or resale transactions.

The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for the state and provides legal counsel to the Comptroller regarding the enforcement and interpretation of tax laws, including changes to the Tax-General Article.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a Mattress Stewardship Program in Maryland, requiring mattress producers to develop and implement a plan for the collection, transportation, and recycling of postconsumer mattresses. Beginning July 1, 2031, producers must submit program plans to the Department of the Environment. The program is funded by a stewardship assessment fee added to the purchase price of mattresses sold in the state. The bill also prohibits the disposal of mattresses in landfills or incinerators beginning January 1, 2035, with limited exceptions, and creates a Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board to oversee implementation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (Office of Recycling)
stakeholders: Mattress producers, retailers, consumers, waste management and recycling entities, and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill establishes a self-funding regulatory framework. It creates an indeterminate revenue increase for the State Recycling Trust Fund through plan review and annual report fees paid by producers to cover the Department of the Environment's administrative and oversight costs. A Mattress Stewardship Assessment fee will be added to the purchase price of mattresses to fund the program's collection and recycling operations. Local governments may experience reduced expenditures as the financial responsibility for mattress disposal shifts from the public sector to producers and consumers. Specific dollar estimates are not provided in the bill text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency responsible for implementing and overseeing the Mattress Stewardship Program. Its Office of Recycling is tasked with reviewing plans, approving annual reports, setting assessments, and adopting enforcement regulations.
MES is explicitly required to coordinate with MDE's Office of Recycling to study and report on the progress of diverting mattresses from landfills and incinerators.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board to advise on the implementation and sustainability of the program.
The Comptroller (or designee) is a designated member of the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board. The agency is also responsible for accounting for the State Recycling Trust Fund.
The Secretary of Health (or designee) is a designated member of the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board.

The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is a designated member of the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board. The bill impacts mattress producers and retailers, which falls under economic development and business regulation.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the majority of members to the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board, including representatives from industry and advocacy groups.
OAG provides legal counsel to the implementing agencies. The bill also addresses immunity from antitrust and trade practice claims for activities undertaken in accordance with the approved program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program plan must specifically describe how Minority Business Enterprises (MBEs), women-owned businesses, and veteran-owned businesses will be solicited and supported, which aligns with this office's mission.
The bill establishes civil penalties for violations by retailers and producers; contested enforcement actions or appeals of these penalties would be adjudicated by OAH.
The State Treasurer is the custodian of the State Recycling Trust Fund, which will receive new fees and penalties established by the bill.
DBM oversees the personnel and fiscal impacts on MDE and other agencies tasked with staffing the Advisory Board and administering the new program.
This office will manage the recruitment and vetting of the diverse stakeholders the Governor must appoint to the Mattress Stewardship Advisory Board.
The bill requires the program to prioritize training and hiring individuals with disabilities and ensures that collection infrastructure is accessible to disabled residents.
The bill emphasizes creating jobs for homeless individuals and those experiencing housing insecurity, which are populations served by DHS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The program plan must include strategies for hiring and training individuals reentering society after imprisonment, aligning with DPSCS's rehabilitation and re-entry goals.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits child placement agencies, the Social Services Administration, and the Department of Human Services (DHS) from discriminating against prospective adoptive or foster parents, children in foster care, or employees based on characteristics such as race, sexual orientation, and gender identity. It sets criteria for the approval or denial of adoption applications and mandates that DHS and its funded contractors provide public services and maintain employment practices without discrimination, while allowing specific exceptions related to age, sex, and the religious heritage of minors.
stakeholders: Prospective adoptive and foster parents, children in foster care, employees of the Department of Human Services and its contractors, and the general public receiving services from those entities.
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the bill text. Financial implications explicitly mentioned include a prohibition on adoption agencies from denying applications due to an applicant's inability to pay fees, which could impact agency revenue. Additionally, there may be indeterminate administrative costs for the Department of Human Services to ensure compliance with the bill's non-discrimination mandates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary agency responsible for the Social Services Administration, local departments, and the management of foster care and adoption services, DHS is the central body tasked with implementing the bill's non-discrimination mandates.
The Commission enforces Maryland's anti-discrimination laws in employment and state contracts, which are key areas regulated by the bill's prohibitions for DHS and its funded entities.
The OAG serves as the chief legal representative for DHS and will be responsible for providing legal counsel on the implementation and enforcement of the bill's new statutory requirements.
The bill's focus on non-discrimination in child welfare, foster care, and adoption directly aligns with the GOC's mission to promote the well-being of Maryland's children and families.

The bill explicitly prohibits discrimination based on physical or mental disability in the provision of services by DHS and its funded entities, directly involving this department's coordination role.
The OAH may be called upon to adjudicate administrative disputes and contested cases arising from alleged violations of the bill's non-discrimination mandates or adoption application denials.
As the central personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and practices, which are affected by the bill's specific non-discrimination requirements for DHS and its funded partners.

The Board approves significant state procurement contracts; the bill's prohibition on purchasing services from entities that discriminate in public services or employment impacts DHS contract approvals.

bill_summary: The Maryland E–ZPass Commuter Fairness and Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) to submit a report to the General Assembly by September 1, 2026, regarding E-ZPass discount plans and unused commuter trips. The report must analyze data from 2023 to 2025 and provide recommendations to reduce the forfeiture of prepaid funds, such as extending usage windows or allowing trip rollovers. If more than 25% of discount plans have unused trips, the MDTA must also submit a corrective action plan to mitigate consumer harm.
stakeholders: Maryland commuters, E-ZPass discount plan holders, low-income and underbanked motorists, and the Maryland Transportation Authority.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the fiscal note, State expenditures for the Maryland Transportation Authority to complete the required report are expected to be minimal and absorbable within existing resources. No impact on State revenues or local government finances is anticipated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly names the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) as the primary agency responsible for analyzing E-ZPass data, submitting the required report, providing recommendations for lowering unused commuter trips, and implementing corrective action plans if necessary.

MDTA is a modal administration closely associated with MDOT. The bill affects the broader state transportation network operations, particularly how commuters use toll facilities versus other state-maintained highways and transit systems overseen by MDOT.

GOPI utilizes data-driven strategies and performance metrics to enhance state government responsiveness and eliminate waste. The bill's requirement for a data-driven report on unused prepaid funds and a corrective action plan to mitigate consumer harm aligns with GOPI's mission.

As the principal fiscal agency, DBM oversees budget execution and long-term fiscal planning. The bill requires reports to the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee and the House Appropriations Committee regarding toll revenue forfeitures and prepaid commuter funds.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and policy initiatives. The bill addresses significant public policy concerns regarding equity, transparency, and consumer protection for Maryland residents and commuters.

The OAG serves as legal counsel to state agencies, including MDTA. They would likely be involved in reviewing the legal implications of 'forfeiture of unused commuter trips' and the consumer protection aspects mentioned in the bill's preamble.

The bill's preamble highlights inequitable barriers to compliance for unbanked and underbanked residents and the disproportionate financial burden on low-income motorists, which falls under the commission's focus on anti-discrimination and civil rights.
DHS assists residents in economic need. The bill addresses financial burdens and banking access issues that directly impact the vulnerable populations DHS serves.

OLA conducts fiscal compliance and performance audits of executive branch agencies. If MDTA fails to accurately report on the fiscal impact of unused commuter trips, OLA could be tasked with auditing these accounts.

MVA handles vehicle registration and is often involved in the enforcement of toll violations (e.g., registration holds for unpaid tolls). The bill's focus on commuter fairness and transparency in tolling systems interacts with MVA's customer service and enforcement functions.

E-ZPass is part of a multi-state interstate compact/network. Any changes to the discount structures or usage windows in Maryland may require coordination with interstate partners or impact interstate tolling agreements.

The Innovation Team is tasked with piloting novel initiatives to enhance economic mobility and address the needs of Maryland families. The bill's requirement for a 'corrective action plan' to reduce consumer harm for commuters fits this incubator mission.

As the agency managing the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM is affected because the state program generally provides coverage for health benefits as required by state law. The fiscal note provides a specific analysis of the bill's impact on this program.

The bill's mandates on insurers directly affect the qualified health plans offered through the exchange, as the exchange is responsible for ensuring plans meet state and federal standards for coverage.

bill_summary: This bill requires owners of solid waste containers, excluding those for single-family homes, to contract with professional cleaning services for monthly cleaning and sanitization. It mandates specific cleaning protocols, including the use of approved disinfectants and high-pressure washing, and requires owners to maintain service documentation for 12 months. The Maryland Department of the Environment is authorized to impose administrative penalties of up to $250 for violations that remain uncorrected for three months.
stakeholders: Owners of commercial and multi-family residential solid waste containers, professional cleaning services, and local health departments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill creates an indeterminate increase in state or local revenue from administrative penalties of up to $250 per violation. The Maryland Department of the Environment and local health departments will incur administrative costs to implement the new standards and provide oversight. A formal Fiscal Note with specific dollar estimates was not included in the provided text.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) is the primary implementing agency for this bill. It is responsible for approving disinfectant methods, testing protocols for professional cleaning services, providing guidance to local health departments, and exercising or delegating enforcement and administrative penalty authority.

As the state's primary operational support agency, DGS manages and maintains state-owned facilities. It would be responsible for procuring professional cleaning service contracts to meet the monthly sanitization requirements for solid waste containers at most state-operated buildings.

The bill allows MDE to delegate enforcement authority to local health departments. MDH oversees and coordinates with these local departments, and the mandate for cleaning waste containers is closely linked to public health and the control of harmful microorganisms.

MDOT operates diverse facilities including BWI Airport, the Port of Baltimore, transit stations, and highway rest areas, all of which utilize large numbers of solid waste containers that would require monthly professional cleaning under this bill.

The University System manages numerous campuses with extensive solid waste infrastructure. The requirement to contract professional cleaning services for every dumpster and waste container monthly represents a significant operational and fiscal impact on the member institutions.

MFCA manages wholesale food markets in Jessup and Rock Hall. Given the high volume of organic waste at these facilities, the sanitization requirements for their solid waste containers are directly relevant to their daily operations and food safety environment.

As an independent state university with a large urban campus, Morgan State University owns and manages numerous solid waste containers that would fall under the monthly sanitization mandate, incurring a fiscal and operational impact.

The OAG would provide legal counsel to the Department of the Environment in drafting regulations and would represent the state in matters related to the enforcement and collection of administrative penalties established by the bill.

MSDE provides leadership to local school systems. Public schools utilize numerous solid waste containers that would be subject to these requirements, and the agency may need to issue guidance or coordinate with local boards on compliance costs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS manages correctional facilities statewide. These facilities generate substantial waste and utilize many containers that must be cleaned and sanitized monthly under the new mandate.
DNR manages over 500,000 acres of public lands and state parks. Many of these parks utilize solid waste containers for public use which would require monthly professional cleaning and sanitization.

MES provides technical environmental services to state and local governments, including waste management. They may be tasked by other agencies to manage compliance with these cleaning requirements or could potentially offer such services as a provider.

The Judicial Branch manages numerous court facilities throughout the state. As the owner/operator of these facilities, they would be responsible for the fiscal cost of monthly sanitization contracts for their waste receptacles.

As an independent public college, St. Mary's College would be responsible for ensuring all solid waste containers on its campus are professionally cleaned and sanitized monthly in accordance with the bill.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Office of State Elected Officials Information Privacy within the Department of Legislative Services to administer the State Elected Officials Address Confidentiality Program. The program allows current and former high-ranking state officials and their families to request that governmental entities and private persons remove or refrain from publishing their personal information—such as home addresses, phone numbers, and Social Security numbers—on the internet and social media. The bill also provides for civil relief for violations and creates a criminal misdemeanor for knowingly publishing protected information if it poses an imminent threat that results in specific crimes like assault or harassment.
responsible_party: The Office of State Elected Officials Information Privacy in the Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Current and former Maryland state elected officials (including the Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Comptroller, and members of the General Assembly) and their spouses, children, or dependents residing in the same household.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, state general fund expenditures will increase by at least $682,700 in fiscal year 2027 to fund seven new positions (including a director, analysts, and an assistant attorney general) and associated operating costs. These expenditures are projected to grow to approximately $921,800 by fiscal year 2031. Additional indeterminate costs may be incurred by other state agencies, such as the Department of State Police, for software to redact records. The bill is expected to have no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor of Maryland is specifically designated as a 'protected individual' under the bill, and the agency is responsible for overseeing the executive branch, which must comply with the new information privacy and address confidentiality requirements.
The Lieutenant Governor of Maryland is designated as a 'protected individual' whose personal information is subject to the protection and removal requirements of the bill.

The Comptroller is a 'protected individual' under the bill. Additionally, the agency maintains significant state records, including tax records, that may contain personal information subject to shielding and removal requests.

The Attorney General is a 'protected individual.' Furthermore, the OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies on compliance with the Act, and the fiscal note indicates the office has already provided analysis on the bill's constitutionality and the separation of powers.

The bill has a notable fiscal impact exceeding $680,000 annually for the creation of a new office. DBM is responsible for supervising budget execution and long-term fiscal planning related to these expenditures.

The fiscal note indicates that the Department of Planning anticipates a significant operational impact, including the need to hire a database administrator to comply with the 72-hour requirement for removing protected information from its data systems.

The Maryland State Police may face substantial fiscal impacts (estimated at $1.65 million) for software to redact personal information from traffic accident reports and incident records as required by the bill.

The Archives is the central depository for government records, including land records affected by the Address Confidentiality Program. The fiscal note specifies the agency will need an additional archivist trainee to handle the increased volume of shielded records.

The AOC administers the existing Judicial Address Confidentiality Program, which is used as a model and reference for the new program. The bill also impacts how circuit courts handle and shield real property records.

The Secretary of State administers the primary Address Confidentiality Program for survivors of domestic violence, which the bill amends and references as part of the broader framework for protecting elected officials' information.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency noted a specific operational concern regarding the bill's lack of exceptions for individuals required to register with the Maryland Sex Offender Registry.

The bill protects vehicle license plate numbers and unique identifiers, which are managed by the Motor Vehicle Administration (a division of MDOT). MDOT records are subject to the bill's shielding and removal requirements.

The bill establishes new criminal penalties (misdemeanors) for knowingly publishing personal information of protected individuals under certain circumstances, which falls under the OSP's purview regarding the integrity of state officials.

The Register of Wills maintains probate and estate records that contain residential addresses and personal identifiers of protected individuals, requiring compliance with the bill's shielding provisions.

As an agency that adjudicates contested cases for over 30 state agencies, the OAH may be involved in disputes regarding the denial of access to records or compliance with removal requests under the Act.

The bill explicitly excludes information required to be published under the Maryland Public Ethics Law from the definition of 'protected information,' requiring coordination with the Commission's existing disclosure requirements.

Synopsis: Authorizing a landlord to enter a leased premises without providing certain written notice on written request of a tenant to complete a repair or perform maintenance within 7 days after the tenant's request or if a repair is in progress and is being completed in a timely manner.
Title: Residential Real Property - Notice of Landlord Entry - Tenant Consent
Status: In the Senate - Hearing 2/19 at 1:00 p.m.
bill_summary: This bill allows landlords to enter a rental property without the standard written notice if the entry is made to perform maintenance or repairs requested in writing by the tenant. The exception applies if the landlord enters within seven days of the request or while the repair is already in progress, provided they are making a reasonable effort to complete the work in a timely manner.
stakeholders: Residential landlords and tenants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable because a formal Fiscal Note was not provided with the bill text. The legislation clarifies procedural rules for landlord entry into leased premises, which typically does not result in a direct impact on State or local government revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Section 8-221 of the Real Property Article regarding landlord entry notice. Disputes between landlords and tenants concerning entry rights and maintenance requests are adjudicated within the Maryland District Courts, making this highly relevant to the operational and legal support functions of the Judiciary.

As the primary state agency responsible for ensuring safe, secure, and affordable housing, DHCD is concerned with any legislation that impacts the rights and responsibilities of landlords and tenants in residential properties.

The OAG's Consumer Protection Division provides guidance on landlord-tenant law and investigates complaints related to consumer housing rights. Additionally, the OAG provides legal counsel to state agencies and the General Assembly regarding the implementation of real property laws.

The MCCR enforces anti-discrimination laws in housing. Modifications to the protocols for landlord entry can intersect with allegations of harassment or discriminatory treatment of tenants, making the bill relevant to their oversight of housing rights.

This bill affects the notice requirements for repairs and maintenance in residential leases. The Department of Aging is relevant as it advocates for the rights of older adults who are tenants and may be impacted by changes in landlord-tenant dynamics.

Changes to landlord entry notice for repairs can affect residents with disabilities who may require specific accommodations or advance notice for entry, making this relevant to the agency's mission to improve housing accessibility and inclusion.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain line-of-duty disability allowance to be paid to a member of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System or the State Police Retirement System who is found to be totally and permanently incapacitated, either mentally or physically, for the further performance of duty, and unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and State Police Retirement System - Line-of-Duty Catastrophic Injury Disability
Status: In the Senate - Returned Passed

bill_summary: This bill establishes a catastrophic disability benefit for members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS). Eligible members who are totally and permanently incapacitated by a line-of-duty physical accident and unable to engage in any substantial gainful activity receive a benefit equal to 100% of their average final compensation plus an annuity. The bill includes provisions for annual income verification and benefit reduction if the retiree returns to gainful employment.
stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) and the Law Enforcement Officers’ Pension System (LEOPS)
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal note indicates that the bill likely has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates because the catastrophic disability benefit is expected to apply in only a very limited number of circumstances. The State Retirement Agency can implement the administrative requirements, such as processing applications and reporting to the Joint Committee on Pensions, with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency is the primary administrator of the State Retirement and Pension System, including the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and the State Police Retirement System (SPRS). It is responsible for processing disability applications, managing medical board certifications, verifying income through tax returns, and submitting annual reports on the new catastrophic disability benefit.

The bill directly impacts the retirement and disability benefits of Maryland State Police officers, as it amends the State Police Retirement System (SPRS) to include a 100% disability benefit for catastrophic injuries.
As the principal personnel agency for the state, DBM manages employee benefits and policies. It oversees the fiscal and personnel impacts of pension system changes on state government resources.

The department employs the Natural Resources Police, whose officers are members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS) and thus eligible for the enhanced disability benefits provided by this bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency employs law enforcement personnel, such as those in the Division of Parole and Probation and internal investigative units, who are members of LEOPS and directly affected by changes to line-of-duty disability allowances.
MDOT oversees several administrations with law enforcement components, including the Maryland Transportation Authority Police, whose members are covered by the LEOPS retirement system.

The MDTA maintains its own police force, which is part of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System (LEOPS). Its officers are directly impacted by the new catastrophic disability benefit provisions.

The OAG provides legal counsel to the State Retirement Agency and the Maryland State Police. It would be involved in interpreting the legal standards for 'substantial gainful activity' and 'catastrophic injury' defined in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office advises the Governor on public safety and criminal justice strategies. Enhancing disability benefits for law enforcement officers is a significant policy area for this agency.
The Governor oversees the executive branch, including the state's law enforcement agencies, and is responsible for the state budget which includes pension contributions affected by benefit changes.

The Comptroller serves as the state's chief financial officer and is a member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System, which oversees the administration of these benefits.
The Treasurer is a key member of the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and is responsible for the management and distribution of state funds used for pension benefits.

The Board, composed of the Governor, Comptroller, and Treasurer, oversees significant state fiscal matters and integrity, overlapping with the leadership of the pension system impacted by this legislation.

bill_summary: This bill requires Maryland law enforcement agencies to dispatch at least one officer to observe and report on immigration enforcement actions occurring within their jurisdiction. The responding officer is tasked with recording the event using a body-worn camera, ensuring safe custody transfers, filing a detailed report on the incident, and preserving evidence. All reports and recordings are subject to the Public Information Act and must be stored for specified periods.
responsible_party: Maryland State, county, and municipal law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Individuals subject to immigration enforcement, law enforcement officers, federal immigration officials, and the general public
fiscal_impact_summary: Specific dollar estimates are unavailable as a formal Fiscal Note was not provided in the text. However, the bill creates potential expenditure increases for state and local law enforcement agencies to cover the costs of dispatching officers to immigration actions, administrative costs for filing detailed reports, and costs associated with recording and storing body-worn camera footage for a minimum of four months and reports for four years.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state-level law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is directly mandated to respond to, observe, and report on immigration enforcement actions occurring within its jurisdiction, involving significant operational and recording requirements.

The Department of Transportation oversees the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) Police, Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) Police, and Maryland Aviation Administration (MAA) Police, all of which fall under the definition of state law enforcement agencies required to comply with the bill's reporting and observation mandates.

The Maryland Natural Resources Police (NRP) is a primary state law enforcement agency. Under this bill, NRP officers would be required to respond to and document immigration enforcement actions within their jurisdictional areas, such as state parks and waterways.

The OAG provides legal counsel to all state agencies and boards. It would be responsible for advising law enforcement agencies on the implementation of these new requirements and the legal implications of the Public Information Act as applied to the required reports and body-worn camera footage.

The Maryland Capitol Police, managed by the Department of General Services, is a state law enforcement agency that would be required to follow the bill's procedures for responding to and recording immigration enforcement actions within its jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the Governor's primary coordinating body for public safety and criminal justice strategies, this office would likely oversee the policy development and interagency collaboration required to implement the bill's mandates effectively across the state.

The University System of Maryland manages several institutions with their own campus police departments. These departments are state law enforcement agencies and must comply with the requirements to respond to and document immigration enforcement actions on their campuses.

The Comptroller's Field Enforcement Division possesses law enforcement powers. If immigration enforcement actions occur within their regulatory or criminal investigative scope, they would be subject to the bill's mandates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department employs law enforcement personnel, including the Intelligence and Investigative Division and correctional police officers, who may be required to respond to or document immigration actions that intersect with their jurisdictional responsibilities.
As a state agency with its own police force, Morgan State University is subject to the bill's requirements regarding law enforcement response to immigration enforcement actions on its campus.
Saint Mary's College operates an independent state police force which would be required to implement the observation, recording, and reporting mandates of this bill.

The bill may have a fiscal impact related to staffing, body-worn camera data storage costs, and reporting administrative burdens across various state agencies, necessitating budget review and planning by DBM.

The Governor's Office oversees the executive branch and coordinates state policy initiatives. The bill affects multiple executive departments and aligns with the Governor's role in overseeing the enforcement of state laws.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to intercept a wire, oral, or electronic communication that is a recording or part of a recording of the commission or attempted commission of a certain crime; providing that the contents of a certain intercepted communication and evidence derived from the communication may be received in evidence in a criminal trial or hearing before the District Court or circuit court under certain circumstances; and providing for a certain affirmative defense to a charge under the wiretap statute.
Title: Wiretapping and Electronic Surveillance - Intercepted Communications - Admissibility of Evidence
Status: In the House - Hearing 3/31 at 1:00 p.m.
